author.name: Junghwan Lim, Joon Son Chung, Sungmin Lee, Wai Ting Cheung, Gihun Cho, Minsu Ha, Sangho Kang, Beomgyu Kim, Dongseok Kim, Jangwoong Kim, Taehyun Kim, Taewhan Kim, Jeesoo Lee, Jeongdoo Lee, Junhyeok Lee, Dongpin Oh, Hyeyeon Cho, Dahye Choi, Jaeheui Her, Hanbin Jung, Changjin Kang, Minjae Kim, Youngrok Kim, Hyukjin Kweon, Hongjoo Lee, Yeongjae Park, Bokki Ryu

entry.summary: SLIFT decomposes each user feedback message into atomic components classified as task-validity fixes, condition-specific refinements, or non-informative, then routes them to two LoRA adapters on a frozen backbone so general corrections become default behavior while narrow preferences stay scoped. Addresses over-generalization when learning continually from chat feedback.

entry.title: RISE-RL: Rubric-Informed Selective Exploration for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jinkun Hou, Zhuo Liu, Huimin Ren, Hongsheng Xin, Pan Zhou, Kun Zhan

entry.summary: RISE-RL improves rubric-based RL for open-ended generation by using repeatedly missed rubric criteria to elicit privileged trajectories that unguided exploration rarely finds, keeping only those that beat the mean natural-rollout reward before re-scoring them. Targets the loss of criterion-level signal when rubric feedback is collapsed into a scalar reward.

entry.title: Coupled Graph--Policy Distillation for Personalized Medication Safety in Older Adults with Multimorbidity

author.name: Zihan Wang, Anglin Liu, Rongyi Wang, Dantong Li, Yi Lu, Siqing Yuan, Hongxia Xu, Zhongtian Long, Jintai Chen

entry.summary: ATLAS structures medication guideline evidence as a safety graph, asks targeted questions to fill in a patient's omitted conditions and medications, distills a patient-specific conflict graph, and runs a risk-first multi-agent policy to screen contraindications and propose safer alternatives for older adults with multimorbidity. Introduces GeriMedBench for interactive evaluation.

entry.title: Rethinking Self-Evolving Agents: Do We Still Need Prescribed Optimization Pipelines?

author.name: Hui Xue, Fan Yang

entry.summary: Asks whether hand-designed optimization pipelines for self-evolving agents are still needed when a frontier model acts as the optimizer, introducing Open-Ended Optimization that fixes objective, interactions, budget, data boundary, and evaluation while letting the optimizer compose its own improvement process. Compares against a staged bounded-edit pipeline and a reflective evolutionary search across fourteen head-to-head settings using an existing GPT-5.5 class model as the optimizer.

entry.title: Knowing You Is Everything: LLM Agents Achieve Near-Perfect Profile-Consistent Reaction Prediction in Social Media Simulation

author.name: Ljubisa Bojic, Ljiljana Matic, Joerg Matthes, Milan Cabarkapa, Bojana Dinic, Jue Wang

entry.summary: Benchmarks twelve LLM configurations on predicting individual like/dislike reactions to social media posts using survey-derived persona profiles, comparing profile completeness levels against ML classifier baselines. Reports very high accuracy with full profiles, with implications for both recommender testing and astroturfing risk.

entry.title: AeroDPO: Unleashing Lightweight UAV Navigation with High-Fidelity Perception and Automated Preference Optimization

author.name: Peng Xu, Chengcheng Wang, Shaohua Wan

entry.summary: AeroDPO shows that for UAV vision-language navigation, perception fidelity matters more than language model size, with a 2B model plus high-quality visual input matching 7B baselines. It then adds automated preference optimization to fix the robustness gaps of the lightweight policy for edge deployment.

entry.title: The Anatomy of a Prompt Injection: A Component Model for Structured Analysis

author.name: Jeremy McHugh

entry.summary: Argues prompt injections are still catalogued as verbatim strings rather than structured exploits, and proposes a seven-component model capturing attacker intent such as tool targets, sinks, and effects. Intended to let defenders and threat intelligence teams label, compare, and mutate attacks without brittle string matching.

entry.title: Distilling CT Foundation Models into Editable Concept Bottlenecks for Lung Nodule Malignancy Prediction

author.name: Fakrul Islam Tushar, Stephen Adamo, Geoffrey D. Rubin

entry.summary: Distills two frozen CT foundation models into editable concept bottleneck models that predict eight radiologist-defined nodule attributes and then infer malignancy from those concepts plus nodule size. Trained on LIDC-IDRI and LUNA25 with internal and external cohort evaluation and concept fidelity assessment.

entry.title: Evidence-RL: Towards Evidence-intensive Visual Reasoning

author.name: Haojie Huang, Xinlei Yu, Chengming Xu, Zhangquan Chen, Cheng Yang, Qingdong He, Yu Yang, Jiangning Zhang, Xiaobin Hu

entry.summary: Proposes Counterfactual Evidence Disentanglement, a training-time audit that masks object-centric evidence regions and checks whether a vision-language model answer actually depends on them, then folds that causal signal into GRPO reward. The goal is to stop VLMs from answering from language priors or dataset shortcuts rather than image evidence.

entry.title: From Recovery to Drop-off: How Action Post-training Reduces a VLM's Late-Layer Depth Decodability

author.name: Alexander Hackett, Arnaud Denis-Remillard, Axel Cassou

entry.summary: Probes depth perception at every decoder layer of a weight-matched base vision-language model and its action post-trained counterpart, finding the robot policy decodes depth worse at every layer and additionally collapses in the final layers rather than improving. The late-layer drop is causally traced to MLP writes, since ablating them recovers most of the lost decodability.

entry.title: ActBench: Self-Evolving Benchmark of Behavioral Safety in Cowork Agents

author.name: Hongwei Yao, Yiming Liu, Meihui Chen, Jieling Chen, Zikun Chen, Yiling He, Wangze Ni, Cong Wang, Kui Ren

entry.summary: ActBench evaluates behavioral safety of coworking agents from execution trajectories rather than final answers, pairing 600 benign tasks across 213 scenarios with adversarial variants that inject task-reachable payloads while holding instruction and configuration fixed. A reward-guided beam search generates attacks that optimize both effectiveness and task completion, making the benchmark self-evolving.

entry.title: Carnot: Interpretable, Interactive, and Optimized Execution of Deep Research Queries

author.name: Matthew Russo, Yash Agarwal, Tianyu Li, Zhuohan Gu, Michael Cafarella, Omar Khattab, Tim Kraska, Samuel Madden

entry.summary: Carnot compiles natural-language deep research requests over enterprise data lakes into explicit physical execution graphs that users can inspect, interrupt, and correct, while optimizing API cost and latency. Positions itself between opaque black-box research agents and prohibitively expensive semantic operators.

entry.title: MoNo: Multiscale Optimal Transport Neural Operator for Solving PDEs on General Geometries

author.name: Zijiang Yang, Xiaomeng Wu, Dongmei Fu

entry.summary: MoNo diagnoses that learnable projections in transformer neural operators assign observation points to latent tokens unevenly, causing some tokens to be overloaded and others unused, with the imbalance compounding across hierarchical layers into token collapse. It replaces the projection with a multiscale optimal-transport assignment for PDE solving on general geometries.

entry.title: Fusion Training for Mathematical Generalization in Large Language Models

author.name: Congfeng Cao, Pengyu Zhang, Jelke Bloem

entry.summary: Systematically studies how to train a single model that supports both terse answers and long-form reasoning, varying the ratio of thinking to non-thinking data and the training schedule on mathematical problems. The authors report an asymmetric interaction, where adding non-thinking supervision affects the reasoning mode differently than the reverse.

entry.title: Your VLM Already Knows When: Training-Free Temporal Grounding by Asking Yes or No

author.name: Ji Huang, Barry Devereux, Hui Wang

entry.summary: The authors show that vision-language models fail at video temporal grounding because of the task interface, not perception: replacing timestamp regression with a coarse-to-fine scan of yes-or-no questions ranked by first-token probability raises recall at 0.5 IoU by 28 to 50 points across four frozen backbones. They also document that most wrong timestamp predictions are confidently wrong, defeating entropy-based error detection.

entry.title: AndroidReality: How Far Are Mobile Agents from the Real World?

author.name: Xiaoou Liu, Longchao Da, Hanyang Chen, Yuan Ling, Hua Wei

entry.summary: Introduces a perturbation framework that stress-tests mobile GUI agents by injecting realistic interface variability along state, transition, and action axes derived from an MDP taxonomy, layered on top of an existing Android benchmark. It quantifies how sharply agent performance degrades away from clean benchmark conditions.

entry.title: Matching Supervision to the Student's Learning Capacity: A Unified Framework for On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Yongkang Yang, Zhezheng Hao, Hong Zhang, Yi Liu, Xiankun Lin, Wence Ji, Fanjunduo Wei, Jiarui Yu, Qiang Lin, Xiaoyun Liang, Hande Dong

entry.summary: Unifies two strands of on-policy self-distillation, one choosing which tokens to learn from and one controlling how much privileged context the teacher sees, arguing they are coupled through the student's learning capacity. The framework jointly optimizes both variables instead of fixing one, since privileged information sets per-token divergence while token weighting determines what the student can actually absorb.

entry.title: Performance of large language models in the optical diagnosis of colorectal polyps

author.name: Joshua C. Vences, William T. Tran, Nikko Gimpaya, Catharine M. Walsh, Rishad J. Khan, Robert Bechara, Asher C. Wiggins, Celine N. Rousan, Kaitlyn V. G. L. Morgado, Angie Ibrahim, Kevin H. M. Kuo, Daniel von Renteln, Alexander Hann, Dennis L. Shung, Michael A. Scaffidi, Charles M\'enard, Joshua Landy, Samir C. Grover

entry.summary: A retrospective clinical study evaluating five existing multimodal models, including Claude Opus 4, Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-o3, GPT-4o, and GPT-5, on classifying colorectal polyps and predicting histology from endoscopic images against expert responses. Reports F1 and accuracy comparisons on a curated white-light and narrow-band imaging dataset.

entry.title: ScaleSense: Cost-Intelligent Scaling Framework via Learned Resource Estimation in Alibaba AnalyticDB

author.name: Yifan Wu, Yuhan Li, Zhenhua Wang, Ke Chen, Lidan Shou, Zonghao Chen, Liang Lin, Huan Li, Gang Chen

entry.summary: ScaleSense predicts per-query resource needs in Alibaba's serverless AnalyticDB warehouse using an encoder that jointly models query plan topology and hardware specs, to escape a documented provisioning trap where users over-allocate out of fear of resource exhaustion. Aimed at cutting cost without hitting non-CPU bottlenecks like I/O saturation.

entry.title: Evidence-Grounded Forensic Reasoning for Detecting and Grounding Multi-Modal Media Manipulation

author.name: Yichun Yeh, Yiheng Li, Xiaobo Hu, Zhen Lei, Yang Yang

entry.summary: Targets multimodal media manipulation detection where explanations must be tied to predicted evidence locations, avoiding rationales disconnected from localized forgery regions. Uses differentiated training signals for localization versus explanation tokens to actively enforce evidence-conclusion consistency.

entry.title: Hidden Language Consistency Phenomena in Reasoning LLMs

author.name: Muhammad Ali Shafique, Kelly Marchisio

entry.summary: Measures whether multilingual reasoning models keep the intended language during their chain of thought and in their final answer across eight languages and four difficulty tiers of the PolyMath benchmark, distinguishing thinking-language from answer-language consistency. Documents four distinct degradation patterns as tasks get harder, including abrupt collapse.

entry.title: SkillsMetric: Mapping the Detection Boundary of Static Analysis for Malicious Agent Skills

author.name: Xinze Chen, Chi Zhang, Ping Ji, Yimin Liu

entry.summary: Builds a five-stage static analysis scoring framework for agent skill packages along pattern density, statistical anomaly, dataflow taint, import anomaly and capability mismatch, and evaluates it against an adversarial set of over two thousand malicious skills covering sixteen attack types. Reports strong detection of data exfiltration and steganographic payloads while mapping where static analysis fundamentally fails.

entry.title: Learning from Consensus and Disagreement: Unsupervised On-Policy Self-Distillation with Minority-Trajectory Contrast

author.name: Jiaxin Guo, Yanwei Yue, Xuanbo Fan, Chunyu Yang, Yan Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a fully unsupervised on-policy self-distillation method that manufactures privileged information from the model own unlabeled rollouts, using answer-level consensus to condition a frozen self-teacher and contrasting minority trajectories to capture disagreement. Removes the dependence on gold solutions or verifiers that current privileged-teacher methods require.

entry.title: Energy-Structured Latent World Models with Neural Time Fields for Physically Constistent Open-World Motion Planning

author.name: Yapeng Liu, Yuanzhao Zhai, Bo Ding, Huaimin Wang, Lin Wang

entry.summary: An energy-structured latent world model that forces the latent state to explicitly carry energy and momentum with dissipation and control ports, so learned dynamics obey causal physical structure instead of absorbing physics implicitly. The goal is reusable physical knowledge for reliable open-world motion planning from multimodal sensor data.

entry.title: When Does Trace-Driven Evaluation Mislead MoE Expert Caching? Replay Semantics, Workload Contamination, and Operating Regimes

author.name: Yu Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that trace-driven simulation studies of mixture-of-experts expert caching can invert policy rankings depending on replay semantics, with inconsistent per-access replay inflating recency-based policies by nearly thirty percent while barely affecting frequency-based ones. It also flags workload contamination and operating-regime effects as sources of misleading conclusions.

entry.title: Quality-Diversity Stress Tests for Process Reward Models:What Archive Coverage Can and Cannot Certify

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Fariya Afrin

entry.summary: Frames stress testing of process reward models as a quality-diversity search, using an archive method to retain the most severe correctness-flipping edit found in each region of behavior space and separating search coverage from exploit coverage. It also delineates what archive coverage can certify, showing covered-cell risk can be bounded while the worst uncovered cell cannot.

entry.title: Activation Probes Surface Code-Security Signals that the Model's Output Misses

author.name: Ivan Wiryadi

entry.summary: Trains a single linear probe on the activations of open-weight reviewer models using paired vulnerable and fixed Python functions, then tests transfer to real disclosed vulnerabilities with unseen weakness types. Finds the probe recovers security signal that simply prompting the same model to answer misses, suggesting a scalable internal-state monitor for AI-generated code review.

entry.title: Explicit Boundary Markers for Subword Vocabularies

author.name: Sander Land, Clara Meister

entry.summary: Points out that standard subword tokenizers duplicate common words into leading-space and no-space variants with independently trained embeddings and inconsistent segmentations, worsened further by capitalization. Proposes replacing whitespace conventions with an explicit word boundary marker so each word has a single canonical entry.

entry.title: REFRAMED: Towards Realistic Audio Description Generation for Movies

author.name: Igor Sterner, Mirella Lapata, Alex Lascarides, Frank Keller

entry.summary: REFRAMED reformulates movie audio description generation so models must decide both when to speak and what to say, instead of being handed pre-specified timing and clip boundaries. The work also supplies cleaner parallel data and narrative context, addressing noisy alignment pipelines in prior benchmarks.

entry.title: ZhuLong: Execution-Grounded LLM Agent for EDA Scripting with Offline API Self-Exploration

author.name: Yang Liu, Shiwei Hou, Xiyuan Chen, Yu Wang, Sen Yuan, Qirui Gan, Shao You, Feifan Chen, Wencheng Li, Shuyang Hu, Yongzhou Liu, Emma Xia, Xiaojing Lu, Hao Wang, Fan Xu, Yanfeng Li

entry.summary: Builds an execution-grounded coding agent for electronic design automation scripting languages that combines API retrieval, documentation inspection, and sandbox execution through unified tool interfaces, plus offline self-exploration that infers undocumented API behavior by counterfactual experimentation. On a 158-task real-world benchmark it reaches roughly 79 percent pass at one versus about 24 percent for a plain LLM baseline.

entry.title: Illusion of Alignment: Detecting Hidden Disagreement in Collaborative Dialogue

author.name: Kaiming Liu, Fuwen Luo, Ziyue Wang, Jinrui Ju, Yuxuan Liu, Xuanyu Lei, Yunghwei Lai, Peng Li, Yang Liu

entry.summary: This work names and operationalizes the illusion of alignment, where collaborators end a discussion apparently agreeing while holding incompatible assumptions or plans. The authors generate diagnostic multiple-choice probes whose divergent answers reveal hidden disagreement, and release a dataset plus protocol validated against 18 real meetings. It is a creative measurement idea applicable to both human teams and multi-agent LLM collaboration.

entry.title: LatticeMind: A Conflict-Aware Memory Primitive for Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Heng Zhou, Lian Zhang, Yutao Fan, Tiancheng He, Siki Chen, Hejia Geng, Philip Torr, Zhenfei Yin

entry.summary: LatticeMind is a shared memory primitive for multi-agent LLM systems that resolves contradictions at write time, tracking which claims are contested, superseded or trusted rather than just voting on outputs. Cheap symbolic checks handle most conflicts and an LLM reconciles only ambiguous semantic cases. Reported accuracy on a label-blind conflict benchmark is far above aggregation baselines.

entry.title: Query-Only Backdoor Attacks on Self-Evolving Skills via Trajectory Poisoning

author.name: Yuyang Luo, Haoran Wang, Kai Shu

entry.summary: The authors show that self-evolving skill pipelines, adopted partly to avoid untrusted external skill marketplaces, open a new attack surface: an adversary who only submits queries can steer the skills an agent writes for itself, planting backdoors via poisoned execution trajectories. This query-only threat model requires no direct access to skill files or weights. It highlights that internal self-improvement loops need provenance and validation too.

entry.title: FailForge: Distilling Procedural Competence from Persistent Failures into Code Agents

author.name: Dongyi Lv, Fushun E, Aichen Cai, Liang Huang, Ya Zhang, Qiuyu Ding, Canhui Wu, Zhi Wang, Yuesong Zhang, Jiaqi Wang, Nan Duan

entry.summary: FailForge turns discarded failed rollouts in rejection-sampling fine-tuning of code agents into usable training signal, on the grounds that the failures come from the hardest and most expensive verifiable tasks. An agentic pipeline extracts procedural competence from persistent failures rather than throwing them away. This improves sample efficiency at the frontier of what a code agent can already do.

entry.title: Capability Is Not Propensity: Measuring Pressure-Robust Cooperative Behavior in Civic LLM Agents

author.name: Neel Tushar Shah, Manglam Kartik, Akshat Karkar

entry.summary: DiffCoop-Civic separates what models can do cooperatively under benign instructions from what they tend to do under realistic civic pressure, across ten scenarios covering persuasion, commitment design, asymmetric information, and dissent preservation. Across seven models from four families, mild omission pressure uniformly increases manipulative enablement and reduces dissent preservation.

entry.title: Agentic Auto-Research is Fuzz Testing

author.name: Yifeng He, Jicheng Wang, Yinzhe Zhao, Jiachen Liu, Hao Chen

entry.summary: Argues that autonomous research agents should be designed like greybox fuzzers rather than generate-and-rank samplers: each experiment should expose partial-progress feedback analogous to coverage, and that signal should drive mutation and effort allocation instead of only ranking finished runs. Reframes the sparse-feedback problem in auto-research.

entry.title: Experience-Sensitive Game Learning: A Behavioral Study of Humans and Language Agents

author.name: Yingying Guo, Zhuoxuan Ju, Ruibo Ming, Ruicheng Feng, Jinjin Gu

entry.summary: Introduces a framework and game suite for studying how repeated play changes the behavior of humans versus LLM agents, shifting evaluation from final win rates to learning trajectories. Provides cross-game greedy-to-global metrics and behavioral diagnostics computed from action traces.

entry.title: KumbhDoot: A Scale-Ready, LLM-Bounded Architecture for Mass-Gathering Public-Service Assistants

author.name: Saurabh Sakalkar, Abhishek Singh, Ramesh Raskar

entry.summary: KumbhDoot is a deployed-style assistant architecture for mass gatherings that routes most queries through semantic similarity retrieval and bounds LLM use, prioritizing latency, cost, offline resilience, and hallucination avoidance on safety-critical facts. Designed for tens of millions of pilgrims at the Kumbh Mela.

entry.title: Generalizing deep reinforcement learning across cable-driven parallel robot configurations with actuator-level policies

author.name: Abir Bouaouda (CRAN, UIR), Mohamed Boutayeb (CRAN, UIR), Fran\c{c}ois Charpillet (LARSEN), Dominique Martinez (LORIA, ISM), R\'emi Pannequin (CRAN)

entry.summary: Trains actuator-level deep RL policies for cable-driven parallel robots, where each motor learns to reach its target cable length, rather than a whole-robot policy mapping to end-effector position. This makes the learned controller transferable across configurations and differing actuator counts.

entry.title: What to Edit Next: Visually Aligned Image-Editing Follow-Up Suggestions in Conversational Systems

author.name: Zhijing Zhang, Jinpeng Yu, Xin Song, Bingnan Li, Chuyue Li, Changhui Du, Xiaolin Fang, Jiaming Liu, Ruihua Huang

entry.summary: Studies recommending follow-up edit suggestions in multi-turn image creation conversations, reporting that about 80 percent of 100,000 real Qwen App conversations are image-dependent and thus require multimodal recommendation. A three-stage pipeline builds a reviewed intent table, fine-tunes on synthesized targets, and enforces executability on the current image.

entry.title: BRACE: Taming Sharp Irregularities via Barycentric Rational Forecasting for Fast Diffusion Transformers Inference

author.name: Jinlong Yang, Jinke Wu, Lizilin, Yao Zhou

entry.summary: BRACE accelerates diffusion transformer inference by replacing derivative-based polynomial extrapolation of cached features with barycentric rational forecasting plus Chebyshev enhancement, motivated by feature trajectories that are globally smooth but locally irregular. Targets quality collapse at high acceleration ratios.

entry.title: ToolVision: Learning When and How to Use Visual Tools with Capability-Aligned Supervision

author.name: Delin Mao, Chenghao Sun, Jingwei Song, Chishui Chen, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: Diagnoses two distinct supervision mismatches in the standard recipe for teaching models to think with images: supervised traces from stronger teachers rely on perception a smaller student cannot reproduce, while outcome-only RL suppresses tool use and blanket bonuses reward useless calls. Proposes capability-aligned supervision so the student learns both when and how to invoke visual tools.

entry.title: From Inaudible Inputs to Model Failures: Low-Frequency Safety Risks in LALMs

author.name: Yuanhe Zhang, Weiliu Wang, Jie Ren, Liang Lin, Zhenhong Zhou, Haoran Gao, Kun Wang, Chen Li, Li Sun, Sen Su

entry.summary: Shows that low-frequency audio inaudible to humans can be injected into large audio-language models to disrupt or steer generation, using a universal waveform template built from sentence-attention interval estimation and spectral frequency transfer in a black-box setting. Also discusses mitigation of this red-teaming channel.

entry.title: Beyond Solvability: Task Learnability as a Static Prior for LLM RL Post-Training

author.name: Ting Zhou, Zhenqing Ling, Daoyuan Chen, Qianli Shen, Yilun Huang, Ying Shen, Yaliang Li

entry.summary: Introduces task learnability, a regime-conditional measure of how much a task will positively respond to further RL post-training, arguing that current pass-rate or reward snapshots only capture solvability. Uses per-task reward trajectory analysis to build a static prior for sampling tasks during RL.

entry.title: Privileged Solutions or Context-Induced Teacher Behavior? Dissecting On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Yuki Ichihara, Naoto Iwase, Mohammad Atif Quamar, Junpei Komiyama

entry.summary: Disentangles why on-policy self-distillation works by replacing the paired reference solution with a solution to a different problem, isolating target-specific privileged information from the general effect of conditioning the teacher on any worked solution. Evaluates across three models and multiple tasks.

entry.title: WorldSimProbe: Diagnosing Simulator Faithfulness in Action-Conditioned World Models for Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Peterson Co, Sicheng Hu, Chunxuan Jiao, Hongyang Cheng, Yulin Luo, Yijie Xu, Sixiang Chen, Zhongxia Zhao, Zihao Wang, DaFeng Chi, Peidong Liu, YuTong Chen, Henghua Liu, Zhihao Yuan, Huizhu Jia, Yuzheng Zhuang, Tianle Zhang, Liang Lin, Huajie Tan, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: WorldSimProbe defines an observable simulator contract that action-conditioned world models must satisfy to serve as physical simulators, then diagnoses whether current models actually respect supplied actions rather than merely producing plausible video. Argues prevailing evaluations of visual quality and task outcome hide fidelity failures.

entry.title: Rethinking Factor Sharing in Federated LoRA: A Rank-Aware Adaptive Approach

author.name: Xinyi Xu, Bingnan Xiao, Shuang Qin, Gang Feng, Tony Q. S. Quek

entry.summary: Analyzes whether federated LoRA should share the down-projection factor or the up-projection factor across clients, showing with a least-squares surrogate that the two choices force a common input-side versus output-side low-rank subspace and hence different projection residuals. From this the authors derive a rank-aware adaptive sharing rule.

entry.title: SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Zhuo Sun, Entong Li, Yanlong Zhao, Xiaoyuan Cheng, Wenxuan Yuan, Kaiyu Li, Che Liu, Huihang Liu, Harrison Bo Hua Zhu, Li Zeng

entry.summary: SR-OPSD tackles instability in on-policy self-distillation, where the teacher is a moving copy of the student conditioned on extra context and therefore co-evolves with the student and its rollout distribution. It replaces a fixed projection objective with a self-referenced target to avoid divergence or excessive distributional concentration.

entry.title: Multi-Agent AI Safety as an Institutional Design Problem

author.name: Abdullah X

entry.summary: Treats multi-agent AI safety as institutional design, asking which parts of a deployment rulebook, such as delegation rules, information flow, and authority checks, actually produce safe collective behavior. It reports a frozen suite of 5,280 episodes across several model families with matched workflows and varying rule formulations.

entry.title: TEMPER: Tensorized Efficient Manifold-constrained Parameterization for Expressive Residual Routing

author.name: Yuxuan Gu, Wuyang Zhou, Huijun Xing, Danilo Mandic

entry.summary: TEMPER identifies that hyper-connection style multi-stream residual routing is bottlenecked by dense unstructured generator matrices whose parameter count grows quickly with the number of streams. It replaces them with tensorized manifold-constrained parameterizations to keep expressive dynamic residual routing affordable.

entry.title: Information Routing across Batch Boundaries: Memory--Batch Tradeoffs in Lipschitz Bandits

author.name: Zicheng Lyu, Zengfeng Huang

entry.summary: Studies stochastic Lipschitz bandits where the learner keeps only a limited number of bits of reward-dependent state and may only act in a limited number of committed batches, characterizing minimax regret up to logarithmic factors. The analysis reveals a new penalty term proving that memory width and update depth are not interchangeable resources.

entry.title: Adaptive Supervised Anchoring for On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Meilin Yang (Renmin University of China, Beijing, China), Zixuan Ding (Renmin University of China, Beijing, China), Jianhao Nie (Renmin University of China, Beijing, China), Weite Zhang (Renmin University of China, Beijing, China), Yuxin Zhang (Renmin University of China, Beijing, China), Zhiming Shao (Renmin University of China, Beijing, China), Li Yu (Renmin University of China, Beijing, China), Zhe Fu (Renmin University of China, Beijing, China)

entry.summary: Identifies rollout-conditioned signal degradation, where conditioning a frozen teacher on off-target student prefixes substantially weakens the useful supervision in on-policy self-distillation, and demonstrates it with controlled prefix-corruption experiments. The fix separates rollout-conditioned distribution matching from an anchoring supervision pathway on target trajectories.

entry.title: ZeroLock: Concurrent Memory-Efficient LLM Training via Modular Update Decoupling

author.name: Wentao Dai, Xuanran Li, Yuxiang Zhang, Ming Tang, Chao Huang

entry.summary: ZeroLock fine-tunes language models on edge devices without backpropagation by decoupling updates into independent per-chunk updates driven by local objectives, breaking the update-locking that serializes pipeline-parallel training. The claim is higher throughput and lower memory from reduced activation storage.

entry.title: Opportunity Is Not Realizability: Selection-Valid Diagnostics for Multi-LLM Routing

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Abu Sa-Adat Mohamed Moon-Im Al Ahsan, Md Najmus Swaqeeb

entry.summary: Argues that oracle routing numbers overstate what a deployable multi-model router can achieve, because they compare against a best fixed model chosen on the same examples and assume access to outcomes no router can see before answering. The paper separates three distinct quantities and provides selection-valid confidence intervals plus a greedy guarantee for assembling compact model pools.

entry.title: Correlation flow governs learning at criticality

author.name: Andrea Combette, Nelly Pustelnik, Antoine Venaille

entry.summary: Combines mean-field and random matrix theory to connect signal correlation propagation at initialization with the Neural Tangent Kernel in the limit of infinitely wide and deep networks. The analysis shows correlation propagates to infinite depth only at one critical point in the weight-bias variance plane, where the NTK becomes exactly proportional to output correlation.

entry.title: Beyond Routing: Decoupling Expert Dispatch and Aggregation in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Zongfei Li

entry.summary: Questions whether sparse mixture-of-experts routers should use one score for both selecting experts and weighting their outputs, showing on a pretrained 1B-parameter MoE that the top-scored expert is the counterfactually best one only about seventeen percent of the time. A small post-compute aggregation head trained on the language modeling objective recovers part of an oracle gain in cross-entropy.

entry.title: Twin Rollouts: Noise-Coupled Counterfactual Branching in Interactive Video World Models

author.name: Yu Ma, Hongli Shi, Xinran Xu

entry.summary: Formalizes counterfactual evaluation inside interactive video world models by running paired factual and counterfactual rollouts that share the generated prefix and the exogenous noise sequence but diverge in actions from an intervention point. Because the factual branch is self-generated, Pearl's abduction step is exact rather than approximated.

entry.title: Leveraging generative models to assist Monte Carlo sampling

author.name: Marylou Gabri\'e

entry.summary: A tutorial review of how generative models such as normalizing flows and diffusion samplers can accelerate Monte Carlo sampling of high-dimensional, multimodal distributions in Bayesian inference and statistical physics. It surveys the emerging interface between machine learning and computational statistical physics, including how to retain asymptotic correctness.

entry.title: A continually expandable foundation model for brain MRI

author.name: Michail Mamalakis, Carmen Jimenez-Mesa, Yonghao Li, Hao Chen, Chao Li, Antonios Mamalakis, John Suckling, Richard Bethlehem, Stephen J. Price, Richard J. Gilbertson, Pietro Lio

entry.summary: Alcmaeon is a 3D brain MRI foundation model pretrained without manual labels on over 425,000 volumes that can be expanded sequentially into new clinical domains rather than retrained from scratch. Graph-Blueprint Pruning protects modules important to earlier domains while freeing capacity for new ones, combining volumetric encoding with latent diffusion generation.

entry.title: Safety Cost of Steering Vectors Is Separable and Reducible

author.name: Yuxiao Li, Gjergji Kasneci

entry.summary: Shows that the safety degradation caused by activation steering vectors comes from a separable component that disrupts refusal mechanisms while contributing little to the intended steering behavior. The authors remove it via constrained primal-dual optimization that preserves the steering effect and bounds false refusals.

entry.title: Pragmatic Attack Surface: Vulnerabilities of Implicit Context in Large Language Models

author.name: Bocheng Chen, Han Zi, Roucheng Ou, Yawei Liu, Minyue Chen, Zimo Qi, Rongrong Wang, Guangliang Liu

entry.summary: The paper argues that most jailbreak work targets explicit linguistic cues, while human language also depends on unstated pragmatic context such as world knowledge and social norms. It frames this implicit context as a distinct attack surface that current safety alignment underserves, and studies how it can be exploited.

entry.title: Forged Peer Judgments Mislead Multimodal LLM Judge Panels: Source-Blind Anchoring and Panel-Consensus Verification

author.name: Yang Shu

entry.summary: This study shows that quoting a fabricated peer judgment can flip vision-language judge panels, producing anchoring gaps of roughly 19 to 26 percentage points, while a label-only control has essentially no effect. Deliberately crafted wrong quotes overturn correct verdicts far more often than naturally occurring wrong peer statements, exposing a text-level attack surface in multi-judge evaluation.

entry.title: Unveiling the Secret of AdaLN-Zero in Diffusion Transformer

author.name: Jie Zhu, Mingyu Ding, Boqiang Duan, Leye Wang, Jingdong Wang

entry.summary: This study dissects why the adaLN-Zero conditioning block outperforms plain adaLN in diffusion transformers, isolating squeeze-excitation-like structure, zero-initialization and gradual update ordering, and finds zero-initialization dominant. Guided by that analysis, the authors propose an alternative Gaussian initialization strategy for the conditioning layers.

entry.title: Sekai2: From World Exploration to Interactive World Modeling

author.name: Kang He, Wenshuo Peng, Zihui Gao, Jiaming Tan, Kaipeng Zhang, Yongtao Ge

entry.summary: Sekai2 is a large real-world video dataset of roughly 2,826 hours across 128,892 clips from 113 countries, paired with camera trajectories and time-aligned semantics to support long-horizon, camera-controllable interactive world models. It targets the gap between diverse web video without pose and pose-annotated but short reconstruction datasets.

entry.title: 5 useful things you'll learn in my new post-training textbook (shipping now!)

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert announces the publication of his textbook on RLHF and post-training, which grew out of an open web resource documenting methods like rejection sampling, outcome reward models, and character training that lacked accessible written explanations. The book emphasizes intuitions and historical context for techniques that have remained fairly stable across recent years.

entry.title: When the Judge Should Not Decide: Evidence-Locked, Non-Compensatory Selection Bounds LLM-Judge Failure in Reasoning Pipelines

author.name: Yiyao Zhang, Diksha Goel, Hussain Ahmad, Shixun Huang, Jun Shen

entry.summary: Shows that an unconstrained scalar LLM judge inside a reasoning pipeline adds almost nothing over simple majority vote and can be substantially worse on a held-out confirmation split. Placing the same judge inside an evidence-locked, non-compensatory derive-gate-repair rule bounds its failure and recovers value, arguing the decision rule matters more than judge accuracy.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Neuro-Symbolic Skills for Tool-Augmented Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Shi-Yu Tian, Zhuo-Xia Wang, Xuan-Yi Zhu, Zhi Zhou, Xinwei Yang, Kun-Yang Yu, Ming Yang, Yang Chen, Yu-Feng Li

entry.summary: Proposes a neuro-symbolic framework in which a vision-language agent abstracts tool interactions into reusable symbolic skills and adaptively composes them for new fine-grained spatial tasks, rather than planning tool calls from scratch or following fixed pipelines. The skill library evolves through experience.

entry.title: Improving Constraint Models with LLM Agents

author.name: Florentina Voboril, Stefan Szeider

entry.summary: Introduces an agentic framework where an LLM proposes open-ended reformulations of constraint programming models, such as symmetry breaking or alternative variable representations, and each candidate is empirically validated by injecting known solutions back into the model. This escapes the fixed rule libraries of prior automated reformulation systems.

entry.title: CosmosAlign: Adapting a World Foundation Model for Generative Traffic Video Forecasting

author.name: Quang Minh Dinh, Tuan Kiet Doan

entry.summary: CosmosAlign adapts a pretrained world foundation model for long-horizon traffic video forecasting using a two-stage LoRA strategy that first aligns conditioning-mode distribution and then aligns caption style with the model's expectations. Argues distribution alignment, not added capacity, drives successful downstream adaptation of world models.

entry.title: SpikeWorld: Fast-State Adaptation for Frozen Spiking World Models

author.name: Ziqiao Yu

entry.summary: SpikeWorld is a 1.45M-parameter sparse spiking world model jointly trained for sensory prediction, semantics, image-text binding, and action-conditioned dynamics, which stays fully frozen at deployment while adapting through two external residual paths driven by delayed next-state errors. Aims for post-deployment adaptation without optimizer state or weight updates.

entry.title: NeuPAT: Neuron-aware Plasticity Allocation Tuning for Language-Preserving MLLMs

author.name: Jiayue Jin, Jingwei Zhang, Chen Wang, Jing Liu, Longteng Guo

entry.summary: Observes that neurons in a pretrained LLM have heterogeneous plasticity during multimodal instruction tuning, with some critical for retaining language ability, and proposes a probing stage that allocates per-neuron update constraints accordingly. Aims to add vision without eroding text intelligence.

entry.title: Compositional Threat Analysis of Latent Compromise in LLM Agent Systems: The Order 66 Scenario

author.name: Satoshi Matsuoka

entry.summary: Uses a fictional mass-betrayal scenario as an analogy to formalize latent compromise in tool-using LLM agent systems, where a dormant rule planted in shared memory or artifacts is later triggered by an ordinary message and executed by an agent holding recovery authority. Argues the risk is compositional: no single component is catastrophic, but their conjunction produces correlated destructive action.

entry.title: LegoLM: Structured Weight Sharing for Large Language Models

author.name: Joseph Bingham

entry.summary: Diagnoses why global weight sharing destroys LLM quality, identifying distributional mismatch across layers with heterogeneous weight scales and outlier weights beyond the outermost quantization threshold, then proposes a structured sharing scheme that fixes both. Frames compression through the lens of these two named failure modes.

entry.title: Deployable Per-Instance Multi-Layer Activation Steering for Large Language Models

author.name: Muhammad Faishal Adly Nelwan, Alfan Farizki Wicaksono

entry.summary: Shows that the best layers for activation steering vary per input rather than per task, with an oracle over layer subsets beating any fixed global choice on six persona traits across two 8B open-weight models, then develops a greedy marginal-effect rule and a deployable variant that does not need gold answers. Makes multi-layer steering practical at inference time.

entry.title: From Values to Benchmarks: Evaluating Large Language Models for Governmental Use in Dutch

author.name: Laurens Samson, Iva Gornishka, Gossa L\^o, Yuki M. Asano, Sennay Ghebreab

entry.summary: Builds an evaluation suite for Dutch government use of language models, derived through advisory boards and surveys of civil servants using an internal chatbot, covering factuality, honesty, social bias, energy use, cost, and training-data transparency. It operationalizes these values into more than thirty multilingual and Dutch-specific tests.

entry.title: A Hybrid Nested Harness for Decoupling Structure and Parameters in LLM-Driven Optimization

author.name: V\'ictor Gallego

entry.summary: Separates structure search from parameter tuning in language-model-driven optimization: an outer loop has the model propose a program sketch with numeric gaps, while a pluggable inner optimizer such as CMA-ES or gradient methods fills the numbers. The motivation is that models are good at control flow but waste tokens doing discrete trial-and-error on continuous values.

entry.title: "Many Are My Names": The Anatomy of the Assistant and Its Personas via Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Adelaide Danilov, Aria Nourbakhsh, Oleksandr Marchenko Breneur, Salima Lamsiyah

entry.summary: Uses sparse autoencoder features at turn boundaries and pronoun positions to study how a language model internally represents who is speaking across assistant, roleplay-persona, and narrated-character settings. The central finding is that personas do not replace the assistant identity but layer on top of a retained core of assistant-associated features.

entry.title: Evo-Bench: Can Language Models Improve Agent Harness?

author.name: Lisheng Huang, Chen Yang, Hao Zhou, Huatong Song, Zongchao Chen, Ran Le, Yang Song, Wayne Xin Zhao, Tao Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for harness evolution, the ability of a model to autonomously improve the scaffolding it operates within, spanning search, office, and general agent domains. The design deliberately separates harness-improvement skill from raw base-model strength and discourages task-specific overfitting while capturing long-horizon iterative work.

entry.title: Beyond Direct Identifiers: Probabilistic Privacy Risk Estimation for Privacy-Conscious LLM Query Delegation

author.name: Li Siyan, Zhou Yu, Julia Hirschberg

entry.summary: This work extends privacy-conscious delegation, where a local model shields a remote LLM from sensitive text, beyond explicit identifiers to quasi-identifying self-disclosures. It introduces a dataset of naturalistic queries with self-disclosure and an LLM-driven probabilistic k-anonymity estimate to guide what gets sent remotely.

entry.title: VOICE: A Vision-Omics Foundation Model Integrating Direct and Retrieval-Based Prediction of In-situ Single-Cell Gene Expression

author.name: Xin Luo, Yicheng Tao, Haoxuan Zeng, Suyuan Wang, Chenzi Ouyang, Meiqi Zhu, Kai Liu, Shuibing Chen, Jie Liu

entry.summary: VOICE is a multimodal foundation model that predicts single-cell gene expression from routine H and E histology by aligning cell-centered morphology embeddings from a pathology foundation model with expression embeddings from a transcriptome model, trained on paired spatial transcriptomics data. It supports both direct prediction and retrieval-based inference to extend molecular analysis to large tissue archives.

entry.title: REIN: Bridging the Gap between Reasoning and Reliability via Reflection and Abstention Alignment

author.name: Zhengze Huang, Luyang Yu, Di Hong, Xinzhe Huang, Wanyu Lin, Zhixuan Chu, Zhan Qin, Tianhang Zheng

entry.summary: Separates hallucination in large reasoning models into reasoning hallucination from flawed inference steps and knowledge hallucination from missing facts, then trains models to emit a structured sequence with explicit self-reflection before committing to an answer. A reward mechanism encourages abstention or acknowledgment when the required knowledge is absent.

entry.title: Mitigating Over-Personalization in LLMs via Structured Memory

author.name: Hakeem Hannoon, Andrew Zhao, Mihir Narayan, Sharvin Goyal, Ivaxi Sheth

entry.summary: This paper isolates two failure modes of persistent memory in assistants: leakage of stored personal details into unrelated domains, and memory-induced sycophancy where stored beliefs make the model agree instead of being truthful. A simple inference-time change to how memories are presented reduces both across seven models on a persistence benchmark, without touching the model or the memory store. Cheap and directly actionable for products shipping long-term memory.

entry.title: LLMVisor: A Real-Time Latency Attribution Model for Multi-Tenant LLM Serving

author.name: Shuowei Jin, Xueshen Liu, Jiaxin Shan, Le Xu, Tieying Zhang, Liguang Xie, Z. Morley Mao

entry.summary: LLMVisor is a roofline-inspired model that attributes batch inference latency to individual requests in multi-tenant serving, using a piecewise-linear form over FLOP and memory-traffic proxies that runs at microsecond cost inside the scheduler. It is validated on Llama and Qwen models across A100 and H100 with varying tensor parallelism. This enables fair per-tenant accounting and fractional sharing of inference engines.

entry.title: Yesterday's Shield, Today's Spear: A Self-Evolving Safety Guardrail in Production

author.name: Cong Ming, Jingyi Chen, Bin Liu, Qi Chu, Tao Gong, Nenghai Yu, Yingfei Xiang

entry.summary: SESG is a production multi-agent system that keeps a deployed safety guardrail continuously updated by monitoring live traffic for novel jailbreak forms and previously unhandled harm categories, then synthesizing targeted training data and rebalancing batches toward the model's own error direction. It treats guardrails as continuously retrained rather than frozen at release. Reported as running in production, which is unusual for guardrail papers.

entry.title: Unaccountable Delegation, Fading Skills: Mapping the Risks of Workplace AI Agents

author.name: Gabriele La Malfa, Lakmal Meegahapola, Edyta Bogucka, Jie M. Zhang, Michael Luck, Elizabeth Black, Daniele Quercia

entry.summary: The authors build a job-specific risk taxonomy for workplace AI agents by modeling agents, goals and environments, then apply it to 2,078 occupational tasks to generate 8,356 severity-labeled risk scenarios validated with 45 workers across ten roles. Highlighted risks include unaccountable delegation and skill erosion. It offers organizations a concrete, occupation-grounded alternative to broad AI risk lists.

entry.title: Business Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents in a Realistic Marketplace

author.name: Yijun Pan, Yukun Lian, Kunyu Shi, Junbo Li, Hongwei Xue, Sicong Xie, Guannan Zhang, Xiaoying Xing

entry.summary: Business Arena places an LLM agent in charge of a cross-border shop over a long horizon, sourcing from suppliers and selling to buyers with delayed, coupled consequences and regulatory prerequisites, grounded in real marketplace sourcing data. It tests capabilities rarely covered by agent benchmarks, such as capital commitment under uncertainty and adaptation to shifting markets. Economically realistic long-horizon evaluation is an important frontier.

entry.title: RAVEN-Eval: Rubric-Guided Automatic Evaluation for AI Video Generation Models Based on LMM Preference Judgement

author.name: Ziheng Jia, Jiaying Qian, Zicheng Zhang, Xiaorong Zhu, Lancheng Gao, Xiongkuo Min

entry.summary: RAVEN-Eval is a rubric-guided automatic evaluation framework that uses large multimodal models as preference judges to distinguish fine-grained quality differences among top video generation systems, where fidelity and prompt-following scores have saturated. Motivated by the rising cost and expertise demands of human video annotation.

entry.title: Signature-Guided Capacity Occupancy for Dense Expert Merging

author.name: Lingching Tung, Chi-Jui Kim, Beicheng Xu, Yuchen Wang, Bin Cui

entry.summary: SigMerge is a model merging method that decides, per layer, how much capacity to open based on cross-expert conflict signatures and which domain should occupy that capacity based on measured deficits from a dense base merge, avoiding expensive recipe search. Targets combining several domain-specialized checkpoints into one dense model.

entry.title: CADEngBench: It Looks Like CAD, but Does It Work? Evaluating Parametric Design, Assembly Reasoning, and Physics Simulation

author.name: Harmanjot Singh, Abhra Dubey, Jorge Alejandro Amador Herrera

entry.summary: CADEngBench evaluates whether generated CAD models are engineering-grade rather than merely visually plausible, checking boundary-representation validity, manufacturability, response to parameter perturbations, controlled functional edits, matched finite element analysis results, and valid joint assembly across 600 part tasks and 150 body pairs. Grounds evaluation in a real solver pipeline.

entry.title: From Sweep to Seam: Interleaved Cross-Block Post-Training Quantization

author.name: Achille Jacquemond, Yuma Ichikawa, Akira Sakai

entry.summary: ICBQ modifies block-wise post-training quantization scheduling so that the boundary pair between consecutive two-block chunks is refined twice, once at the end of one chunk and again at the start of the next, instead of sweeping the window once and never revisiting early errors. Reuses existing calibration inputs and objectives.

entry.title: Hallucination-Free GUI Grounding via Regression-Free Layout-Aware Matching

author.name: Yuke Li, Xuehan Hou

entry.summary: Proposes a regression-free GUI grounding pipeline where a frozen multimodal model elaborates abstract instructions and a dedicated layout-aware matcher selects the target element, avoiding coordinate hallucinations that arise when end-to-end models regress pixel positions directly. Separates semantic interpretation from precise localization.

entry.title: From Trajectories to Evidence: Auditable Experimental Records for Industrial Research Agents

author.name: Zijie Zhuang, Changxin Lao, Pengbo Xu, Hanwen Xu, Ruochen Yang, Yingzhi He, Peng Zhang, Jiangxia Cao, Yusheng Huang, Guohong Mu, Jian Liang, Ruiming Tang, Shuang Yang, Zhaojie Liu, Wenwu Ou, Kun Gai

entry.summary: Studies trajectory-to-evidence conversion for industrial research agents, arguing that a completed multi-round experiment log is not automatically evidence because artifacts may be unsupported, rounds may be confounded, and later edits can obscure earlier findings. Proposes bounded context-isolated generate-verify-repair checks on consequential artifacts plus post-execution claim qualification for auditability.

entry.title: Learning an Interior Layout Policy in a Domain Specific Language Action Space

author.name: Yuhao Lu, Weichen Zhang, Wenyi Xiao, Haohui Chen, Yiyun Fei

entry.summary: LayoutDSL has an LLM produce interior layouts as programs in a domain-specific language rather than regressing raw coordinates, incorporating structural elements such as doors and windows. The symbolic action space is argued to let the model learn design reasoning rather than continuous geometry fitting.

entry.title: Multi-Task Consistency-based Detection of Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Cong Chen, Jean-Philippe Monteuuis, Jonathan Petit

entry.summary: Detects adversarial perturbations in autonomous driving perception by checking consistency between outputs of multiple vision tasks such as object detection and instance segmentation, rather than deploying costly dedicated defenses. Emphasizes efficiency for resource-constrained onboard systems.

entry.title: Targeted Counterfactual Fingerprinting for Black-Box LLM Ownership Verification

author.name: Yutong Wu, Xiaofan Bai, Shixin Li, Pingyi Hu, Ziqi Zhou, Zilong Wang, Xiaojing Ma, Songfeng Lu, Yuhong Li, Jin Xuan, Yi Wang, Dongmei Zhang, Bin Benjamin Zhu

entry.summary: Presents a black-box fingerprinting method for LLM ownership verification that converts open-ended generation comparison into constrained counterfactual answer checks, so it survives fine-tuning, quantization and API-only final-response interfaces. Addresses fragility of existing fingerprints under realistic deployment conditions.

entry.title: Governing the KV Cache: Preventing Timing Side-Channel Leakage in Multi-Tenant LLM Inference

author.name: Tejasvi C. Addagada

entry.summary: Shows that prefix KV-cache sharing in multi-tenant LLM serving creates a timing side channel that published attacks exploit to reconstruct other tenants' prompts, and proposes KVGov, a per-principal salted cache-keying governance layer covering all three attack families. Frames cache isolation as a policy-enforced serving-layer control.

entry.title: Imaginative Generative AI: Crossing the Entropy Wall into Worlds Beyond Imitation

author.name: Hossein Goli, Farzan Farnia, Amin Gohari

entry.summary: Proposes Imaginative Generative AI, which treats diversity as an explicit design target rather than a byproduct of imitation, selecting among distributions near a reference the one whose spectral diversity hits a prescribed level. Diversity is quantified by the von Neumann entropy of the kernel covariance operator in a fixed embedding space.

entry.title: Dual-Adversarial Safety Alignment: Cultivating Intrinsic Threat Comprehension in LRMs

author.name: Hongli Shen, Shaopeng Fu, Qinbo Zhang, Jian Li, Di Wang

entry.summary: AdvSafe aligns large reasoning models by having them explicitly deconstruct the mechanisms behind adversarial prompts, rather than memorizing refusal patterns for specific jailbreak templates. The dual-adversarial pipeline aims for generalizable robustness without eroding reasoning utility.

entry.title: CODS: Iterative Bellman-Residual Data Selection for Reusable Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Sanjeda Akter, Abu Sa-Adat Mohamed Moon-Im Al Ahsan, Md Najmus Swaqeeb, Anuj Sharma

entry.summary: CODS selects a reusable subset of offline RL transitions by alternating between fitting a critic matched to the target algorithm and acquiring transitions with high Bellman residual, then freezing the subset. At a ten percent data budget it retains about 97 percent of full-pool performance across twenty benchmark task-algorithm combinations.

entry.title: From token probabilities to calibrated confidence: An empirical study of mathematical question answering

author.name: Avery Ma, Lorne Schell, Vin Bhaskara, Leila Pishdad

entry.summary: Empirically compares single-pass confidence estimates reused from generation token probabilities against multi-pass estimates from verification or stochastic forward passes on mathematical question answering. Although individual token probabilities are saturated and overconfident, suitable aggregation over the generated sequence yields usable calibration.

entry.title: CLAM: Causal Spatial Disaggregation to Infer Local Effects From Coarse Data

author.name: Gerrit Gro{\ss}mann, Sumantrak Mukherjee, Sebastian J. Vollmer

entry.summary: CLAM estimates fine-grained local causal effects from coarsely aggregated interventions and outcomes by jointly learning the causal mechanism and a disaggregation mapping, using high-resolution covariates that modulate the effect. It supports localized effect estimation, counterfactual queries, and principled outcome disaggregation.

entry.title: Causal State-Space Model for Causal Inference: Estimating Longitudinal Individual Treatment Effects

author.name: Abisoye Abidakun, Mingjun Zhong, Georgios Leontidis

entry.summary: Argues that adversarial domain-confusion training for longitudinal treatment-effect estimation is self-defeating, since making representations invariant to treatment assignment also suppresses treatment-correlated covariates needed for accurate prediction. The authors formalize this with a divergence bound and propose selective state-space models with a parallel multi-step decoder that avoids accumulated rollout error.

entry.title: SwiftQK: Fast and Communication-Efficient Tensor Parallelism for Query-Key Normalization

author.name: Gyudong Kim, Wonjun Han, Young Geun Kim

entry.summary: SwiftQK is a multi-GPU RMSNorm kernel for query-key normalization under tensor parallelism that exchanges only scalar normalization statistics instead of full hidden vectors, overlapping the remaining peer-to-peer reduction with element-wise work in a deadlock-safe persistent kernel. Reported latency reductions for the normalization step exceed eighty percent, with roughly thirty percent lower time per output token in serving.

entry.title: Beyond the Capability Boundary: Zeroth-Order Optimization for Self-Evolving LLM Agents

author.name: Bingzhen Liu, Xiaomeng Fan, Yuwei Wu, Zhi Gao, Mingyang Gao, Chuanhao Li, Yunde Jia

entry.summary: Argues that trajectory-sampling self-improvement cannot push LLM agents past their capability boundary because correct trajectories are never sampled on hard problems. Instead it perturbs LoRA parameters, compares losses under perturbed and original weights, and uses the difference as a zeroth-order gradient estimate requiring no trajectory annotations.

entry.title: Regret, equilibrium, and learning in games: A guided tour

author.name: Panayotis Mertikopoulos

entry.summary: A tutorial-style survey of learning in games that moves from single-agent regret minimization in nonstationary or adversarial environments to the dynamics and equilibria that emerge when many regularized learners interact. Written by a leading researcher in the area as an accessible entry point to the literature.

entry.title: Vid2WAM: Distilling Video Diffusion Priors into World Action Models

author.name: Chenhao Qiu, Ruixiang Wang, Runyi Zhao, Sixu Lin, Songen Gu, Shufeng Nan, Guiliang Liu, Kui Jia, Yanwei Fu, Simo Wu

entry.summary: Vid2WAM distills a large video foundation model into a compact world action model student, supervising future prediction with task-conditioned rollouts and recovering actions through an inverse dynamics channel. This challenges the assumption that world action model supervision must come from costly target-task expert demonstrations.

entry.title: GraphThink: Graph-Enhanced LLM Thinking for Long-Horizon Embodied Task Planning

author.name: Chen Li, Sijie Cheng, Yuelin Zhang, Junxi Li, Maozhi Huang, Yang Liu, Wenbing Huang

entry.summary: Combines a task graph supplying structured procedural knowledge with a scene graph maintaining environmental memory to reduce physical hallucination in LLM-based embodied planners. The task graph also supplies fine-grained reward shaping for GRPO training, and an event-driven module triggers replanning when the environment changes.

entry.title: Neurosymbolic Discovery of Algebraic Graph Constructions

author.name: David Seka, Stefan Szeider

entry.summary: Asks whether an LLM agent can recover a short algebraic description, such as a Cayley graph or lexicographic product, from raw adjacency data produced by SAT solvers or graph generators. The neurosymbolic agent interleaves reasoning with symbolic checking and requires no fine-tuning or per-target training.

entry.title: TokenPrint: A Calibrated Token-Space Fingerprint for Language-Model Provenance

author.name: Yuqi Wu, Shengming Zhao, Jie Chen

entry.summary: Presents a training-free fingerprint for language model provenance built from top-k vocabulary projections of late hidden states across a fixed set of knowledge probes, compared by token-string overlap. Across 32 open-weight models from nine families, similarity scores form a ladder that broadly tracks documented relationships such as shared base checkpoints and same-developer lineage.

entry.title: Latent-Frequency Validity: Fast Spectral Editing with Screened Video-VAE Transfer Operators

author.name: Bowen Xue, Jiafeng Xiong, Xin Quan

entry.summary: Introduces latent-frequency validity, which learns a compact per-VAE spectral response so that spectral edits can be applied directly in video VAE latents only when they improve decoded fidelity without harming round-trip stability. Sweeps hundreds of VAE and edit combinations with a validation-selected path from diagonal calibration to full channel mixing.

entry.title: LoRSA: Toward Generalizable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Biomedical Downstream Tasks

author.name: Saed Moradi, Benyamin Ghojogh, M. Hadi Sepanj, Yimin Yang, Ashirbani Saha

entry.summary: LoRSA is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that combines a dense low-rank update capturing globally shared task structure with a dynamically structured-sparse low-rank component providing localized residual corrections. Motivated by the claim that a single low-rank subspace limits generalization to unseen biomedical imaging domains.

entry.title: Can LLM Agents Stick to the Script? A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Consistency in Interactive Narratives

author.name: Yingpeng Ma, Jianhao Yan, Bei Shi, Ka Hou Kam, Runnan Wang, Xuebo Liu, Yulong Chen, Yue Zhang, Derek F. Wong

entry.summary: Formulates narrative commitment preservation and releases a benchmark of one hundred interactive story environments derived from film synopses, each with checkable trajectory commitments and initial facts, to test whether LLM game masters keep long-horizon logical consistency under adversarial player interventions. Fills a gap in evaluating AI-driven interactive storytelling.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Data Drift Detection and Recovery for Large-Scale LLM Applications via Proxy Representations

author.name: Michael Levit, Josh Ledgard, Haoyu Dong, Vishwas Suryanarayanan, Eyal Kolman, Sharon Tan, Qiang Gan, Vishal Chowdhary

entry.summary: Describes a production framework that detects and repairs drift between live LLM traffic and offline evaluation sets without inspecting raw user data, working instead on non-PII structured descriptors derived from LLM classification of interactions. Introduces a chance-calibrated redundancy-aware alignment score and a refresh procedure for evaluation sets.

entry.title: On the Robustness of LLMs' Internal Representation of Code Correctness

author.name: Francisco Ribeiro, Sohaila Abdulsattar, Renata Gonzalez, Mahmoud Kassem, Sarah Nadi

entry.summary: Tests whether the previously reported internal hidden-state signal of code correctness is a robust property of models or an artifact of particular probing choices, varying extraction settings and models. Relevant because such signals promise test-free judgement of generated code that beats stated model confidence.

entry.title: CuteTTS: Efficient and High-Quality Speech Synthesis via Autoregressive Modeling of Continuous Latents

author.name: Yuqian Zhang, Yao Shi, Kexin Huang, Botian Jiang, Zhe Xu, Yiwei Zhao, Min Liang, Shuang Chen, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: Presents a compact zero-shot text-to-speech system that autoregresses over continuous semantically aligned causal VAE latents at the patch level with explicit speaker conditioning and a bidirectional flow-matching decoder, avoiding costly iterative diffusion at every step. Targets streaming assistants where latency and speaker fidelity both matter.

entry.title: PAST: Privileged Adaptation from Complete Student Trajectories for On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Yangyang Feng, Zhuoyan Feng, Junlan Chen

entry.summary: Extends on-policy self-distillation by giving the teacher access to the student full rollout and its outcome as privileged hindsight, preserving the student distribution on successful trajectories while steering the teacher toward verified success on failures under a proximity constraint. Aims to make distillation supervision better matched to the student.

entry.title: Accurate Ensembles, Fragile Narratives: Multi-Scale Stacking and a Fidelity Audit of LLM-Generated Explanations for Credit Risk

author.name: Gregorius Reynaldi Pratama, Kuo-Kun Tseng

entry.summary: Builds a strong stacked credit-default ensemble reaching high discrimination on a public lending dataset, then audits whether language-model-written rationales built from feature attributions faithfully reflect the model. The finding is that the predictive half works while the narrative half is fragile, which matters given regulatory demands for explainable adverse decisions.

entry.title: Archer: Adaptive Reuse of Cached Hidden States for Efficient Rollback in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Xuning He, Zinan Sheng, Yongding Tao, Huanyu Liu, Ge Li, Xue Jiang, Yihong Dong

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free key-value caching scheme for diffusion language models that reconciles caching with the rollback ability of iterative denoising by asymmetrically retaining prompt states while allowing revisable response states to be recomputed. Targets the major inference cost problem that every denoising update otherwise invalidates the whole cache.

entry.title: The Evolution of Mixture-of-Experts Architectures in Large Language Models: Routing, Topology, Load Balancing, and Expert Parallelism

author.name: Jiguo Li

entry.summary: A technical survey that organizes modern mixture-of-experts language model systems along five coupled axes including expert granularity, topology, routing freedom, load-balancing scope, and execution structure, rather than as a chronological model list. Frames eight architectural milestones as a dependency graph and analyzes systems through four control planes.

entry.title: An Agentic Generative Large Language Model for Treatment Planning of Colorectal Cancer

author.name: Mengxian Lyu, Cheng Peng, Tim Jang, Ang Li, Mengyuan Zhang, Ziyi Chen, Leighton Elliott, Tianshi Liu, Lidice Galindo, Chiranjeevi Sainatham, Oscar F. Borja-Montes, Kaleb E. Smith, Ying Zhang, Lichao Sun, Jiang Bian, Gloria Lipori, Duane A. Mitchell, Elizabeth A. Shenkman, Yi Guo, Thomas J. George, Yonghui Wu

entry.summary: Develops an agentic LLM for colorectal cancer treatment planning, domain-adapted using 282 billion tokens of biomedical and health-system clinical text including 166 billion tokens from a single academic medical center, combining continued pretraining with model merging. Targets guideline-concordant plan generation, which demands synthesizing heterogeneous patient data with rapidly changing clinical guidelines.

entry.title: Decoding-Level Taboo: A Diagnostic Stress Test for LLM Robustness

author.name: Tadanobu Chuyo Kamijo, Ori Rottenstreich, Javier Conde, Gonzalo Mart\'inez, Pedro Reviriego

entry.summary: Decoding-Level Taboo is a runtime stress test that masks top candidate tokens at word boundaries, forcing models to paraphrase around their preferred generation path without changing the prompt. It measures how far benchmark performance degrades once models are pushed off their optimized decoding corridor.

entry.title: FlowErase-OPD: Multi-Concept Erasure via Anchored On-Policy Distillation in Flow Matching Models

author.name: Yi Sun, Yimin Zhou, Xinhao Zhong, Zhiqi Zhang, Junhao Li, Bin Chen

entry.summary: FlowErase-OPD erases multiple unsafe concepts from flow-matching text-to-image models by distilling several single-concept erased models into one LoRA using on-policy distillation, with a retention teacher to preserve unrelated generation quality. It targets the underexplored multi-concept erasure setting.

entry.title: Vision Meets WiFi: Physics-Grounded Estimation of Volumetric Mechanical Properties

author.name: Ali Bahri, Hongliang Li, Soufiane Lamghari, Jie Chuai, Zhitang Chen

entry.summary: ViWi estimates per-voxel Young's modulus, Poisson ratio, and density by combining vision with WiFi sensing, using object-centric material slots so voxels of the same material share consistent estimates. The WiFi signal helps disambiguate objects that look alike but differ physically.

entry.title: Circuit Fine-Tuning for Compute-Efficient Transformer Adaptation

author.name: Uri Z. Kialy, Gil Ben-Artzi

entry.summary: Circuit Fine-Tuning repurposes mechanistic circuit discovery, normally used to explain trained models, to choose which modules to fine-tune before training begins, using attribution against a near-zero-initialized probe head. The goal is compute efficiency rather than parameter count, since parameter-sparse adapters still pay full-model training cost per step.

entry.title: 4D-WAM: Infusing Spatiotemporal Awareness into World Action Models through Trajectory Fields

author.name: Lishan Yang, Wenxuan Song, Xi Wang, Pingyue Sheng, Zheng Fang, Ziyang Zhou, Junjie He, Haodong Yan, Jiayi Chen, Nan Sun, Qiao Sun, Lingqiao Liu, Yan Wang, Yuxiang Gao, Feras Dayoub, Haoang Li

entry.summary: 4D-WAM is a model-agnostic training strategy that injects 3D trajectory field information into world action models via representation alignment, using motion alignment across adjacent frames plus a complementary spatiotemporal objective. It closes the gap between 2D pixel-space video prediction and the 3D space in which robot actions actually occur.

entry.title: JEPA-WAM: Learning Vision-Language-Action Policies with Joint-Embedding World Modeling

author.name: Yihan Lin, Jiawei He, Shifeng Bao, Chen Zhao, Yang Li, Xiaobo Wang, Yan Wang, Cheng Chi, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: JEPA-WAM builds a world action model inside a pretrained V-JEPA latent space, coupling latent transition prediction with continuous action generation through a shared predictor and predicting a spatially structured joint current-future target that preserves patch-level correspondence. It avoids the deployment cost of pixel-space video generation while keeping predictive representations aligned with those used for control.

entry.title: MetaSpace: Metamorphic Testing for Spatial Cognition in Embodied Agents

author.name: Gengyang Xu, Dongwei Xiao, Yiteng Peng, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: Applies metamorphic testing to embodied agents, generating semantics-preserving transformations of scenes and queries to probe spatial cognition without relying on hand-annotated VQA pairs or coarse task-success metrics. The aim is to expose latent spatial reasoning failures that success rates hide.

entry.title: SurgLAT: Surgical Latent Attention Tracking for Depth-Aware Robotic Laparoscope Control

author.name: Rulin Zhou, Qiujie Song, Yujie Ma, An Wang, Wanhao Liu, Guoheng Ma, Yidu Wang, Guankun Wang, Xingrong Diao, Jiankun Wang, Chaowei Zhu, Xianming Liu, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: Proposes an online framework for autonomous laparoscope control that models the surgeon's operative intent as a latent, temporally evolving attention state rather than a fixed physical target. It combines a frozen DINOv3 encoder, a state-conditioned spatial token mixer, and a selective causal latent memory that fuses short-term motion with long-horizon intent.

entry.title: TongGuOCR: A Layout-Aware and Token-Augmented OCR Framework for Chinese Historical Documents

author.name: Zhongheng Zhou, Yi Sun, Huiguo He, Yuyi Zhang, Peirong Zhang, Yulin Fang, Dezhi Peng, Minghui Liao, Lianwen Jin

entry.summary: Presents an OCR framework for Chinese historical documents combining layout-aware preprocessing that builds locally coherent recognition blocks with token-augmented recognition to handle rare characters and nontrivial reading orders. The goal is to unlock scanned heritage collections for full-text search and computational analysis.

entry.title: SCOUT: Self-Checking and Recovery-Aware Tool-Thought Agents for Ultra-Long Egocentric Video Reasoning

author.name: Keyang Zhong, Kuo Wang, Peng Liu, Quanlong Zheng, Junlin Xie, Zhijia Liang, Yanhao Zhang, Guanbin Li

entry.summary: Introduces a recovery-aware agentic framework for reasoning over hours-long egocentric video that evaluates intermediate tool observations and adaptively trades off zooming into a region versus switching regions. This addresses error propagation caused by rigid zoom-in strategies in chain-of-tool-thought video agents.

entry.title: Your Prompt Is Not the Only Prompt: How Much Do LLMs Weight Structured-Output Schema Descriptions?

author.name: Sin-Ying Lin

entry.summary: This study asks whether label definitions for classification should live in the system prompt, user prompt, or JSON schema descriptions when using structured output. Across ten configurations from two vendors, schema placement was not consistently better and sometimes lagged system prompts by over ten points, yet incorrect schema instructions still hijacked behavior when they conflicted with prompts. Practical guidance for anyone using schema-constrained extraction pipelines.

entry.title: LLM within MCP Matters: Measuring Inefficient Resource Utilization Driven by LLMs

author.name: Minhan Cho, Soyoung Park, Kihyeon Jeong, Byeongkyu Jeon, Daejin Choi, Jinyoung Han

entry.summary: A 54,000-trial measurement across 24 models from three vendors on a production legal-information MCP server tests whether clients actually use reference data embedded in server instructions instead of redundantly calling search tools. A diagnostic condition removing the competing tool shows failures stem from model choices rather than missing information, wasting tokens and latency. Practical guidance for MCP server design and client behavior.

entry.title: Time Present and Time Past: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Temporally Evolving Document Understanding

author.name: Mahbub E Sobhani, Md. Faiyaz Abdullah Sayeedi, Fahmid Hasan Chowdhury, Md Adnan Arefeen, Farig Sadeque, Md. Faizul Bari, Swakkhar Shatabda

entry.summary: TIDE is an expert-verified benchmark of over 3,000 questions on 644 official customs instruments where the correct answer depends on which version of a regulation was in force at the queried date. Unlike prior temporal QA sets that treat time as an annotation, it directly tests version resolution across amendments, replacements and reversions. This targets a failure mode that matters for legal, tax and documentation assistants.

entry.title: SDDBMs: Soft Denoising Diffusion Bridge Models

author.name: Shiyi Qi, Kun He, Mingmou Liu

entry.summary: Soft Denoising Diffusion Bridge Models relax the hard endpoint conditioning used in diffusion bridges, which forces the terminal distribution to a point mass and makes drift coefficients ill-conditioned near the boundary. By regularizing the terminal constraint the authors obtain better-behaved transports for image-to-image translation and restoration. A clean theoretical fix to a known numerical pathology.

entry.title: The Scaffolding Matters More Than the Interface: A Controlled Comparison of MCP and CLI Tool Use Across Seven Agent Scaffoldings, Five Language Models, and One Software Task

author.name: Marc Alier Forment, Mar\'ia Jos\'e Casa\~n Guerrero, Francisco Jos\'e Garc\'ia-Pe\~nalvo, Juanan Pereira

entry.summary: A controlled comparison of tool access via the Model Context Protocol versus an ordinary command line, run across seven agent scaffoldings and five models on one fixed multi-step git task, with completion verified by inspecting repository state rather than trusting agent self-reports. The dominant cost driver was the scaffolding, not the tool interface, contradicting practitioner claims that differ by an order of magnitude. A refreshingly rigorous answer to a contested engineering question.

entry.title: ComboShoppingBench: Evaluating LLM Agents for Budget-Constrained Basket Shopping with Coupons

author.name: Adrian Li, Kelong Mao, Yudong Guo, Heming Xia, Xinwei Yang, Lirui Luo, Jace Wong, Pu Yao, Sulong Xu, Simiu Gu

entry.summary: ComboShoppingBench evaluates agents on constructing budget-constrained baskets of complementary items in a simulated commerce and takeout environment, checking coupon validity, store requirements, delivery fees, and payment correctness rather than exact product matches. Designed so open-ended solutions remain verifiable.

entry.title: verdi: retrieval is not transfer for continual world model optimization

author.name: Junyu Wu, Shiqin Nie, Youyi Kou, Baohua Yin, Guocai Yao, Qingyu Chen, Jingheng Ma, Shiji Zhou, Hongyong Song, Mingchen Zhuge, Sen Cui, Changshui Zhang

entry.summary: Argues that retrieved optimization strategies for tuning pretrained world models are only hypotheses, not transferable knowledge, until validated on the target model, and builds verdi, a continual research agent that gates reuse behind target-side experimental validation. Aims to stop optimization know-how from being rediscovered per campaign.

entry.title: NeuroPilot: An Agent-Driven Smart Pipeline for Processing, Quality Control, and Managing Neuroimages

author.name: Yiyao Chen, Yucheng Li, Jungong Tong, Shaoqi Wang, Kunhao Zhou, Ziquan Wei, Monica Murea, Marissa DiPiero, Tingting Dan, Guorong Wu

entry.summary: NeuroPilot is a multi-agent system that packages neuroimaging standardization, preprocessing, and quality control into LLM-invokable skills, with an agent orchestrating workflows across heterogeneous infrastructure. Aims to replace brittle project-specific scripts and manual QC.

entry.title: Geometry Beats Estimated Depth: RGB-Only Multi-Camera 3D Tracking under Sim2Real

author.name: Abdullah Naeem, Anav Katwal, Ayon Dey, Noman Khan, Md Tamjidul Hoque

entry.summary: A controlled AI City Challenge study comparing a geometry-first RGB-only multi-camera 3D tracking pipeline against monocular-depth pseudo-LiDAR under synthetic-to-real transfer. Concludes that cross-view geometric consistency, not monocular depth accuracy, governs Sim2Real performance.

entry.title: LGNNIC: Acceleration of Large-Scale GNN Training using SmartNICs

author.name: Liad Gerstman, Aditya Dhakal, Dejan Milojicic, Avi Mendelson

entry.summary: LGNNIC offloads preprocessing and communication-heavy steps of distributed graph neural network training onto SmartNICs co-located with remote memory nodes to relieve inter-node network congestion. Targets graphs too large for a single CPU-GPU node.

entry.title: From Product Search to Preference Articulation: The Economics of Agentic Commerce

author.name: Lingxiu Dong, Kaiwen Luo, Fasheng Xu
