entry.summary: BioM-JEPA adapts joint-embedding predictive architectures to single-cell transcriptomics by predicting aggregate representations of gene blocks defined by protein-association and coexpression graphs, rather than reconstructing individual genes. The resulting embeddings show higher effective rank and less dependence on sequencing depth artifacts.

entry.title: SkillTFM: Gated Skill Evolution for Training-Free Adaptation of Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Yi He, Zhengkang Guan, Anpeng Wu, Peng Cui, Fei Wu, Kun Kuang

entry.summary: SkillTFM adapts tabular foundation models to new datasets without any gradient updates by evolving a gated library of reusable skills at inference time. It targets deployment obstacles such as distribution shift, heterogeneous feature semantics, and task-specific structure that normally require fine-tuning or extra labels.

entry.title: KVAE: Family of Tokenizers for Multimodal Generative Models

author.name: Andrey Shutkin, Denis Parkhomenko, Ivan Kirillov, Kirill Chernyshev, Kirill Malakhov, Ilia Vasiliev, Ilia Trushkin, Valeriya Kobenko, David Chikovani, Alexander Ivanov, Azat Saginbaev, Egor Silvestrov, Ivan Mikheev, Konstantin Zakharov

entry.summary: This technical report presents a family of KVAE tokenizers for audio, image, and video designed for text-conditioned latent diffusion generation, including a 48 kHz continuous audio tokenizer, two causal video tokenizers at different compression ratios, and an 8x image tokenizer. The report examines how reconstruction metrics relate to downstream generation quality.

entry.title: A neural operator view on U-Nets for inverse imaging problems

author.name: Alexander Auras, Martin Burger, Samira Kabri, Michael Moeller, Michael Schopf-Kuester

entry.summary: The paper analyzes U-Net architectures for inverse imaging problems through the lens of neural operator learning, asking how these networks behave as discretization resolution increases and the problem becomes truly ill-posed. It compares operator-learning variants on a 1D toy example and extensive numerical experiments.

entry.title: Operating Multi-Node Full Fine-Tuning on NVIDIA B300: A Field Report on Telemetry-Based Triage, Negative Results, and Operational Hardening

author.name: Seon Ho Kim, Ui Jeong Jeon, Su Hyeon Kim, Min Tae Hwang

entry.summary: A field report on full fine-tuning a 32.76B dense model across 16 NVIDIA B300 GPUs with FSDP/ZeRO-3, offering a power-draw triage table that distinguishes compute, communication, data-starvation, and deadlock states by board wattage, since utilization can read 100 percent during an NCCL hang. It also reports honest negative results dispelling common optimization folklore at this scale.

entry.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling

author.name: Ishan Patel, Sahil Sen, Elias Lumer, Vamse Kumar Subbiah

entry.summary: Empirically compares programmatic tool calling, where tools are exposed as typed Python stubs invoked through code, against native JSON tool calling across 14 models on a function-calling benchmark. Finds programmatic calling allows chaining and parallelism within a single agent turn and examines how the advantage varies across model generations.

entry.title: Vorch-Director: Interactive World Story Model via Noise-Aware Error Rectification

author.name: Lisai Zhang, Yidi Wu, Qi Liu, Xin Ma, Yang Ding, Gang Yue, Siqian Yang, Jingyuan Chen, Lin Ma, Yaohui Wang

entry.summary: Vorch-Director addresses error accumulation in autoregressive minute-scale audio-visual generation, where models trained on clean histories drift when conditioned on their own outputs. It finds that residual-based self-correction works only at particular flow-matching noise levels and proposes noise-level-aware residual correction. This targets identity drift, over-smoothing, and audio-video desynchronization in long generations.

entry.title: Ordered Diffusion for 3D Human Registration

author.name: Mattia Masiero, Ilya A. Petrov, Daniel Cremers, Gerard Pons-Moll, Riccardo Marin

entry.summary: ODin recasts 3D human registration from a regression problem with one assumed correct alignment into a diffusion process that samples a distribution of plausible template alignments while preserving consistent point ordering. This avoids the blurred average predictions that regression produces under scan noise, occlusion, and soft-tissue ambiguity. Authors include established 3D vision groups.

entry.title: Universal Concept Disruption for SAM3 Image Segmentation

author.name: Hao Wang, Yuxuan Zhang, Wei Yang

entry.summary: Universal Concept Disruption presents what the authors claim is the first universal adversarial attack against SAM3-style promptable concept segmentation, learning a single bounded image perturbation from image and noun-phrase pairs. It jointly attacks the text-conditioned grounding path, prompt-shared visual features, and the presence gate that decides whether a concept exists. It highlights an unexamined robustness surface in open-vocabulary segmentation foundation models.

entry.title: The Loss Does Not See the Basis, but Adam Does

author.name: Devender Singh

entry.summary: Analyzes why gradient descent on a factored matrix model is implicitly biased toward low-rank solutions while Adam from the same initialization is not, attributing the difference to whether an optimizer respects the gauge symmetry of the factorized loss. It proves a structure theorem characterizing memoryless gauge-equivariant update rules as Gram-determined left preconditioners, placing gradient descent, momentum, Muon, and Shampoo on one side and Adam and RMSProp on the other. This gives a principled reason why matrix-aware optimizers behave differently from coordinate-wise ones.

entry.title: LC-GRPO: Bridging Train-Inference Gap for Flow-Based GRPO with Langevin Correction

author.name: Yingqing Guo, Hui Yuan, Zijian He, Mengdi Wang, Zheng Ding

entry.summary: LC-GRPO addresses a train-inference mismatch in reinforcement learning for flow-based generative models, where training uses noisy stochastic rollouts while deployment uses a deterministic ODE sampler, causing blurry exploration samples. A Langevin correction aligns the stochastic training trajectories with the finite-step deterministic sampler used at test time.

entry.title: Conditional Cognitive Biases in LLMs: How Biased User Turns Modulate In-Context Reasoning

author.name: Sachini Weerasekara, Sagar Kamarthi, Jacqueline Isaacs

entry.summary: The authors benchmark eight frontier LLMs on cognitive bias expression in multi-turn conversations, using 24,300 jury-validated prompts covering a 9x9 matrix of human bias types interacting with target biases, and a design that separates exposure to a biased user turn from its semantic content. Biased conversational context increased bias expression relative to zero-shot baselines in six of eight models.

entry.title: Physics-Based Molecular Fingerprints from Spectral Graph Theory Provide Efficient Geometry-Aware Measures of Chemical Similarity

author.name: Jacob W. Toney, Ayleen Y. Farnood, Samir Darouich, Heather J. Kulik

entry.summary: The authors introduce molecular fingerprints derived from spectral graph theory that incorporate 3D geometry, giving interpretable and computationally cheap similarity measures able to distinguish stereoisomers and conformers that 2D connectivity fingerprints conflate. They are designed to scale to large chemical spaces unlike pairwise 3D alignment methods.

entry.title: Verifiable Regularity Criterion for Conditional Expectation Operators and Conditional Mean Embeddings with Applications to Nonparametric Regression, Bayesian Inverse Problems, and Koopman Operators

author.name: Maximiliano Hertel, Ilja Klebanov, Manuel Schaller, Karl Worthmann

entry.summary: This paper gives a verifiable sufficient condition, based on regularity of the Radon-Nikodym density of the conditional law, for a conditional expectation operator to map boundedly and Hilbert-Schmidt into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. The criterion reduces to a Sobolev-smoothness requirement and applies to nonparametric regression, Bayesian inverse problems, and Koopman operator theory.

entry.title: One Ranking, Any Budget: Matryoshka Evidence-to-Context Frame Selection for Long-Video Understanding

author.name: Wang Chen, Yu Chen, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li, Jinfa Huang, Xiawu Zheng

entry.summary: This work reframes long-video frame selection as a Matryoshka ranking problem so that a single ranked ordering serves any frame budget through prefix reuse, instead of re-optimizing a separate subset per budget. Position-aware ranking objectives account for the different roles frames play at different ranks. The practical payoff is one selector that adapts to varying context windows and latency constraints of downstream multimodal models.

entry.title: Beyond Relevance: Bayesian Evidence Acquisition for Agentic Whole-Slide Image Reasoning

author.name: Bryan Wong, Xun Xu, Huazhu Fu, Nancy F. Chen, Mun Yong Yi

entry.summary: BEACON reframes agentic whole-slide-image diagnosis as Bayesian evidence acquisition rather than semantic relevance retrieval, selecting patches that most reduce diagnostic uncertainty instead of those that merely match the question text. The authors note that in pathology many relevant-looking patches are non-discriminative among competing diagnoses. It is a plug-and-play, training-free addition to existing agent frameworks.

entry.title: HOPE: Hand-Object Pressure Estimation from Monocular Videos

author.name: Subin Jeon, Byungjun Kim, Hanbyul Joo

entry.summary: HOPE estimates per-vertex contact pressure on the hand mesh over time from monocular video, reformulating pressure estimation as hand-centric video prediction so the output space is independent of object shape or sensor layout. Prior vision-based pressure work was restricted to planar surfaces and single images. Tactile-glove measurements are lifted onto the mesh to build supervision.

entry.title: Small Foundation Models of Human Cognition and Behaviour

author.name: Nick Oh, Fernand Gobet

entry.summary: Trains fourteen models from 135M to 14B parameters on Psych-101, a corpus of 10.7 million human trial-level choices, to test how much scale cognitive foundation models really need. In-distribution, sub-1B models match a 70B baseline against an apparent ceiling, but out-of-distribution generalization to novel tasks shows a much steeper scaling gradient.

entry.title: When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents

author.name: Linfang Shang, Ming Xu, Yiding Sun, Tianle Xia, Lingxiang Hu, Lan Xu, Ning Zheng

entry.summary: Finds that self-evolving agents exhibit a capability-contamination phase transition: past a critical skill-pool size, newly distilled skills degrade rather than improve performance, because a defective skill becomes reference material for later skills and forms cross-round contamination chains. The damage is shown to be structurally irreversible since removing the source skill leaves inherited flawed reasoning intact, motivating a pre-commit gate before skills enter the pool.

entry.title: Observation-Grounded Self-Predictive Reinforcement Learning for Visual Continuous Control

author.name: Xinwei Liu, Junyuan Liang, Jianting Zhang, Wuhui Chen

entry.summary: The paper argues that neither latent self-prediction nor observation-space prediction alone yields sample-efficient visual RL, and proposes combining them so that observation-level grounding and latent dynamics regularization reinforce each other. The target is pixel-based continuous control with limited training data.

entry.title: WorldClaw: Agentic 3D Open-World Generation at Scale

author.name: Chunchao Guo, Jinpeng Li, Yang Li, Zilong Huang

entry.summary: WorldClaw is an agentic coarse-to-fine pipeline that turns open-ended text into large, explorable 3D worlds by planning regions, terrain, assets, materials, and spatial relations, then building a coherent height-field terrain with editable reusable assets. It aims to preserve global coherence while producing artifacts suitable for downstream editing rather than a monolithic scene.

entry.title: C$^3$PO: Evaluating Cross-Modal Composition and Counterfactual Performance in Omnimodal Models

author.name: Swapnanil Mukherjee, Agyeya Negi, Tanuja Ganu, Ponnurangam Kumaraguru

entry.summary: C3PO is a 3,404-sample benchmark spanning video, audio, image, and text that tests two abilities: composing dispersed evidence across modalities and resolving deliberate cross-modal contradictions. Humans reach 88.6 percent while the best evaluated model, the existing Gemini-3.1-Pro, reaches 73.2 percent, exposing persistent dominant-modality bias.

entry.title: DreamGuard: Efficient Runtime Guardrail for LLM Agents via Risk-Aware World Model

author.name: Wenhao Lin, Chenyu Yu, Xingwei Lin, Sicong Cao, Xiang Chen, Lei Xue, Le Yu, Letian Sha, Chunming Wu

entry.summary: DreamGuard is a runtime guardrail for tool-using LLM agents built around a risk-aware world model that anticipates how risk evolves across a trajectory rather than only judging the apparent safety of the current action. It targets long-horizon drift where individually benign actions accumulate into hazardous states.

entry.title: FinEvo-Bench: A Longitudinal Benchmark for Self-Evolving Agents in Professional Financial Workflows

author.name: Bo Deng (Beihang University, Qwen DianJin Team, Alibaba Cloud Computing), Kang Zhou (Qwen DianJin Team, Alibaba Cloud Computing), Lifan Guo (Qwen DianJin Team, Alibaba Cloud Computing), Chongyang Tao (Beihang University), Xuanren Chen (Beihang University), Chenggang Xie (Beihang University), Renzhao Liang (Beihang University), Feng Chen (Qwen DianJin Team, Alibaba Cloud Computing), Chi Zhang (Qwen DianJin Team, Alibaba Cloud Computing)

entry.summary: FinEvo-Bench is a longitudinal benchmark of 120 real-case-grounded professional financial tasks across 20 business scenes, designed so that experience gained on earlier cases can transfer to later related ones. Each scene shares an institution-provided procedure and a manually reviewed rubric covering both deliverable quality and financial compliance.

entry.title: TRAJDEBUG: Tracing Error Lifecycle to Identify Critical Failures in Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories

author.name: Yunjia Qi, Zehua Yin, Xintong Shi, Hao Peng, Songyuanyi Lu, Yixian Liu, Richeng Xuan, Yuhong Liu, Zhichao Hu, Xiaozhi Wang, Lei Hou, Bin Xu, Juanzi Li

entry.summary: TrajDebug tackles critical error detection in long agent trajectories by tracing the lifecycle of errors, distinguishing local mistakes that get absorbed from those that causally drive final failure. It addresses the twin difficulties that judging a step needs evidence scattered across distant context and that multiple local errors coexist with different downstream effects.

entry.title: The Low Frequency Trap: Video Language Models Fail at Simple Event Bookkeeping

author.name: Sarvesh Baskar, Zikui Cai, Shayan Shabihi, Anirudh Satheesh, Muhammad R. Islam, Udari Madhushani Sehwag, Tom Goldstein, Furong Huang

entry.summary: The authors build parametric, trace-grounded video benchmarks for event counting across bouncing-ball contacts, blinks, and state transitions, varying event count and frequency across 2,190 videos while holding rendering fixed and providing executable event traces for timestamp-level scoring. They show video language models degrade in a controlled way, notably at low event frequencies, exposing basic bookkeeping failures.

entry.title: Innocent Panels, Hateful Stories: Evaluating and Detecting Hateful Intent in Multi-Turn Visual Story Generation

author.name: Ye Leng, Junjie Chu, Yiting Qu, Mingjie Li, Yun Shen, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: This work studies hateful meaning that emerges only at the level of an ordered image group rather than any single panel, enabled by conversational text-to-image systems that maintain consistent characters across turns. The authors build a dataset and evaluate both generation-side vulnerability and detection of group-level hateful intent.

entry.title: Learning Context-Free Grammars for Grammar-Constrained Decoding via Declarative Agentic Programming with Guarantees

author.name: Kevin Cheang, Geoff Hulette, Rahul Kumar, Felipe R. Monteiro, Federico Mora, Robin Salkeld, Lin Tan, Serdar Tasiran

entry.summary: Autogrammar is an agent that automatically learns context-free grammars for low-resource domain-specific languages from documentation and execution traces, so grammar-constrained decoding can eliminate syntactically invalid model outputs. It is formalized as a Kripke structure whose nondeterministic choices are resolved by a language model, giving guarantees about the learned grammar.

entry.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games

author.name: Boning Li, Yu Chen, Longbo Huang

entry.summary: Combines a variance-reduction estimator for imperfect-information games with anytime-valid confidence sequences so that agent-versus-agent comparisons can stop as soon as evidence is sufficient without invalidating the statistical guarantee. Across 15 LLM agent configurations and over 71,000 paired poker hands the combination reports large reductions in the cost of reaching a verdict.

entry.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization

author.name: Xian Sun, Wei Chow, Yingshuo Wang, Junhao Liu, Wei Gao, Qing Wu, Lingdong Kong

entry.summary: Reframes context robustness as selective trust, noting that a model which ignores all external context looks robust on adversarial tests while being useless when context is genuinely helpful. The authors release a human-annotated benchmark presenting each reasoning item under clean, misleading, helpful, and irrelevant context, plus a paired metric counting misleading-induced flips, and propose a preference optimization method.

entry.title: EvoHarness-RL: Learning Self-Evolving Runtime Harness for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Xuying Ning, Dongqi Fu, Tianxin Wei, Hanqing Zeng, Yuanchen Bei, Bingxuan Li, Zihao Li, Qifan Wang, Xiang Shen, Yifan Wu, Jiayi Liu, Hong Li, Yinglong Xia, Xiangjun Fan, Hanghang Tong, Jingrui He

entry.summary: Formulates harness policy learning, where long-horizon LLM agents learn offline how to build and update their external workspace, including memory, progress tracking, tool invocation, and experience reuse, instead of relying on hand-written prompts and conventions. The reinforcement learning approach then deploys these learned policies to manage external state during task execution.

entry.title: Reasoning Errors Have a Region and a Direction in the Residual-Stream Trajectory of LLMs

author.name: Hamed Damirchi, Ignacio Meza De la Jara, Damith Ranasinghe, Yuhang Liu, Javen Shi

entry.summary: Argues that trajectory-based reasoning-error detectors relying only on layerwise residual-stream displacement discard where an update started, while using full states reintroduces shortcut features. The authors propose a three-stream detector combining motion with a coarse vector-quantized region reader and a fine direction reader over normalized states.

entry.title: CircuitSteer: Geometrically Aligned Multi-Layer Steering via Sparse Autoencoder Circuits

author.name: Mehrshad Saadatinia, Parsa Razmara, Ardalan Aryashad, Ali Abbasi, Seyedarmin Azizi

entry.summary: Proposes a steering method that uses sparse autoencoders to identify coherent semantic circuits spanning multiple layers, then intervenes along those circuits instead of applying a single fixed-layer activation offset. The motivation is that contrastive activation addition applies one intervention to semantically diverse inputs and fails to sustain behavior change across layers.

entry.title: Alternating Levenberg-Marquardt Training of Physics-Informed Neural Networks with Fourier-Enhanced Features

author.name: Yulun Wu, Matthieu Barreau, Miguel Aguiar, Karl H. Johansson

entry.summary: FALM-PINN attacks two known failure modes of physics-informed neural networks, spectral bias and entanglement of representation learning with coefficient fitting, by alternating a Fourier-enhanced basis learning step with a Levenberg-Marquardt coefficient solve. The bilevel decoupling targets PDEs with high-frequency, multi-scale, or strongly nonlinear solutions.

entry.title: THBKG: A Temporal Biomedical Knowledge Graph for Decision-Aligned Clinical Advancement Prediction

author.name: Pui Chung Siu, Claudia Cabrera, Mani Mudaliar, Arkaitz Zubiaga

entry.summary: THBKG is a temporal biomedical knowledge graph with about 110k entities and 11.1M edges across nineteen relation types, where each edge carries the year its supporting evidence changed, enabling reconstruction of what was known when a drug program entered the clinic. It is used to predict which target-disease programs advance clinically without leaking future evidence.

entry.title: SAGA: Score-Weighted Adaptive Generation Alignment for Low-Resource Nordic Language Models

author.name: Hoda Fakharzadehjahromy, Emil Wiman, Andreas Bueff, Hafsteinn Einarsson, Fredrik Heintz

entry.summary: SAGA replaces scarce human preference labels for Danish, Icelandic, and Norwegian with dependency-parser judgments, converting them into preference pairs for a delta-DPO objective with a composite reward combining parse quality and lexical diversity. It also filters low-information pairs and monitors reward hacking.

entry.title: MetaboLLM: a metabolomics-specialized large language model for biochemical knowledge integration and predictive metabolite graph construction

author.name: Dohyun Ku, Min Gu Kwak, Francisco J. Pasquel, Jing Li

entry.summary: MetaboLLM is a metabolomics-specialized LLM built through continual pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and structured retrieval, paired with a graph isomorphism network that turns generated biochemical descriptions into metabolite graphs for patient-level prediction. It beat base and medically adapted models on domain knowledge tasks and achieved the best AUC for stress hyperglycemia prediction.

entry.title: The Tamed Subgradient Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm beyond Convexity

author.name: Iosif Lytras, Nikolaos Makras, Sotirios Sabanis

entry.summary: SG-TULA is a Langevin sampling algorithm that operates directly on subgradients for target distributions that are simultaneously non-smooth, non-convex, and have superlinearly growing gradients, using taming for stability. The authors give explicit non-asymptotic Wasserstein-2 convergence bounds improving prior subgradient Langevin rates.

entry.title: SR-JEPA: Learning Predictive Latent State in 3D Scenes

author.name: Zihan Zhou, Qifu Wen, Xi Zeng

entry.summary: SR-JEPA trains a point-native joint-embedding predictive architecture on scene-scale point clouds using only self-contained 3D targets from an exponential moving average teacher, with no reconstruction, labels, language, or lifted 2D features. The authors probe what the frozen predictive pathway itself infers when an entire object is removed and replaced by a shape-free query at its centroid.

entry.title: To See a World in a Living Context: Unified Indoor-Outdoor Urban World Generation

author.name: Xiaobin Huang, Zilong Huang, Yang Luo, Hongchao Fan, Yiping Chen, Ting Han

entry.summary: HoloWorld generates coherent urban worlds where interiors and exteriors correspond, by maintaining a continuously updated cross-scale world context from city planning down to individual buildings. Blocks are generated autoregressively conditioned on that evolving context and previously generated neighbors. It addresses the usual disconnect between separately synthesized indoor and outdoor 3D generation.

entry.title: Respect Your Zero-Shot Uncertainty: Conservative Calibration for Test-Time-Adapted Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jingyan Jiang, Yaru Sun, Xiao Chen, Jiazhen Huang, Caiting Li, Zhijian He, Yin Chen, Pingting Hao

entry.summary: This paper shows that test-time adaptation of vision-language models can sharpen confidence and reduce entropy without changing the prediction or its correctness, a failure mode it names prediction-preserving sharpening, and links larger entropy drops to worse calibration. It proposes a conservative calibration approach that respects the original zero-shot uncertainty. Reliable confidence matters when adapted models feed downstream decisions.

entry.title: Recursive Synthesis for Long-Horizon Terminal Tasks

author.name: Zhongzhi Li, Yucheng Shi, Zongxia Li, Ruhan Wang, Anhao Li, Zixun Huang, Junyao Yang, Lei Ke, Ninghao Liu, Haitao Mi, Leowei Liang

entry.summary: Recursive Synthetic Terminal Tasks builds long-horizon terminal-agent training tasks at scale by extending a verified seed solution, realigning verifier and instruction to the new workflow, revalidating in a fresh sandbox, and recycling accepted tasks as seeds. It targets the very high per-task cost of keeping instruction, environment, solution, and verifier mutually consistent.

entry.title: ARGUS: Aligning Robot Scene Geometry Under Shifting Views with Large 3D Vision Models

author.name: Rishik Sathua, Haonan Chen, Katherine Driggs-Campbell

entry.summary: ARGUS preprocesses robot camera observations by using large 3D vision models to warp arbitrary viewpoints into a canonical frame before feeding downstream visuomotor policies. This attacks the entanglement whereby policies learn where objects are in the image rather than in task space, which blocks learning from viewpoint-diverse datasets like DROID and BridgeV2. It is a drop-in pipeline compatible with existing policies.

entry.title: Hyper-ES: Effective Evolution Strategies for LLM Reasoning via Descent Direction Merging

author.name: Yu Gu, Zhi Zheng, Yunpeng Ba, Xialiang Tong, Mingxuan Yuan, Zhenkun Wang

entry.summary: Hyper-ES makes evolution strategies viable for billion-parameter LLM reasoning by first running a few cheap gradient-based fine-tuning runs to obtain descent directions, then evolving in the low-dimensional subspace those directions span rather than in full parameter space. This avoids the problem that random perturbations in high dimensions are nearly orthogonal to useful update directions.

entry.title: AppDeltaWorld: Transition-Grounded Delta Code World Model for Mobile GUI Agents

author.name: Weikai Xu, Yunren Feng, Haoxiang Lei, Kun Huang, Yuxuan Liu, Kang Zhao, Xiaolin Hu, Shuo Shang, Bo An

entry.summary: AppDeltaWorld is a GUI world model that predicts the next screen as a constrained code delta applied to retrieved app-specific HTML structure, instead of generating an unconstrained image or free-text description. This is intended to fix instability, limited modality coverage, and inconsistent action-transition logic in existing GUI world models, and to substitute for real trajectories on privacy-sensitive apps.

entry.title: DASH: Divergence-Adaptive Supervision Horizons for On-Policy Self-Distillation of Reasoning Models

author.name: ZhiYan Hou, Xinyu Tang, Hongyan An, Jianjin Zhang, Weizhen Wang, Yunyun Han, Gengsheng Li, Xiangzhao Hao, Haiyun Guo, Wenbin Hu, Jinqiao Wang, Yafeng Deng

entry.summary: DASH improves on-policy self-distillation for reasoning models by making the weight on each token-level teacher-student divergence depend on its position and on the sequence of preceding divergences, instead of treating all local divergences equally. It argues that identical divergence magnitudes have very different downstream consequences in autoregressive rollouts.

entry.title: Large Language Models Threaten Double-blind Review

author.name: Bulambo Mwendelwa Gloire, Prasenjit Mitra

entry.summary: Using only titles and abstracts of papers published after model training cutoffs, the authors show LLMs can deanonymize authorship more efficiently than humans, concentrating belief on a few candidates from expert pools of five. The vulnerability persists after stylistic and bibliographic mitigations, threatening the premise of double-blind review.

entry.title: In-Context Forcing: Uncovering Context Effects in Autoregressive Video Diffusion

author.name: Lingxiao Yang, Liu Liu, Moran Li, Han Feng, Wenjian Cao, Jiangning Zhang, Ye Shi

entry.summary: In-Context Forcing observes that few-step autoregressive video diffusion models conditioned on fully denoised previous frames take shortcuts from leaked local detail, harming temporal semantics and dynamics. The fix is a progressive scheme where context frames carry decreasing noise levels, balancing guidance strength against detail leakage.

entry.title: Big, Bright, or Invisible: A Frozen-Feature Benchmark of 3D CT Foundation Models

author.name: Maulik Chevli, Johannes Brandt, Rickmer Braren, Daniel Rueckert, Philip M\"uller

entry.summary: Benchmarks ten frozen 3D CT encoders on thoracic scans across three cohorts including an unseen clinical dataset, using nearest neighbors, zero-shot prompting, and linear probing. The headline finding is that no encoder is universally best, rankings swing with evaluation protocol, and a lightweight supervised model stays competitive with large foundation models.

entry.title: Continual Learning in Transition

author.name: Zhiyan Hou, Dan Zhang, Tao Feng, Liyuan Wang, Wei Li, Xiangzhao Hao, Hongyan An, Junfeng Fang, Haokai Ma, Zhaohui Xu, Haiyun Guo, Jinqiao Wang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: A position and survey paper arguing that continual learning is shifting away from parameter-centric updates toward system-level evolution involving on-policy learning, test-time training, external memory, skill libraries, and interaction protocols. It reorganizes the field around the idea that capability can grow outside the static weight space.

entry.title: BaKron: Efficient Quantization with Kronecker-Factored Hessians

author.name: Johann Birnick, Rayan Saab

entry.summary: Speeds up post-training quantization methods that use two-sided Kronecker-factored Hessian approximations, which capture output-coordinate correlations that ordinary activation-only GPTQ misses but are expensive in the vectorized weight domain. The proposed solver uses anti-diagonal parallelism and divide-and-conquer to reduce sequential steps to linear in the matrix dimensions.

entry.title: KV-Skill: Forging Expertise in the Model's Native Language

author.name: Zhaowei Han, Xiang Zhang, Bing Han, Kai Liu, Danqi Hu, Jie Liu

entry.summary: Proposes storing task knowledge as external factorized key-value operators that a frozen language model reads through a lightweight interface, occupying no prompt positions and remaining loadable, removable, and shareable. One path converts authored text skills into operators and another learns compact latent operators directly from task rewards, evaluated across ten benchmarks and four backbones.

entry.title: A Six-Dimensional Taxonomy of Post-Training Adaptation Techniques with Applications in AI Governance

author.name: Fardin Afdideh, Fernando Seoane, Farhad Abtahi

entry.summary: A survey organizes post-training adaptation methods, spanning fine-tuning, parameter-efficient tuning, alignment, retrieval augmentation, model editing, unlearning, and calibration, along six dimensions covering mechanism, goal, data needs, persistence, structural scope, and model type. The taxonomy is pitched at governance use, giving regulators vocabulary for describing how a deployed model was modified.

entry.title: RxnCLF: Contrastive Transformation-Aware Reaction Foundation Model for Improved Reactivity Prediction

author.name: Yiting Zheng, Cheng Fang, Anthony Donofrio, Haote Li

entry.summary: RxnCLF learns reaction representations by contrastive self-supervision over condensed reaction graphs that merge reactants and products into one structure, so the model encodes the transformation itself rather than disconnected molecules. The aim is better yield and reactivity prediction under scarce labels.

entry.title: Hypothesis Testing with Conditional Queries: Learnability and the Value of Interaction

author.name: Zonghuan Xu

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes distinguishing distribution classes when a tester can only ask conditional queries, comparing adaptive testing that uses earlier responses against non-adaptive testing that fixes all queries in advance. It characterizes learnability by pairwise conditional separation and quantifies the extra query cost of losing adaptivity.

entry.title: PoolBench: A Benchmark for Pooling Strategies in Concept Representation Evaluation for Decoder-Only LLMs

author.name: Ayushi Agarwal

entry.summary: PoolBench isolates the choice of pooling strategy for turning token-level hidden states into passage vectors in decoder-only models, comparing 19 pooling rules across 17 concepts and three open-weight models on one audited corpus. It aims to remove the confounds that make current concept-representation results incomparable.

entry.title: Effective pruning of task-trained recurrent neural networks using noisy fluctuations and connection rescaling

author.name: Sanjith Senthil, Rishidev Chaudhuri

entry.summary: The authors evaluate noise-prune, a biologically plausible local rule that uses noisy fluctuations to score connection importance, on task-trained recurrent networks rather than random ones. It preserves task performance far better than magnitude pruning and matches or exceeds a non-local second-order method.

entry.title: Evidence-Driven Dynamic Visual Selector for Efficient Long Video Understanding

author.name: Bo Zhang, Wenxin Wang, Feng Chen, Zhihao Zhang, Zixuan Wang, Changsheng Li, Yinjie Lei

entry.summary: EviSelect selects frames for long-video understanding using the target multimodal model's own internal attention as the evidence signal, obtained via cheap sparse prefilling, rather than an external proxy scorer. It then performs distribution-aware dynamic sampling that adapts to uneven spatiotemporal information density. The motivation is that external scorers are misaligned with what the downstream model actually attends to.

entry.title: Learning from Failures: Retrieval-Centric CoT via Hard Negatives for Unified Multimodal Retrieval

author.name: Zelong Sun, Jun Wang, Kaicheng Yang, Tiancheng Gu, Ziyong Feng, Zhiwu Lu

entry.summary: This work argues that chain-of-thought used for multimodal retrieval should be conditioned on retrieval feedback rather than the query alone, so it explains what the retriever gets wrong instead of restating the query. It builds rationales from hard negatives, that is, from the retriever's actual failures. The aim is finer-grained discrimination among semantically similar candidates.

entry.title: When Privileged Guidance Misaligns: State-Matched Routing and Contextualized Self-Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents

author.name: Junzhuo Liu, Weiwei Li, Jun Ling, Peng Wang

entry.summary: Identifies a state-reference mismatch problem in privileged on-policy distillation for multi-turn agents: as the student diverges from the reference trajectory, teacher guidance conditioned on training-only references becomes unreliable for the state actually reached. The paper proposes state-matched routing plus contextualized self-distillation so privileged guidance is applied only where it is valid.

entry.title: StepReflect: Structured UI Transition Reflection for Mobile GUI Agents

author.name: Linqiang Guo (Peter), Wei Liu (Peter), Li Gu (Peter), Yang Wang (Peter), Tse-Hsun (Peter), Chen

entry.summary: StepReflect reframes per-step GUI action reflection as supervised structured prediction over explicit transition specifications plus paired visual evidence, rather than open-ended multimodal reasoning after each action. Trained via SFT, teacher-student distillation, and preference and reward refinement, the resulting 8B model reaches 82.16 percent transition-level accuracy on AndroidWorld, about 11.8 points above zero-shot performance from the existing GPT-5.2.

entry.title: SemiAdapt-Instruct: Extensible Instruction Tuning via Latent Domain-Specialised Adapters

author.name: Josh McGiff, Salma Mekaoui, Robert Shanahan, Nikola S. Nikolov

entry.summary: SemiAdapt-Instruct discovers latent instruction domains, trains one LoRA adapter per domain in parallel, and routes at inference without learned routing parameters, so new domains can be added by training a single adapter. It reportedly beats full fine-tuning on ROUGE-L and LLM-judge scores while remaining extensible.

entry.title: Reversible Unlearnable Examples: Towards the Copyright Protection in Deep Learning Era

author.name: Binze Wang, Jinyu Tian, Xingrun Wang, Xiaochen Yuan, Jianqing Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes reversible unlearnable examples that simultaneously prevent unauthorized model training on protected data and enable ownership verification against data leakage, arguing that naively combining availability attacks with watermarking causes destructive interference. The perturbation can be inverted by the rightful owner. It frames copyright protection as needing to counter two distinct threats at once.

entry.title: Search2Skill: Skill Distillation Beyond Knowledge Boundaries Via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Muyang Ye, Tian Lan, Feihu Jiang, Yongshi Ye, Wuyunsiqin, Bin Zhu, Qianghuai Jia, Zhao Xu, Weihua Luo, Ye Wang, Jinyang Zhang, Longyue Wang, Lingfeng Bao

entry.summary: Search2Skill identifies an agent's capability gaps, searches external sources to fill them, and distills the retrieved evidence into structured reusable skills using rubric-based reinforcement learning. The premise is that professional domain conventions lie outside the model's parametric knowledge, so purely self-generated skills are bounded by what the model already knows.

entry.title: From Economic Agents to Agentic Economies: A Systems Blueprint for Economic World Models

author.name: Jiale Han, Xiang Li, Jing Qian, Wenyuan Gu, Pin Gao, Ye Luo, Hongyuan Zha, Dacheng Tao, Benyou Wang, Lin William Cong

entry.summary: Proposes a systems blueprint for Economic World Models, generative simulators in which heterogeneous agents with beliefs and actions co-evolve with markets and institutions to produce macro dynamics endogenously. It organizes the space into a six-level capability ladder running from rule-based agent worlds through LLM-based and self-evolving agents to sim-to-real economic twins.

entry.title: Evaluating Investment Logic in Large Language Models: A Real-World Benchmark Towards Personalzied Financial Agents

author.name: Yuanhong Jiang, Jingjie Zou, Zhenghong Lin, Xusheng Yu, Qiqi Huang, Shuai Jia, Shijie Dai

entry.summary: InvestLogicBench evaluates financial LLM agents on the reasoning process rather than only final profit, using roughly 201k documented decisions from 151 real investors structured as profile-evidence-reasoning-decision-outcome traces. It argues that current evaluation rulers (static QA or terminal profit and loss) cannot distinguish grounded, profile-consistent decisions from lucky ones.

entry.title: Autonomous Research Agents: A Survey of AI Scientists and the Verification Gap

author.name: Tianyu Ding, Aditya Nannapaneni, Bingfan Liu, Ling Zhang

entry.summary: A survey of 35 autonomous research agent systems, with full-text coding of 26 across seven audit dimensions including autonomy level, evaluation method, released artifacts, and human-in-the-loop points. Its central claim is a verification gap: end-to-end AI scientist systems produce manuscript-like claims that are much harder to verify than their code is to run.

entry.title: Matrix Zonotopic Attention: A Context-Adaptive Value Projection for Set Transformers

author.name: Zhen Zhang, Amr Alanwar

entry.summary: The authors note that multi-head attention pairs input-dependent softmax routing with an input-independent value projection, so the operator mapping aggregated values to outputs is identical for every input set. They define transformation degrees of freedom, prove that context-rigid attention needs depth proportional to that quantity, and propose matrix zonotopic attention with a context-adaptive value family that can match the target in one layer.

entry.title: MACRO: Markov Chain Routing of Transformer Layers

author.name: Pawe{\l} Batorski, Abtin Pourhadi, Akylgali Aitaza, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek, Paul Swoboda

entry.summary: Learns task-specific execution paths through a frozen transformer, allowing layer skips, repetitions, and other moves, by modeling routing as a context-dependent Markov policy over layer indices and compute budget phases. No model weights are changed and no per-instance search or labels are needed at inference.

entry.title: Visual Grounding in Zero-Shot Vision-Language Control

author.name: J. de Curt\`o, Dayani Plasencia, Diego S\'anchez, I. de Zarz\`a

entry.summary: Runs an extensive ablation battery on VLMs used as zero-shot controllers, including blind images, repeated inputs, and reflected scenes, across nine direct-action models and two embodiments with nearly 33,000 scored calls. Results are largely negative, with a constant slow-driving policy beating scripted and VLM controllers, showing that good scores can arise without visual grounding.

entry.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Benchmarks for Conversational Agents

author.name: Noam Koren, Roy Bar-Haim, Abigail Goldsteen

entry.summary: Proposes a reference-free framework that uses LLM judges to score the quality of benchmarks for task-oriented conversational agents along consistency, complexity, and policy coverage, with diagnostics of specific weaknesses. Validation includes agreement with human annotation and detection of deliberately degraded benchmarks.

entry.title: PPDL: LLM-Based Flows as Probabilistic Programs

author.name: Louis Mandel, Guillaume Baudart, Mandana Vaziri, Martin Hirzel

entry.summary: Introduces a probabilistic programming language for LLM-based workflows so developers can quantify and propagate uncertainty through chains of model and tool calls, and swap inference-scaling strategies without rewriting flow logic. This targets the compounding unreliability of multi-step LLM pipelines.

entry.title: Disentangling 3D Modeling from Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Haoze Sun, Jiequan Cui, Qingshan Xu, Richang Hong

entry.summary: Argues that spatial reasoning is better served by separating explicit 3D perception from symbolic reasoning instead of learning both implicitly through large-scale multimodal training. Off-the-shelf geometry estimators reconstruct structured 3D evidence and a LoRA-tuned LLM reasons over that explicit representation.

entry.title: QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding

author.name: Ayushman Garg, Akshita Gupta, Shaswata Bhattacharya, Abhishek Gupta, Sandeep Kumar, Manoj Kumar

entry.summary: Argues that KV cache eviction policies make irreversible decisions that break down during long generations, because token importance drifts as new queries are produced and evicted tokens can later matter. The authors introduce diagnostics measuring future missed attention mass and propose a recoverable quantized eviction scheme that can bring states back.

entry.title: Align-RAG: Alignment Is All You Need for TSFM In-Context Learning

author.name: Mohammad Asadi, Soheil Hor, Bardiya Akhbari, Jack W. O'Sullivan, Tahoura Nedaee, Layne C. Price, Raviteja Anantha, Euan Ashley, Ehsan Adeli

entry.summary: Shows that retrieval-augmented forecasting with frozen time series foundation models does not need a trained fusion adapter: a closed-form amplitude rescaling and integer lag shift applied to retrieved windows before they enter the context suffices. This training-free alignment reportedly beats the state-of-the-art trained retrieval adapter on a frozen backbone.

entry.title: Dynamic Graph Prompting via Topology-Routed Mixed-Curvature Experts

author.name: Quanxin Wang, Xuanting Xie, Bingheng Li, Xingtong Yu, Shuo Wang, Ruiyi Fang, Zhao Kang

entry.summary: CurvPrompt observes that temporal changes in clustering and degree heterogeneity shift the curvature spectrum of dynamic graphs, so a single fixed embedding geometry under-adapts. It maintains a bank of curvature-diverse Riemannian experts routed by local topology, adapting a frozen temporal backbone with lightweight prompts.

entry.title: Threshold-Based Early Stopping of Accumulations in Neural Networks with Binary Activation

author.name: Quentin Luquet de Saint-Germain, Massil Ait Abdeslam, Jean Pierre David

entry.summary: For binary-activation networks, only the sign of each accumulation matters, so this work stops accumulating once the partial sum has drifted far enough that the sign cannot flip. The post-training early-stopping rule reduces operations for low-power inference without retraining.

entry.title: A Unified Causal Inference Framework for the Desirability of Outcome Ranking Paradigm in Benefit-Risk Evaluation

author.name: Yuan Feng, Shiyu Shu, Yixin Fang, Ionut Bebu, Toshimitsu Hamasaki, Scott Evans, Guoqing Diao

entry.summary: The paper develops a covariate-adjusted causal framework for the desirability-of-outcome-ranking probability used in benefit-risk evaluation, expressing it as a bilinear functional of marginal ordinal outcome distributions and deriving its efficient influence function. Simulations compare G-computation, IPW, AIPW, and TMLE with machine-learning nuisance estimation.

entry.title: Engram-E2VID: Reference-Based Event-to-Video Reconstruction via Generative Activation of Appearance Engrams

author.name: Feiyu Ji, Xiang Li, Hao Ma, Tianxiang Huang, Qingxin Lu, Mengqi Ji, Lei Han, Xiaokang Yang, Xiaoyun Yuan

entry.summary: Engram-E2VID reconstructs RGB video frames from a reference image plus an event stream by generatively activating appearance memories associated with event-derived structure at the target time. It targets long temporal intervals and complex motion where events encode only sparse log-intensity changes rather than absolute appearance.

entry.title: ML-for-ML

author.name: Yutong Zhao, Noga H. Rotman, Gianni Antichi, Ran Ben Basat

entry.summary: ML-for-ML argues that network-level controls and ML training hyperparameters should be optimized jointly under a shared time-to-target-loss objective, rather than separately as is standard in shared cloud clusters. A preliminary prototype shows co-optimization reaches targets faster than tuning either layer alone.

entry.title: Optimal Rates for Learning with Monotone Adversaries

author.name: Anay Mehrotra

entry.summary: Resolves an open question about learning under monotone adversaries that append correctly labeled but non-exchangeable examples, showing whether the extra logarithmic factor in prior error bounds is necessary. Establishes optimal rates for VC classes in this robustness model.

entry.title: Floating Radiance Networks

author.name: Krzysztof Byrski, Rafa{\l} Tobiasz, Grzegorz Wilczy\'nski, Miko{\l}aj Zieli\'nski, Dawid Baran, Dominik Belter, Jacek Tabor, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek

entry.summary: Floating Radiance Networks represent a scene as floating planar generalized Gaussian primitives, each carrying a compact latent descriptor decoded by a shared lightweight network into color and opacity. This couples explicit ray-traceable geometry with continuous neural radiance, so the representation can slot into conventional graphics pipelines including ray tracing. It aims to break the tight coupling between neural scene representations and one specific renderer.

entry.title: Iterate or Widen? When Test-Time Refinement Helps LiDAR Scene Completion: A Controlled Study of Evidence Geometry, Training Coverage, and Compute

author.name: Shijie Hao, Weining Zhang

entry.summary: A controlled study asking whether extra test-time compute is better spent on iterative refinement or on a wider one-shot predictor for LiDAR semantic scene completion, carefully matching parameters and disentangling confounds like denoising curricula and corruption augmentation. Experiments use five seeds and hundreds of SemanticKITTI frames with exact scene-condition pairing. The result informs when iterative refinement genuinely pays off.

entry.title: World-to-Wrist: Task-Conditioned Future Wrist Modeling for Fine-Grained Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yuhao Pan, Haosong Peng, Zhengshen Zhang, Zhengyang Yan, Yalun Dai, Fushuo Huo, Chujie Wang, Tianyu Qi, Xiucheng Wang, Nan Cheng, Wenchao Xu

entry.summary: W2-VLA argues that main-view and wrist-view observations play different roles and adds a task-conditioned predictor that forecasts future wrist-view observations as a compact interface between the vision-language model and the action head. Anticipating how wrist-local contact evolves under global task context is claimed to help fine-grained manipulation. It is a structural change to standard multi-view VLA conditioning.

entry.title: GeniWorld: A Generalizable Interactive World Model for Robotic Manipulation via Visual Actions

author.name: Chenghao Gu, Hanyang Yu, Jingbo Zhang, Haitao Lin, Wenyao Zhang, Jinghe Wang, Hanglei Jin, Shuzhao Xie, Jingyan Jiang, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: GeniWorld is an action-conditioned interactive world model for manipulation that converts numeric robot actions into visual action renderings via URDF-based rendering, so a pretrained video generator can be controlled in a spatially grounded way. The claimed benefit is stronger action controllability and better generalization to unseen, out-of-distribution scenes, enabling cheaper policy evaluation than real-world rollouts. It targets the bottleneck of scaling robot evaluation.

entry.title: Otter: A Time-Aware, History-Conditioned Human Chess AI

author.name: Tarun Kumar S

entry.summary: Otter is a 15.3M-parameter model that predicts human chess moves by conditioning on the last 20 moves and on clock pressure, trained on 6.1 billion positions from Lichess rapid games using a single T4 GPU. It reports 55.2 percent top-1 and 91.0 percent top-5 accuracy, exceeding the prior Maia 2 human-play state of the art with far fewer parameters.

entry.title: SCP-NL2TL: Selective Conformal Prediction with Semantic Verification for Natural Language to Temporal Logic Specifications

author.name: Yixuan Wang, Licheng Luo, Yu Fu, Kaidi Xu, Yue Dong, Mingyu Cai

entry.summary: SCP-NL2TL adds selective prediction to natural-language-to-temporal-logic translation, abstaining when a specification cannot be trusted rather than always emitting one. Reliability is scored by back-translation fidelity and dispersion across repeated translations, combined under a conformal framework with coverage guarantees.

entry.title: Studying People to Study AI: Expert Perspectives on the Epistemic Fit and Barriers of Human Research in AI Safety & Ethics

author.name: Jessica Y. Bo, Paula Akemi Aoyagui, Shalaleh Rismani, Dipto Das, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed, Ashton Anderson

entry.summary: Through a survey of 93 and interviews with 17 AI safety and ethics researchers spanning technical, sociotechnical, governance, and normative backgrounds, this study examines why human-subjects research is undervalued relative to benchmarks and LLM simulations. Respondents broadly see human evidence as valuable but cite perceived validity issues, resource barriers, and epistemic mismatches as constraints on adoption.

entry.title: Learning Globally Reusable Skills for Coding Agents

author.name: Chen Yang, Jiashuo Tian, Ziqi Wang, Xinyin Liu, Meiru Ye, Junjie Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a skill-evolution framework for coding agents that treats accumulated skills as a graph with explicit inter-skill relationships and consolidates clusters of local updates into more general reusable capabilities. This targets the tendency of incremental skill libraries to overfit to individual tasks.

entry.title: Where Privacy Risk Lives in English-Source Multilingual RAG: A Stage-Decomposed Audit Across Five Query Languages

author.name: Yanhang Li, Zhichao Fan, Zexin Zhuang

entry.summary: The paper audits where personal-information leakage occurs in a multilingual retrieval-augmented pipeline with English source documents and five query languages, decomposing risk by stage with an input judge and regex output filter. Contrary to the common assumption, English showed the highest observed leak rate under output-only filtering, with residual leaks in Arabic and Swahili after adding the judge.

entry.title: VSMP-IMU: Video-Grounded Semantic Motion Programs for Sensor-Aware Synthetic IMU Generation

author.name: Lala Shakti Swarup Ray, Vitor Fortes Rey, Mengxi Liu, Paul Lukowicz, Bo Zhou

entry.summary: VSMP-IMU generates synthetic inertial sensor data for wearable activity recognition by extracting structured semantic motion programs from video, separating activity-defining semantics from sensor placement and execution style. It aims to combine the visual grounding of video-driven methods with the controllability of text-driven ones.

entry.title: Prior-SG: Task and Prior Driven Region Segmentation for Scene Graphs in Arbitrarily-Structured Environments

author.name: Giorgio Tonetti, Laurent Kneip, Abel Gawel, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: Prior-SG builds hierarchical 3D scene graphs by treating region segmentation as probabilistic alignment against task and semantic priors, rather than relying on geometric heuristics like wall-separated rooms that fail in open-plan spaces. The robot incrementally fuses RGB-D observations into an open-vocabulary instance graph and infers functional region semantics on top. Authors include a leading legged-robotics group.

entry.title: Beyond Flat Policies: Hierarchical Post-Training for Embodied Agents in Robotic Manipulation

author.name: He Kong, Zengjue Chen, Qi Wang, Qianli Xing, Runliang Niu, Peidong Liu, Jiawei Li, Shiqi Wang, Yi Chang

entry.summary: HiRoC is a post-training framework for vision-language-action models that separates a high-level planner producing subgoals from a low-level action policy, and improves both through online interaction rather than only offline imitation. The goal is more reliable long-horizon manipulation where flat policies lose track of task progress. It sits at the intersection of hierarchical RL and VLA fine-tuning.

entry.title: SkillTrace: Multi-Trace Provenance Auditing for LLM-Agent Skill Reuse

author.name: Jialuo Chen, Minghe Wang, Lingqi Jiang, Jianan Ma, Xinhao Deng, Xiaohu Du, Ruixiao Lin, Yunhao Feng, Linkang Du, Jingyi Wang

entry.summary: Presents SkillTrace, a provenance auditing framework that detects reuse of LLM-agent skill packages by extracting expression, implementation, and operational traces rather than treating skills as single-modality code. It targets the emerging problem of skill marketplaces where reuse may preserve only prompt text, only code, or only workflow structure.

entry.title: EcoAgent-Bench: Evaluating Economic Decision-Making in Budget-Constrained LLM Agents

author.name: Jie Wu, Ming Gong, Feixiang Cheng, Qinqin Zhao

entry.summary: EcoAgent-Bench prices every agent action and imposes explicit budgets across 304 tasks derived from GAIA, HotpotQA, and MuSiQue, testing whether agents avoid unnecessary escalation, escalate when local evidence is thin, choose model tiers sensibly, and stop on false-premise questions. Seven LLM agents are evaluated in tool-API and CLI settings against scripted oracle controls.

entry.title: SkillHEX: Improving Agent Skills via Hypothesis-Driven Autonomous Exploration and Exploitation

author.name: Yuru Feng, Yaoqi Chen, Beidi Zhao, Qianxi Zhang, Xinjiang Wang, Jianan Lu, Zhirui Wang, Shusen Xu, Zengzhong Li, Qi Chen

entry.summary: SkillHEX performs test-time agent skill evolution under tight interaction budgets by generating explicit hypotheses about failure causes and exploring multiple candidate skills, instead of greedily refining a single incumbent. The motivation is that sparse rewards conflate several latent failure causes, so greedy refinement can get trapped exploiting an early misdiagnosis.

entry.title: GSBF: Gaussian Splatting for Environment-Aware Beamforming

author.name: Yijie Bian, Wei Guo, Zixin Wang, Shenghui Song, Jun Zhang, Khaled B. Letaief

entry.summary: GSBF adapts 3D Gaussian Splatting to wireless beamforming by learning a persistent Gaussian representation of the environment with reciprocity-preserving bidirectional spherical Gaussian kernels, replacing the need for accurate instantaneous channel state information and iterative optimization. The premise is that radio propagation is governed by physical geometry that can be captured once and reused.

entry.title: HERALD: Counterfactual Audits and Minimal Repairs for Proof-of-Retrieval Rewards

author.name: Zhuowen Liu, Bohan Cui, YinShang Guo, Yuting Wang, Hao Li

entry.summary: HERALD is an offline audit for search-agent reward functions that applies exact same-question counterfactual interventions and separates candidate-visible from oracle information to test whether high rewards actually imply grounded retrieval. On four Qwen3-8B pools across HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and MuSiQue, the base reward resists search deletion and fake identifiers but is defeated by a label-free citation-laundering attack, and a full ablation isolates the minimal repair.

entry.title: When History Lies: Evaluating and Improving Tool Use under Misleading Multi-Turn Histories

author.name: Xiaoqing Wu, Xingyu Fan, Feifei Li, Wenhui Que

entry.summary: Studies how tool-calling agents are hijacked by stale but structurally valid dialogue and tool history, reporting that pollution flips 32.1 percent of decisions on a small model that were correct under the original trajectory. It introduces a paired benchmark with synchronized original, polluted, and oracle-state views plus eleven gold-preserving interventions to isolate where decisions break down.

entry.title: PaDoc: Layout-Grounded Parallel Decoding for Document Parsing

author.name: Hao Yu, Jiabo Zhan, Kang Liu, Linnan Zhao, Dongxu Yue, Rui Chen, Jinglin Wang, Chong Sun, Chen Li, Jing Lyu, Chun Yuan

entry.summary: PaDoc reformulates end-to-end document parsing so that predicted layout acts as a branching structure over a shared page representation, letting layout and per-region content decode in parallel instead of one long autoregressive sequence. This keeps full-page context while cutting decode length that otherwise scales with total page content.

entry.title: The Judgment-Consequence Gap: LLM Moral Reasoning in Healthcare Decisions

author.name: Hadi Hosseini, Samarth Khanna, Leona Pierce

entry.summary: The study traces LLM moral reasoning across successive levels in healthcare rationing vignettes: whether patient behavior is blameworthy, whether that makes the patient responsible for illness, and whether care should therefore be denied. It finds a judgment-consequence gap where models agree with human responsibility attributions but diverge on translating those judgments into allocation consequences.

entry.title: Search-Aided Joint Agent-Environment Reinforcement Learning for Robust Lifelong Multi-Agent Path Finding with Rotations

author.name: He Jiang, Jingtian Yan, Yulun Zhang, Yimin Tang, Tanishq Duhan, Rishi Veerapaneni, Guillaume Sartoretti, Jiaoyang Li

entry.summary: This work studies lifelong multi-agent path finding under realistic warehouse constraints including in-place rotations and robust safety requirements, which sharply increase coordination difficulty in tight spaces. The proposed approach combines search assistance with joint agent-and-environment reinforcement learning to plan continuously as agents receive new goals.

entry.title: Once a Response, Always a Response: Detecting LLM-generated Text via Latent Prompt Restoration

author.name: Hongrui Bao, Yubing Ren, Yanan Cao, Jinhan You, Fang Fang, Shi Wang

entry.summary: Presents a training-free detector for machine-generated text based on the idea that model output carries traces of the prompt that produced it, so an approximate prompt can be recovered and used as a detection signal. The method targets robustness limits of purely probability-statistic zero-shot detectors.

entry.title: ProDVI: Programmatic Dynamics Priors for Value Network Initialization

author.name: Xinwei Liu, Junyuan Liang, Jianting Zhang, Wuhui Chen

entry.summary: Uses a code-generating LLM to write approximate programmatic models of environment dynamics, then uses those programs to initialize the value network of a deep RL agent. This avoids requiring offline datasets, high-fidelity simulators, or meta-learning over related tasks to get an informative starting point.

entry.title: Hardware Keystores for AI Agent Signing Workflows: A Zero-Trust MCP Enforcement Architecture

author.name: Leo Sambrook, Sampo Sovio

entry.summary: Argues that AI agents currently keep signing keys in software-readable locations and proposes replacing them with hardware-confined keys accessed through a vendor-neutral interface, adding content-aware authorization for each key use. The motivation includes a production incident where keys were exfiltrated from a popular framework through email injection within minutes.

entry.title: When Does Consensus Mean Correctness? Measuring the Agreement-Accuracy Coupling with Semantics-Preserving Re-Rendering

author.name: Rasul Khanbayov, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: Tests the widespread assumption that a model's agreement across perturbed inputs tracks correctness, using programmatically redrawn scientific figures that are semantically equivalent by construction and come with exact ground-truth answers. On three open-weight vision-language models, re-rendering the figure gives a better reliability signal than simply resampling outputs.

entry.title: CLARA: Clarification of Language Ambiguity through Result Analysis for Natural-Language Cancer Genomics Queries

author.name: Pratyush Kumar Shukla, Manveer Singh Tib, Siddhant Garg

entry.summary: CLARA converts natural-language cancer genomics questions into typed query specifications, executes several plausible interpretations, and requests user clarification only when the resulting estimates diverge materially. It was evaluated on 330 executable mutation-prevalence contrasts over TCGA cohorts with a preregistered divergence criterion.

entry.title: Can Open-Weight LLMs Produce Kernel-Verified Coq Proofs? A Pilot Study

author.name: Ahmed Ryan, Md Erfan, Akond Ashfaque Ur Rahman, Md Rayhanur Rahman

entry.summary: A pilot study evaluates six open-weight LLMs on 100 theorems from CoqStoq at temperature zero, accepting a proof only if the Coq kernel verifies it in the original project environment. Success rates were low, with the best model verifying roughly one in eight theorems, underscoring the gap between proof-like text and machine-checked correctness.

entry.title: Discrete energy as an exact label-free training objective for finite-element surrogates

author.name: Ruifeng Cao (The University of Manchester), Xidan Song (Wuhan University)

entry.summary: This short note proves that minimizing assembled discrete potential energy is an exact label-free training objective for finite-element surrogates in linear elastostatics, since the energy gap equals half the squared stiffness-norm error and its gradient equals the stiffness-weighted error. Label-free energy minimization and supervised regression in the stiffness norm therefore share the same minimizer.

entry.title: A Foundational EDM2-Based Generative Model for High-Resolution Synthetic Fetal Ultrasound Imaging from Open Datasets

author.name: Harvey Mannering, Yilin Zhang, Ziao Liu, Zhiwu Huang, Jacqueline Matthew, Miguel Xochicale

entry.summary: An EDM2-based diffusion model trained on pooled public datasets generates 512x512 synthetic fetal ultrasound images across six anatomical planes, improving FID and boosting downstream plane classification to about 93 percent ensemble accuracy, above real-data-only training. A specialist rated realism at 2.67 out of 5, well below real images.

entry.title: GenGA: Editable and Data-Grounded Graphical Abstract Generation for Academic Papers

author.name: Takuro Kawada, Shunsuke Kitada, Hitoshi Iyatomi

entry.summary: GenGA defines the task of generating editable, data-grounded graphical abstracts from paper content and produces vector-style outputs that can be revised, rather than the raster images most vision-language pipelines emit. This supports the iterative figure revision inherent to writing and peer review.

entry.title: Deep Generalised Mixed Models: a Novel Neural Network Structure for Analysing Hierarchical Data

author.name: Nina van Gerwen, Dimitris Rizopoulos, Manon Hillegers, Loes Keijsers, Sten Willemsen

entry.summary: Deep generalised mixed models combine neural networks with mixed-effects structure to analyze hierarchical experience-sampling data, where standard statistical models scale poorly and standard ML is biased by informative dropout. The motivating case is adolescent daily emotion data in which participants with strong negative emotions were more likely to stop responding.

entry.title: MAVISEG: Manifold Propagation and Visual Prototypes for Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Segmentation in Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Rajatsubhra Chakraborty, Xujun Che, Ritabrata Chakraborty, Xi Niu, Depeng Xu

entry.summary: MAVISEG is a training-free refinement layer for zero-shot open-vocabulary segmentation extracted from text-to-image diffusion transformers, exploiting the generative trajectory, per-concept appearance statistics, and pairwise feature geometry rather than scoring pixels independently against a fixed text embedding. It operates only on pixel-by-concept score maps, so it can wrap existing attribution methods. This makes generative models more usable as free segmentation labelers.

entry.title: Diff-VF: Training-free High-quality Long Video Generation via Diffusion Model

author.name: Haoning Yang, Xinyuan Chen, Yaohui Wang, Guo Lu

entry.summary: Diff-VF converts existing short-video diffusion backbones into long-video generators without any fine-tuning, combining hybrid noise initialization for global semantic consistency, weighted window sampling to smooth inter-window seams, and temporal strategies to retain motion diversity. It is plug-and-play and model-agnostic. The problem it addresses is degradation when short-trained diffusion models are extrapolated to long durations.

entry.title: Adaptive-WAM: Quality-Guided Early-Exit Planning from Intermediate Video-Diffusion Features

author.name: Sining Ang, Yuguang Yang, Yan Wang

entry.summary: Adaptive-WAM asks how much of a large video diffusion model actually needs to run to produce a good driving trajectory, and finds planning quality is largely insensitive to video noise level while good trajectories can be decoded from intermediate transformer layers. The authors build a multi-exit planner on a 5B video backbone that exits early based on a quality estimate. This is a concrete efficiency argument against full future-video rollout in world-model-based driving.

entry.title: The Ignition Index: Measuring Global Workspace Dynamics in Language Models

author.name: Saman Rahbar

entry.summary: Introduces a scalar Ignition Index that fits a sigmoid to layerwise probe accuracy versus input signal strength, operationalizing the all-or-none ignition prediction of Global Workspace Theory inside transformers. Across 11 models and five architecture families it reports that feedforward transformers show substantially sharper ignition-like transitions than state-space models, with shuffled-label controls for probe capacity.

entry.title: Negotiating Risk Boundaries in AI for Policing Through Mixed-Stakeholder Deliberation

author.name: Mackenzie Jorgensen, Jo Reilly, Alex Sutherland, Miri Zilka

entry.summary: Reports a mixed-stakeholder deliberation workshop with 30 community representatives, police officers, and academics assessing risks of 13 AI use cases in UK policing with an explicit racial-bias focus. Participants were broadly open to adoption and rejected only three use cases outright, most notably recidivism risk assessment where objections targeted the premise rather than the implementation.

entry.title: When Do Prompt-Side Agent Playbooks Transfer? Accuracy, Cost, and Runtime Shift in Agent Deployment

author.name: Weihong Lin, Lin Sun, Xiangzheng Zhang

entry.summary: Studies whether frozen prompt-side playbooks for tool-using agents transfer beyond their source setting, using a shared distill-validate-transfer protocol across ALFWorld, TAU2-Bench, and XBench-DeepSearch. Transfer helps on ALFWorld under greedy decoding, but with global multiple-comparison correction only one of 135 route-level effects on TAU2-Bench survives, indicating largely compatibility-sensitive heterogeneity.

entry.title: OPERA: Operator-residual feedback for reliable autonomous optical experiments with language-model agents

author.name: Ning Xu, Xiang Zheng, Fuqiang Zhong, Huadong Wang, Xiaolong Wu, Zhiyuan Liu, Hui Ning

entry.summary: OPERA represents optical experiment actions as operators and evaluates them with physically interpretable residuals rather than model-internal scores, with independent evaluation against a withheld reference. Across three optical tasks, score-only feedback produced score gains without physical improvement in 23.6 to 39.0 percent of decisions versus about 1 to 2 percent under residual feedback.

entry.title: Contextual Information Policy Optimization for Search Agents

author.name: Xingyu Guo, Wei Chen, Linlin Yang, Baochang Zhang

entry.summary: This work introduces an RL objective for search agents that rewards whether post-retrieval actions are actually grounded in retrieved evidence, rather than only final-answer correctness or intermediate progress. The stated motivation is to curb prior-driven reasoning where agents form conclusions from parametric memory and use retrieval only for confirmation.

entry.title: Beyond Top-K: Replacing Black-Box Retrieval with Interpretable Agentic Operations

author.name: Sagar Tamang, Ayush Vyas, Tabarakul Hazarika

entry.summary: The paper argues that chunk-embed-top-k retrieval is structurally unsound for table-heavy financial and regulatory documents, quantifying the problem on a 780-page government report where most lines are table rows and a figure inherits its unit from a header a median of 13 lines above. It proposes replacing opaque nearest-neighbor retrieval with interpretable agentic operations over document structure.

entry.title: Marginal Matching Does Not License Factorized Sampling: Auditing Conditional Style Leakage in Factorized Generative Models

author.name: Duong Bach, Hai Nguyen Hong, Cuong Do

entry.summary: The paper shows that matching a latent style variable to a Gaussian prior in aggregate places no constraint on class-conditional style distributions, so style can remain highly label-predictive while appearing perfectly Gaussian. An exact decomposition identifies this as one of four conditions needed for valid factorized sampling, and removing it is necessary but not sufficient.

entry.title: SkillMemo: Expert-guided Skill Memory Framework for Compositional Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Changyuan Wang, Chubin Zhang, Zhenyu Wu, Runhao Li, Angyuan Ma, Ke Chao, Yinan Liang, Xiuwei Xu, Ziwei Wang, Yansong Tang, Jiwen Lu

entry.summary: Addresses weak compositional generalization in diffusion policies and vision-language-action models by implicitly decomposing long-horizon demonstrations into latent atomic skills stored in a dynamic episodic memory bank. Retrieved skill-level features are then reused to compose behavior in out-of-distribution tasks.

entry.title: FormBharo: Designing and Evaluating a Voice Agent for Conversational Form Filling in Rural India

author.name: Aman Dalmia, Sanskriti Midha, Jigar Doshi

entry.summary: Describes a deployed-oriented Hindi voice agent that completes structured government benefit forms over ordinary phone calls, pairing LLMs with deterministic rule-based validation and flow control to hold latency and cost down. It is being piloted with an NGO enrolling low-income mothers in maternal health programs.

entry.title: Beyond Sequence Order: Syntax-Informed Positional Embeddings for Transformers

author.name: Haris Riaz, Hyungji Kim, Mihai Surdeanu

entry.summary: Adds a lightweight syntactic prior learned from dependency parses into absolute, relative, and rotary positional embeddings during pretraining, leaving attention and the rest of the architecture untouched. The study isolates where the prior should be injected, finding architecture-dependent answers such as multiplicative coupling for relative-position decoders.

entry.title: Potential Matching Optimal Transport: Continuous Normalizing Flows for Exact $p$-Wasserstein Dynamics

author.name: Lishuo Zhang (School of Mathematical Sciences, Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Ruizhi Huang (School of Mathematical Sciences, Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Yang Yu (School of Mathematical Sciences, Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Lei Li (School of Mathematical Sciences, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Institute of Natural Sciences, MOE-LSC, Shanghai Jiao Tong University)

entry.summary: Presents a continuous normalizing flow framework for general p-cost optimal transport that parameterizes velocity through a scalar potential in the generalized Benamou-Brenier form and trains it with a self-induced matching loss along straight bridges. The main theorem shows that zero training loss implies exact recovery of the p-optimal transport map and dynamics.

entry.title: Learning to Rank Tensor Network Contraction Plans for GPU-Accelerated Quantum Circuit Simulation

author.name: Alfred M. Pastor, Maribel Castillo, Jose M. Badia

entry.summary: A learning-to-rank system predicts which tensor-network contraction plan will run fastest on GPUs for quantum circuit simulation, using structural features of the pairwise contraction sequence and gradient-boosted rankers trained on measured GPU timings. It targets the gap between theoretical contraction complexity and real hardware performance.

entry.title: Surv-IPTB: An Attention-Based Model for Estimating Individual Probability of Treatment Benefit with Survival Data

author.name: Lev V. Utkin, Stanislav K. Kogan, Andrei V. Konstantinov

entry.summary: Surv-IPTB estimates the individual probability that a patient benefits from treatment in survival settings by recasting it as a binary classification over paired treated and control patients, with attention over pairs. Right-censoring is handled via interval-valued (imprecise) probability representations.

entry.title: How Much Reconstruction Does Quantum Machine Learning Need? Late Fusion of Independently Trained Quantum Subcircuits

author.name: Prabhjot Singh, Adel N. Toosi, Rajkumar Buyya

entry.summary: For quantum machine learning under circuit cutting, this work replaces the exponentially expensive classical reconstruction step with late fusion, training and measuring each subcircuit independently and combining outputs with a small classical head. A tunable quantumness dial interpolates between pure fusion and full reconstruction, with a cut-entanglement diagnostic indicating when reconstruction actually matters.

entry.title: Enhancing Anomaly Resilience in Research Networks: A Large-Scale Forecasting Benchmark for Dynamic Security Baselining

author.name: Mohammad Arafath Uddin Shariff, Byrav Ramamurthy

entry.summary: Using a 57-day Internet2 dataset covering ten backbone routers and 13.7 billion packets, this work benchmarks traffic forecasting models to build dynamic security baselines for research networks, where legitimate elephant flows resemble volumetric DDoS attacks. Better baselines aim to cut the false positives that blind operators to real threats.

entry.title: Beyond Marginal Validity: Finite-Sample Guarantees for Localized Conformal Prediction

author.name: Anton Conrad, Rustam Isaev, Denis Belomestny, Eric Moulines, Sergey Samsonov

entry.summary: Provides finite-sample guarantees for randomly localized conformal prediction, jointly bounding conditional coverage validity and oracle efficiency under Holder regularity assumptions. Addresses the known gap where marginal coverage hides severe covariate-specific miscalibration.

entry.title: Minimax Optimal Early-Stopped Gradient Descent for Gaussian Mixture Classification

author.name: Alex Buna, Shirley Xiaoqi Liu, Patrick Rebeschini

entry.summary: Proves that early-stopped gradient descent on logistic loss attains minimax-optimal zero-one risk in a Gaussian mixture model with label noise, whereas the max-margin interpolating solution that GD converges to directionally is statistically suboptimal. Covers polynomial and exponential covariance spectral decays with matching lower bounds.

entry.title: Scaffold-Mediated Post-Training: Co-Evolving Model Parameters and Procedural Scaffold Graphs

author.name: Fei Ding, Yongkang Zhang, Runhao Liu, Yuhao Liao, Zijian Zeng, Huiming Yang

entry.summary: Proposes co-evolving model parameters with an evolvable graph of inference-time procedural scaffolds, so that discovered agentic strategies are progressively distilled into weights. Reports pass-rate gains on FeatureBench and high retention of skill performance after scaffold removal.

entry.title: DBLAST: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding

author.name: Amirmohammad Karimi, Chao Gao, Negar Hassanpour

entry.summary: Identifies that block and diffusion-style speculative decoding drafters assume conditional independence across draft positions, which degrades accepted draft length as target sampling entropy rises. Proposes dependent block drafting to better match stochastic target distributions and recover speedups under non-greedy decoding.

entry.title: Where Models Converge and Humans Diverge: A Coverage Framework for Distributional Pluralism in Open-Ended Generation

author.name: Zini Yang, Emily Wenger, Richard So

entry.summary: Proposes a human-grounded coverage framework to quantify the well-known gap between the narrow, average-seeming distribution of LLM open-ended writing and the much broader distribution of human-written text, using fanfiction as a testbed. Turns an anecdotal observation into a measurable quantity.

entry.title: Runtime Observability for Heterogeneous Attention Memory

author.name: Fanzhe Wei, Li Liu, Ziyang Wang, Chenyu Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a runtime observability contract covering four heterogeneous memory classes in modern models, including plain KV caches, latent caches, learned sparse selectors, and recurrent states, using three operators with typed error metrics. Per-stage bounds compose into a request-level risk ledger, and composition is rejected when error metrics do not match, with unprovable parts measured empirically.

entry.title: Seeing Is Not Deciding: Can Multimodal LLMs Act as Effective CEOs?

author.name: Yuyang Dai, Xueqing Peng, Yuxia Wang, Preslav Nakov, Zhuohan Xie

entry.summary: C-SuiteBench places nine frontier models in a chief-executive role across five decision tasks and 50 scenarios under paired text-only and multimodal conditions, isolating whether visual business evidence improves decision quality. Multimodal inputs consistently help evidence-centric reasoning, with the largest reliable gains in risk forecasting and board-facing judgments.

entry.title: MicroEvo: Knowledge-Guided LLM Sampling for Efficient Microarchitecture Design Space Exploration
