author.name: Jia Xiong, Runkai Li, Chenxu Niu, Guangyuan Gao, Changwen Xing, Yifan Zhang, Xinlai Wan, Jieran Cui, Chen Bai, Yusheng Hua, Ying Wang, Ming Ling, Xi Wang, Tao Xie

entry.summary: MicroEvo couples off-the-shelf LLMs with Monte Carlo Tree Search for multi-objective microarchitecture design-space exploration, adding LLM evolutionary operators, a Pareto-aware tree policy, and accumulated design knowledge to guide sampling under tight simulation budgets. It targets faster Pareto convergence than blind search baselines.

entry.title: Universal Pathologies, Conditional Consequences: A Triple-Robustness Analysis of RAG for Multi-Hop Traceability

author.name: Meftun Akarsu, Burak Ozdemir

entry.summary: A large factorial study varying embedder, corpus, and LLM judge across thousands of runs to determine when GraphRAG loses to vector RAG on citation precision. It finds over-citation is architecturally universal, with GraphRAG emitting 11 to 15 identifiers per answer at low citation precision, while the faithfulness consequence of that over-citation is corpus-dependent.

entry.title: SkillZip: Contract-Preserving Graph Compression for Scalable Agent Skill Libraries

author.name: Xingyu Tan, Xiaoyang Wang, Qing Liu, Xiwei Xu, Xin Yuan, Liming Zhu, Wenjie Zhang

entry.summary: SkillZip compresses agent skill libraries at the sub-skill level by identifying contract-bearing procedural units and compressing them as graphs, so compressed routines remain executable, expandable, and updatable as skills evolve. It diagnoses a unit mismatch in which skills are retrieved as packages, compressed as text, and only later turned into execution graphs.

entry.title: Relay, Don't Route: Adaptive Population Handoff for Cost-Efficient LLM-Driven Evolution

author.name: Sichun Luo, Yi Huang, Guanzhi Deng, Haibo Wang, Haochen Luo, Lei Li, Zefa Hu, Junlan Feng, Qi Liu

entry.summary: The authors analyze LLM-driven evolutionary program search and find progress is strongly front-loaded, early signals are informative but noisy, and cheap models capture much of the early gains. Instead of routing individual queries, they propose handing off the whole evolving population from a cheap model to a strong model at an adaptive point, exploiting the stateful nature of evolutionary search.

entry.title: The em-dash em-beds in Congress: A population-level rise in em-dash frequency in U.S. congressional press releases at the dawn of the large-language-model era, 2021-2025

author.name: Przemys{\l}aw Czuma (Polish Association for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine)

entry.summary: Preregistered analysis of roughly 146,000 U.S. congressional press releases from 2021 to 2025 testing whether the unspaced em-dash, a widely rumored LLM stylistic tell, rose in frequency after chatbots became available. Density stayed essentially flat in a narrow band, indicating the popular marker is not a reliable population-level detector in this corpus.

entry.title: TRACE: Learned Proprioceptive Odometry for Legged Robots under Unreliable Contact Conditions

author.name: Taehyeon Kong, Woojin Kim, Jemin Hwangbo

entry.summary: Presents a learned proprioceptive odometry estimator for legged robots that predicts displacement, rotation, and body velocity from recent IMU and joint history, using cross-attention that adaptively weights per-foot kinematic tokens instead of hand-tuned contact or slip thresholds. Physics-inspired auxiliary losses encourage kinematic consistency under slippage.

entry.title: Does FLAIR super-resolution erase or hallucinate small white-matter lesions?

author.name: Zahra Khodakarami, Yue Li, Pulkit Khandelwal, John Detre, Sandhitsu Das, Christopher Brown, David Wolk, Paul Yushkevich

entry.summary: Tests whether applying super-resolution to thick-slice clinical FLAIR brain scans before lesion segmentation erases small real white matter lesions or invents absent ones, using 29 high-resolution ADNI scans with expert lesion labels degraded to simulated 3 and 5 mm slices. The design gives a controlled answer to a safety-relevant question about generative preprocessing in clinical pipelines.

entry.title: Resourced Authority A Mechanism-Design Model for Participatory Governance of Deployed AI Agents

author.name: Praphul Chandra, Sujit Gujar, Ganesh Ghalme

entry.summary: Gives a formal mechanism design model for participatory governance of deployed AI agents in which stakeholders allocate a governance currency that determines the agent's compute budget, making authorization self-enforcing. Each governance period is modeled as an extensive-form game with sequential stakeholder contributions and a funding aggregator.

entry.title: Consistency Has a Computable Blind Spot: A Commutation Theory of Label-Free Reliability for Vision-Language Figure Reading

author.name: Rasul Khanbayov, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: Formalizes a blind spot in invariance-based label-free reliability: an error is invisible to a perturbation exactly when the two operations commute, so the unreachable errors of a test suite form a computable centralizer set that shrinks as edits are added. The authors instead advocate equivariance checks where editing the underlying data changes the correct answer by a predictable amount, proving completeness for affine reading errors.

entry.title: CohortHijack: Robustness of Single Cell Annotation to Companion Cell Removal

author.name: Arash Vashagh, Yasmin Vashagh

entry.summary: CohortHijack audits whether single-cell annotation pipelines that refine labels using neighboring cells can be manipulated by deleting other cells from the query batch while leaving the target cell untouched. Search-based removal flipped roughly a fifth to a quarter of target predictions on standard datasets, exposing a batch-composition vulnerability.

entry.title: LLM Inference Under Bursty Workload Distribution: Modifying the WAIT Algorithm

author.name: Anjali Gangadhar Katageria, Shobha Rani, Raghu Nandan Sengupta

entry.summary: This paper extends the WAIT scheduling algorithm for LLM inference to handle bursty, time-varying request arrivals by estimating request intensity online from observed interarrival times. Evaluation uses Markov-modulated Poisson synthetic workloads that better match real traffic than constant-rate Poisson assumptions.

entry.title: Velocity- and Regime-Aware Detection of Intraday Options Market Manipulation, with Explainable Attribution

author.name: Alex Chen, Maria Hybinette

entry.summary: The paper detects intraday options market manipulation by looking at the velocity of market state, such as option-delta velocity, rather than levels, capturing a pump-and-crash dynamic signature. Alerts are explained with SHAP attribution and evaluated on a strictly out-of-sample time-partitioned test period.

entry.title: Behavioral Residualization for Unsupervised Intrusion Detection in Automotive CAN Networks

author.name: Chandan Hegde, Mukundh R Reddy

entry.summary: The paper argues that CAN bus intrusion detectors relying on presence-based cues such as novel arbitration IDs fail when attackers reuse legitimate IDs, and proposes per-ID behavioral residualization extracting fourteen temporal and protocol features. The unsupervised approach targets more realistic stealthy automotive attacks.

entry.title: OmniMech: All-in-one Multimodal Mechanical Benchmark for 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Taiting Lu, Runze Liu, Ziwei Dong, Sisong Bei, Jingying Zeng, Mingjia Wang, Zhenghao Li, Kaiyuan Lin, Yi-Shan Wu, Yangshoudu Zheng, Hongxing Pan, Kai Zhang, Guoliang Shi, Ling Ma, Yifan Yang, Jiaying Lu, Qi He, Sung-Liang Chen, Yi-Chao Chen, Yincheng Jin, Mahanth Gowda

entry.summary: Releases a million-scale multimodal benchmark of over 251,000 fully dimensioned and toleranced industrial engineering drawings paired with native CAD models, multi-view renderings, meshes, STEP and B-rep representations, and semantic annotations. Defines four tasks including parametric CAD program synthesis from drawings, targeting millimeter-level industrial tolerances that general 3D benchmarks ignore.

entry.title: Flow-Map Distillation on Relation Manifolds for Image Restoration

author.name: Zihao He, Songhua Liu

entry.summary: FoRM treats knowledge distillation for image restoration as learning a flow map on a relation manifold, predicting relation states at arbitrary target times rather than matching static teacher relation matrices. This gives trajectory-level rather than endpoint-level supervision during transfer. The claim is richer and more stable knowledge transfer between teacher and student restoration networks.

entry.title: STAIL: Semantic Text-Anchored Incremental Learning for Medical Imaging via Large Language Models

author.name: Songpan Gao, Yajie Zhang, Guanxing Chen, Jiayu Qian, Zhenzhen Liu, Shijun Li, Xiaowei Zhu, Yao Hu, Kay Chen Tan, Yu-An Huang, Shiqi Wang, Zhi-An Huang

entry.summary: STAIL mitigates catastrophic forgetting in sequential medical imaging tasks by replaying compact text-based semantic anchors generated with language models instead of storing raw historical images. This reduces storage cost and avoids the privacy issues of pixel-level rehearsal buffers. It targets clinical deployments where models must continually adapt to new tasks.

entry.title: BendTwin: Robust Dense-to-Sparse Physical Reconstruction with Bending-Aware Differentiable Spring-Mass Models

author.name: Yixiong Jing, Qi Wang, Lin Chen, Junwei Jiang, Guangming Wang, Haibing Wu, Olaf Wysocki, Wanli Ma, Brian Sheil

entry.summary: BendTwin adds bending stiffness to differentiable spring-mass reconstruction of deformable objects from video, arguing that axial-spring-only formulations are mechanically under-constrained when the physical graph is coarsened. The result is more stable local deformation and better future-state prediction from sparse observations. Applications include robotic planning and physically consistent digital twins.

entry.title: EmoWorld: A Decoupled Affective Field for Controllable Emotional Video Generation

author.name: Bingyuan Wang, Baistan Zhyldyzbekov, Kunyu Feng, Zeyu Wang

entry.summary: EmoWorld disentangles emotional atmosphere, affect-bearing semantic cues, and temporal emotional progression in video generation by steering a frozen flow-matching video diffusion transformer along extracted affect directions. A one-time preparation stage builds layer-specific directions and a reusable cue library from neutral versus emotion-edited panoramas. Each factor can then be scaled independently at inference.

entry.title: Near-sensor Computing for Rapid Visuotactile Perception

author.name: Zhengying Zhu, Ruilin Zhang, Runze Hu, Chenxi Xiao

entry.summary: This work implements the depth reconstruction for visuotactile sensors as a fully streaming near-sensor hardware pipeline with a spectral Poisson solver, eliminating host transfer delays and scheduling jitter. The core logic draws an estimated 347 mW and yields deterministic latency, emitting the first depth value tens of thousands of cycles into each frame. Faster, predictable tactile perception directly bounds robot reaction speed.

entry.title: Project2Task: Graph-Guided Project-Level Planning for Autonomous Research

author.name: Huirui Xu, Runtao Xu, Shuo Ren, Jiajun Zhang

entry.summary: Project2Task adds a project-level planning layer above single-task research agents, representing candidate contributions as innovation atoms in a dependency graph so a research agenda is decomposed into bounded, ordered, non-overlapping tasks. It targets the gap between one-shot research agents and genuinely long-horizon research programs.

entry.title: OrchestraBench: Evaluating Multi-Agent Orchestration Failure Modes, Recovery, and Decomposition Quality

author.name: Yidian Chen, Yingzi Gu, Natan Vidra, Spurthi Setty, Sharon Zheng

entry.summary: OrchestraBench evaluates multi-agent orchestration through seed-reproducible failure injection over templated enterprise workflows, introducing cascade radius and per-failure-mode recovery as metrics rather than only end-task accuracy. A headline diagnostic shows a keyword-flag router scoring zero on adversarial cases with misleading surface signals while an intent-reasoning router scored perfectly.

entry.title: Agentic self-driving microscopy benchmarks support qualification but do not necessarily generalize to unseen tasks

author.name: Nathan S Johnson, Ian Abshire

entry.summary: Examines whether benchmarks used to qualify LLM-agent controllers for self-driving microscopes predict generalization to unseen tasks, across design choices such as LLM selection, agent count, delegation rules, and retrieval configuration. The finding is that benchmark performance supports qualification for known tasks but does not necessarily transfer to novel ones.

entry.title: Innovation-Residual Auditing of Autonomous Analysis Agents: Localization, Detection Limits, Error Control, and Identifiability

author.name: Ahmed Hassoon, Mark Dredze

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical analysis of innovation-residual auditing, an unsupervised method that flags erroneous operations in autonomous data-analysis agents by learning from known-sound analyses. It shows the choice of scoring rule determines whether errors can be localized at all, since scoring each operation against only its immediate predecessor makes inherited errors indistinguishable from originating ones.

entry.title: SkillTV-Bench: Benchmarking How Well Judges Perform on Skill-Augmented Agentic Execution

author.name: Zhi Han, Chenxi Zeng, Liuhaichen Yang, Zihan Guo, Ming Zhou, Yang Li

entry.summary: SkillTV-Bench is a 681-case benchmark of real agent trajectories across 50 tasks and eleven domains for evaluating whether LLM judges can verify skill-augmented agent executions, including inspectable artifacts and environments rather than only final responses or static traces. The premise is that procedural knowledge in task-time skills determines what evidence a verifier should inspect.

entry.title: Poli-Bias: Understanding and Measuring Large Language Model Biases in International Political Conflicts

author.name: Massi-Nissa Abboud, Aladin Djuhera, Elena Cabrio, Holger Boche

entry.summary: Poli-Bias is a counterfactual audit that swaps country identities in legally equivalent international-conflict scenarios and decomposes response differences along five interpretable dimensions such as framing, argumentation, and legal reasoning. It shows geopolitical asymmetries that single-score bias metrics would miss.

entry.title: iARCS: Iterative Agentic RL for Controllable 3D Scene Generation

author.name: Saugat Adhikari, Ashok Prasad Neupane, Pramish Paudel, Ajad Chhatkuli, Danda Pani Paudel

entry.summary: iARCS adapts a pretrained 3D scene generator with two-stage agentic RL: universal-reward pretraining for physical plausibility, then task-specific tuning against LLM-authored reward programs that are iteratively refined. The aim is synthetic scenes that satisfy functional constraints like traversability and spatial rules, not just visual realism.

entry.title: Failing Gracefully: Mitigating Impact of Inevitable Robot Failures

author.name: Duc M. Nguyen, Saad A. Ghani, Andrew Marshall, Allison Andreyev, Gregory J. Stein, Xuesu Xiao

entry.summary: This paper formulates household robot safety in terms of the joint probability and severity of impactful interactions with people, pets, and objects when failures such as crashes or hardware degradation occur. Quantifying failure consequences lets planners trade task efficiency against expected harm instead of assuming failures away.

entry.title: Perturbation Sensitivity at Convergence: A Simple Signal for Identifying Spuriously Correlated Samples

author.name: Nilesh Kumar

entry.summary: The paper shows that spuriously correlated samples can be identified after training converges, without group labels or the fragile choice of an early-training intervention epoch, by measuring sensitivity to input perturbations. Samples fit by the shared spurious rule behave differently from those fit through input-specific configurations.

entry.title: EvReflection: Event-Driven Micro-Dynamics for Reflection Removal

author.name: Jiaxiao Wang, Dachun Kai, Huyue Zhu, Quanquan Hu, Zhenyang Xu, Xiaoyan Sun

entry.summary: EvReflection uses event camera data to separate reflection from transmission layers by exploiting their differential micro-motion, which static single-image priors cannot disambiguate. A micro-dynamics decoupler extracts layer-specific motion cues that then guide a parallax-attention rectifier. It reduces the residual artifacts that plague conventional reflection removal.

entry.title: KILVO: Kinematic-Inertial-LiDAR-Visual Odometry with Robust Multimodal Adaptation for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Jixin Gao, Fucheng Liu, Teng Zhang, Fusheng Zha

entry.summary: KILVO is a tightly coupled odometry system for humanoid robots fusing joint encoders, IMU, LiDAR, and camera in an asynchronous-sequential error-state iterated Kalman filter, with high-rate leg kinematics providing proprioceptive constraints and exteroception updating sequentially. It is tailored to the sensor suites and gait-induced disturbances specific to humanoids. The design aims for robustness in real-world complexity.

entry.title: Epistemic Trustworthiness in Generative AI: A Normative Framework for Warranted Reliance in High-Stakes Workflows

author.name: Nimisha Karnatak, Max Van Kleek, Nigel Shadbolt

entry.summary: Argues that existing responsible-AI criteria such as accuracy, fairness, explainability, and user trust do not directly specify when reliance on generative AI output is epistemically warranted, and proposes warranted reliance as a distinct evaluative target for high-stakes professional workflows. The contribution is a normative framework rather than an empirical study.

entry.title: Cautious Context Steering for Language Model Personalization

author.name: Gihoon Kim, Jeyoung Lee, Suhan Woo, Sekwon Oh, Minsu Jeon, Hyounsoo Han, Euntai Kim

entry.summary: Proposes cautious context steering for personalization, noting that in-context learning and existing context-steering methods apply user-context influence uniformly across decoding steps rather than adapting it token by token. The approach avoids per-user adapters and reward models, which suffer from sparse data and poor generalization to unseen users.

entry.title: Training a Conditioned Video Game Agent on a VLM Annotated Dataset

author.name: Katrin Schmid, Iuri Frosio

entry.summary: Companion work showing that a video game dataset annotated by vision-language models with human-defined reward concepts can be used to train a conditioned agent via offline reinforcement learning that responds to desired behavior specifications. This bypasses the need for engine access and manual reward weighting.

entry.title: HoloCount: A Holistic Visual Counting Benchmark for MLLMs

author.name: Jinhong Deng, Limeng Qiao, Guanglu Wan

entry.summary: HoloCount is a hierarchical visual counting benchmark for multimodal LLMs that goes beyond simple perception to test counting under logical constraints and adversarial conditions. It is motivated by persistent numerical hallucination even in otherwise strong scene-understanding models.

entry.title: PRISM: Priority-aware Rubric Internalization via Structured Multimodal Data Synthesis

author.name: Xiaomin He, Dongling Xiao, Jiahao Xie, Ruiqi Lu, Qianle Wang, Zhongbin Guo, Wanxuan Sun

entry.summary: PRISM synthesizes multimodal training data where the model must act as an executor of typed, prioritized rubrics, verifying each rule against an image before issuing an overall judgment, and pairs this with an evaluation suite. It addresses the gap between real instructions that bundle unequally important requirements and training data that reduces instructions to single self-contained questions.

entry.title: ABC: Numerical Data Collection under Local Differential Privacy without Prior Knowledge

author.name: Incheol Baek, Hyungbin Kim, Yon Dohn Chung

entry.summary: Addresses a practical gap in local differential privacy for numeric data: existing mechanisms need a predefined value range, and choosing it badly causes either clipping loss or excessive noise. The proposed adaptive framework has users help estimate the domain dynamically while retaining privacy guarantees.

entry.title: Multivariate Time Series Forecasting needs Cross Variable Loss

author.name: Kuiye Ding, Yifan Hu, Hanchen Wang, Hao Xue

entry.summary: Argues that standard direct multi-step forecasting objectives are point-wise and therefore ignore dependencies among future values across variables, creating a mismatch with real co-evolving systems. The paper proposes a plug-in structural loss that constrains cross-variable relationships in the forecast horizon.

entry.title: Domain-Grounded Candidate Selection for Agentic Image Editing: A Shadow Removal Case

author.name: Shilin Hu, Jingyi Xu, Dimitris Samaras, Hieu Le

entry.summary: Tests whether commercial vision-language generative editors can replace physics-informed low-level vision using shadow removal as a case study, finding that they often produce clean results but sometimes hallucinate objects or misread shadows as material. The proposed remedy is a domain-grounded candidate selection stage that picks physically plausible edits from multiple generations.

entry.title: PRISM: Distribution-Gated Flow Matching for Controllable Unpaired Image Translation

author.name: Elad Yoshai, Natan T. Shaked

entry.summary: Introduces a GAN-free flow matching method for unpaired image translation that replaces a single global preservation strength with a learned per-feature gate, derived from how far each source feature sits from the target feature distribution. The same gate controls both initialization and the translation trajectory so content can be kept while appearance changes.

entry.title: When Do Corrective Features Help? An Agent for Corrective Feature Discovery on Black-Box Forecasters

author.name: Fangxin Wang, Ziyi Zhang, Diyi Zhuang, Langzhou He, Shiyu Wang, Baichuan Mo, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: Studies corrective feature discovery, which mines interpretable features of a frozen forecaster's residual errors to drive a lightweight post-hoc corrector, explicitly modeling the model-failure process instead of the data-generating process. The agent combines compositional search over input channels with an LLM that proposes named features, flags, and short executable transforms.

entry.title: Decoupling Perception from Description: Computation-Grounded Representation Alignment between Multivariate Time Series and Language

author.name: Xinran Feng, Yi Xie, Chao Zhang, Ruikun Li, Wanyun Ling, Ziyue Li, Chenxi Liu

entry.summary: Points out a self-supervision trap in time-series-to-language alignment: if an LLM writes the descriptions used as training labels, label quality is bounded by the very perceptual skill being taught, and this is worst for multivariate patterns like lead-lag and cross-channel correlation. The proposal decouples perception from description by grounding labels in explicit computation rather than LLM reading.

entry.title: IFlowNets: Extending Generative Samplers to Learn Strategies in Incomplete Information Games

author.name: Conor M. Artman, Nicholas Di, Scott Perkins

entry.summary: Extends generative flow network methods to imperfect-information games, proving that constraints established for the complete-information adversarial variant do not yield valid strategy densities or a valid training objective in the incomplete-information case. The proposed generalization fixes this and offers an alternative to blending reinforcement learning with counterfactual regret minimization.

entry.title: BioKD: Selective Physiology-to-Video Knowledge Distillation via Reliability Gate for Emotion Recognition

author.name: Bojing Hou, Ruohao Li, Yitong Zhu, Hongjun Liu, Luwen Yu, Yuyang Wang

entry.summary: BioKD distills physiological signal knowledge into a video-only emotion recognition student, using physiological data as privileged information at training time only. A sample-wise reliability gate suppresses noisy teacher supervision arising from subject variability and signal artifacts.

entry.title: An Inertial Block Proximal Linearized Method with Adaptive Momentum for Nonconvex and Nonsmooth Optimization

author.name: Weifeng Yang

entry.summary: The paper proposes an inertial block proximal linearized method with a two-phase adaptive momentum strategy and two independently parameterized extrapolation points for multiblock nonconvex nonsmooth optimization. Convergence guarantees are provided alongside applications including machine learning problems.

entry.title: Evidence Lock Before Commitment: A Frozen Interface Degrades LLM-as-Judge Evaluation

author.name: Divyansh Singh

entry.summary: Tests whether forcing an LLM judge to freeze extracted criteria and evidence in one call and use only that record for a later verdict improves evaluation. Across 24,000 judgments on three preference datasets using existing models including Claude Sonnet 4.5 and GPT-5, evidence locking actually lowered agreement with human preferences by several points.

entry.title: Different Perturbations, Different Mechanisms: Understanding Continued Pre-training for Zero-Shot Dialect Robustness

author.name: Aarohi Srivastava, David Chiang

entry.summary: Systematically compares six perturbation-based continued pre-training conditions across nine German, Italian, and Arabic dialect tasks, finding character-level noising most reliably improves zero-shot dialect robustness while preserving standard-variety performance. Goes further by showing that methods with similar downstream scores work through different internal mechanisms.

entry.title: Routing Is Least Learnable Where It Is Most Valuable: Bounds on Representation Routing for Web Agents

author.name: Jiaming Wei, Zekun Wu, Adriano Koshiyama, Maria Perez-Ortiz

entry.summary: Measures six browser observation modes (text, pixels, hybrids) across eight site-model combinations on two web-agent benchmarks and asks what per-task routing would gain. Finds modes are complementary but that oracle routing gains are largely inflated by run-to-run noise of 12 to 14 percent, leaving mainly a cost bound as a real benefit.

entry.title: DynaPix: Can Vision-Language Models Identify the Exact Future?

author.name: Thong Nguyen, Vinh-Hien Do, Quynh Vo, Cong-Duy Nguyen, See-Kiong Ng

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark that requires models to identify the actual future frame from visually similar candidates or a large gallery after a video clip stops before a key event, using a physics simulator so ground truth timing is exact. Finds models do reasonably when a visible event marks the target but fall to near chance when only elapsed time distinguishes options.

entry.title: Confidence matters: Leveraging Multi-view Geometric Priors for GS-based Reconstruction

author.name: Hongyu Zhou, Zorah L\"ahner

entry.summary: This study evaluates how injecting predicted depth and normal priors into 3D Gaussian Splatting affects geometric reconstruction quality, and finds that multi-view geometric predictions such as those from VGGT outperform single-view priors. Photometric optimization alone yields poor geometry, especially for specular objects. It offers empirical guidance on prior selection and confidence weighting for splatting pipelines.

entry.title: Support Operation Factorization: Compositional Readout of Frozen Vision Encoders under Controlled Interventions

author.name: Zhongyao Wang, Wanli Ouyang, Taoyong Cui, Pheng Ann Heng

entry.summary: This paper introduces a controlled protocol and readout, SO-OPF, for testing whether frozen vision encoders compose support and operation factors, and identifies a scoring failure it calls operation laundering where multiple operations reuse the same predicted slot. It uses a leave-one-cell-out design over support-by-operation grids with frozen DINOv3 features. The framing separates composing held-out bindings from recovering the grid structure itself.

entry.title: A Survey of Adversarial Efficiency Degradation for Vision Transformer by Exploiting Input-adaptive Optimization

author.name: Anadi Goyal, Nandish Chattopadhyay, Anupam Chattopadhyay, Chandan Karfa

entry.summary: A survey of adversarial attacks that target the input-adaptive efficiency mechanisms of vision transformers, such as token pruning and early exiting, forcing maximum computation without necessarily hurting accuracy. It unifies SlowFormer and DeSparsify across three pruning frameworks under standardized GFLOPs, accuracy loss, and attack success metrics. This is a denial-of-service style threat model that accuracy-focused robustness work misses.

entry.title: PathCover: A Fast Convex Decomposition along a Path via Randomized Iterative Space Partitioning (RISP) on Point Clouds

author.name: Kunal S. Narkhede, Abhijeet M. Kulkarni, Guoquan Huang, Ioannis Poulakakis

entry.summary: PathCover generates sequences of overlapping convex obstacle-free polytopes directly from raw point clouds using a randomized iterative space partitioning algorithm with expected linear-time construction under a mild condition. These safe corridors constrain downstream model predictive control and trajectory optimization. The paper provides finite-termination and progress guarantees along a reference path.

entry.title: TriQua: Reconciling Granularity and Context in Factuality Evaluation

author.name: Jin Liu, Steffen Thoma, Achim Rettinger

entry.summary: TriQua reconciles the granularity-versus-context tension in decompose-then-verify factuality evaluation by extracting simple claims as triples and complex claims as hyperrelational facts with contextual qualifiers. Verification annotates concrete errors within specific claim components rather than issuing a binary judgment.

entry.title: LUNAR: Benchmarking Personalized Large Language Models on UNiversal User BehAvioR Logs

author.name: Jiahao Zhang, Yongzhi Tong, Zelin Fu, Pengde Zhao, Yanmei Jiang, Jiang Feng, Min Yang

entry.summary: LUNAR is a benchmark for evaluating whether LLMs can personalize responses from longitudinal app interaction logs spanning everyday domains such as clothing, food, housing, and mobility. It uses a coarse-to-fine synthesis pipeline grounded in real behavioral patterns to sidestep privacy and sparsity constraints, with fidelity analyses comparing synthetic to real distributions.

entry.title: DoctorAgents: an agentic framework to iteratively refine AutoML pipeline for small clinical temporal data

author.name: Ruilin Wang, Bo-Hong Wang, Elizabeth Kourbatski, Jun Bai, Hegang Chen, Ziyang Song, Gilles Boire, Marie Hudson, Yue Li

entry.summary: DoctorAgents reframes AutoML for small, heterogeneous, temporally complex clinical datasets from brute-force search to reasoning-driven iterative refinement, using specialized LLM agents with explicit memory to construct and optimize end-to-end pipelines. The target setting is scarce clinical data where conventional AutoML search is inefficient.

entry.title: Post-Hoc Trajectory-Risk Certification for Modular LLM-Based Security Agents

author.name: Zhenpeng Li

entry.summary: The paper extends split conformal prediction to give trajectory-level risk guarantees across multi-stage LLM security pipelines, showing that per-stage coverage does not compose and that a natural pairwise-correlation extension to three or more stages is invalid because it yields a lower rather than upper bound. A valid spanning-tree allocation is derived as the alternative.

entry.title: SafeDivertor: Faithful Divertor Heat Flux Reconstruction from Macroscopic Plasma State Signals via Time-Frequency Prior Exploitation

author.name: Hao Si, Zehua Chen, Qingquan Yang, Xiao Wang, Dengdi Sun, Wanli Lyu, Gaoting Chen, Guosheng Xu, Hang Su, Jin Tang, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: SafeDivertor reconstructs time-resolved radial divertor heat-flux profiles directly from macroscopic plasma-state signals available during a fusion discharge, avoiding conventional post-discharge infrared inversion that needs device-specific material and geometry modeling. The authors build a multi-source dataset and exploit time-frequency priors to make reconstruction feasible online.

entry.title: Coordinated Multi-Robot Disassembly for Makespan Optimization of Large-Scale Assemblies

author.name: Niklas Hargus, Andreas Orthey, Marc Toussaint

entry.summary: CoMuDi is a task-and-motion planning method that schedules a team of robots to disassemble large assemblies while minimizing makespan, using a dependency graph, compound pick or place or exit tasks, temporal constraint propagation, and a space-time RRT* motion planner. It targets tight shared workspaces where robots must avoid each other. Useful for automated recycling and remanufacturing lines.

entry.title: FlowAdam: Implicit Regularization via Geometry-Aware Soft Momentum Injection

author.name: Devender Singh, Tarun Sheel

entry.summary: IcFuzz is presented as the first fuzzing framework aimed at NVIDIA Isaac Sim, using semantic understanding of scene stages and multi-level mutation to explore the simulator state space and surface bugs. Since embodied AI research depends heavily on simulator fidelity, silent simulator bugs can corrupt training and evaluation results. The work brings software-testing methodology into the embodied AI toolchain.

entry.title: Personalized Deep Research Query Refinement with Graph-Scaffolded Evidence Grounding

author.name: Soojin Yoon, Dongha Lee

entry.summary: Refines a user request into a personalized deep-research specification before handing it to an unchanged research agent, resolving which framing factors matter, whether available context supports them, and whether to retrieve memory, ask the user, or proceed. Evidence grounding is scaffolded by a graph over user context.

entry.title: VLMs for Videogame Data Annotation

author.name: Katrin Schmid, Iuri Frosio

entry.summary: Investigates using vision-language models to annotate video game frame sequences with reward signals for downstream uses such as conditioned training and offline RL, finding that VLMs often fail on basic questions about racing and other game footage. The paper discusses mitigations including output mixing and prompting strategies.

entry.title: Temporal Bridges for Spatial Resolution: Enhancing Climate Data Super-Resolution with Bidirectional Alignment

author.name: Yichen Zhang, Yixiong Xiao, Congxi Xiao, Jingbo Zhou

entry.summary: Improves climate data super-resolution by exploiting temporal correlations between frames through bidirectional alignment, rather than relying on single-frame spatial information as most deep learning approaches do. It also addresses the inherently stochastic nature of climate fields.

entry.title: TS-RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Yixiong Xiao, Congxi Xiao, Jingbo Zhou

entry.summary: TS-RAG brings retrieval augmentation to time-series forecasting by retrieving similar historical sequences as references, arguing that naive prompt-style concatenation fails for small non-generative forecasting models. It proposes an integration mechanism suited to the constrained capacity of time-series backbones.

entry.title: Mean-Field Dynamics of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Hao Ai

entry.summary: This theory paper models chain-of-thought reasoning as guided discovery on a clue graph and derives a one-dimensional differential equation for the fraction of clues discovered using a mean-field approximation. Clue tokens are identified empirically via normalized surprisal of a student model on a stronger model's outputs.

entry.title: F$^2$Agent: Financial Fusion of Agentic Intelligence for Multimodal Trading

author.name: Changshuo Liu, Yanzheng Jin, Shangfeng Cai, Peng Fang, Xiaokui Xiao, Beng Chin Ooi

entry.summary: F2Agent is a hierarchical multimodal trading framework where specialized agents extract modality-specific signals that are then fused to capture cross-modal dependencies and resist market noise. It targets three claimed weaknesses of existing LLM trading agents: shallow multimodal modeling, weak fusion, and poor robustness.

entry.title: UniVVT: A Unified End-to-End Framework for High-Fidelity Video Virtual Try-on

author.name: Yushe Cao, Shikun Feng, Fei Shen, Haikuo Peng, Jianqiang Xia, Yiheng Zhu, Dianxi Shi, Chun Yu

entry.summary: Replaces the usual multi-stage video try-on pipeline of parsing, pose estimation, and garment warping with a single end-to-end generative model conditioned semantically through a multimodal LLM perceiver. This removes brittle geometric priors whose errors otherwise propagate into the output video.

entry.title: A Two-Tier Perspective on Inference-Time Parallelism in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Zihan Xu, Haolin Tian, Hai Jiang

entry.summary: Formalizes inference-time parallelism in multi-agent LLM systems as two distinct decision levels: running multiple full solution paths versus decomposing one path into concurrent subtasks. It studies how each form trades off accuracy, latency, and compute cost.

entry.title: Evidential Rule Learning for Interpretable Classification with Abstention

author.name: Javier Fumanal-Idocin, Javier Andreu-Perez

entry.summary: Introduces a fuzzy rule learning method whose outputs carry evidential belief and plausibility measures, enabling the model to abstain when evidence is insufficient without post-hoc calibration or extra inference passes. The authors also prove a Lipschitz stability property for the evidential outputs.

entry.title: BALANCE: Hybrid Autoregressive-Speculative LLM Inference in Wireless Edge Networks

author.name: Guanqiao Qu, Shuo Chen, Qian Chen, Kin K. Leung, Xianhao Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a serving framework that mixes autoregressive and speculative decoding across users at wireless network edge nodes, since speculative decoding cuts latency but costs extra memory for the draft model. The scheduler allocates modes to heterogeneous user demands under tight edge resource constraints.

entry.title: Is Self-Pretraining really useful to improve diagnosis in medical Time Series?

author.name: Omar Coser, Antonio Orvieto, Paolo Soda, Loredana Zollo

entry.summary: Asks whether self-pretraining, which helps transformers on long-context benchmarks, also helps on medical time series ranging from univariate to multimodal signals. Across rehabilitation robotics, stress detection, and Parkinson gait tasks the authors compare training from scratch against four masking objectives under limited data.

entry.title: Tytan: Interactive Neurosymbolic Construction of Analytic Semantic Schemas from Relational Data

author.name: Donna Hooshmand, Shubham Shahi, Cameron Barrie, Abhratanu Dutta, Marko Sterbentz, Harper Pack, Kristian J. Hammond

entry.summary: Presents a neurosymbolic system that automatically builds an analytic semantic layer over a relational database, identifying real-world entities, distinguishing measures from identifiers, and inferring how tables join into units of analysis. It combines symbolic schema analysis with LLM semantic inference and interactive user correction.

entry.title: Hybrid Probabilistic Zonotopes for Identifiable and Refinable Predictive Uncertainty

author.name: Zhen Zhang, Amr Alanwar

entry.summary: Introduces a prediction head that separates three distinct uncertainty sources, namely discrete mode choice, bounded systematic drift, and irreducible noise, by representing them as binary, bounded, and stochastic generators of a zonotope with a closed-form likelihood. Sharing the bounded generator across horizon steps means observing one step algebraically sharpens predictions for all remaining steps.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Closed-Loop Control of Laser Powder Bed Fusion with an In-Loop Ontology

author.name: Gisuk Hong, Jaebong Cho, Hyunbo Cho

entry.summary: A neuro-symbolic control loop for laser powder bed fusion places a standards-aligned ontology and a description-logic reasoner inside the controller, translating unmeasurable quality objectives such as melt-pool depth into observable bounds on melt-pool width. The result is a geometry-conditioned constraint-aware predictive controller for additive manufacturing defect avoidance.

entry.title: Hybrid-Adaptive Thread Tuning to Mitigate Simulation Execution Bottlenecks in High-Performance Reinforcement Learning Inference

author.name: Jiming Su, Hantao Hua, Lujia Yin, Yiping Yao, Feng Zhu

entry.summary: AutoThread adaptively tunes simulator thread counts during reinforcement learning inference, identifying the ratio of task execution time to scheduling time as the key predictor of the optimal configuration and using a physics-informed neural operator to set it online. The goal is to relieve simulator-side bottlenecks in simulation-in-the-loop decision systems.

entry.title: Equation-Free Period-Aware Forecast-Error Contraction for Estimating Negative Largest Lyapunov Exponents from Short Trajectory Ensembles

author.name: Andrei Velichko, N'Gbo N'Gbo, Viet-Thanh Pham

entry.summary: The authors estimate negative largest Lyapunov exponents from short scalar trajectory ensembles without governing equations or Jacobians, by training a nearest-neighbor predictor and reading the exponent off the slope of phase-consistent forecast-error contraction. This targets stable dynamics where contraction is hard to measure before noise dominates.

entry.title: On Same-Sample and Independent-Sample Stochastic Extragradient for Monotone Variational Inequalities

author.name: TaeHo Yoon, Nicolas Loizou

entry.summary: Theoretical study of stochastic extragradient methods for monotone variational inequalities, comparing the same-sample and independent-sample variants and removing restrictive compactness or bounded-variance assumptions. Shows the same-sample variant is sensitive to per-sample Lipschitz constants and derives sharper convergence conditions. Relevant to min-max and adversarial training optimization theory.

entry.title: RIG-RoPE: Relation- and Instance-Gated Rotary Positional Encoding with Duration-Aware Temporal Coordinates

author.name: Donggen Li

entry.summary: Identifies two problems with multidimensional rotary positional encodings in interleaved multimodal LLM contexts: spatial rotations applied across tokens with ill-defined geometric displacement, and temporal coordinates treated as equal-step counters regardless of media duration. Proposes relation- and instance-gated rotations with duration-aware temporal coordinates.

entry.title: Grad-CAM for Vision Transformers: A Systematic Taxonomy and Audit of Methodological Ambiguity in Explainable AI

author.name: Casey Wall, Longwei Wang, Rodrigue Rizk, KC Santosh

entry.summary: Audits 175 papers, drawn from more than 550 screened, that apply Grad-CAM or related saliency methods to vision transformers, and builds a taxonomy of how the CNN-derived formulation is adapted to tokens, attention, and residual streams. Finds most papers fail to justify their adaptation choices, undermining comparability of explanations.

entry.title: MOSAIK: Multi-Patch Content-Aware Spatial Allocation of Image Tokens for Efficient Generation

author.name: Mohammadreza Hami, Mohammadreza Samadi, Chao Gao, Negar Hassanpour

entry.summary: Reduces the cost of pixel-space diffusion generation by varying patch size spatially and across denoising steps according to how much fidelity each region loses when coarsened, rather than applying one patch size uniformly. Adapts a pixel diffusion transformer backbone to handle heterogeneous token layouts.

entry.title: VideoArgus: Agentic Rubric-Grounded Unified Evaluation for Video Generation and Editing

author.name: Ziyun Zeng, Zixuan Wang, Yongsheng Yu, Hang Hua, Jiebo Luo

entry.summary: Presents an agentic evaluation framework for video generation and editing that first produces an output-blind, sample-specific rubric with criteria, scoring rules, failure modes, and evidence plans, then reuses it to score all candidate videos using VLM question answering and visual tools. Ships with a companion benchmark.

entry.title: G$^2$ARD-GS: Geometry-Guided Anchor-Regularized Gaussian Splatting Distillation

author.name: Puyuan Zhang, Jianming Huang, Wenkai Ye, Wei Dong

entry.summary: G2ARD-GS distills dense LiDAR-derived 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes into a compact, surface-aware set of anchor primitives while preserving novel-view quality and geometric fidelity. The method progressively consolidates a dense Gaussian prior into representatives and then relearns appearance on a fixed topology. It targets the practical storage, transmission, and rendering cost of city-scale splatting maps.

entry.title: ConceptADapt: Concept-guided Adaptive Feature Reconstruction with Dynamic Attention for Few-Shot Industrial Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yufei Li, Yicheng Ruan, Long Tian, Dongsheng Wang, Liang Bao

entry.summary: ConceptADapt tackles few-shot industrial anomaly detection by pre-learning a bank of normal concepts from a handful of defect-free samples and reconstructing features through dynamic attention over those concepts. The design aims to stabilize generalization when foundation-model features alone overfit tiny normal-sample sets. It targets the cold-start phase of industrial visual inspection.

entry.title: Multi-Year Geospatial Reasoning using Interannually-Consistent Historical Predictions as a Free Input Modality

author.name: Syed Roshaan Ali Shah, Kasper Bonte, David Bekaert, Kristof Van Tricht, Dieter Wens

entry.summary: This paper feeds an operational Earth-observation system's own archive of past annual predictions, plus partner-produced ancillary layers, back into the model as additional input modalities rather than using them only as post-processing rules. It is demonstrated on Copernicus high-resolution crop-type mapping. The idea exploits interannual consistency as essentially free supervision signal.

entry.title: Learning visual representations for compositional analysis of artworks and photographs

author.name: Fatemeh Behrad, Tinne Tuytelaars, Johan Wagemans

entry.summary: This paper compares two routes to representing visual composition in artworks and photographs: a human-inspired pipeline using object-centric decomposition plus a graph attention network over spatial relations, versus fine-tuned foundation models trained on new large compositional datasets. Composition is central to aesthetic meaning yet remains poorly formalized and prone to semantic bias in learned features. The comparison clarifies which paradigm captures spatial arrangement rather than content.

entry.title: UQ-Loc: Uncertainty-Aware LiDAR Scene Coordinate Regression

author.name: Jacek Komorowski

entry.summary: UQ-Loc adds an anisotropic Gaussian covariance head to LiDAR scene coordinate regression so each voxel prediction carries a full uncertainty estimate, trained with a negative log-likelihood loss and a spatial smoothness regularizer. Uncertainty is then used in the pose solver through weighted seed scoring and Mahalanobis inlier tests. This makes learned localization more robust and its outputs more usable downstream.

entry.title: Guiding Large Language Models with Genetic Programming-Evolved Heuristic Knowledge for Dynamic Multi-Mode Project Scheduling

author.name: Yuan Tian, Yi Mei, Mengjie Zhang

entry.summary: This work uses genetic programming to evolve scheduling priority rules and then supplies them as domain knowledge to guide large language model decisions for dynamic multi-mode project scheduling under uncertain durations. The motivation is that zero-shot LLM scheduling lacks domain grounding, burns tokens, and gives inconsistent answers across repeated queries. The hybrid keeps the LLM interpretable interface while grounding it in evolved heuristics.

entry.title: ATP: Anatomical Torque with Passivity-based Control Framework for Safe Upper-Limb Exoskeleton Assistance

author.name: Yu Chen, Gong Chen, Xiang Li

entry.summary: ATP trains a unified reinforcement learning muscle controller in a scalable musculoskeletal simulator to generate anatomically grounded reference torques for upper-limb exoskeleton assistance, wrapped in a passivity-based control framework for safety. Anatomical assistance has mostly been demonstrated on lower limbs, where periodic weight-bearing motion is more forgiving of torque error. Nonperiodic upper-limb movement demands higher precision.

entry.title: Adaptive Arena-based Contestable Argumentative Network-of-Experts for Open-Ended Care Plan Coordination

author.name: Truong Thanh Hung Nguyen, Hoang-Loc Cao, Phuc Ho, Phuc Truong Loc Nguyen, Ren\'e Richard, Hung Cao

entry.summary: CANOE is a neuro-symbolic multi-agent system for clinical care plan coordination that recruits role-specialized agents, has them generate supporting and attacking arguments in a quantitative bipolar argumentation framework, and supports human contestation before synthesizing a plan. It targets the opacity and safety limits of monolithic LLM pipelines in multidisciplinary care.

entry.title: Stochasticity Is Not the Hard Part: Reduction and Complexity in Instructional Sequencing over Prerequisite DAGs

author.name: Zonglin Han (Department of Computer Science, University of California, Davis), Yichen Chen (Department of Computer Science, University of California, Davis), Jiawen Jiang (International Digital Economy College, Minjiang University), Tongan Shi (School of Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence, Liaoning Normal University), Kristian A. Stevens (Department of Computer Science, University of California, Davis)

entry.summary: Analyzes instructional sequencing over prerequisite DAGs as a stochastic shortest-path problem, proving the stochasticity can be exactly eliminated by reduction to a deterministic shortest-path problem on the lattice of prerequisite order ideals. It then shows optimal sequencing remains NP-hard via reduction from feedback arc set in tournaments, so combinatorial rather than stochastic complexity is the barrier.

entry.title: ErgoSurf: Ergodic Control for the Coverage of Unknown Surfaces

author.name: Stefan Schneyer, Timo Bachmann, Maged Iskandar, Korbinian Nottensteiner, Alin Albu-Sch\"affer, Freek Stulp, Jo\~ao Silv\'erio

entry.summary: ErgoSurf brings ergodic control, which allocates coverage time in proportion to a desired spatial distribution, to surfaces whose geometry is unknown in advance, reconstructing the surface online through contact while covering it. This removes the usual requirement of a prior scan or CAD model for tasks like sanding, cleaning, and inspection. The authors are from DLR, a strong robot control group.

entry.title: Refining Over Resampling: Test-Time Self-Correction for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Ahsan Bilal, Muhammad Ahmed Mohsin, Muhammad Umer, Lena Trigg, Ali Subhan, Muhammad Ali, Dean F. Hougen

entry.summary: Proposes a verifier-free test-time scaling scheme that samples multiple reasoning rollouts for breadth, refines each through iterative self-critique and self-correction for depth, then majority-votes the refined answers. The motivation is that wider sampling alone yields diminishing returns because new rollouts repeat existing answer patterns, while verifier-based selection depends on reward-model calibration.

entry.title: RA-CAD: Learning Post-Execution Critique for State-Aware Text-to-CAD Generation

author.name: Shuhao Yan, Changhao He, Xi Peng, Peng Hu

entry.summary: RA-CAD is a state-aware ReAct-style agent for text-to-CAD that loops through generate, execute, critique, and rewrite, learning how to interpret post-execution feedback into corrective edits rather than relying on fixed or externally supplied critique. The target is parametric CAD code that is both editable and executable.

entry.title: ECG-LENS: Lead-Aware Clinical Context Enriched ECG Report Generation and Evaluation

author.name: Akanta Das, Tasinul Islam Ahon, Ahmed Mahir Sultan Rumi, Md Mahbubur Rahman, Tausif Amim Shadly, Tanzima Hashem

entry.summary: ECG-LENS generates clinical ECG reports with lead-aware modeling and clinical context enrichment, targeting the gap between classification-focused systems and reports usable in practice. It also proposes evaluation suited to dense diagnostic terminology and subtle temporal morphology.

entry.title: Mind the Gaps: Mixture-of-Minds for Human Simulation

author.name: Pranav Dahiya

entry.summary: Anacreon targets individual-level rather than population-average human simulation by learning an authorship embedding, clustering a qualitative corpus around seed individuals, and training a per-cluster adapter mixture on a Gemma 4 12B base (an existing open model). The goal is to preserve heterogeneity that standard LLM simulators flatten.

entry.title: DREAM: LLM-based Dynamic Role-playing via Event-Aware Memory Graph

author.name: Zhihao Xiao, Mengting Li, Xintao Wang, Linfeng Li, Limin Shui, Mengqi Ji, Borui Cai

entry.summary: DREAM converts literary text into an event-aware memory graph organized around an activating-event, belief, consequence cognitive schema so role-playing agents can reason causally and stay temporally consistent. It replaces static character descriptions and unstructured memory used by most role-play systems.

entry.title: Beyond Information Retrieval: Generative AI as an Epistemic Arbiter to Enhance Collaborative Problem-Solving

author.name: Jiaxin Zou, Xiaoming Zhai, Chunlei Gao

entry.summary: A six-week quasi-experiment with 201 fifth-grade students compares collaborative problem solving with and without generative AI, using chi-square and lag-sequential analysis of interaction behaviors. The AI-supported group showed more social engagement and conflict management but less task planning and solution reasoning, suggesting cognitive offloading.

entry.title: The ethics of artificial intelligence in the life sciences: Universality, cultural diversity and an architecture of care

author.name: Jean-Pierre Changeux, Gustavo Deco, Morten L. Kringelbach

entry.summary: Three prominent neuroscientists argue that ethical concerns about AI in life sciences are real but not categorically special, and should be grounded in how human brains are built and socialized. They contrast the brain's low-cost global workspace and wanting-liking-satiety reward cycle with machine reward maximization, and propose an architecture of care spanning universal ethics and cultural diversity.

entry.title: DistMedVL: Distributional Vision-Language Alignment for Uncertainty-Aware Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Jiaxuan Li, Qing Xu, Xiangjian He, Yue Li, Daokun Zhang, Fiseha B. Tesema, Rong Qu

entry.summary: Proposes a probabilistic adapter placed on top of frozen vision and language encoders so that medical image segmentation models represent both ambiguous-boundary noise and limited-data uncertainty rather than doing deterministic cross-modal matching. The aim is better robustness when the model is applied to shifted clinical domains.

entry.title: Task-Conditional Flow Matching for Balanced Multilingual Text Embedding Adaptation

author.name: Tirth Bhatt, Naren Kumar S, Mayank Singh

entry.summary: Adapts multilingual text embedding models by applying flow matching only to translation-style objectives while using task-appropriate objectives for retrieval and classification, combined with teacher-guided preservation and a staged curriculum. Reports state-of-the-art results on an Indic embedding benchmark.

entry.title: Audio-to-Score Transcription using Pre-trained Features, Data Augmentation, and the New SheetSage-A2S Dataset

author.name: Eoin Cummins, Zhongyi Huang, Alexandre D'Hooge, Zhuoro Mo, Yaolong Ju

entry.summary: Releases a 61-hour audio-to-score dataset for popular music with symbolic score encodings for over nine thousand clips, filling a gap left by classical-focused transcription research. Combining pretrained music audio features with augmentation lowers symbol error rate on a classical benchmark and extends transcription to pop.

entry.title: Depth-Guided Video Object Counting in Crowded Scenes

author.name: Yuanjing Xu, Xinyan Liu, Weidong Chen, Zixuan Zou, Linhao Zhang, Zhuangzhe Meng, Antoni B. Chan, Weigang Zhang

entry.summary: Improves prompt-based video object counting in dense scenes by fusing depth cues with RGB through cross-attention and explicitly predicting occlusion, plus a de-duplication stage that avoids counting the same instance across frames. A new dataset accompanies the method.

entry.title: Rectifying Geometric Misalignment: Online Source-Free Adaptation for Class-Imbalanced EEG

author.name: Shiwen Chu, Shanglin Li, Motoaki Kawanabe, Reinmar Kobler

entry.summary: Shows that Riemannian alignment techniques widely used for cross-subject EEG decoding implicitly assume balanced class priors, so dynamically varying label distributions in real online brain-computer interface use cause geometric misalignment. The proposed source-free online method adds manifold-constrained information maximization to correct for label shift.

entry.title: Scalable estimation of VARMA models

author.name: Daniel Paulin, Victor Elvira

entry.summary: Introduces an estimation framework for high-dimensional VARMA time-series models where per-iteration cost is independent of series length, combining a partial-autocorrelation reparametrization guaranteeing stationarity and invertibility with structured Gaussian priors. Makes previously impractical VARMA models tractable at scale.

entry.title: How to Recognize New Words: A Comparison Between Context Biasing Methods and Speech LLMs

author.name: Christian Huber, Alexander Waibel

entry.summary: Compares contextual biasing methods built on Whisper against three speech LLMs prompted with context lists for recognizing rare words, named entities, and acronyms. Finds biasing cuts biased-word error rates by up to 88 percent relative, while speech LLMs do well on read speech but generalize less well elsewhere.

entry.title: Decomposed Entailment for Factuality Checking and Hallucination Detection

author.name: Achir Oukelmoun, Nasredine Semmar, Ga\"el De Chalendar

entry.summary: Presents a lightweight reference-free hallucination detector that decomposes generated text into atomic claims and verifies each with a compact entailment model against multi-scale source chunks, aggregating with an asymmetric score where one confident contradiction dominates. Evaluated beyond summarization across source-grounded generation settings.

entry.title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer

author.name: Xinye Wang, Junxiao Liu, Shujian Huang

entry.summary: Improves cross-lingual reasoning transfer by concentrating on-policy self-distillation supervision around reasoning pivots, the tokens where the reasoning process advances or redirects, rather than distributing dense supervision uniformly. Aims to extend strong reasoning from high-resource to other languages.

entry.title: A Study of LLMs' Preferences for Libraries and Programming Languages

author.name: Lukas Twist, Mark Harman, Don Syme, Joost Noppen, Helen Yannakoudakis, Detlef Nauck, Jie M. Zhang

entry.summary: Empirical study of the design choices LLMs make when generating code, showing strong overuse of popular libraries such as NumPy in up to 45 percent of unnecessary cases and a pronounced default preference for Python even where it is a poor fit. Extends code evaluation beyond functional correctness to design bias.

entry.title: StyleComposer: Training-Free Multi-Reference Style Composition

author.name: Sanghyeok Lee, Jihye Kang, Namhyuk Ahn

entry.summary: Observes that painting style is not monolithic and finds no single diffusion representation isolates color, texture, and structure, so it routes each style attribute through the representation where it best separates and coordinates routes over denoising time. Enables training-free composition from three references with per-attribute strength sliders.

entry.title: A Paragraph is Worth a Thousand Captions: Rethinking Text Supervision for Vision-Language Retrieval

author.name: Mahyar Ghazanfari, Amin Tabrizian, Arsyi Aziz, Binshuai Wang, Peng Wei

entry.summary: Systematically isolates the effect of training text granularity on long-text image retrieval, from single captions to multi-sentence paragraphs, using a synthetic pipeline that produces diverse captions, hard negatives, and quality-scored paragraphs for 500K images. Tests whether granularity alone, rather than positional embedding extension, drives long-text retrieval gains.

entry.title: HERA: Historical Evidence Routing Adapter for Physical Prediction in Latent World Models

author.name: Yuanruyi, Yue Cao, Haojia Gao, Guanqiu Guo, Ziyuezhang, Shangqin, Junbo Tan, Bokui Chen, Zhuo Zou, Xueqian Wang

entry.summary: Proposes an adapter for latent video world models that selectively retrieves historical visual evidence when it becomes relevant to a later prediction, rather than merely enlarging temporal context or caching generic features. Targets physical events under occlusion where needed evidence has left the current view.

entry.title: TruthLens: Object Hallucination Detection via Self-Evaluating Truthfulness Scores in LVLMs

author.name: Yanqi Wu, Runhe Lai, Xinhua Lu, Qichao Chen, Zhiping Zhou, Jia-Xin Zhuang, Weijiang Yu, Ruixuan Wang

entry.summary: Finds that real and hallucinated object tokens are linearly separable in LVLM hidden states but that this separability is lost at the language modeling head, then repurposes a rarely used special token as a reference to expose a per-object truthfulness score. Requires no auxiliary model and adds no inference cost.

entry.title: Vorch-Streamer: Extending Human Audio-Visual Generation to Real-Time Long-Form Streaming

author.name: Menglin Han, Yang Ding, Yulei Lu, Haoran Yu, Xin Ma, Junyi Chen, Zhangkai Ni, Lin Ma, Yaohui Wang

entry.summary: Post-training framework that converts a pretrained bidirectional audio-visual human generation model into a causal streaming generator for real-time long-form text-to-audio-video avatars. Tackles exposure bias from autoregressively reusing generated blocks and the ambiguity of which part of an utterance to speak next given only local context.

entry.title: Patient Pose Assessment Using a CT-Based Framework for Synthetic Data Generation

author.name: Manuel Laufer, Dominik Mairh\"ofer, Malte Sieren, Hauke Gerdes, Fabio Leal dos Reis, Arpad Bischof, Thomas K\"aster, Erhardt Barth, J\"org Barkhausen, Thomas Martinetz

entry.summary: This work synthesizes depth-image and radiograph training pairs from CT scans to build an AI system that assesses patient positioning before an X-ray is taken, sidestepping the regulatory barriers to collecting real paired data. Pretraining on the synthetic data improves downstream pose assessment. Good positioning is a primary determinant of radiograph diagnostic quality.

entry.title: DyPES-VLA: Learning Shared Dynamics Priors and Embodiment-Specific Control for Cross-Embodiment Manipulation

author.name: Junfeng Li, Junjie He, Zhide Zhong, Yangyang Zheng, Pingyue Sheng, Jiayu Dong, Ruixin Li, Haodong Yan, Jiaguan Zhu, Tianran Zhang, Runze Yu, Wen Chen, Liuqing Yang, Yuxiang Gao, Haoang Li

entry.summary: VIDP learns variable impedance control from kinematic-only human demonstrations by combining a diffusion policy with a task-parameterized mixture model, disentangling deliberate compliance from mere geometric variation across differing spatial layouts. The output is a policy that modulates stiffness during contact-rich tasks. It addresses the problem that force information is usually absent from demonstration data.

entry.title: CASCADE: An Agentic Regulatory Network Framework for Patient-Data-Validated Downstream Perturbation Prediction

author.name: Jose A. Bird

entry.summary: CASCADE is an agentic framework exposed via MCP that predicts downstream transcriptional effects of gene perturbation from precomputed ARACNe regulatory networks. Instead of only checking whether predicted genes are known cancer genes, it validates the predicted direction of change against real TCGA tumor expression using copy-number amplification as a dosage proxy, reporting 72 to 90 percent concordance for MYC across three cancer types.

entry.title: ViSR-KGC: Visual Subgraph Reasoning with Vision-Language Models for Multimodal Knowledge Graph Completion

author.name: Jiafan Li, Mengxue Yang, Jiaqi Zhu, Liang Chang, Ying Li, Hongan Wang

entry.summary: ViSR-KGC performs multimodal knowledge graph completion by rendering subgraph topology visually so vision-language models can reason over structure and images together, avoiding the loss of topology that occurs when graphs are linearized into text prompts. It targets cases where relation-specific evidence is too sparse for embedding-based methods.

entry.title: Bias Analysis of L2 Speaking Assessment Systems Using Concept Activation Vectors

author.name: Arya Labroo, Mengjie Qian, Kate Knill

entry.summary: The authors extend Concept Activation Vector analysis from feature-based to neural automatic speaking-assessment systems, probing whether a BERT text grader and a speech-plus-text grader encode irrelevant speaker attributes such as first language or age. The goal is interpretable fairness auditing of high-stakes L2 test scoring.

entry.title: GAUGE: Granularity-Adaptive Counterfactual Gating of Evidence for Incomplete Multimodal Classification

author.name: Yunping Shi, En Yu, Kairui Guo, Jie Lu

entry.summary: GAUGE handles incomplete multimodal inputs by imputing missing modalities with a frozen imputer, encoding observed and recovered inputs as fine-grained evidence units, and gating them by estimated counterfactual effect rather than trusting or discarding whole modalities. This lets reliable parts of a recovered modality be kept while misleading parts are suppressed.

entry.title: LC-Implicit-QAOA: Active-Workspace-Capped Exact Objective-and-Gradient Evaluation for Training over Bounded QUBO Light Cones

author.name: Chih-Chung Hsu

entry.summary: LC-Implicit-QAOA performs exact QAOA objective and gradient evaluation within bounded QUBO causal light cones, avoiding materialization of the global state and cost table by profiling cone structure and jointly choosing microbatch sizes and checkpoint schedules under a workspace memory budget. Correctness is cross-checked against an independent dense adjoint implementation.

entry.title: Convergent Evolution in Neural Representation Space: Emergent Order in Deep Belief Networks

author.name: Patrick Krauss, Achim Schilling, Andreas Maier, Thomas Kinfe, Claus Metzner

entry.summary: This study measures whether unsupervised Deep Belief Networks spontaneously organize their internal layers according to unseen class structure, using discrimination-value metrics, post-hoc supervised probes, abstraction distance, and effective dimensionality on MNIST-family datasets. Class clustering generally strengthens with depth despite no labels being available during training. Control experiments tie the effect to specific learning conditions.

entry.title: PD-GS: Phoneme-Driven 3DGS for Audio-Driven Talking Heads

author.name: Ao Fu, Yi Zhou

entry.summary: Phoneme-Driven Gaussian Splatting supplies explicit frame-aligned phoneme targets to a 3D Gaussian Splatting talking-head pipeline, addressing the leaky-mouth artifact where regression on continuous audio embeddings averages away discrete articulatory events such as bilabial closures. The linguistic supervision is meant to enforce hard articulatory constraints.

entry.title: ChainClaw: A Layered Agent Framework for Reliable On-Chain Execution

author.name: Jiacheng Wei, Zhaoxin Fan, Xin Wen, Yuqin Lan, Dongrun Li, Wenjun Wu, Faguo Wu, Xiao Zhang

entry.summary: ChainClaw is a layered blockchain-native agent framework addressing reactivity, irreversibility, and observability gaps through event-driven orchestration, simulation-based safety checks before execution, and on-chain monitoring, unified by cross-layer memory. The motivation is that on-chain execution is stateful, adversarial, and economically irreversible.

entry.title: Simulator-Grounded Large Language Models for Industrial Causal Reasoning: Tool-Use, Structured Injection, and Plant-Portable Retrieval for Wastewater Treatment Decision Support

author.name: Gary Simethy, Daniel Ortiz Arroyo, Petar Durdevic

entry.summary: The paper compares three ways to ground a frozen 32B open model in an interpretable wastewater-treatment simulator for causal operational questions: live simulator oracle, structured parameter injection, and a small decoupled recall-reasoning retriever. Accuracy on a 198-question causal benchmark forms a clear ladder from 99.5 percent down to 75.8 percent, all far above a retrieval-augmented baseline at 48 percent.

entry.title: APQF: Agentic Profiling-Guided Structured Pruning and Mixed-Precision Quantization with Adaptive Fine-Tuning

author.name: Sadegh Jafari, Mohiuddin Bilwal, Fan Zhou, Brian Gelder, Ali Jannesari

entry.summary: APQF automates edge model compression by having a profiling agent measure where cost sits and how sensitive each layer is to compression, then driving per-layer pruning ratios and mixed-precision quantization-aware training plus accuracy recovery in one pipeline. It replaces uniform, expert-chosen compression settings.

entry.title: Does Latent Context Help? A Controlled Evaluation of Inverse Reinforcement Learning in Arctic Shipping

author.name: Vaishnav Vaidheeswaran, Dilith Jayakody, Biruk Ambaw, Jaswanth Kumar, Md Mahbub Alam, Gabriel Spadon

entry.summary: Uses over three thousand real Arctic vessel voyages to ask whether latent context variables in meta inverse reinforcement learning genuinely recover hidden operator preferences or merely re-encode information already in the observed state. The controlled comparison against a linear baseline probes an assumption underlying much latent-context IRL.

entry.title: From Passive Mirrors to Active Agents: Holonic Digital Twins for Physical AI over Networks

author.name: Christo Kurisummoottil Thomas, Omar Hashash, Walid Saad

entry.summary: Proposes a network architecture in which digital twins act as active agents rather than passive mirrors, organized holonically so that wireless infrastructure maintains shared spatiotemporal context for physical AI systems. The argument is that current networks optimize throughput and latency and cannot support real-time coordination of embodied agents.

entry.title: RASP-QAOA: Resource-Aware Per-Instance Selection for Exact QAOA Simulation

author.name: Chih-Chung Hsu

entry.summary: RASP-QAOA selects, per problem instance, among ten exact QAOA simulation actions that bundle representation, adapter, precision mode, and memory policy, first pruning infeasible actions then ranking the rest using instance features with analytical fallbacks. It succeeded on every request in a held-out GPU evaluation for which any admissible action existed.

entry.title: Enhancing Social Intelligence in LLMs with Hierarchical Reasoning and Utterance-Level Goal Rewarding

author.name: Xiaofeng Wang, Kakam Chong, Shuai Xiao, DeXin Kong, Qingyuan Tian, Chen Ju, Xu Yan, Shuai Zhao, Fei Huang, Rui Wang, Shuguang Han, jufeng chen

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical framework that splits social dialogue into strategic planning and linguistic execution, trained with a linearized hierarchical RL algorithm using variance-gated, utterance-level goal rewards instead of uniform episode-level rewards. Motivated by the theory of planned behavior.

entry.title: EpiBench: Can LLMs Understand Epitopes for Antibody Drug Discovery?

author.name: Zirui Wang, Jiaqi Wang, Qinghan Wang, Yuzhi Xu, Gang Du, Tingjun Hou, Odin Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a closed-book, sequence-based, automatically scorable benchmark testing whether LLMs can infer antibody epitope information directly from antigen and antibody sequences, spanning decisions across the antibody development workflow. Fills a gap between isolated epitope prediction tasks and general protein benchmarks.

entry.title: Bayesian adaptively-weighted ensembles for few-shot abdominal segmentation

author.name: Abbas Al-Sabbagh, Shalom F. Mushtaq, Tom\'as M. da Silva, Kushagra Soni, Binawei Gbamila, Sri Atluri, Qianye Yang, Yipeng Hu, Claire C. Villette, Shaheer U. Saeed

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Bayesian optimization framework that adaptively weights an ensemble of few-shot abdominal segmentation algorithms according to the target domain, rather than using fixed ensemble weights. The motivation is that different few-shot methods have complementary strengths that vary by anatomy and institution. It targets label scarcity combined with domain shift in clinical segmentation.

entry.title: Overcoming Attention Drift: Homogeneity-Heterogeneity Guided Feature Aggregation for Low-Light Remote Sensing Image Enhancement

author.name: Yaozi Zhong, Xingxing Yang, Shaohui Mei, Mingyang Ma

entry.summary: HALO enhances extremely low-light remote sensing imagery by using foundation-model priors to fix what the authors call attention drift, where attention aggregates features across genuinely different physical boundaries. It combines an illumination-invariant semantic prior for regional homogeneity with a pseudo-3D topological prior for heterogeneity cues. The target is reliable Earth observation and downstream machine vision under severe degradation.

entry.title: DTRNet: Dual Text-Radical Decoding for Handwritten Chinese Text Recognition with Faked Character Detection

author.name: Runrui Li, Lin Zhu, Hua Huang

entry.summary: DTRNet decodes both text and radical (character-component) sequences for handwritten Chinese recognition so that it can flag fabricated or malformed characters written by students, not just transcribe them. The dual decoding preserves character-structural evidence while keeping line-level efficiency. The target application is K-12 educational assessment.

entry.title: Bar-JEPA: Extracting Values from Bar Chart with Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture

author.name: Poonam Poonam, Alexander Epple, Timo Ropinski

entry.summary: Bar-JEPA applies joint-embedding predictive architecture pretraining to bar chart images so that a simple decoder can recover per-bar numerical values with less labeled data. Chart de-rendering normally requires costly real-world annotation, which self-supervised semantic features can partially replace. It is an efficiency-oriented take on chart data extraction.

entry.title: Risk-Aware Quantile Learning for Personalized Dynamic Treatment Regimes

author.name: Chunyin Lei, Annie Qu

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for learning dynamic treatment regimes that optimizes a chosen quantile of the cumulative outcome instead of the mean, while explicitly penalizing treatment-related risk and supporting more than two treatment options through an angle-based multicategory formulation. Aimed at sequential clinical decisions where tail outcomes and safety matter. Extends quantile DTR methods beyond efficacy-only binary settings.

entry.title: Abstract Event Causal Rules: Induction and Application

author.name: Ziwei Zheng, Peiqiong Chen, Bang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Abstract Event Causal Rules, converting instance-level cause-effect pairs into generalized relation-level causal templates via a multi-agent concrete-to-abstract induction pipeline with similarity-constrained clustering. The goal is better generalization to long-tail and unseen event combinations in event-centric analytics.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Trajectory Prediction with Explicit Planning and Reaction Decomposition

author.name: Jiaheng Chen, Jiaxing Li, Tinghe Zhang, Chaopeng Guo

entry.summary: INTraJ decomposes social influence in trajectory prediction into a planning stage that builds reference trajectories from future social information and a reaction stage that recovers local adjustments as residuals from full-context prediction. The staged formulation reflects the intuition that agents plan by anticipating others before making reactive corrections.

entry.title: Shaping Human-AI Interactions to Provide Improvement Pathways and Balance Competing Objectives

author.name: Keziah Naggita

entry.summary: A thesis-style overview of designing human-AI interaction loops where individuals form beliefs about a deployed system and strategically present themselves, aiming to help users build accurate beliefs, encourage genuine improvement over gaming, and preserve system accuracy. It draws on strategic classification and recourse literatures.

entry.title: Unified Agent: Managing Interactions across Devices

author.name: Xinshuang Liu, Runfa Blark Li, Shaoxiu Wei, Xin Lin, Truong Nguyen

entry.summary: Argues that cross-device, cross-time agents need a compact carried state organizing engagement evidence, stated facts, and the standing request, since single agents treating devices as tools lack state management and multi-agent systems coordinate without maintaining such state. Proposes a unified agent design around this state abstraction.

entry.title: When Agentic AI Meets Integrated Sensing and Communication

author.name: Kai Li, Conggai Li, Sarah Ali Siddiqui, Syed Sohail Ahmed, Xin Yuan, Shenghong Li, Wei Ni

entry.summary: A survey unifying learning-based sensing, resource allocation, reconfigurable surfaces, edge intelligence, and multi-agent coordination for Integrated Sensing and Communication under a six-stage closed-loop agentic framework, plus a five-level agentic maturity model. It positions ISAC as evolving from a physical-layer function to a goal-driven closed-loop system.

entry.title: Improving the Realism of Synthetic Clinical Benchmarks Under Utility Constraints

author.name: Omid Bazgir, Md Nasir, Jacob Hoffman, Yang Yang, Manu Agrawal, Anusua Trivedi, Vinay Rao Dandin, Chris Gibbons, Christine Swisher

entry.summary: This paper formalizes synthetic clinical benchmark revision as utility-constrained realism improvement: edit a Synthea-derived care-gap dataset to look more like operational EHR data while staying above an operational utility floor. It highlights that benchmarks can pass current utility checks while remaining structurally unrealistic.

entry.title: Hierarchical Server Architecture for Agentic Science

author.name: Vanessa Sochat, Daniel Milroy

entry.summary: The authors present a hierarchical, dynamic architecture with secretary agents that discover and negotiate compute resources across cloud, edge, and HPC systems for agentic scientific workloads. They probe 51 real and simulated providers across seven categories and run nearly 20,000 negotiation simulations.

entry.title: Spectral Aliasing Pretext: A novel task for Self-Supervised fault diagnosis in rotating machinery

author.name: Victor Gialis, Maxime Metz, David Esteve, Abdenour Soualhi

entry.summary: Introduces a self-supervised pretext task for vibration signals in which a transformer must reconstruct an unfolded spectrum from a deliberately undersampled, aliased one, avoiding hand-designed augmentations. Linear probing on a standard bearing-fault dataset shows strong representations from unlabeled data.

entry.title: Human-Like Anaphor Resolution in Large Language Models

author.name: Keane Zhang, Varshini Chinta, Raj Sanjay Shah, Sashank Varma
