entry.summary: Tests whether cognitive factors known to modulate human anaphor resolution, such as discourse structure and situation-model properties, also affect five open-weight LLMs using surprisal as a linking hypothesis to reading times. Compares model and human accuracy on comprehension questions.

entry.title: Causal Episodic Memory for Feedback-Driven Agent Repair

author.name: Khang Nhat Hoang Vo, Tam Minh Chu, Anh Trac Duc Dinh, Thuyen Vinh Ha Bui, Tho Quan

entry.summary: Introduces a training-free agent that keeps an online dual-polarity memory of verified successful corrections and observed failed directions, retrieved via a failure-type classifier plus hybrid lexical-dense search, to improve later text-to-SQL repair episodes. Uses a frozen 7B model with fixed repair budgets.

entry.title: From Sports to Safety: Benchmarking Proactive Risk Inference in MLLMs

author.name: Jiawei Qiu, Yichen Xu, Jianzhe Ma, Mingyang Yu, Wenbin Zhu, Yang Han, Pinzheng Lv, Wenxuan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a project-level benchmark of 28 projects across seven software areas to measure Python over-selection, consistency between recommended and implemented languages, and language diversity, evaluating 25 models. Finds Python is heavily over-chosen and that smaller open-weight models show stronger bias and less diversity.

entry.title: EffectLearner: World-Aware Object-Effect Reasoning for Real-World Video Object Removal

author.name: Feier Wu, Wanke Xia, Xu He, Zilang Zhou, Si Chen, Dongxia Liu, Liyang Chen, Qimeng Wu, Zhengbo Zhang, Wenming Yang, Zhiyong Wu

entry.summary: Combines a VLM-based reasoner that analyzes object-induced effects such as shadows, reflections, and interactions with a diffusion transformer video eraser, so removal generalizes to compositional, spatially detached, and long-tail physical effects. Uses a structured effect-analysis prompt to guide cross-modal reasoning before erasing.

entry.title: Beyond Frame Selection: Rethinking Long-Video Understanding with MLLMs

author.name: Ziling Huang, Shin'ichi Satoh

entry.summary: Reframes long-video understanding as coordinating complementary evidence views rather than selecting one subset of frames, organizing each video into a question-agnostic coarse-to-fine temporal hierarchy and routing among views. Aims to preserve both global storyline context and temporally sparse fine-grained evidence under token limits.

entry.title: ChronoVision: Temporal Reasoning via Latent State Reconstruction

author.name: Yifan Shen, Jian Xu, Boyi Li, Yuner Zhang, Tianjiao Yu, Bingxuan Li, Houze Yang, Rushi Wang, Xu Cao

entry.summary: Aims to reduce reliance on ambiguous language-only chains of thought for visual temporal reasoning by having the model predict the latent representation of the final transformed visual state during fine-tuning, plus an attention module that focuses on key regions. Adds reinforcement learning with implicit process grounding in post-training.

entry.title: Comparative Approaches to Agent Retrieval over Large Skill Libraries

author.name: Indivara Kolluru, Nathan Sportsman

entry.summary: The authors compare a hybrid lexical plus dense retriever against a typed knowledge graph encoding prerequisites and data-flow ordering for selecting which of 690 agent skills to load. The retriever gets the right skill in the top five about 73 percent of the time, leaving roughly a quarter of realistic queries unserved, and graph neighbors are examined as a substitute for extra ranked results.

entry.title: One Qubit Can Beat One Bit: Quantum Advantage for Post-Training Quantization

author.name: Yuma Ichikawa, Moeto Mishima

entry.summary: QRAQ encodes context-dependent weight signs in a quantum random-access code so that one-bit post-training quantization need not share a single binary sign matrix across deployment contexts with different activation statistics. The authors prove a row-wise separation from shared-sign one-bit quantization under a fresh-copy readout model with quantified shot noise.

entry.title: D-CLOT: Double Closed Loop Optimal Transport for Unsupervised Action Segmentation

author.name: Elena Bueno-Benito, Mariella Dimiccoli

entry.summary: Improves optimal-transport-based unsupervised action segmentation by re-estimating action prototypes from refined frame embeddings instead of letting them drift only through pseudo-label gradients. A graph-constrained mechanism targets ambiguous transitions and rare or short actions.

entry.title: Beyond Full-Model Rollback: AuroSFT for Adapter-State Multi-Task Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yue Han, Ziniu Liu

entry.summary: Reformulates overfitting-aware multi-task supervised fine-tuning so that the scheduler state consists of small mergeable adapters rather than full model checkpoints, since different tasks peak at different times and rolling back full models is expensive. The backbone stays frozen and only adapter checkpoints are rolled back at per-task peaks.

entry.title: Beyond Rotations: AuroOFT for Expressive Quantized Orthogonal Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yue Han, Dianlin Wang

entry.summary: Extends quantized orthogonal fine-tuning, which adapts low-bit models via learned activation rotations, by attaching a zero-initialized gated low-rank nonlinear residual to each adapted layer. The construction is functionally identical to the base method at initialization while adding input-dependent nonlinear corrections.

entry.title: DG-FedReuse: Proxy-Gradient-Gated Cached-Update Reuse with Matched Sparse Uplink Accounting

author.name: Rahil Aftab, Vineet Kumar Rakesh, Soumya Mazumdar, Tapas Samanta

entry.summary: Studies a federated learning mechanism where selected clients contribute age-decayed cached updates when a gradient-discrepancy proxy stays below a threshold, with hard cache-age limits and a fresh-client quota, plus adaptive sparse uplink encoding. Simulated experiments over six image datasets report larger uplink savings than matched sparse averaging at a fixed round budget.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware World Model for Aerial Image-Goal Navigation

author.name: Deyi Zhu, Haoyu Fan, Yinan Zhu, Weichen Zhang, Shilin Ma, Xinlei Chen, Yansong Tang

entry.summary: Proposes a latent world model for aerial image-goal navigation that treats trajectory scoring as conditional out-of-distribution detection, representing plausible futures with an uncertainty subspace instead of a few point predictions. Decomposes prediction-goal discrepancy into uncertainty-explained and residual components for large outdoor environments.

entry.title: Mapping Armenian Paris: Extracting and Geocoding Commercial Advertisements from the 20th-Century Diaspora Press

author.name: Chahan Vidal-Gor\`ene (CJM, LIPN), Seda Kirakosyan (UFAR), Edita Matevosyan (UFAR)

entry.summary: An end-to-end pipeline that detects, reads, and structures commercial advertisements from digitized 20th-century Western Armenian diaspora newspapers, then geocodes them into an interactive map of Armenian Paris. Vision-language models are used as a bootstrapping annotator because off-the-shelf layout and OCR tools do not support this under-resourced script and fail on curved scans. The release includes a 500-page annotated corpus.

entry.title: Topology-Aware Neighborhood Learning for Source-Free Cross-Scene Hyperspectral Image Classification

author.name: Qingmei Li, Juepeng Zheng, Jiarui Zhang, Jianxi Huang, Haohuan Fu

entry.summary: A source-free domain adaptation framework for cross-scene hyperspectral classification that uses entropy-momentum pseudo-labeling to refine clustering assignments and contextual neighborhood topology to exploit local structure without access to source data. The motivation is that privacy rules and storage limits often prevent retaining source-domain imagery. It targets realistic operational remote sensing constraints.

entry.title: PaCoNet: Deep Data Extraction for Parallel Coordinates

author.name: Poonam Poonam, Hannah Kniesel, Pere-Pau V\'azquez, Timo Ropinski

entry.summary: PaCoNet is presented as the first method for extracting underlying data from parallel coordinate plots, recovering both polyline coordinates and individual high-dimensional data samples. Chart de-rendering research has focused on bar, line, and pie charts, leaving high-dimensional visualizations unaddressed. The work targets cluttered, densely populated plots that are hard even for humans.

entry.title: DARAD: Dual Adapters and Ranking-Aware Distillation for Continual Remote Sensing Image-Text Retrieval

author.name: Xi Chen, Xu Chen, Xiangyang Jia, Wei Wang, Xu Zhang, Zhenyuan Sun

entry.summary: DARAD supports continual remote sensing image-text retrieval with separate visual and textual adapters plus a distillation loss that preserves the historical cross-modal ranking structure as new archives arrive. Scale variation and distribution shift in satellite imagery distort the shared alignment space over successive tasks. The goal is reliable retrieval over continuously expanding Earth observation archives.

entry.title: Unified Planning-Learning Framework for Robust UUV Navigation Under Partial Observability

author.name: Md Ether Deowan, Eleni Kelasidi

entry.summary: This framework combines persistent sonar-and-depth occupancy mapping, a clearance-aware global planner, and a reinforcement learning local controller for underwater vehicle navigation using observations only, with a learned latent state to handle partial observability. Underwater environments provide poor localization and dynamic obstacles. The design splits long-horizon structure from reactive avoidance.

entry.title: Evaluating and Improving Pedagogical Fit in LLM-Based AI Tutors with the Pedagogical Suitability Index

author.name: Benjamin Barlog, Hudson Craig, Zedong Peng

entry.summary: Defines a Pedagogical Suitability Index of six theory-informed sub-scores measuring whether an LLM tutor response matches learner readiness, course sequencing, and concept-introduction timing rather than only correctness. The index is also used as structured feedback to improve tutoring responses.

entry.title: Bayesian Expected Uncertainty Reduction (B-EUR) Model: A Computational Account of What Makes Design Options Worth Trying

author.name: Shimon Honda, Takuma Miyaguchi, Koji Koizumi, Takanori Sano, Tristan Briard, Hideyoshi Yanagisawa

entry.summary: Proposes a Bayesian Expected Uncertainty Reduction model that scores the value of trying a design action by how much epistemic uncertainty about action-outcome relations it is expected to remove, examining generalizability of knowledge across candidates and discriminability of outcomes. It is tested in simulations and a human graph-shape guessing experiment.

entry.title: Activity Frames: Deterministic Screen-Activity Compilation for Agent Memory and Replay

author.name: Nossa Iyamu

entry.summary: Compiles passively captured screen activity into deterministic typed activity frames with application, site, timing, and input-volume metadata plus pointers back to raw rows, with no model in the loop so output is byte-identical and auditable. On a single-user corpus of 128,756 frames over 51 days it compresses a day of capture into a context block 86 times smaller in 68 milliseconds.

entry.title: Signal or Spurious Cue? A Randomized Audit of Survey-Country Metadata in LLM Social Inference

author.name: Yifan Lyu, Xinran Li, Jiaqi Qiao, Xiujuan Xu

entry.summary: The authors run a randomized audit testing whether telling an LLM that a survey-country label was assigned at random reduces the model's tendency to shift its predicted individual survey response toward that country. Disclosure produced essentially no attenuation, while verified country labels did improve held-out prediction loss, indicating the metadata acts as an uncontrollable steering cue rather than reasoned evidence.

entry.title: CogVis: Must Open-Vocabulary Change Detection Perceive the Scene Anew for Every Query?

author.name: Zijie Wang, Chen Zhong, Wei He

entry.summary: CogVis restructures open-vocabulary change detection in remote sensing into a perception-memory-verification pipeline, extracting a reusable category-agnostic change prior from frozen bi-temporal features so the scene is not re-perceived for every query. A semantic memory calibrator then handles category-specific discrimination.

entry.title: HyTBE: Hyperbolic Target-Background Expert Model for Cross-Domain Infrared Small Target Detection

author.name: Aohua Li, Jin Kuang, Yubing Lu, Pingping Liu

entry.summary: Frames cross-domain failure in infrared small-target detection as a shift in the relationship between target and background patterns rather than simple appearance shift, and proposes a hyperbolic expert model to widen the range of representable relations. Aims at generalization to unseen infrared domains.

entry.title: Toward Deployable Bangla Sign Language Recognition with Expert-Validated Data and a Lightweight Attention-Based Model

author.name: Saad Ahmed, Md Khalid Syfullaha

entry.summary: Releases an expert-validated dataset of about 10,900 images covering all 38 Bangla Sign Language hand signs recorded from real signers at special-needs schools, and proposes a roughly 300,000-parameter attention-based convolutional network for on-device recognition. The focus is deployability on personal phones rather than heavyweight pretrained backbones.

entry.title: SEAM: Global consistency beyond local accuracy in scientific machine learning

author.name: Gnankan Landry Regis N'guessan, Bum Jun Kim

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for checking whether local explanations of scientific machine learning models, validated per subdomain or per prediction, can be glued into one globally admissible explanation. The sheaf-inspired instantiation compares neighboring regional explanations on their overlaps to detect inconsistency.

entry.title: Stochastic Dynamics on Persistence Diagram Space via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Farzana Nasrin

entry.summary: Introduces a reinforcement learning framework for stochastic evolution on the space of persistence diagrams, where diagrams change through topology-aware local edits defining controlled Markov processes. Establishes ergodicity conditions guaranteeing unique stationary distributions.

entry.title: ConWriter: Transition-Constrained Stateful Long-Form Story Generation with Lightweight Neuro-Symbolic Consistency Control

author.name: Jindong Li, Yang Yang, Zihao Liu, Yutao Yue, Menglin Yang

entry.summary: Presents a training-free framework for long-form story generation that writes scene by scene while maintaining symbolic narrative state, checking required transitions, and using uncertainty signals to flag risky continuations. Targets accumulation of temporal, factual, character, and stylistic inconsistencies.

entry.title: Constraint-First Reasoning: A Training-Free Protocol for Exploiting Answer-Space Constraints in Mathematical Problem Solving

author.name: Hongbo Ma, Bangji Yang, Yunqian Selina Cheng, Jiajun Fan, Hanwen Zhang, Ge Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a two-stage training-free prompting protocol where the model first extracts answer-space constraints and then solves while verifying against them, with a regex router that activates the protocol only for constraint-heavy problems. Reports improvements over direct chain-of-thought on several competition math benchmarks.

entry.title: NeSy-RAG: Neuro-Symbolic RAG for Explainable Question Answering

author.name: Jonas Gann, Michael Gertz

entry.summary: Proposes a modular neuro-symbolic RAG framework that synthesizes attributable Prolog modules from retrieved text chunks, generating predicates encoding Boolean claims that may depend on user-specific facts. Aims to make reasoning steps verifiable and to detect missing user context systematically.

entry.title: Context Matters: Support Set Selection and Failure Detection for In-Context Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Youssef Gehad, Emmanuel Zerefa, Krish Kabra, Guha Balakrishnan

entry.summary: Studies the support set as a controllable lever for in-context medical image segmentation, comparing random against similarity-based exemplar retrieval, and trains a transformer classifier to predict from query and support images alone whether segmentation quality will fall below a threshold. Combines context selection with failure detection.

entry.title: CDSeg: A Renderable Gaussian Carrier for Image-to-3D Label Transfer

author.name: Wentao Sun, Yiping Chen, Zhengsen Xu, Jonathan Li, John S. Zelek

entry.summary: Uses Gaussian splatting primitives as a renderable carrier to transfer 2D image-model masks into consistent 3D labels, with renderer-derived visibility deciding which primitives receive which labels and no task-specific 3D segmentation training. Supports both point-completed and native optimized Gaussian scenes.

entry.title: Hierarchical Flow Matching for 3D Point Cloud Generation

author.name: Linhao Wang, Qichang Zhang, Ye Su, Hao Wang

entry.summary: Extends flow matching to a two-level hierarchy for unconditional 3D point cloud generation, with a latent flow modeling global shape structure and a second level generating local detail, avoiding expensive ODE solving and trace estimation required by continuous normalizing flows. Uses optimal-transport flow matching at both levels.

entry.title: SCI-CLIP: Segment-Centric Inference with Reference Memory for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Segmentation

author.name: Mohamad Zamini, Diksha Shukla

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free open-vocabulary segmentation framework organized around a segment-level abstraction, building a region-consistent interaction graph over frozen CLIP tokens, propagating features over it, adding selective cross-window support where local evidence is weak, and applying retrieval-based correction from reference memory. Argues one consistent region unit should govern all stages of dense prediction.

entry.title: Vorch-IR: Long-Form Unified Multimodal Identity Replacement Video Generation

author.name: Yaole Wang, Xiaoyu Chen, Xin Ma, Yang Ding, Gang Yue, Jingjing Chen, Lin Ma, Yaohui Wang

entry.summary: Presents a unified video identity-replacement model supporting single- and dual-person swaps with optional background replacement in one model, conditioning jointly on a driving video, indexed reference images, and text edit instructions without task-specific structural controls like masks or poses. Built on a modern video generation backbone and addresses the scarcity of paired multi-person data.

entry.title: TAU-Bench: From Anomaly Instance Tracking to Fine-Grained Video Anomaly Understanding

author.name: Kepeng Yang, Dongxuan Liu, Rongxin Gao, Zixin Su, Rui Wu, Shuzhao Xie, Chenxin Li, Panwang Pan, Yuzhi Huang, Yue Huang, Jingyan Jiang

entry.summary: Argues that fluent VLM anomaly descriptions are not necessarily grounded in the correct anomalous instance over time, and introduces a benchmark that jointly evaluates instance tracking and fine-grained semantic understanding rather than treating them as separate protocols. Aims to mirror how humans identify, follow, and explain anomalous events.

entry.title: Topometric Autonomous Vehicle Localization by Combining Visual Embeddings and Feed-Forward 3D Models

author.name: Eulogio Quemada-Torres, Alberto Jaenal, Francisco-Angel Moreno, Javier Gonzalez-Jimenez

entry.summary: A topometric localization pipeline for vehicles that fuses probabilistic visual place recognition over compact image embeddings with metric local trajectory estimates from feed-forward neural 3D geometry models. The aim is a map that is simultaneously compact, appearance-robust, and metrically accurate. Targets long-term autonomous driving localization under appearance change.

entry.title: Structured Dimension-Matched Joint Variational Transdimensional Inference

author.name: Pingping Yin, Xiyun Jiao

entry.summary: Presents a variational approach to Bayesian model selection over enumerable model spaces where a construction graph encodes models as sequences of local stop or child decisions, and each edge carries an exact dimension-matching lift plus a learned normalizing flow for the residual transport. This avoids embedding all candidate models into a single saturated maximum-dimension space. The result is one joint variational distribution over discrete model indicator and continuous parameters.

entry.title: From Continuous Predictors to Clinical Thresholds: Early Evidence on Performance Trade-offs of Guideline-Based Categorisation for Ischaemic Stroke Outcome Prediction

author.name: Esra Zihni, Katryna Cisek, Hamzah Ziadeh, Hendrik Knoche, Robert Mikulik, John D. Kelleher

entry.summary: Tests whether replacing continuous predictors with clinical-guideline-aligned categorical cut-offs degrades gradient-boosted models for 90-day ischaemic stroke outcome prediction on a multi-centre European registry. The categorised models are statistically indistinguishable from continuous ones, suggesting clinician-aligned explanations can be obtained at little accuracy cost.

entry.title: Improving Interoperability among Defence and National Security Ontologies: Analysis and Evaluation Tasks

author.name: Jonathon Dilworth, Pedro Giesteira Cotovio, David Herron, Paul Cripps, Nigel Dewdney, Catia Pesquita, Ernesto Jim\'enez-Ruiz

entry.summary: Analyzes over 60 publicly available defence and national security ontologies and contributes a new Ontology Alignment Evaluation Initiative track with eight matching tasks, consensus alignments from multiple state-of-the-art matchers, and manually curated silver-standard mappings. The aim is measurable progress on interoperability in a highly specialized domain.

entry.title: Nonvisual Classification of Ground-Condition by Artificial Proprioception in an Amoeba-Inspired Autonomous Walking Robot

author.name: Hyoto Yamaguchi, Zenji Yatabe, Seiya Kasai

entry.summary: Builds a legged walking robot that classifies flat versus rough terrain using only accelerometer and foot pressure signals processed by reservoir computing, without any camera. The robot then switches gait on the fly based on the inferred ground condition.

entry.title: Investigating Artificial Intelligence Digital Sovereignty in Mobile Shopping Apps: A Case Study of Nigeria

author.name: George Grispos, Sajda Qureshi

entry.summary: Combines forensic analysis of Nigerian Android shopping applications with document analysis to identify embedded AI features and evaluate how transparently their use is disclosed. It finds AI widely deployed but poorly disclosed, and interprets this as a digital sovereignty concern for users in the region.

entry.title: Evaluating Machine Learning Models for Post-Wildfire Debris-Flow Prediction

author.name: Quinn Ledingham, Zhengsen Xu, Yimin Zhu, Zack Dewis, Mabel Heffring, Saeid Taleghanidoozdoozan, Motasem Alkayid, Megan Greenwood, Lincoln Linlin Xu

entry.summary: Systematically compares 15 machine learning models, including a tabular prior-fitted network, for predicting debris flows after wildfires from basin-scale observations across the western United States. The evaluation covers predictive performance, feature importance, and whether synthetic data augmentation helps under limited and overlapping data.

entry.title: Accelerating nanodrug development in continuous flow systems using informed prediction models based on low-cost surrogate nanoparticles

author.name: Kai Dahms, Eilien Heinrich, Jochen Schmid, Michael Bortz, Iryna Savych, Regina Bleul

entry.summary: The paper builds shape-constrained predictive models of nanoparticle size and polydispersity as a function of microfluidic process parameters, using cheap surrogate nanoparticles to inform predictions for costlier nanotherapeutic formulations. The aim is to replace iterative experimental screening in continuous-flow nanodrug development.

entry.title: A Low-Power Wearable Respiratory Sensor for Non-Invasive Stress Monitoring

author.name: Mohammad Hosseini, Hamed Khatounabadi, Mohammad Fakharzadeh

entry.summary: A wearable belt-mounted force-sensitive resistor with a custom Bluetooth Low Energy board captures abdominal expansion for respiration-based stress monitoring, using a mechanical holder instead of analog amplification to stay low power. The pipeline is evaluated across multiple breathing patterns and postures.

entry.title: OTLesMix: Wasserstein Barycenter and Optimal Transport Map for Synthetic Lesion Generation with Diverse Shapes and Locations

author.name: Robin Trombetta, Carole Lartizien

entry.summary: Proposes a data augmentation method for medical image segmentation that uses Wasserstein barycenters and optimal transport maps to synthesize lesions with more diverse shapes and locations than existing mixing strategies. Aims to improve training of lesion segmentation models.

entry.title: M$^3$R-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Metaphor Understanding

author.name: Hong Jiang, Junnan Zhu, Jingwang Huang, Xiao Sun, Yuming Yang, Jiang Zhong, Ruirui Chen, Jingman Shi, Hao Wu, Nayu Liu, Xinyi Jiang, Kaiwen Wei

entry.summary: Introduces a unified benchmark of 1,000 human-verified image-text instances for multimodal metaphor understanding that requires evidence-grounded explanations rather than isolated classification subtasks. Grounded in conceptual metaphor theory to test whether models build genuine target-source mappings.

entry.title: MoCA: Implicit Social Context Analysis

author.name: Wenhao Xu, Kaiwen Zhang, Hao Li, Maowei You, Yongzheng Ji, Siyuan Zuo, Jingxuan Yu, Sina A, Xinyao Tan, Bobo Li, Hao Fei, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu

entry.summary: Defines a new task for analyzing implicit social context along affection, intent, and stance dimensions, with a benchmark of 3,108 multimodal real-world instances annotated for who expresses what toward whom. Targets indirect, culturally grounded social signals that current models handle poorly.

entry.title: Text-Guided Refinement of Multi-sequence Glioma Subregion Segmentation with a Vision-Language Foundation Model

author.name: Zach Eidex, Yu-nong Lin, Mojtaba Safari, Sean Pitroda, Ralph Weichselbaum, Zhen Tian, Xiaofeng Yang

entry.summary: Adapts a 3D vision-language foundation model so clinicians can refine glioma subregion segmentations with text instructions, injecting frozen prompt embeddings through trainable projections into the segmentation network. Uses oracle prompts encoding target, action, location, imaging evidence, edit size, and preservation constraints.

entry.title: TLNM: Externally Validated Tooth Detection, Numbering and Segmentation from Smartphone Photographs Using Mask R-CNN

author.name: Arash Nedaei, Henna Tiensuu, Elina V\"ayrynen, Saujanya Karki, Jaakko Suutala

entry.summary: TLNM adapts Mask R-CNN to detect, number, and segment teeth from ordinary smartphone photographs, with a white-balancing step for artificial color casts and an anatomically constrained detection layer. It is externally validated, which is uncommon in this application area. The goal is accessible self-screening where clinical radiographs are unavailable.

entry.title: Grounded Well-Condition Anomaly Detection on the Volve Field: Constructed Labels, a Baseline, and a Dual-Head Model

author.name: Gospel Bassey, Vincent Fakiyesi

entry.summary: Builds anomaly labels for the open Volve production field data by cross-checking statistical patterns against engineering documents describing physically plausible failures, releasing the reasoning behind each label. It provides a baseline plus a dual-head model and stresses the hidden assumptions in unlabeled industrial anomaly detection.

entry.title: ECHO: A Locally-Deployable Agentic Health Assistant with Temporal Memory, Safety Guardrails, and Speech Assessment

author.name: Abdulkadir K\"ul\c{c}e, Alihan Esen, Ca\u{g}la Fikir, Berke Kurt, Kuzey Arar, G\"okhan Ercan, Faik Boray Tek

entry.summary: ECHO is a locally deployable chronic-care assistant combining a ReAct agent with 17 clinical tools, a temporal knowledge graph for cross-session memory, a two-stage rule plus graph-neural-network safety filter, and a speech assessment module. Reported results include a high tool-execution pass rate on a 59-scenario benchmark using a small GPT-5 class backend.

entry.title: Schema-Guided Hierarchical Information Extraction and Semantic Evaluation Using Generative AI

author.name: Modhurita Mitra, Jan-Willem Versteeg, Maarten D. Schermer, Shiva Nadi Najafabadi, Marie L. De Bruin, Lourens T. Bloem

entry.summary: The paper presents a zero-shot, single-call schema-driven pipeline for extracting deeply nested, variable-cardinality structured information from documents, plus a path-based semantic matching algorithm to score extractions against a gold standard. The setting is regulatory and pharmacovigilance-style document analysis.

entry.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering

author.name: Soorya Ram Shimgekar, Michelle Hu, Dorisa Shehi, Daniel Kang, Roy Ka-Wei Lee, Koustuv Saha, Christian Poellabauer, Christopher Lee, Sajeev Singh, Piyum Zonooz, Navin Kumar, Zeeshan Ahmed, Priyadarshini Kachroo

entry.summary: nMAS is a multi-agent, evidence-linked pipeline that automates heart-failure feature engineering from fragmented EHR tables with rubric grounding and traceability to guideline sources, evaluated on 500 dummy patient records across nine source tables. It targets the large share of clinical data-science effort consumed by feature construction.

entry.title: Quality Diversity for Reliable Data Driven Time-Use Optimization

author.name: Aneta Neumann, Ty Stanford, Dorothea Dumuid, Frank Neumann

entry.summary: The authors introduce a quality-diversity optimization framework with uncertainty quantification for recommending how to allocate a 24-hour time budget across activities to improve health outcomes. Incorporating predictive uncertainty avoids the unrealistic recommendations that pure expected-benefit optimization produces.

entry.title: Why do models task game?

author.name: aditya singh

entry.summary: MRI-compatible master-slave manipulator for needle-based abdominal interventions, using elastomeric fluid actuators and low-friction graphite pistons to transmit sub-newton forces and sub-millimeter motion from outside the scanner bore. Adds a digital master controller for multimodal shared control beyond simple mode switching. Purely mechatronic medical robotics.

entry.title: Agentic Nesting: A New Methodology for Existing Enterprise Application Integration and Services

author.name: Xi Wang, Kun Li, Xianyao Ling, Gang Yin, Liang Zhang, Jiang Wu, Wenbo Lei, Jun Xu, Annie Wang, Fu Zhang, Weizhe Wang

entry.summary: Proposes an Agentic Nesting methodology for wrapping legacy enterprise systems (ESB, API gateways, RPA) into LLM-agent-orchestrated services to reduce data silos and process fragmentation. The contribution is largely architectural and industrial rather than a new learning method.

entry.title: Posture and Sustainment Optimization Under Adversarial Uncertainty

author.name: Amelie Norris, Alyssa Lee, Natan Vidra, Spurthi Setty

entry.summary: Formulates pre-conflict military asset posture as a finite-horizon MDP and proposes a Composite Expected Value optimizer that is scenario-weighted and adversarially robust, replacing greedy value-maximizing heuristics that ignore geographic coverage. The stated motivation is vulnerability of current practice to adversaries targeting high-value locations.

entry.title: Integrating Implicit and Explicit Relational Biases through Graph-Based Multiple Instance Learning: A Case Study in Skin Lesion Diagnosis

author.name: Rafa{\l} Buler (Gda\'nsk University of Technology), Jakub Buler (Gda\'nsk University of Technology), Maciej Bobowicz (Medical University of Gda\'nsk), Micha{\l} Grochowski (Gda\'nsk University of Technology)

entry.summary: Investigates a dual-level relational framework for skin lesion classification, combining implicit inter-patch relations learned by a convolutional masked autoencoder with explicit graph structures such as grid, random, and k-nearest-neighbour topologies over the learned embeddings, benchmarked against an EfficientNetB3 baseline. It tests how relational inductive biases at two levels interact.

entry.title: Who Gets Access? Global Region and Academic Status Bias in AI-Generated Academic Gatekeeping Scenarios

author.name: Nouar AlDahoul, Hezerul Abdul Karim, Myles Joshua Toledo Tan

entry.summary: A controlled simulation where LLM-based professors must grant a scarce resource such as a paywalled article or CV to only one of several requesters who vary by global region and academic seniority. The models show inconsistent and sometimes contradictory status and region preferences across scenarios, revealing latent allocation bias.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Transformer for Queue-Level XR Traffic Scheduling in TSN Networks

author.name: Marcos Carvalho, Fatih Temiz, Shavbo Salehi, Melike Erol-Kantarci, Daniel F. Macedo

entry.summary: A multi-agent transformer policy schedules queue-level extended-reality traffic in time-sensitive networking within mobile edge environments, where co-located services contend for shared resources and traffic classes differ in timing criticality. It targets decentralized queue coordination that centralized or high-level multi-agent designs miss.

entry.title: Why the Third Axis Is Freedom

author.name: Michael Timothy Bennett

entry.summary: A theoretical commentary arguing that what recent explorative-modeling work calls a third pretraining axis of exploration is better understood as freedom, meaning the weakness of the behavioral constraint a model implies. The author claims freedom is a property of function rather than of parameters, architecture, description length, or data.

entry.title: Beyond Feature Importance: A Comparative Analysis of Pattern Detection Methods in Cluster Interpretation

author.name: Benjamin Connor, Anna Jurek-Loughrey, Lu Bai, Muhammad Fahim

entry.summary: Compares common post-hoc explanation techniques on their ability to recover structured patterns inside clusters rather than just rank feature importance, using synthetic datasets with deliberately injected patterns. The controlled setup lets the authors measure whether surrogate models and similar tools actually surface cluster-level structure.

entry.title: Quantum-Structured World Models (QSWMs) for Predictive Latent Dynamics

author.name: Hailong Jiang, Emran Hossain, Feng Yu, Jianfeng Zhu, Guilin Zhang, Wulan Guo

entry.summary: Proposes a quantum-inspired world model framework using complex-valued representations and density-matrix-like latent states, with structured transition operators and measurement-style decoding. The authors establish foundational properties and ask whether quantum mathematical structure provides useful inductive biases for prediction and planning.

entry.title: Equipment-centric workpiece localization in near real-time using deep learning-based vision and event-driven finite state machines

author.name: Dohyeon Kong, Jaebong Cho, Hyunbo Cho

entry.summary: An industrial vision system tracks hot-forging workpieces indirectly by watching the handling equipment with multiple fixed 2D cameras, estimating 3D positions and recognizing grasp/release actions. Event-driven finite state machines convert recognized actions into validated handling events that update workpiece location state. A keypoint-guided attention module inside a 3D CNN improves activity recognition.

entry.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction

author.name: Chenglong Wang, Ziming Zhu, Yifu Huo, Bei Li, Qiaozhi He, Yan Ding, Xiaoyang Hao, Yuxin Gao, Tianhua Zhou, Xiaojia Chang, Tongran Liu, Jingbo Zhu

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.06310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in reward modeling show a paradigm shift from discriminative reward models to generative reward models. However, despite their strong c...

entry.title: Analysis of Numerical Localisation in LLM Translations

author.name: Patrizia Kaye

entry.summary: A small study measures how well five locally runnable LLMs localize times, dates, and numbers rather than translate them, and compares three improvement strategies. Placing explicit localization principles in the prompt context gave a statistically significant accuracy gain over direct translation.

entry.title: FOCUS: Decoupling Expert Personas in LLMs to Enhance Domain Expert Capabilities

author.name: Guanyu Wang, Zidi Zhang, Xu Chu

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.05611v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) can exhibit diverse personas, and activating expert personas has been shown to improve domain expertise and task accurac...

entry.title: Sparse Mutual Information Graph Averaging for Improving Random Indexing Embeddings

author.name: Sriram Loganathan, Gokul Anand, Aung Bo Bo, Yourui Shao, William B. Andreopoulos

entry.summary: The paper refines Random Indexing word vectors by weighted averaging over a sparse positive pointwise mutual information graph, avoiding dense matrix factorization and gradient training. On a small fairytale corpus it substantially improves a weak Random Indexing baseline on family analogies but degrades other embedding pipelines.

entry.title: CNM-BERT: A Drop-In Structural Embedding for Chinese Characters via Ideographic Description Sequences

author.name: Thomas Sing-wing Wu, Liqian Yan

entry.summary: Adds compositional structure to BERT-style Chinese encoders by parsing ideographic description sequences into trees, encoding them with a recursive tree MLP, and fusing structural embeddings without touching the backbone. Reports notable gains on rare and out-of-vocabulary characters.

entry.title: Mitigating Scoring Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge via Random Number Generation

author.name: Yuma Asato, Kiyoaki Shirai, Natthawut Kertkeidkachorn

entry.summary: Proposes measuring an LLM latent numeric bias by asking it to generate random numbers and comparing the resulting distribution to uniform, then using that measured deviation to correct scoring bias when the model is used as an evaluator. Task descriptions are inserted into the probing prompt to capture task-specific bias.

entry.title: Mapping Similarity Spaces across Embedding Models with Synthetic Query Probing

author.name: Marcin Rozmus, Peter van der Putten

entry.summary: Addresses the practical problem that retrieval similarity thresholds do not transfer when swapping embedding models, by learning mappings between score distributions rather than between embeddings. Uses synthetic queries generated from documents to build controlled query-chunk pairs and fits linear, isotonic, and quantile score conversions.

entry.title: Training-Free Token-Level Steering for LLM Personalized Co-Writing

author.name: Wenhao Mao, Chengbin Hou, Weixiao Wang, Jialiang Zhu, Min Liu, Yibin Hao, Hairong Lv

entry.summary: Presents a training-free token-level steering framework for personalized co-writing that adapts a base model to specialized domains without gradient updates, aiming to fill the gap between costly fine-tuning and coarse retrieval augmentation. Designed for small personal datasets and a co-writing rather than chat interface.

entry.title: Decolonizing Linguistic Policies in Automated Speech Recognition: A Framework for Cross-Culturally Competent Speech AI

author.name: Jay L. Cunningham, Mark Atta Mensah, Richard Martinez, Joao Vieira da Silva Neto, Efi Dawodu

entry.summary: Argues that persistent ASR failures for Indigenous, low-resource, and non-standard language varieties function as implicit language policy reproducing colonial hierarchies, and offers a three-harm taxonomy plus a seven-layer situatedness model for speech AI. Draws on raciolinguistics and decolonial computing.

entry.title: The Vulnerability With No CVE: Managing Persistent Gaps Between Mandate and Authority in AI Coding Agents

author.name: Shayell Aharon Salomon Amir Shaked Matan Noga

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.05884v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Existing guidance identifies excessive agency, excessive permission, weak task-bound authorization, and inadequate agent controls as important risks....

entry.title: LangChoiceBench: Measuring and Explaining Programming-Language Choice in LLMs

author.name: Lukas Twist, Twm Stone, Helen Yannakoudakis, Jie M. Zhang

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.06041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have been shown to exhibit strong Python preferences when generating project-level code, but there is currently no syste...

entry.title: MapTCL: Temporal Consistency Learning via Bidirectional Alignment for Vectorized HD Map Construction

author.name: Hyeonseo Kim, Juyeb Shin, Hyeonjun Jeong, Hiwon Shin, Dongsuk Kum

entry.summary: Adds an auxiliary temporal consistency loss for online vectorized HD map construction, penalizing geometric noise and jitter between consecutive predicted maps via bidirectional alignment of past and current vector instances. Improves stability in dynamic urban scenes with occlusions.

entry.title: Adapting Vision Foundation Models with Cascaded Semantics

author.name: Xi Xiao, Xingjian Li, Cheng Han, Tianyang Wang, Lin Zhao, Yunbei Zhang, Guosheng Hu, Runmin Jiang, Xi Li, Xiao Wang, Min Xu

entry.summary: Improves visual prompt tuning by replacing random prompt initialization with semantic priors: hand-crafted color, texture, and shape descriptors injected into the input space and self-attention maps supplying instance-aware semantics in feature space, combined in a cascaded scheme. Targets parameter-efficient adaptation of frozen vision transformers.

entry.title: CoordRefer: Coordinate-Aware 3D Visual Grounding from Multiview Images

author.name: Haijie Li, Jiaxin Zhang, Dave Zhenyu Chen, Youyu Chen, Yanmin Wu, Jian Zhang

entry.summary: Addresses coordinate-relative ambiguity in multiview image-based 3D visual grounding, where the same box has different numerical forms in different coordinate frames, creating conflicting optimization targets. Decouples reference frame selection from coordinate-conditioned box regression.

entry.title: ALTER: Modeling Longitudinal Changes via Regional Differencing for 3D CT Report Generation

author.name: Dongchen Li, Jitao Liang, Wei Li

entry.summary: Improves 3D CT radiology report generation by explicitly modeling patient-specific longitudinal change within anatomical regions and aggregating interval changes that span multiple regions into a coherent global assessment. Addresses the limitation that prior region-based methods focus only on the current examination.

entry.title: Iterative Hybrid Discrete-Continuous Viewpoint Planning for UAV Photogrammetry

author.name: Alan Grech, Daniel Pisani, Andre Grima, Carl James Debono, Saviour Formosa, Dylan Seychell

entry.summary: An iterative planner for UAV photogrammetry that mixes discrete viewpoint selection with continuous pose refinement, scoring candidate views on frontality, distance, parallax, overlap, and graph connectivity derived from a proxy reconstruction. The aim is to fix local reconstruction errors that fixed lawnmower flight patterns produce. It is an applied geometry and planning contribution rather than a learning one.

entry.title: Accurate Localization of Road Traffic Objects on the Road Plane Using Surveillance Camera Imagery

author.name: Jan Gawro\'nski, Witold Czajewski

entry.summary: A two-stage pipeline for localizing vehicles on the road plane from monocular roadside surveillance, first detecting with a YOLO-family detector and then regressing four footprint corner points with a ResNet backbone. This avoids the large perspective and parallax errors from using bounding-box centers, especially for elevated cameras and large vehicles. It targets traffic monitoring and conflict analysis.

entry.title: CFGPNet: Cross-Attention-Based Fused Gradient Programmed Network Framework for Multispectral Object Detection

author.name: Nima Hatami, Karim Faez, Saeed Sharifian, Hamidreza Amindavar

entry.summary: CFGPNet fuses visible and infrared imagery for multispectral object detection using a re-parameterized GELAN backbone and a computationally efficient cross-attention module, aiming at low-light and adverse-weather robustness. Existing RGB-thermal fusion approaches are criticized for weak cross-modal interaction and heavy attention cost. The emphasis is on accuracy at manageable compute.

entry.title: Sliding Sensors: Configurable Confidence in State Estimation for Continuum Robots

author.name: Ella Walsh, Spencer Teetaert, Eric Diller, Timothy D. Barfoot, Jessica Burgner-Kahrs

entry.summary: This extended abstract proposes mechanically sliding a sensor along a continuum robot so that state-estimation confidence can be concentrated where the task requires it, rather than optimizing uniform global accuracy. A hardware concept demonstrates feasibility of longitudinal sensor translation. It reframes uncertainty as something to be physically shaped, not just estimated.

entry.title: IcFuzz: Fuzzing Isaac Sim with Semantic Stage Guidance and Multi-level Mutation

author.name: Zhixiang Chen, Zhuangbin Chen, Ruoxi Jia, Zeqin Liao, Wei Li, Jinyang Liu, Zibin Zheng

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.06088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robotics simulators serve as a foundational infrastructure for embodied AI, facilitating safe and scalable robotic system development. NVIDIA Isaac Sim...

entry.title: VIDP: Variable Impedance Diffusion Policy for Compliant Robot Manipulation from Diverse Demonstrations

author.name: Hisham Khalil, Neil Fernandes, Thomas M. Kwok, Hsiu-Chin Lin, Yue Hu

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.06210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Contact-rich manipulation requires precise tracking and mechanical compliance, where variable impedance control can improve robustness in task success,...

entry.title: A Master-Salve Robot Manipulator for Needle-Based Teleoperation in MRI Chamber

author.name: Omar Curiel, Jing-Yuan Huang, Po-Chih Chen, Ji Ma, Qing Dai, Wenqi Zhou, David Lu, Holden H. Wu, Tsu-Chin Tsao

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.06354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a MR safe, master-slave robot manipulator for abdominal interventions in the MRI chamber. A human operated 2+1-DoF master controller manipul...

entry.title: $\omega$-0: A Latent Predictive World Action Model for Concurrent Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Zhe Li, Zhenzhe Zhang, Yangyang Wei, Wenjie Zhang, Xichen Yuan, Peiyuan Zhi, Gen Li, Xinying Guo, Fengjie Gao, Jianfei Yang, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.06375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Humanoid household tasks often require concurrent loco-manipulation, where the robot must move, adjust posture, maintain balance, and manipulate object...

entry.title: Transcutaneous Spinal Cord Stimulation Disrupts Conscious Ankle Proprioception and Produces a More Constrained Locomotor Pattern in Unimpaired Adults

author.name: Christopher A. Johnson, Andria J. Farrens, Parastoo Ali Pour, Arjan Gillan, Hui Zhong, David J. Reinkensmeyer, Alexandra S. Voloshina

entry.summary: A human-subjects study of transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation in fourteen unimpaired adults, finding that stimulation degrades conscious ankle proprioception and yields a more constrained walking pattern, with an unstimulated control group doing identical training. Uses a bilateral robotic assessment to quantify proprioceptive acuity. Relevant to neurorehabilitation protocols that assume stimulation is uniformly beneficial.

entry.title: Acoustic-driven millimetric helical robot: ultrasonic synergistic manipulation in confined fluidic environment

author.name: Hanlin Wang, Xin Wang, Xinwei Wei, Jiaxu Liu, Le Wang, Shengze Cai, Chao Xu

entry.summary: Proposes driving millimeter-scale helical robots through fluids using coordinated multiple acoustic fields, combining radiation forces with acoustic streaming to boost propulsion in confined spaces. Multiphysics simulation plus bench experiments demonstrate planar navigation and climbing on inclines. Relevant to untethered medical microrobotics rather than to AI methods.

entry.title: ASTELD: A Six-Axis Classification Framework for Autonomous AI Agents - Design, Evaluation, and an OpenClaw Case Study

author.name: Siyuan Li, Peng Shu, Churan Yu, Peilong Wang, Ruidong Zhang, Bowen Guo, Xinliang Li, Ruiyu Yan, Arif Hassan Zidan, Yi Pan, Wei Ruan, Lifeng Chen, Junhao Chen, Zhaojun Ding, Yiwei Li, Zhengliang Liu, Haixing Dai, Lin Zhao, Yu Bao, Xiang Li, Wei Zhang, Tianming Liu

entry.summary: ASTELD proposes a six-axis operational taxonomy for autonomous agent platforms covering architecture, security posture, tool integration, execution paradigm, autonomy level, and deployment topology, applied to eight frameworks with one in-depth case study. It aims to give the field a common vocabulary for comparing agent design choices.

entry.title: IMMENSE: Inductive Multi-perspective User Classification in Social Networks

author.name: Francesco Benedetti, Antonio Pellicani, Gianvito Pio, Michelangelo Ceci

entry.summary: IMMENSE detects malicious social network accounts using an inductive hybrid classifier that combines post semantics with additional user and network perspectives, aimed at supporting law enforcement at platform scale. Inductive design allows classification of previously unseen users.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Online Traffic Scheduling in Time-Sensitive Application

author.name: Marcos Carvalho, Fatih Temiz, Shavbo Salehi, Melike Erol-Kantarci, Daniel F. Macedo

entry.summary: A companion study applying multi-agent reinforcement learning to online time-sensitive networking traffic scheduling for latency-critical extended-reality flows in mobile edge computing. It argues that static optimization and centralized learning fail to capture evolving traffic and inter-queue dependencies.

entry.title: MS-MLB: An Open Machine Learning Benchmark for Blood-Based MS Classification

author.name: Adam Simson, Ankush Dutta, Quang Bui

entry.summary: Provides a reproducible open benchmark for classifying multiple sclerosis versus healthy controls from whole-blood RNA expression using a single public cohort under a leakage-controlled shared pipeline. The authors explicitly caution that such a classifier cannot substitute for clinical diagnosis.

entry.title: Robot Learning from Human Demonstrations: Handwritten Alphabet Trajectories and Human-Likeness Evaluation

author.name: Alperen Kenan, Paul Bremner, Manuel Giuliani

entry.summary: Presents a learning-from-demonstration pipeline for human-like robot handwriting, with a new dataset of about 3,142 touchscreen demonstrations from 22 participants across all Latin character-case combinations, probabilistic trajectory learning, and a perceptual human-likeness user study. Targets trust and naturalness in human-robot interaction.

entry.title: Clinical Communication Processing with Models Trained on LLM-Generated Synthetic Data: A Structured Survey and Novel Application Case Studies

author.name: Alexander Apartsin, Yehudit Aperstein

entry.summary: Surveys the use of LLM-generated synthetic data for training clinical communication models, covering patient descriptions, clinician instructions, handovers, and shift reports, and adds novel application case studies. Motivated by the scarcity of annotated authentic clinical dialogue.

entry.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing LLMs for Rule-Intensive Review of National Standard Documents

author.name: Tao Wang, Qihao Yang, Rongjiao Liang, Lianghong Lin, Haitao Wang, Xinyu Cao, Tianyong Hao

entry.summary: Introduces the first benchmark for structured intrinsic quality review of Chinese national standard documents, testing LLMs on scope, terminology, normative wording, and cross-section consistency rules over long structured texts. Also proposes enhancements to improve model performance on the task.

entry.title: LoDA: A Level of Detection Aware Method and a Multimodal Sensing Benchmark for Object Level Change Detection

author.name: Haitian Wang, Xinyu Wang, Sheldon Fung, Xian Zhang, Zichen Geng

entry.summary: Proposes an object-level 3D change detection pipeline for multi-temporal urban LiDAR that combines detection-limit-aware registration, rule-based semantic and instance proxies, and displacement cues in height, volume, and surface-normal direction to assign five change labels. Accompanied by a multimodal sensing benchmark.

entry.title: Dual-Output Multi-Exposure HDR Reconstruction via SDR Fusion and Gain Map Inverse Tone Mapping

author.name: Jinho Kim, Jinwoo Kim, Seon Joo Kim

entry.summary: Presents a dual-output multi-exposure HDR framework that synthesizes a perceptually balanced SDR image with a LoRA-adapted latent diffusion model and dual cross-attention fusion of bracketed exposures, then uses it to guide a gain map network for inverse tone mapping. Evaluated on standard HDR benchmarks with reference and no-reference metrics.

entry.title: URNet: A Unified Reparameterized Network for Efficient RGB-D Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Guoan Xu, Zhengxue Wang, Yang Xiao, Ligeng Chen, Guangwei Gao, Dongchen Zhu

entry.summary: Replaces the usual dual-encoder plus fusion-module design for RGB-D semantic segmentation with a single reparameterized encoder that performs multi-modal extraction and cross-modal fusion jointly, compacting the architecture for fast inference. Targets the redundant computation of a separate depth branch.

entry.title: A Multi-Layer System for Ultra-High-Resolution Static 360-Degree Telepresence

author.name: Jiapeng Chi, Gerd Bruder, Carsten Neumann, Carolina Cruz-Neira, Dirk Reiners

entry.summary: A three-layer telepresence system combining an 8K panoramic camera with a steerable 4K pan-tilt-zoom camera, offline-stitching high-detail scans into an ultra-high-resolution static background layered with dynamic content. It targets installations with fixed viewpoints and largely static scenes, where display and capture resolution is the binding constraint. The contribution is systems engineering for immersive presence.

entry.title: A System for Train Condition Monitoring and Structural Health Assessment of Rail Vehicles

author.name: Maximilian Posner, Martin Dazer, Daniela Lauer, Robert Winkler-H\"ohn, Mathilde Laporte, Tobias Herrmann, Martin K\"oppel

entry.summary: An industrial system for real-time rail vehicle condition monitoring and impact detection, motivated by the gap that camera, radar, and lidar perception detects objects but cannot reliably confirm collisions or drive-over events. It supports the push toward higher grades of automation on mainline rail where safety requirements are stringent. The contribution is a deployed sensing and assessment architecture.

entry.title: Coherence-Oriented Dream Scene Visualisation

author.name: Azra A\c{c}{\i}l, Simon Colton

entry.summary: The Dream Scene Visualiser splits written dream reports into four chronological segments with an LLM, generates a coherent four-panel image sequence, and regenerates panels that fail text-image matching. It is evaluated on 50 DreamBank descriptions with CLIP, DINOv2, and a vision-language judge.

entry.title: Turing's Frist Imitation Game: Design Concepts and a Human-Approximates-Machine Reading

author.name: Sharon Temtsin, Christoph Bartneck

entry.summary: A historical and conceptual reading of Turing's 1948 report, extracting design principles behind his chess-based imitation game, including that machines may err, that irrelevant physical features are excluded, and that intellectual activity is largely search. The authors argue that restricting the human contestant to a weak chess player makes the game a human-approximates-machine test.

entry.title: BlockPython: A Process-Aware Agent-Supported Platform for the Transition from Block-Based to Python Programming

author.name: Jesse Yusuf Chan (Zexi Chen), Haoming Wang, Mingwei Xu, Xianlong Xu

entry.summary: BlockPython is an agent-supported learning platform that scaffolds the transition from block-based to Python programming through bidirectional block-code translation across four staged activities, while collecting process evidence such as block artifacts and interaction traces. It targets the cognitive gap between understanding computational concepts and expressing them in text syntax.

entry.title: A Study of ASR Adaptation and Representation Dimensionality Reduction in Persian Speech Emotion Recognition Using Whisper

author.name: Ali Shendabadi, Parnia Izadirad, Mostafa Salehi

entry.summary: A study of Persian speech emotion recognition that reduces Whisper encoder embeddings with PCA instead of learned projections, aggregates via attention pooling, and tests whether Persian ASR fine-tuning helps emotion transfer. The emphasis is on parameter efficiency for a low-resource language.

entry.title: Dual-Attention and Adversarial Transfer Networks for Sim-to-Real Cross-Orientation Wireless Sensing

author.name: Linfeng Du, Kehan Wu, Tong Zhang, Rui Wang

entry.summary: Tackles orientation sensitivity in millimeter-wave human activity recognition by building a physics-guided simulator that synthesizes orientation-diverse training data from single-orientation motion, plus a dual-attention network for orientation-robust features and adversarial unsupervised transfer to bridge the simulation-reality gap. Reduces the need for exhaustive multi-orientation data collection.

entry.title: SciQNet: Two-Stage Multimodal Adaptation for Scientific Image Quality Assessment

author.name: Yin-Loon Khor, Yi-Jie Wong, Jing Jie Tan, Ming Jie Lee

entry.summary: Introduces a two-stage multimodal framework for assessing scientific image quality, which depends on scientific informativeness as well as visual clarity, using domain-adaptive pretraining on scientific document images followed by joint scoring and understanding fine-tuning. Combines instruction tuning, a Huber loss over rating-word logits, and multiple-choice understanding supervision.

entry.title: Dense-Cast: A lightweight ensemble of deep learning architectures for precipitation nowcasting

author.name: Gourav Jyoti Kalita, Hidam Kumarjit Singh

entry.summary: Dense-Cast is a lightweight ensemble combining DenseNet-style blocks, residual connections, and transformer encoders for half-hourly precipitation nowcasting, evaluated on Northeast India. The emphasis is on reduced parameter count while capturing spatiotemporal dependencies. It targets disaster preparedness in a high-rainfall region.

entry.title: A Special Point Skeleton Reconstruction Algorithm for Dynamic Multiobjective Optimization

author.name: GuangXian Gan, MinRong Chen

entry.summary: SPSR-DMOEA improves dynamic multi-objective evolutionary optimization by extracting centroid, knee, and extreme points from the current Pareto set and reconstructing a skeleton whose anchor positions are predicted forward when the environment changes. This exploits structural relationships among representative solutions rather than migrating individuals independently. It targets faster recovery after environmental shifts.

entry.title: Fuzzy network jump models for soft dynamic clustering of graph-structured data

author.name: Federico P. Cortese

entry.summary: Proposes a fuzzy jump model for soft clustering of time-varying signals observed at nodes of a weighted graph, with regularization that encourages smooth membership across neighboring nodes and consecutive time steps. Estimation uses an alternating optimization exploiting the quadratic penalty structure, validated on simulations and San Francisco traffic network data. Aimed at interpretable regime detection in spatiotemporal networks.

entry.title: Learning Latent Memory States from Longitudinal Athlete Monitoring Data

author.name: Dae-Jin Lee

entry.summary: Argues for treating a learned summary of recent longitudinal history, called a Latent Memory Table, as a first-class reusable statistical object comparable to principal component scores or random effects estimates, rather than as a byproduct of an encoder. Validation is structured around six properties including recoverability, personalization, and temporal coherence, demonstrated on athlete monitoring data. The emphasis is on workflow reusability and uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: CourseGraph: Finding overlaps and differences in Computer Science courses across universities

author.name: Arthur Nijdam, Paul Stankovski Wagner, Sara Ramezanian

entry.summary: CourseGraph automates assessment of overlap between external and home-curriculum courses for student mobility programs by scraping titles, descriptions, and learning outcomes and comparing them with BERT-style semantic representations. It mimics the manual process curriculum administrators follow.

entry.title: Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for Herd-Level Cattle Growth Pattern and Weight Gain Forecasting in Grazing-Based Production Systems

author.name: Muhammad Riaz Hasib Hossain, Rafiqul Islam, Shawn R. McGrath, Md Zahidul Islam, David W. Lamb

entry.summary: Develops a hybrid machine learning framework combining residual, stacked, cascade, and ensemble architectures for herd-level cattle weight forecasting from irregular grazing sensor data collected in southeastern Australia, benchmarked against ARIMA, LSTM, and GRU. Animal-level predictions are temporally aggregated into herd trajectories.

entry.title: Beyond Sentiment: Comparing Traditional NLP and LLM-Based Multi-Dimensional Analysis for Political News Evaluation

author.name: Maryam Fooladi, Federico Bottino

entry.summary: The authors compare a RoBERTa sentiment classifier with an LLM-based multidimensional framing analysis over 50 political news articles from 17 outlets. They report that the classifier labels 70 percent of articles neutral, a collapse that erases rhetorical and ideological content that the LLM pipeline surfaces.

entry.title: Vibe Compiler: A Research-Logic Synthesis Tool That Runs without Prompt Engineering -Toward Enhancing Metacognition for Sustaining Agency in the Age of Generative AI-

author.name: Riichiro Mizoguchi, Tomoki Aburatani, Kento Koike, Machi Shimmei

entry.summary: The Vibe Compiler is a tool built on a synthesis-analysis reciprocity model that helps researchers convert loose ideas into explicit research logic while preserving epistemic agency, without requiring prompt engineering. The stated motivation is that generative AI used as a capable servant erodes critical evaluation of AI-produced reasoning.

entry.title: Handling Missing Data in Probabilistic Regression Trees

author.name: Taiane Schaedler Prass, Alisson Silva Neimaier, Guilherme Pumi

entry.summary: Extends probabilistic regression trees so that missing predictor values are handled natively during tree construction rather than via prior imputation, with three strategies that preserve probability conservation and marginal compatibility. Aims at tabular regression settings with arbitrary missingness patterns.

entry.title: Design and Evaluation of a Touchscreen-Based Teleoperation Interface for Robotic Manipulators

author.name: Juan Jos\'e Garc\'ia C\'ardenas, Alperen Kenan, Hamidreza Raei, Paul Bremner, Manuel Giuliani, Arash Ajoudani, Adriana Tapus

entry.summary: Designs and user-tests a touchscreen teleoperation interface that maps finger motion directly to manipulator motion with integrated visualization, aimed at nuclear-industry surface tasks like swab sampling. A study with 20 participants compares it against conventional joystick control on precision and workload. It is human-robot interaction rather than autonomy research.

entry.title: LiteKD-Net: Lightweight Knowledge-Distilled Network for Mobile Image Denoising

author.name: Zhou Zhiyi

entry.summary: LiteKD-Net builds a lightweight mobile denoiser by simulating realistic sensor noise including pixel crosstalk, adapting a Real-ESRGAN teacher, and distilling into a depthwise-separable student. The goal is good restoration quality without on-device inference overhead or large paired clean-noisy datasets. It is a straightforward pipeline engineering contribution.

entry.title: Challenges in Evaluating Explanation Methods for Static and Evolving Data

author.name: Jerzy Stefanowski

entry.summary: A workshop-style discussion of why explainable AI evaluation remains inadequate, illustrated with a bias-detection and concept-unlearning image system, a human-grounded explanation study, and the problem of adapting counterfactual explanations to drifting data streams. It closes by framing the co-evolution of data, models, and explanations as an open challenge.

entry.title: An Emerging Retail Portfolio Management Application: Personalized, Tax-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Natural Language Goals

author.name: Ramin Pishehvar

entry.summary: An application paper describing an integration-tested system where a retail investor states a goal in natural language, the goal is routed to one of six mandates, and a three-phase reinforcement learning stack produces a tax-aware, broker-integrated portfolio recommendation. The pitch is bringing institutional-grade personalization to individuals.

entry.title: JTA: Joint Testability Architecture for Scenario-Based Validation of Safety-Critical Software

author.name: Wenyao Xue, Jiandi Wang, Yichen Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Joint Testability Architecture, a framework that treats the test scenario, the test system, and the system under test as one analyzable object, characterized along controllability, observability, and isolability. The goal is to make scenario-based validation of safety-critical software produce verdicts that can be traced to actionable causes. It is conceptual systems-engineering guidance rather than an empirical result.

entry.title: Counterfactual Analysis via Large Language Models

author.name: Zonghao Yang

entry.summary: Applies GPT-3.5 to counterfactual return-on-investment estimation for online lending interest-rate schemes, comparing it to gradient-boosted regression. Prompt engineering raises R-squared from about 2.0 to 2.8 percent versus 3.5 percent for the gradient-boosted baseline.

entry.title: Stability of Ranking-dependent Pair-wise Comparison Patterns in the Analytic Hierarchy Process

author.name: Vitaliy Tsyganok, Sergii Kadenko, Oleh Andriichuk

entry.summary: Compares three incomplete ranking-dependent pairwise comparison patterns used within the Analytic Hierarchy Process, namely best-worst, best-second-best, and the maximum difference method, and derives conditions under which their stability to expert errors can be compared. The aim is to cut the number of comparisons experts must perform.

entry.title: From Siloed Algorithms to Compliance-First Agentic Platforms: A Multi-Layered Architecture for Hospital AI Systems

author.name: Manideep Dhar, Ritwik Singh, Sharat Chandra Kumar Manikonda

entry.summary: A blueprint paper proposing a layered, compliance-first agentic architecture for hospital AI, including an agent orchestration layer spanning clinical and operational workflows, aimed at the widely cited failure of most healthcare AI pilots to scale. It is a reference architecture rather than an implemented or evaluated system.

entry.title: Automatic Detection of Deaths from Social Networking Sites

author.name: Nuhu Ibrahim, Riza Batista-Navarro

entry.summary: A dissertation-derived study of linguistic differences between pre- and post-mortem social media content, building a dataset from Wikidata and Twitter and comparing classical classifiers, BiLSTM, CNN, and BERT for detecting that an account holder has died. Random forest led among traditional models while transformer models performed best overall.

entry.title: Example-Guided Prompting for Document-Level Text Simplification

author.name: Marina Litvak, Ariel Perstin, Ilan Shtilman, Michael F\"arber

entry.summary: Studies whether retrieving parallel document-simplification examples into prompts improves document-level text simplification by LLMs, testing on an English readability corpus with multiple models. Finds example-guided prompting can supply patterns that instructions alone do not convey.

entry.title: NeuroAdaptTrainer: A Fiji/ImageJ Plugin for YOLO-Based Neuron Segmentation, InteractiveCorrection and Transfer Learning

author.name: Daniela Eraso-Casas, Gerard Villarroya-Pique, Esther Serrano-Pertierra, M. Teresa Fern\'andez-S\'anchez, Antonello Novellie, Angel Rio-Alvarez, V\'ictor M. Gonz\'alez

entry.summary: Releases an open-source Fiji/ImageJ plugin that embeds a YOLO instance-segmentation model for neuron counting, supports in-tool manual correction of detections, and uses those corrections for transfer learning to new imaging conditions. Includes an external validation module comparing base and adapted models.

entry.title: Shape-Aware Oriented Bounding Box (OBB) to Horizontal Bounding Box (HBB) Conversion

author.name: Badha Rathna Sabhapathy, Gotam Dahiya, Vishesh Vatsal

entry.summary: A geometric post-processing method that converts oriented bounding boxes to tighter horizontal bounding boxes for ship detection in satellite imagery, using hull shape, hull fullness, and box orientation. Standard conversions either include excess background or clip real object extent. The method is benchmarked against conventional conversion baselines.

entry.title: QuanTiMedAI: Quantum-Enhanced Time-Series Model guided by Agentic AI for Cardiac Arrest Mortality Prediction

author.name: Mutasim Fuad Sarker, Adiba Rahman Namira, Wafa Binte Alam, Md Adnan Arefeen, Mahzabeen Emu, Sumaiya Tabassum Nimi

entry.summary: QuanTiMedAI predicts cardiac-arrest ICU mortality by pairing an agentic LLM for clinically informed feature discovery with a compact quantum recurrent time-series model over the ICU stay rather than early-admission snapshots. The temporal framing is the more defensible part of the contribution.

entry.title: Challenges for Musical Education in the Age of AI and Digital Transformation

author.name: Jean-Pierre Briot

entry.summary: A reflective essay on how generative AI, streaming platforms, and digital audio workstations jointly reshape what and how music should be taught. It argues music education faces one of its most consequential turning points and outlines pedagogical implications.

entry.title: The interface of intonation and lexical tone: Boundary phenomena in Mandarin varieties

author.name: Cong Zhang, Yiya Chen

entry.summary: A linguistics book chapter reviewing how intonation and lexical tone interact in Mandarin varieties, focusing on fundamental frequency at intonational boundaries and the resulting communicative and attitudinal functions. Discusses theoretical models and analysis techniques.

entry.title: Controllable Clothing: Precise Labels and Generation for Virtual Try-On with Latent Diffusion Models

author.name: Max Rehman Linder

entry.summary: A short technical report on virtual try-on that uses open-source models to auto-label garment attributes such as length and style, then trains adapters on those labels so users can control generated garment fit. The stated goal is helping retailers produce images faithful to actual fit rather than misleading consumers. It is an applied e-commerce pipeline description.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 06, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's batch is dominated by measurement science and pretraining-mechanism studies. The headline item is a large-scale controlled study of natively unified multimodal pretraining, disentangling knowledge flow and modality synergy across language, visual understanding, and visual generation, and distilling early-unification training recipes with direct relevance to omni-model builders.

Safety, alignment and evaluation validity

  • FAR.AI's AI Security Leaderboard composes 67 accessible static jailbreak techniques into a very large attack surface and proposes a minimal safeguard standard for frontier deployments
  • Chain-of-thought monitoring is shown unreliable in *implicit-influence* settings, undercutting a load-bearing assumption in frontier-lab safety plans; a companion paper formalizes a faithfulness-vs-safety tension
  • Item Response Theory applied to 8 safety benchmarks across 192 models (with UK AISI) is the largest psychometric analysis of safety evaluations to date
  • SciCode-Verified audits all 65 problems and finds 263 defects, 192 of which reject correct solutions, meaning published scientific-coding ability was underestimated
  • Related eval-integrity work shows pre/post-training-cutoff score comparisons are uninformative as contamination tests, and that reachability ≠ realization in benchmark gains

Efficiency, long context, and interpretability

  • AnchorKV achieves ~20× KV-cache compression using exact anchor vectors plus residual encodings of remaining tokens
  • PI-Mem pushes long-context reasoning to 3.6M tokens via parallel-iterative memory rather than sequential recurrence
  • Production Microsoft Azure measurements deliver the first architectural characterization of agentic workloads, actionable for inference-serving design
  • Sparse Weight Decomposition factorizes pretrained projections into sparse factors, offering an alternative to SAEs and transcoders for circuit extraction
  • A scoped negative result shows privileged-information-conditioned teachers break self-distillation, challenging a popular compute-efficient post-training shortcut; agentic memory, robotics (BridgeVLA++), and world-model RL (WorldCycle) form a secondary cluster
entry.content:
Today's batch is dominated by measurement science and pretraining-mechanism studies. The headline item is a large-scale controlled study of natively unified multimodal pretraining, disentangling knowledge flow and modality synergy across language, visual understanding, and visual generation, and distilling early-unification training recipes with direct relevance to omni-model builders.

Safety, alignment and evaluation validity

  • FAR.AI's AI Security Leaderboard composes 67 accessible static jailbreak techniques into a very large attack surface and proposes a minimal safeguard standard for frontier deployments
  • Chain-of-thought monitoring is shown unreliable in *implicit-influence* settings, undercutting a load-bearing assumption in frontier-lab safety plans; a companion paper formalizes a faithfulness-vs-safety tension
  • Item Response Theory applied to 8 safety benchmarks across 192 models (with UK AISI) is the largest psychometric analysis of safety evaluations to date
  • SciCode-Verified audits all 65 problems and finds 263 defects, 192 of which reject correct solutions, meaning published scientific-coding ability was underestimated
  • Related eval-integrity work shows pre/post-training-cutoff score comparisons are uninformative as contamination tests, and that reachability ≠ realization in benchmark gains

Efficiency, long context, and interpretability

  • AnchorKV achieves ~20× KV-cache compression using exact anchor vectors plus residual encodings of remaining tokens
  • PI-Mem pushes long-context reasoning to 3.6M tokens via parallel-iterative memory rather than sequential recurrence
  • Production Microsoft Azure measurements deliver the first architectural characterization of agentic workloads, actionable for inference-serving design
  • Sparse Weight Decomposition factorizes pretrained projections into sparse factors, offering an alternative to SAEs and transcoders for circuit extraction
  • A scoped negative result shows privileged-information-conditioned teachers break self-distillation, challenging a popular compute-efficient post-training shortcut; agentic memory, robotics (BridgeVLA++), and world-model RL (WorldCycle) form a secondary cluster

entry.title: Towards Physics of Multimodal Pretraining: Knowledge Flow, Modality Synergy, Early Unification, and Recipes

author.name: Junlin Han, Shengbang Tong, David Fan, Minghao Chen, Philip Torr, Filippos Kokkinos, Mike Lewis

entry.summary: A systematic controlled study of natively unified multimodal pretraining that disentangles how language, visual understanding, and visual generation transfer knowledge, when data composition produces synergy versus competition, and when modalities should be unified during training. It distills the findings into practical recipes and runs experiments on both synthetic and large-scale real datasets.

entry.title: AI Security Leaderboard: Methodology, Results and Minimal Standard

author.name: Jasper Timm, Lukas Struppek, Ziwei Xu, Grace Cheong, Oscar Mata, Dan Zhao, Mick Yang, Isadora De Andrade, Xiaojun Jia, Yiming Li, Samuel Bauer, Heather McIntyre, Adam Gleave, Edward Yee, Kellin Pelrine

entry.summary: FAR.AI introduces a minimal standard for frontier model safeguards built from 67 accessible static jailbreak techniques composed into a very large attack space, and benchmarks flagship models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI against 360 CBRNE and offensive-cyber attacker goals. The work provides rare public evidence on how consistently layered safeguards hold up across developers.

entry.title: SciCode-Verified: How Benchmark Defects Underestimated the Scientific-Coding Ability of Language Models

author.name: Sihan Hu, Lyuhan Huang, Youjin Deng, Kun Chen

entry.summary: A domain-expert audit of all 65 problems in the SciCode scientific-coding benchmark uncovered 263 defects, 192 of which cause correct solutions to be graded wrong, spanning 91 percent of main problems. The authors argue the apparent plateau of 2026 frontier models near 60 percent subproblem accuracy is partly an artifact of the benchmark rather than a real capability ceiling, and release a corrected version.

entry.title: Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Can Be Unreliable in Implicit-Influence Settings

author.name: Agatha Duzan, Asa Cooper Stickland

entry.summary: Argues that most chain-of-thought monitorability evaluations study explicit-influence settings where the prompt tells the model to hide something, and introduces the first benchmark comparing those against implicit-influence settings where behavior is shaped by context such as an irrelevant biasing detail. It finds monitoring reliability degrades in the implicit regime.

entry.title: Architectural Implications of Agentic AI Workflows

author.name: Jirong Yang, Peizhe Liu, Chaojie Zhang, Jovan Stojkovic

entry.summary: Provides what the authors call the first architectural characterization of agentic AI workloads, combining a production study at Microsoft Azure with controlled experiments on open-source frameworks. It shows that agentic requests fragment into interleaved LLM calls, tool invocations, and orchestration that repeatedly cross the CPU-GPU boundary, putting the host CPU on the critical path with bursty, low-average load.

entry.title: Item Response Theory for AI Safety

author.name: Joshua Fonseca Rivera (Independent), Neil Shah (Independent), David Demitri Africa (UK AI Security Institute), Konstantinos Voudouris (UK AI Security Institute)

entry.summary: Applies Item Response Theory to eight safety benchmarks across 192 language models, described as the largest psychometric analysis of LLM safety evaluation so far, and recovers three interpretable latent factors: refusal strictness, truthfulness, and contextual harm. This addresses the problem that aggregate safety scores are hard to interpret when benchmarks overlap heavily and models may sandbag.

entry.title: AnchorKV: Anchor-Residual KV Cache Compression
