author.name: Malik Khalaf, Yara Shamshoum, Nitzan Hodos, Yuval Sieradzki, Assaf Schuster

entry.summary: AnchorKV compresses the KV cache roughly 20-fold by storing a small set of exact anchor vectors and representing every other token as a residual relative to its nearest anchor, refining only the tokens whose approximation most affects outputs. Unlike eviction schemes it never permanently discards a token, avoiding catastrophic failures when a dropped token later matters.

entry.title: Privileged, but Biased: How PI-Conditioned Teachers Break Self-Distillation

author.name: Sarthak Harne, Chinmay Karkar, Yash Pandya, Ahmed Awadallah, Akshay Nambi

entry.summary: Tests whether self-distillation from a teacher conditioned on privileged information such as a reference solution actually teaches anything when used as the sole objective without a reward term. Reported gains reproduce only in easy settings; across question answering, math, coding, and multi-turn tool use, at multiple model sizes and forms of privileged information, the benefit disappears on difficult tasks.

entry.title: PI-Mem: Pushing Long-Context Reasoning to 3.6M Tokens with Parallel-Iterative Memory

author.name: Dawei Liu, Haixu Song, Shuang Cheng, Shijie Wang, Haozheng Hou, Kaifeng Liu, Ermo Hua, Zhonghang Yuan, Zhijie Zhong, Yuchen Fan, Biqing Qi, Bowen Zhou

entry.summary: Presents a parallel-iterative memory mechanism that reads all context chunks simultaneously against a shared memory and refines that memory over a bounded number of turns, instead of sequential recurrent chunk updates. Claims long-context reasoning scaling to roughly 3.6 million tokens while avoiding early-evidence overwriting and serial latency growth.

entry.title: Temporal Leakage in LLM Backtesting: Measurement, Validation, and Adjusted Scores

author.name: Zeyu Zhang, Bradly C. Stadie

entry.summary: Argues that the standard contamination test of comparing model scores before and after the training cutoff is uninformative, showing four flagship models fail it on questions that resolved only after their cutoffs. The authors prove no passive backtest can separate recency-driven knowledge from leakage, and propose using known cutoffs or matched clean controls to produce leakage-adjusted scores.

entry.title: BridgeVLA++: A Data-Efficient, Generalizable, and Memory-Augmented Vision-Language-Action Framework for 3D Manipulation

author.name: Peiyan Li, Yuze Zhu, Yixiang Chen, Qisen Ma, Yuan Xu, Jiabing Yang, He Guan, Yan Huang, Hongtao Wu, Xiao Ma, Tao Kong, Liang Wang, Tieniu Tan

entry.summary: An extension of the BridgeVLA vision-language-action framework for 3D robotic manipulation that adds explicit memory of past observations while keeping the trick of projecting point clouds into multi-view images and predicting intermediate heatmaps so the pre-trained VLM input-output alignment is preserved. The goal is to make 3D VLA policies work with less training data, generalize under distribution shift, and handle tasks that require remembering earlier states. Matters because memory and data efficiency are two of the biggest practical blockers for deploying manipulation policies outside curated lab settings.

entry.title: Toward Skill-Native LLMs: Skill Entropy for Benchmarking and Training Long-Horizon Reasoning

author.name: Yinghui He, Ling Yang, Jiarui Liu, Yongjin Yang, Lechen Zhang, Yingcheng Wu, Zhenfei Yin, Mengdi Wang, Sanjeev Arora

entry.summary: Defines Skill Entropy as a measure of how hard it is to switch between reasoning skills mid-chain and builds Skill-squared-Bench, a benchmark of cross-skill long-horizon tasks spanning 558 skills across nine domains. It then uses the measure on the training side as well, aiming at LLMs that natively compose heterogeneous skills within one reasoning trace.

entry.title: Risky Business: Measuring The Faithfulness-Safety Tension

author.name: Dominik Meier, Luca Joshua Francis, Marco Bernhard Kaiser, Terry Ruas, Jan Philip Wahle, Bela Gipp

entry.summary: Identifies a tension where reasoning models must be faithful enough that their chain of thought can be monitored, yet robust enough to reject unsafe reasoning injected into that chain. It introduces HazMart, a human-written autonomous-shopkeeper dataset, and a replacement-based faithfulness test that edits the reasoning trace itself rather than planting hints in the prompt.

entry.title: Sparse Weight Decomposition for Efficient Circuit Extraction

author.name: Chuanhao Yan, Xuhan Huang, Yawen Duan, Zhenfei Yin, Hang Zhao, Bryan Dai, Jie Fu

entry.summary: Sparse Weight Decomposition factorizes each pretrained linear projection into two sparse factors whose shared intermediate coordinates act as addressable circuit units, enabling circuit extraction without training a separate sparse replacement network. This avoids the fidelity gap between an auxiliary sparse model and the original weights.

entry.title: Looking under the Wrong Lamppost: On the Limitations of Automated Translation Quality Estimation

author.name: Serge Gladkoff, Angelika Vaasa, Sue Ellen Wright, Ingemar Strandvik, Lifeng Han

entry.summary: Shows empirically and theoretically that supervised fine-tuning suffers severe task conflict in multi-stage multi-task training while reinforcement learning allows tasks to coexist, tracing this to sparse and near-orthogonal parameter updates under RL. Explains the difference through gradient interference that is norm-limited for SFT but variance-limited for RL.

entry.title: OctoLong: Mid-Training On Cross-Repository Code Contexts Enhances Long-Context Modeling

author.name: Indraneil Paul, Falko Helm, Goran Glava\v{s}, Iryna Gurevych

entry.summary: OctoLong builds a context-engineering pipeline that uses an AST parser, a language server, and a package manager to recursively retrieve cross-repository code references, producing dependency-rich training contexts millions of tokens long. It then mid-trains a suite of open long-context instruct models on this data to address the scarcity of genuine long-distance dependencies in existing long-context corpora.

entry.title: Protoreasoning in Tiny Transformers

author.name: Eduardo Valle, Fergal Reid

entry.summary: The authors show that roughly one-million-parameter transformers can benefit from a minimal form of chain of thought, which they call protoreasoning, on Dyck-language tasks well below the scale needed for natural language. This creates a tractable testbed for asking whether step-by-step reasoning reflects general algorithms or collections of heuristics.

entry.title: Gradient Immunity: Null-Space Resistance to Malicious Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yuxuan Huang, Xingyu Zeng, Tianhang Zheng, Chaochao Lu

entry.summary: The paper studies a partially protected open-weight release setting where most weights are trainable but a small safety-critical component is frozen, and proposes a Unidirectional Safety Gate built from a null-space cubic layer plus an inverse adapter after the final transformer block. The gate is designed to block gradients from harmful fine-tuning data while allowing benign adaptation to proceed.

entry.title: MatrAIx: Simulating the World with 8.3 Billion Persona Agents

author.name: Xiaomin Li, Yuexing Hao, Jianheng Hou, Jintao Huang, Qianfeng Wen, Shirley Huang, Yifan Liu, Xiaoyi Liu, Yilan Fan, Yijun Wang, Koutian Wu, Ruoqi Gao, Muhammad Ahmed Mohsin, Jing Tang, Brihi Joshi, Heming Liu, Zheyuan Deng, Zonglin Di, Sankalp Jajee, Jiuyao Lu, Zhiwei Zhang, Saksham Kapoor, Ishan Gupta, Yunhan Zhao, Chanwoo Park, Yucheng Lu, Bing Hu, Weihang Xiao, Aravind Mohan, Hanwen Xing, Runyu Zhang, Mihir Kulshreshtha, Yuanda Xu, Qianyu Zhu, Dianzhuo Wang, Yuxin Xiao, Bowen Jiang, Yongye Su, Wenhao Chai, Zuxin Liu, Lawrence Yunliang Chen, Xuandong Zhao, Ethan Ye, Shivam Patel, Jason Xie, Alex Martin Richmond, Weixiang Ding, Emre Okcular, Diya Mathew, Ziheng Wang, Rana M. Shahroz Khan, Zhejian Peng, Fang Wu, Fan Nie, Xinyang Han, Yubin Kim, Jiawei Zhang, Zhenting Qi, Huangyuan Su, Xu Pan, Abinitha Gourabathina, Hyewon Jeong, Hemanth Neelgund Ramesh, Kumail Alhamoud, Kimia Hamidieh, Zidi Xiong, Samuel Schmidgall, Pengrui Han, Yepeng Huang, Yongheng Wang, Bowen Yang, Alex Gu, Yuchu Wang, Akshay Paruchuri, Brenna Li, Hejie Cui, Jiayuan Ding, Chaosheng Dong, Jiahao Wang, Yixuan He, Chi Wang, Pamela Bhattacharya, Tianyi Peng, Paul Pu Liang, Mitchell Gordon, Yilun Du, Marinka Zitnik, James Zou, Prasanna Tambe, Philip Torr, Emily Fox, Asu Ozdaglar, Dawn Song

entry.summary: MatrAIx is a population-scale infrastructure for evaluating AI systems and digital products against simulated users, built on 8.3 billion persona records described by roughly 1,290 categorical dimensions and sampled from a dependency graph that preserves attribute correlations. The authors release a filtered coreset of about one million personas mixing human-grounded and synthetic profiles.

entry.title: ContextWeave: A Real-World Workflow Benchmark

author.name: Bo Wang, Yuqian Yao, Enxi Wang, Luozhijie Jin, Yang Liu, Yiran Suo, Yuxuan Cai, Enyu Zhou, Yufei Gao, Honglin Guo, Tianyu Huai, Li Ji, Zhikai Lei, Bufan Li, Lizhi Lin, Jinxiu Liu, Jie Yang, Jiazheng Zhou, Maosen Zhou, Pengfang Qian, Shichun Liu, Guanshan Liu, Hao Zheng, Yunhao Yu, Hang Yan, Jihua Kang, Xinchi Chen, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: ContextWeave reconstructs privacy-preserved multi-month office workflows from 14 real participants into roughly a thousand executable tasks with containerized environments, trajectories, and task-specific rubrics, to test whether recalled experience actually improves downstream agent performance. It measures workspace quality and alignment with individual preferences plus diagnostics for relevance, continuity, and robustness.

entry.title: WorldCycle: Self-Verifiable Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Video World Models

author.name: Bohai Gu, Yueyang Yuan, Taiyi Wu, Dazhao Du, Jian Liu, Xiaoyi Pang, Jie Zhang, Xiaocheng Lu, Haobin Zhong, Xiaotong Zhao, Alan Zhao, Song Guo

entry.summary: WorldCycle exploits reversible action cycles to create annotation-free supervision for interactive video world models: a sequence composed with its inverse must analytically return to the starting state, giving a verifiable signal for long-horizon drift where no ground-truth future exists. This enables reinforcement learning post-training against compounding error.

entry.title: Search, Inspect, Fetch: Exploiting Structure-Aware Boolean Retrieval for Deep-Research Agents

author.name: Shuai Wang, Haodong Chen, Yu Yin, Shengyao Zhuang, Bevan Koopman, Guido Zuccon

entry.summary: Sieve replaces the usual search-then-visit loop of deep research agents with a Boolean query language that filters webpage fields, ranks candidates, shows structure-rich result cards, and fetches only the specific sections needed. Across three QA collections it beats the strongest conventional search-visit setup while pulling far less irrelevant text into context.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning with Evolving Rubrics as Rewards for Audio Reasoning

author.name: Fangxu Yu, Tao Feng, Dehai Min, Zinan Lin, Weijia Xu, Michael Xu, Philip S. Yu, Ge Liu, Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes reinforcement learning for audio reasoning where the rubric used to reward intermediate reasoning is generated per question and evolves as the policy improves, rather than being a fixed hand-crafted checklist. This targets a known failure where outcome-only rewards let models guess answers without actually listening to the audio.

entry.title: Reachability Is Not Realization: Tracing the Sources of LLM Benchmark Gains

author.name: Yanchao Li, Wanhao Liu, Jiaqing Xie, Ben Gao, Yanbo Wang, Tianfan Fu, Yuqiang Li

entry.summary: Distinguishes questions a model realizes under its default deployment procedure from those merely reachable by some probe within a fixed budget, and audits benchmark gains question by question under matched budgets. Notably, random inference-time layer routing matches or exceeds structured search in all 43 model-task settings tested, suggesting some reported gains reflect budget rather than capability.

entry.title: When Agents Learn to Be You: Benchmarking Privacy Leakage, Impersonation Risk, and Defenses in Persona Skills

author.name: Yongli Xiang, Zhifang Zhang, Bojun Yang, Ziming Hong, Lei Feng, Miao Xu, Tongliang Liu

entry.summary: AntiSkillBench studies the safety of persona skills, portable artifacts distilled from a user's interaction history for reuse by downstream agents, showing that this concentration of personal signals amplifies privacy leakage and impersonation risk. It provides 7,500 persona-grounded dialogue traces from 50 profiles plus an evaluation suite for leakage, impersonation, and defenses.

entry.title: The RAIL Principles for Neurosymbolic AI: Reasoning, Assurances, Interfacing and Learning

author.name: Agnese Chiatti, Michael Cochez, Cristina Cornelio, Sebastijan Dumancic, Artur d'Avila Garcez, Luis C. Lamb, Lia Morra, Mathias Niepert, Robert Peharz, Alberto Speranzon, Maarten Stol, Annette Ten Teije, Thiviyan Thanapalasingam, Frank Van Harmelen, Emile Van Krieken, Antonio Vergari, Benjie Wang

entry.summary: A community position paper arguing that neurosymbolic integration is not a niche pursuit but already underlies many leading AI systems, organized around four design principles covering reasoning, assurances, interfacing, and learning. It calls for re-examining current system design through this lens for trustworthy, data-efficient deployment.

entry.title: State2State: Environment-Derived Mid-Training for LLM Agents

author.name: Xuanyu Lei, Yiqi Zhu, Chenliang Li, Kaiming Liu, Peng Li, Ming Yan, Jieping Ye, Ya-Qin Zhang, Yang Liu

entry.summary: State2State proposes environment-derived mid-training for LLM agents: instead of expert trajectories or handcrafted verifiers, the agent explores an environment and converts reached states into goal-reaching training objectives. This removes the dependence on externally specified tasks and human-designed reward checks, improving scalability and task diversity.

entry.title: AcceptMoE: Commitment-Weighted Self-Sizing Verifier Expert Sets for Efficient MoE Speculative Decoding

author.name: Shuang Liang (Mark), Hao (Mark), Chen, Zhiwen Mo, Qianzhou Wang, Guoyu Li, Lingxiao Ma, Wayne Luk

entry.summary: AcceptMoE observes that verifying a speculative draft tree on a mixture-of-experts model activates the union of experts across all tree nodes, so cutting token count does not proportionally cut expert-weight traffic. It introduces a verifier-side expert selector that weights router scores by offline-estimated commitment probabilities and self-sizes the eligible expert set.

entry.title: DP-MemView: A Memory Interface for Attribute-Level Transcript Privacy in Long-Term LLM Agents

author.name: Jong Wook Kim, Byoungjae Min, Kennedy Edemacu, Yoonhyuk Choi, Sae-Hong Cho, Beakcheol Jang

entry.summary: DP-MemView formalizes the risk that an LLM agent with long-term memory can cumulatively leak protected attributes across many responses even if it never states them, calling this adaptive transcript privacy. It provides a differentially private memory interface that exposes selected public views rather than raw memory, with per-attribute privacy ledgers and a proof of pure DP over the whole adaptive transcript.

entry.title: Distractor-Aware Truncation: Disentangling Context-Length Effects from Signal Loss in Long-Context LLM Benchmarks

author.name: Mohsen Arjmandi

entry.summary: Tests the common assumption that shorter context is better when relevant information is preserved, by running BABILong and GraphWalks at four retention levels under naive middle-dropping versus distractor-aware truncation that only removes irrelevant content. Evaluations span three Claude model sizes plus a cross-provider OpenAI model to separate genuine context-length effects from accidental signal loss.

entry.title: Attention is Case-Sensitive

author.name: Maximilian Dillitzer, Tin Stribor Sohn, Jason J. Corso, Michael Auerbach

entry.summary: An empirical study across nine LLMs and four vision-language models finding that uppercase or alternating letter casing systematically concentrates internal attention on the affected text spans, mirroring how capitalization draws human visual attention. The effect holds universally in text across every evaluated non-reasoning model regardless of tokenizer.

entry.title: ParVL: Parallel Scaling and Expandable Compute Allocation for Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Yang Yang, Qinyu Zhao, Mouxiang Chen, Xiaohui Li, Lixin Gu, Wenhai Wang, Hongjie Zhang, Wenwei Zhang

entry.summary: ParVL scales multimodal LLMs by reusing existing ViT and LLM backbone parameters across multiple parallel vision and language branches instead of adding parameters or sequential inference steps. It studies how to allocate additional shared-backbone compute between the vision and language sides under a fixed parameter budget.

entry.title: Revealed Rationality: Label-Free Evaluation and Regularization from Representation Theorems

author.name: Isaiah Andrews

entry.summary: This paper imports representation theorems from decision theory to build label-free evaluation and regularization for LLMs: because axioms are necessary and sufficient for rationalizability, axiom compliance can be checked purely from a model's own answers to synthetic choice problems. Passing models cannot be rejected on rationality grounds by any further test of the same kind, and penalties are directly computable for training.

entry.title: Real-time probabilistic tsunami forecasting via generative AI

author.name: Yusuke Oishi, Takashi Furumura, Fumihiko Imamura

entry.summary: A conditional diffusion model produces probabilistic ensembles of onshore tsunami inundation forecasts in real time, replacing deterministic ML predictions that convey false certainty about safe zones. Validated against 2011 Tohoku-oki data, the model tracks observed inundation while providing calibrated uncertainty.

entry.title: Dynamically Allocating Evaluation Effort for Model Ranking

author.name: Vil\'em Zouhar, Julia Kreutzer, Alon Lavie, Tom Kocmi, Matt Post, Ond\v{r}ej Bojar, Mrinmaya Sachan

entry.summary: Formalizes multi-model human evaluation as best-arm identification in a correlated-arm bandit, adaptively allocating annotation budget toward the most competitive systems instead of exhaustively rating everything. Provides optimality proofs and shows improved discrimination at fixed cost.

entry.title: Leak-Resistant Unlearning: A New Benchmark for Evaluating Multi-Hop Reasoning Consistency and Recovery Robustness

author.name: Haoting Qian, Qingjie Zhang, Zhicong Huang, Cheng Hong, Han Qiu

entry.summary: Introduces an unlearning benchmark that stresses two weaknesses of existing evaluations: diverse multi-hop reasoning paths that can leak supposedly removed knowledge, and fragility of unlearning to lightweight post-unlearning adaptation or other recovery attacks. It reframes unlearning evaluation as consistency plus robustness under recovery rather than a static check.

entry.title: When Prompts Become Pixels: Prompt-Region Grounding for Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Yongxin Wang, Ruizhe Zhou, Yueling Tang, Yingying Zhu, Xuemin Zhao, Xiaojun Chang, Xiaodan Liang

entry.summary: Introduces a controlled intervention that moves a benchmark question out of the text prompt and into the image while keeping the underlying problem and answer fixed, revealing accuracy drops in all 24 model-task pairs tested, averaging 17.8 points. Models often transcribe the visual question correctly yet fail to act on it, indicating a semantic channel gap beyond OCR, which the proposed prompt-region grounding partially closes.

entry.title: SSTQ:Privacy-Preserving Vector Quantization via Subsampled Stochastic TurboQuant

author.name: Adel Javanmard, David P. Woodruff, Vahab Mirrokni

entry.summary: SSTQ is a privacy-preserving vector quantization scheme for distributed optimization that combines overcomplete equal-norm tight frames, coordinate subsampling and privacy-aware one-dimensional quantization, in flat randomized-response and metric-aware Laplace variants. It attains optimal mean-squared-error scaling with logarithmic bits per coordinate, improving on prior methods with unfavorable dimension dependence.

entry.title: ArborEnum: Decision Tree Rashomon Sets over Continuous Features

author.name: Zakk Heile, Hayden McTavish, Margo Seltzer, Cynthia Rudin

entry.summary: ArborEnum is presented as the first algorithm to exactly enumerate near-optimal decision-tree Rashomon sets over continuous features, removing the binarization assumption that previous enumerations relied on. Full Rashomon sets matter for robustness analysis, variable importance and letting users choose among equally accurate models.

entry.title: Looking in the Mirror: Introspecting Side-Effect Misalignments Induced by Fine-Tuning

author.name: Kotaro Yoshida, Laura Gomezjurado Gonzalez, Yukinori Yamamoto, Yuji Naraki, Ryotaro Shimizu, Wenya Wang

entry.summary: This work studies whether LoRA-based introspection adapters can let a model describe alignment degradation that arises as an unintended side effect of ordinary domain fine-tuning, rather than from datasets deliberately designed to implant a behavior. That shift matters because real deployments worry about accidental misalignment, not planted backdoors.

entry.title: SiMDex: Mining Similar Egocentric Videos for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Nie Lin, Takehiko Ohkawa, Sijin Chen, Ruoshi Wen, Zhuohang Li, Liqun Huang, Zhengming Zhu, Yiming Bao, Yunfei Li, Minjie Cai, Xiao Ma, Wei Xu, Yoichi Sato

entry.summary: SiMDex frames selection of human egocentric video for vision-language-action post-training as a recommendation problem, mining task-relevant subsets from a pool of roughly 32M human samples through recall, ranking, and re-ranking in a morphology-agnostic action space. Using only about 1.49M mined samples it beats a baseline trained on equal amounts of randomly sampled human data for dexterous manipulation.

entry.title: On MUON optimization: From non-convergence to an error analysis with Polar Express and the Newton-Schulz polynomial from implementations

author.name: Thang Do, Steffen Dereich, Arnulf Jentzen

entry.summary: Provides rigorous convergence analysis of the Muon optimizer, including non-convergence results and an error analysis of the Newton-Schulz orthogonalization actually used in implementations, along with the Polar Express variant. It grounds a widely adopted LLM training optimizer in theory rather than heuristics.

entry.title: Preferred, Not Safer: Pairwise Preference Is a Poor Proxy for Clinical Safety

author.name: Fay Elhassan, David Sasu, Alexandra Kulinkina, Lars Henning Klein, Mary-Anne Hartley

entry.summary: Using 26,804 blinded clinician pairwise judgments over outputs from 13 LLMs contributed by more than 736 clinicians across 28-plus countries, this study shows that preference rankings correlate poorly with rubric-scored clinical safety. Models that win on preference still produce substantial rates of unsafe or misleading content, undermining preference-based leaderboards for medical deployment.

entry.title: Language Models Encode the Contextual Truth of Propositions

author.name: Rupak Sarkar, Pritika Ramu, Rachel Rudinger

entry.summary: Shows that LLMs maintain a linear activation direction encoding whether a proposition is true given in-context evidence, not just world knowledge, and that this direction persists across different output formats and can be causally steered. Uses transcripts from a two-agent grounding task and finds partner statements can sway a model's internal truth representation.

entry.title: LoopMTP: A looped transformer guided by latent multi-token prediction

author.name: Behzad Shomali, Markus Frey, David Berghaus, Joachim Koehler, Mehdi Ali

entry.summary: Connects looped transformers, which reuse one layer stack across several iterations for parameter-efficient depth, with multi-token prediction by aligning each loop iteration to anticipating one future token. This supplies the intermediate supervision that loops normally lack, addressing latent overthinking and undifferentiated per-loop computation.

entry.title: CURV: Enhancing Chart Understanding Through Curriculum Visual Grounded Reasoning

author.name: Xuehang Guo, Pingyue Zhang, Ruiyi Zhang, Zhenhailong Wang, Hanrui Lyu, Heng Ji, Tong Sun, Qingyun Wang, Manling Li

entry.summary: CURV is a curriculum learning framework that turns chart question answering into multi-step reasoning where each step must dynamically ground itself in a specific chart region. The aim is to give multimodal models intrinsic visual grounding rather than relying on external prompting tricks or visual cue overlays.

entry.title: ATFlash: Per-RoPE-Wavelength Attention Windows for Compute/Memory-Efficient LLM Inference

author.name: Shun-ichiro Hayashi, Daichi Mukunoki, Tetsuya Hoshino, Takahiro Katagiri

entry.summary: ATFlash exploits the exact decomposition of rotary position embedding attention into frequency pairs, pruning each pair beyond a distance proportional to its wavelength so that high-frequency components only look locally while low-frequency ones still reach every key. The reduction rate is input-independent and grows logarithmically with sequence length, and the scheme composes with token-level sparse attention methods.

entry.title: The Tell-Tale Trace: Detecting Reasoning Failures in LLMs Using Chain-of-Thought Dynamics

author.name: Shashwat Sourav, Aishwarya Balwani

entry.summary: Rather than checking individual chain-of-thought steps for correctness, this work characterizes how a reasoning trace evolves over time and uses those dynamics to predict reasoning failures that are distributed across the trajectory. It deliberately avoids treating verbalized steps as literal accounts of internal computation, sidestepping faithfulness assumptions.

entry.title: Training Documents Reranker with Search Rubrics for Deep Research Agent

author.name: Wenhan Liu, Yu Lu, Qiaolin Xia, Hui Xu, Tong Zhao, Jian Xi, Yutao Zhu, Haijin Liang, Haibo Shi, Hao Wang, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: Argues that deep research agents need document sets that are collectively diverse, concise and authoritative rather than individually relevant, and synthesizes hierarchical search rubrics with a strong LLM to define these set-level requirements. A reranker called RubricRanker is trained against these rubrics.

entry.title: ContinualSkillBench: Can LLM Agents Truly Evolve Their Capabilities?

author.name: Tianyi Guan, Yiding Wang, Haotong Yang, Siyuan Cao, Shirui Liu, Yi Hu, Jiaqi Li, Muhan Zhang

entry.summary: ContinualSkillBench tests whether agents with external skill libraries genuinely accumulate reusable capabilities, using five domains of 100 interconnected subtasks ordered by difficulty with deliberate cross-task reuse opportunities. Findings include that sequential execution helps unevenly and that in-context learning performs comparably to explicit skill libraries.

entry.title: Agogic: Performance-Timed Music Tokens for LLM-Native Text-to-Symbolic-Music Generation

author.name: Junhao Chen, Mingjin Chen, Jingjia Mao, Lin Chen, Saining Zhang, Minglin Chen, Ruocheng Wu, Liaoyuan Fan, Wenyi Li, Mingju Gao, Henghaofan Zhang, Zhihao Li, Hao Zhao, Yufei Wang, Ruqi Huang

entry.summary: A controlled study that fixes backbone (Qwen3.5 at several sizes), data, budget and decoding while swapping only the music tokenization across seven representations, finding that representation choice rather than model scale drives distributional fidelity. Scaling the backbone 34-fold barely moves Frechet Music Distance while changing representation halves it, and the authors release a performance-resolution token stream with 10 ms timing and per-note velocity.

entry.title: OmniVR: Joint Video-Audio Conditional Generation for Restoring Degraded Historical Films

author.name: Xin Lu, Zihao Fan, Mingchen Zhong, Jie Huang, Xueyang Fu, Zheng-Jun Zha

entry.summary: OmniVR presents joint audio-video generative restoration of degraded historical films, built on a 22B-parameter audio-video generation backbone that denoises low-quality video and audio latents together under one multimodal diffusion transformer. Prior approaches restore each modality independently, leaving cross-modal inconsistencies.

entry.title: Spend Bits Where Queries Look: KV Cache Vector Quantization with Attention-Preserving Transforms

author.name: Samuel Fern\'andez-Mendui\~na, Amir Ziashahabi, Eduardo Pavez, Antonio Ortega, Salman Avestimehr

entry.summary: Proposes KV cache vector quantization using orthogonal transforms derived from a distortion criterion informed by query statistics, rather than data-oblivious random or Hadamard rotations that merely equalize variances. The goal is to preserve attention products at roughly two bits per element so that bandwidth-bound long-context decoding gets faster and cheaper.

entry.title: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents

author.name: Shuhan Xue, Zixin Ding, Yichen Shen, Yinjie Wang, Zhenfei Yin, Yingcheng Wu, Yuxin Chen, Mengdi Wang, Ling Yang

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark testing whether personal agents actually get better from retained experience, running ordered sequences of fresh-session tasks with retained memory switched on and off across 26 scenarios and 204 episodes. Measures both later-task improvement and whether gains genuinely stem from reuse of prior experience rather than task ordering.

entry.title: GROW: Group-Relative Advantage-Weighted On-Policy Reinforcement Learning of Autoregressive-Diffusion Text-to-Speech model

author.name: Guanrou Yang, Tian Tan, Qian Chen, Ziyang Ma, Yakun Song, Zhikang Niu, Qi Chen, Wenming Tu, Haitao Li, Shan Yang, Xie Chen

entry.summary: GROW applies group-relative on-policy RL directly to the flow-matching objective for text-to-speech, avoiding the usual conversion of deterministic ODE sampling into an SDE with per-step likelihood ratios. It standardizes intelligibility and speaker-similarity rewards within each sampled group and anchors updates to a frozen reference with a Wasserstein-2 velocity penalty.

entry.title: An Actionable Diagnosis of Multilingual, Multi-Agent Planning Failures

author.name: Vikas Pahuja, Jonathan Brokman, Omer Hofman, Tamir Nizri, Daniel Vishna, Seraphina Goldfarb-Tarrant, Kelly Marchisio, Hisashi Kojima, Roman Vainshtein

entry.summary: Derives a taxonomy of planning-grounding failures from real failed multi-agent executions, showing that these failures make up an increasing share of errors as language resource availability decreases, hitting low-resource languages hardest. A taxonomy-guided representation called TART is then used to test whether the diagnosis supports mitigation.

entry.title: Poly-OPD: Heterogeneous Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Capability-Selectable Flow Models

author.name: Siming Fu, Haojun Xu, Ruizhe He, Zheming Fu, Hualiang Wang, Jie Huang, Xiaoxiao Ma, Mingchen Zhong, Weihu Huang, Xiaoxuan He, Linjiang Huang, Si Liu

entry.summary: Poly-OPD consolidates complementary strengths of multiple heterogeneous text-to-image teachers (one better at aesthetics, another at compositional instruction following) into one compact flow-matching student. It bridges incompatible autoencoders and noise schedules by doing on-policy distillation through a pixel bridge, re-encoding each student image with the chosen teacher's encoder.

entry.title: ToolArtist: Tool-Using Unified Multimodal Models for Agentic Image Generation

author.name: Jiahao Zhao, Xiaomin Yu, Zhongxiang Sun, Fengwei Teng, Chengwei Qin, Xiaobin Hu, Jun Xu, Shuicheng Yan

entry.summary: ToolArtist post-trains a unified multimodal model so that a single policy orchestrates reasoning, external tool calls, and native image generation, rather than following a fixed agentic workflow or delegating only part of the pipeline. It targets open-world generation tasks needing external knowledge and multi-step reasoning.

entry.title: Diagnosing Tool-Selection Reasoning in LLM Agents with Canary Tools

author.name: Atul Anand, Sourav Chattaraj

entry.summary: Introduces canary tools, deliberately engineered probe tools planted in an agent's tool set to diagnose specific tool-selection failure modes across a six-type taxonomy including semantic decoys, parameter traps, and capability mirages. Eight models are evaluated over 120 tasks and thousands of runs, converting a single wrong-tool outcome into a multi-dimensional reasoning profile.

entry.title: Recurrent Residual Quantization: A Progressive Multi-Precision Representation for LLMs

author.name: Yu Luo, Bo Dong, Wenhua Cheng, Haihao Shen

entry.summary: Recurrent Residual Quantization represents model weights as a 2-bit base plus a sequence of quantized residual corrections, so a single checkpoint can be served at 2, 4, 6, or 8 effective bits depending on deployment constraints. This removes the usual requirement of maintaining a separate quantized checkpoint per target bit width.

entry.title: EuroExec: Frontier Language Models Fall Short of Expert Judgment on European Executive Decision Tasks

author.name: Pau Arnal, Khaled Denfir, Danylo Smahliuk, Amrut Avhad, Marcus A. Castro

entry.summary: EuroExec is a benchmark of 413 open-ended European executive decision tasks authored by 47 vetted domain experts from real cases, evaluated with over 4,000 hours of human expert grading using multi-attribute rubrics, checklists and preference rankings. The strongest of six frontier models solves under 57 percent of tasks, well below expert-written references.

entry.title: What We Observe as LLM Behavior Can Be a Side-effect of Inference Backend

author.name: Shahed Masoudian, Passant Shafaei, Monorama Swain, Markus Schedl

entry.summary: A fully crossed study of three instruction-tuned models, five inference frameworks, six benchmarks and four generation modes shows that the serving backend alone can significantly change benchmark scores, even under greedy decoding with no sampling noise. Since framework names and versions are almost never reported, many published comparisons may be confounded.

entry.title: MarsCast: Transfer Learning of AI Weather Foundation Models to Planetary Atmospheres

author.name: M. L. Carroll, J. Li, S. D. Guzewich, G. Villanueva, J. A. Caraballo-Vega, M. J. Frost

entry.summary: MarsCast tests whether Earth weather foundation models transfer to other planets by adapting GraphCast to Martian atmospheric fields from the Mars Climate Database. Zero-shot forecasts look plausible initially but collapse toward climatology and miss diurnal cycles, motivating fine-tuning strategies for planetary forecasting.

entry.title: Attention-based representations for multi-task computation

author.name: Daniel Hsu, Mingyue Xu

entry.summary: The authors prove bounds on how many attention heads are needed for a shared representation to support multiple downstream tasks, showing for example that computing both the minimum and maximum of a list with a single head requires exponentially larger embedding dimension or precision than two heads. A second scenario analyzes representations enabling polynomial threshold computation of XOR.

entry.title: Manipulation-Proof Oblivious Audits against Deceptive Model Providers

author.name: Augustin Godinot, Sofiane Azogagh, Julien Ferry, S\'ebastien Gambs

entry.summary: The authors design an audit protocol that is oblivious, meaning providers cannot easily detect when they are being audited, to prevent strategic manipulation such as inferring sensitive attributes and temporarily equalizing allocation rates to pass fairness tests. The protocol raises the post-audit cost of gaming while preserving statistical validity.

entry.title: SpecRoll: Fast-Slow Verifier-Feedback Adaptation for Speculative Reinforcement Learning Rollouts

author.name: Nhat Minh Pham, Duy Tung Doan, Thi Duyen Ngo, Vinh Van Nguyen, Khac-Hoai Nam Bui

entry.summary: SpecRoll applies speculative decoding to reinforcement learning rollout generation, where the target policy keeps changing so static drafters go stale and frequent drafter retraining is costly. Lightweight future-token heads propose tokens while a reflex module uses delayed verifier feedback for bounded hidden-state corrections without backpropagation, preserving the target sampling distribution.

entry.title: Every Wrong Answer Counts: Option-Level Psychometrics for LLM Multiple-Choice Benchmarks

author.name: Xiao Fei, Yang Zhang, Sarah Almeida Carneiro, Michalis Vazirgiannis

entry.summary: Introduces a psychometric nominal response model that scores multiple-choice benchmarks using the full distribution over answer options rather than only correctness, separating ability from calibration sharpness, positional bias and fallback behavior. Validated across 189 models and over 31k items from 14 benchmarks.

entry.title: When Attention Goes Blind: Numerical Failure in ALiBi Positional Encodings

author.name: Christopher Schr\"oder, Lukas Gienapp, Ferdinand Schlatt, Martin Potthast, Gerhard Heyer

entry.summary: Identifies a numerical failure mode where the linear bias of ALiBi positional encoding underflows floating-point precision, zeroing many attention weights and effectively blinding affected heads. Demonstrates the problem in deployed ALiBi-based models, isolates it from ordinary out-of-context degradation through 148M-parameter pretraining runs, and evaluates four training-time mitigations.

entry.title: Achieving First-Order Statistical Improvements in Data-Driven Optimization: From No-Free-Lunch to Amplified Decision Perturbation

author.name: Henry Lam, Tianyu Wang

entry.summary: Proposes an umbrella view called EO+ that treats regularization, distributionally robust optimization, transfer learning and related data-driven optimization methods as directionally perturbed empirical optimization, then characterizes when such perturbations can deliver genuine first-order statistical improvements rather than merely intuitive robustness. Includes a no-free-lunch style result and identifies conditions for amplified decision perturbation to help. Provides a unifying answer to a question usually settled case by case.

entry.title: RAG-Stack: Co-Optimizing RAG Serving Performance and Quality

author.name: Haiqiang Zhang, Yuanqing Lei, Wanting Li, Tao Zhang, Wenqi Jiang

entry.summary: RAG-Stack automatically explores the large configuration space of retrieval-augmented generation deployments, spanning index choices, model selection, and how models invoke retrieval, to map quality-versus-serving-performance Pareto frontiers. It combines an iterative design-space exploration component with efficient evaluation across serving systems.

entry.title: EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement

author.name: Jun Nie, Yonggang Zhang, Qianshu Cai, Yiu-ming Cheung, Xinmei Tian, Bo Han

entry.summary: Proposes EvolveNet, a paradigm for evolving the agent harness (the surrounding program that builds context, calls tools, verifies, and recovers) in a decentralized way, where experience streams from different users or organizations cannot be pooled into one optimizer. It targets a real deployment constraint: the most valuable execution experience is often siloed, so harness improvement must be collaborative rather than centralized.

entry.title: MALT: Lightweight Curvature-Aware Muon via Diagonal Preconditioning

author.name: Tongle Wu, Huanyu Dong, Ying Sun, Ziye Ma

entry.summary: MALT augments the Muon optimizer with lightweight two-sided diagonal preconditioners so that orthogonalized momentum updates also account for curvature anisotropy in the loss landscape. It aims to keep Muon memory and compute overhead low while improving robustness of language model pretraining.

entry.title: The Loss Does Not See the Basis, but Adam Does

author.name: Devender Singh

entry.summary: Explains why gradient descent on factored matrices is implicitly biased toward low rank while Adam from the same initialization is not, tracing the difference to gauge symmetry and whether an optimizer is gauge-equivariant. It gives a structure theorem classifying memoryless equivariant update rules and places GD, momentum, Muon, and Shampoo on one side and Adam and RMSProp on the other.

entry.title: Sublogarithmic Swap Regret in Multiplayer General-Sum Games via Hybrid Regularization

author.name: Taira Tsuchiya

entry.summary: Constructs uncoupled learning dynamics with hybrid regularization achieving swap regret that grows sublogarithmically in the horizon for all players in multiplayer general-sum games. This is reported as the first sublogarithmic individual guarantee and implies faster convergence of average play to approximate correlated equilibria.

entry.title: TIDE: A Physically Diverse 3D Turbulence Benchmark Dataset for Advancing Scientific Machine Learning

author.name: Yilong Dai, Yiming Sun, Yiheng Chen, Shengyu Chen, Peyman Givi, Xiaowei Jia, Runlong Yu

entry.summary: Introduces TIDE, a 256-cubed direct numerical simulation corpus of 3D incompressible turbulence with 15 configurations along eight controlled axes, independent ensembles per configuration, pressure fields, and equation-level verification. Multiple ensembles per setting let researchers distinguish learning the dynamics from fitting one flow realization.

entry.title: DeepInvert: Semi-Supervised Embedding Inversion Against Obfuscated Language Models

author.name: Zhicong Huang, Cheng Hong, Tao Wei

entry.summary: DeepInvert is a semi-supervised embedding inversion attack showing that obfuscation-based prompt privacy defenses such as ObfusLM, SentinelLMs, TextObfuscator, and DPNR leak far more than claimed. By combining supervised shadow training with exploitation of residual semantic structure in unlabeled obfuscated embeddings, it recovers original tokens more accurately than prior attacks.

entry.title: SparseDitto: Customizing GPU Kernels for Different Sparsity Patterns with LLM-Based Agentic System

author.name: Shiyang Li, Guangyan Sun, Jinwei Tang, Yanzhi Wang, Mingyi Hong, Caiwen Ding

entry.summary: SparseDitto uses an LLM-based agentic system to synthesize GPU kernels tailored to each sparse matrix, operator, and target GPU, motivated by the observation that no single sparse format dominates and that cuSPARSE can vary by over 300x between formats on the same operation. It adapts representation, execution strategy, and hardware mapping per workload.

entry.title: Evaluating OpenAI's Privacy Filter: Cross-Lingual, Cross-Domain PII Detection Across 42 Benchmarks

author.name: Rohith Uppala

entry.summary: An independent evaluation of OpenAI's 1.5B-parameter Privacy Filter PII detector, which has been available since spring 2026, across 42 synthetic benchmarks in 22 languages and 5 domains. It finds strong performance on structured synthetic PII but sharp degradation when PII appears in narrative prose and near-collapse on non-Latin scripts, with XLM-RoBERTa leading on Indic and non-Latin NER and GPT-4o leading on medical, legal, and financial PII.

entry.title: JudgeArena: A Unified Framework for Reproducible LLM-Judge Evaluation

author.name: Erlis Lushtaku, Bora Kargi, Ali Elganzory, Fabio Ferreira, Alejandro R. Salamanca, Julia Kreutzer, David Salinas

entry.summary: JudgeArena unifies AlpacaEval, Arena-Hard, MT-Bench, and m-Arena-Hard under one open-source interface with swappable judge models, configurable prompts and backends, and comprehensive metadata logging. It enables systematic study of how judge design choices, rather than model quality, drive leaderboard conclusions.

entry.title: Speculative Correction: Draft-then-Refine Decoding for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Brian K Chen, Chong Wu, Kenji Kawaguchi

entry.summary: Proposes a plug-and-play decoding pattern for diffusion language models in which a full draft is generated first and then globally refined bidirectionally, rather than committing block by block. Using LLaDA 2.1 Flash and Mini, it tests both self-refinement and a speculative-correction setup where the smaller model drafts and the larger model edits.

entry.title: EduClaw-Bench: A Long-Horizon Benchmark for Pedagogical LLM Agents with Simulated Learners

author.name: Unggi Lee, Sookbun Lee, Yeil Jeong, Eunjoo Lee, Minchul Shin, Hoilym Kwon

entry.summary: EduClaw-Bench evaluates tutoring agents over a simulated 30-day relationship with a learner whose knowledge state is driven by a knowledge-tracing model trained on real student data, probing measured learning gain across dozens of scenarios. It targets the gap where existing educational LLM evaluations are single-turn point tasks.

entry.title: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Self-Distilled Reward Shaping

author.name: Ranxu Zhang, Guinan Chen, Chenshaodong, Jinghao Lin, Xiaozhou Xu, Sunzhe, Yanyong Zhang, Chao Wang

entry.summary: ADRS densifies sparse trajectory-level rewards in agentic RL by having a frozen snapshot of the policy rescore its own tokens while conditioned on task-matched privileged skills available only during training. The resulting teacher signal is calibrated across interaction steps and folded into advantage construction.

entry.title: GEB-Bench: Abstract Structures Told in Many Voices

author.name: Tong Zhang, Zhiyuan Shi, Yun Peng, Tao Xie

entry.summary: GEB-Bench tests whether models can recognize the same abstract structural motif (self-reference, strange loops, a Mobius twist) across radically different presentations: a natural scene, a folk story with a checkable form device, a theorem, and a code skeleton. Surface parameters are declared nuisance variables and excluded from scoring, and twelve open and proprietary models are evaluated.

entry.title: RUTA: Principled Visual Token Allocation via Rate-Utility Optimization

author.name: Jian Zou, Xiaoyu Xu, Zhihua Wang, Yilin Wang, Balu Adsumilli, Kede Ma

entry.summary: RUTA frames visual token reduction as a rate-utility optimization, jointly learning which tokens to keep and how many to allocate per image-query pair rather than using a fixed budget or hand-tuned thresholds. Query-conditioned candidate tokens each get a learned retention probability.

entry.title: Binding Biometrics with AI Agent Identifiers for Delegation of Authority

author.name: Joseph Geo Benjamin, Anil K Jain, Karthik Nandakumar

entry.summary: BIND uses biometric cryptosystem techniques to cryptographically bind a human user's biometric data to an AI agent's identity and its authorized task scope at the moment of delegation. The resulting token allows later verification that a given agent action was authorized by a specific human.

entry.title: Faster-WAM: Efficient Inference-Time Future Conditioning for Robust World Action Models

author.name: Weiheng Zhao, Haoyi Jiang, Xin Shi, Liu Liu, Fan Huang, Zhizhong Su, Wei Sui, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: Faster-WAM argues that conditioning on predicted future states at inference time, not just during training, is what makes world action models robust to distribution shift, then delivers those future representations without the expensive video-action interleaving that joint models require. It targets the cost-versus-robustness dilemma in robot manipulation policies.

entry.title: Thinking with Anchors: Grounded and Efficient Document Reasoning

author.name: Sichen Zhu, Yuchen Zhu, Wenzhuo Xu, Jason Kuen, Wanrong Zhu, Jing Shi, Xuan Shen, Quanyi Wang, Yiwei Wang, Yujun Cai, Bing Shuai, Qin Zhang, Yongxin Chen, Shilong Liu, Molei Tao, Jiuxiang Gu

entry.summary: ADOPD 2026 extends a document decomposition dataset into a reasoning benchmark by enriching page anchors with cleaned captions, semantic tags, and region-grounded chain-of-thought traces, treating text blocks, entities, labels, boxes, and masks as a shared visual vocabulary. The goal is document understanding that reasons jointly about semantics, spatial relations, and visual structure.

entry.title: OmniRouting: A Semantic-Coupled Multimodal Benchmark for Constraint-Aware Spatial Reasoning in PCB Routing

author.name: Taiting Lu, Kaiyuan Lin, Ziwei Dong, Sisong Bei, Haolin Ye, Yuxin Tian, Runze Liu, Mingjia Wang, Jingying Zeng, Hongxing Pan, Kai Zhang, Haoyu Wang, Guoliang Shi, Ling Ma, Yifan Yang, Jiaying Lu, Qi He, Yi-Chao Chen, Sung-Liang Chen, Yincheng Jin, Mahanth Gowda

entry.summary: OmniRouting is a large benchmark of 1,681 industrial-grade PCB designs testing whether LLMs can reason about printed-circuit-board routing under real geometric, topological, electrical, and manufacturability constraints. It extends constraint-aware spatial reasoning evaluation from toy mazes and graphs to a genuinely hard industrial planning domain.

entry.title: MobileWAM: Bridging World Action Models to Mobile Manipulation with Chain-of-Foresight

author.name: Zehua Fan, Junjie He, Wenxuan Song, Xi Wang, Wenqi Lyu, Linge Zhao, Fuhao Li, Zihan You, Yifei Yang, Kaiming Xu, Qi Jiang, Yue Jiang, Haoang Li, Cheng Chi, Bailin Li, Yan Wang

entry.summary: Extends video-diffusion-based world action models from tabletop settings to mobile manipulation, fusing a pretrained video diffusion transformer with a lightweight action expert through layerwise joint attention and mixture-of-experts feed-forward layers. The goal is whole-body control that couples locomotion with manipulation using internet-scale motion priors.

entry.title: When Is a Conformal Guarantee Fair? Auditing Silent Subgroup Under-Coverage in Alzheimer's Disease Longitudinal Prediction

author.name: Lujia Zhong, Xinkai Wang, Shuo Huang, Yonggang Shi

entry.summary: An audit of conformal prediction for longitudinal Alzheimer's biomarker forecasting showing that population-level coverage guarantees can hide serious under-coverage for clinically important subgroups defined by genetic risk, demographics or disease severity. The authors propose a mechanism-driven framework to detect and repair these gaps, tested across two cohorts, two base forecasters and nine attributes. Important as a caution that formal uncertainty guarantees can be misleading in high-stakes clinical deployment.

entry.title: ABSeeker: Training Long-Horizon Search Agents via Answer-Backtracked Credit Assignment

author.name: Yijun Lu, Rui Ye, Jiajun Wang, Yuwen Du, Tian Jin, Songhua Liu, Siheng Chen

entry.summary: ABSeeker converts sparse trajectory-level outcomes into dense step-level supervision for long-horizon search agents by backtracking from the final answer to identify which intermediate actions were genuinely useful, including within failed trajectories. This distinguishes helpful steps from erroneous or redundant ones during both fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Balancing Efficiency and Efficacy: Training-Free Attention-Guided Switching Between Explicit and Latent Thoughts for MLLMs

author.name: Haoqian Kang, Liupeng Li, Kuofeng Gao, Jinpeng Wang, Zhenyu Lu, Bin Chen, Ke Chen, Yaowei Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free strategy for multimodal models to switch between explicit textual chain-of-thought and cheaper latent reasoning, arguing that prior token-entropy-based switching fails because entropy conflates perceptual ambiguity with logical uncertainty. Attention signals are used instead to decide when explicit reasoning is needed.

entry.title: Fewer Tokens, Smaller Cache: Reward-Coordinated Efficient Reasoning

author.name: Qiyuan Zhu, Dezhi Li, Pengyu Cheng, Tianle Chen, Jiacheng Wang, Ruijie Shen, Hao Gu, Sida Lin, Zirui Liu, Jiacheng Liu, Sirui Han

entry.summary: Proposes coordinating KV-cache compression with process reward signals, based on two observations: tolerance to context loss varies along a reasoning trajectory and correlates with step reward, and aggressive compression backfires by making the model generate more tokens. The method jointly targets fewer generated tokens and a smaller cache instead of judging compression only by what it evicts.

entry.title: Governing Execution Risk in Agentic AI Systems: A Trajectory-Guided Framework for Red Teaming

author.name: Zhihao Zhu, Yi Yang

entry.summary: TrajRed argues that execution risk in tool-using agents is a trajectory-level phenomenon and proposes a red-teaming framework that inspects how attacks unfold through multi-step reasoning and tool calls, rather than relying on fixed templates or only final outcomes. It targets risks from malicious or untrusted external content steering agents toward unintended actions.

entry.title: AgentAntibody: An Adaptive Immune System for Defending LLM Agents against Prompt Injection

author.name: Shihao Weng, Yang Feng, Xiaofei Xie, Jiongchi Yu

entry.summary: AgentAntibody gives LLM agents a self-evolving defense against prompt injection that accumulates knowledge across encounters, motivated by the observation that user requests are underspecified and injections exploit that ambiguity. The system builds an immune-system-like evolving representation of unacceptable behaviors instead of treating each task independently.

entry.title: Perception Before Reasoning: Dynamic Latent Reasoning for Video Understanding and Question Answering

author.name: Haotian Xia, Zilin Xiao, Junbo Zou, Vicente Ordonez, Hanjie Chen

entry.summary: DyLaR answers video questions by first grounding the query in a short block of continuous perception latents encoding relevant visual evidence, then adaptively deciding whether extra latent reasoning steps are needed before responding. This avoids emitting long textual chains of thought for questions that are resolved as soon as the right frame or object is localized.

entry.title: InvFlowFD: Reference-Free and Background-Set-Free Perceptual Music Quality Metric with Flow Matching Inversion

author.name: Alon Ziv, Harel Pogoda, Yossi Adi

entry.summary: InvFlowFD estimates perceptual music quality without a reference recording and without a background set of clean samples, by inverting a pretrained flow matching model with simple Euler integration and comparing groups of inverted samples. It detects diverse distortions and ranks music generation systems in line with human judgments.

entry.title: Training-Free Hashing-Based Attention via Binary Principal Components

author.name: Daohai Yu, Zhanpeng Zeng, Keyu Chen, Wenhao Li, Zhifeng Shen, Luxi Lin, Ruizhi Qiao, Xing Sun, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: BinaryPC is a training-free sparse attention method that builds compact binary hash codes from binary principal components of the data to select which key-value pairs to attend to during long-context decoding. It avoids the accuracy loss of random locality-sensitive hashing and the cost of retraining.

entry.title: The Effect of Perceived Race and Gender on Police Language Use: Experimental Evidence from VR Simulations

author.name: Sandra C. Sandoval, Navita Goyal, Rashawn Ray, Long Doan, Rachel Rudinger, Hal Daum\'e III

entry.summary: Using VR police training simulations, the authors apply causal inference to measure whether officers speak less deferentially to virtual characters depicted as Black adult men, treating character assignment as the treatment. They find most officers use less deferential language toward these characters, with exceptions among some female officer subgroups.

entry.title: Sample Complexity of Multicalibration for Multilevel Properties

author.name: Jiuyao Lu, Krishnakumar Balasubramanian, Aleksandr Podkopaev, Shiva Prasad Kasiviswanathan

entry.summary: The paper extends multicalibration to sequences of nested properties where each quantity (mean, then variance, then skewness or CVaR) is identifiable only once the earlier ones are fixed, and establishes matching upper and lower sample-complexity bounds for every fixed number of properties. This covers Bayes pairs without requiring the properties to come from a single loss.

entry.title: Why Ranking Anomaly Detection Algorithms Isn't as Reliable as You May Think

author.name: Simon Kl\"uttermann, J\'er\^ome Rutinowski, Frederik Polachowski, Alice Kirchheim

entry.summary: Using seven anomaly detection algorithms across 690 datasets, this study shows that algorithm rankings shift substantially with routine benchmarking choices, undermining widespread claims of state of the art. It argues that current anomaly detection benchmarks are not comparable enough to support reliable conclusions.

entry.title: OPTD: On-Policy Transition Distillation with Consistency-Guided Adaptive Compression for Few-Step Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Xiaocheng Lu, Hualei Zhang, Shuhan Guo, Jie Zhang, Xiaoyi Pang, Jian Liu, Haoxi Li, Bohai Gu, Haoxuan Che, Jingcai Guo, Song Guo

entry.summary: Proposes on-policy transition distillation for few-step diffusion language models, addressing the mismatch where a distilled student visits states that drift from the off-policy trajectories used for supervision. Adds consistency-guided adaptive compression so each distilled transition advances as far as reliability allows rather than a fixed number of teacher steps.

entry.title: Logic Before Language: Pre-pretraining on Formal Derivations Fosters Skill Acquisition and Compressibility

author.name: Jo-Ku Cheng, Nikolaos Aletras, Marco Valentino

entry.summary: Proposes pre-pretraining language models on formal logical derivations before natural language, arguing derivations require abstract variable binding and structure that narrow symbolic tasks like Dyck languages do not exercise. Studies effects on downstream skill acquisition speed and on representational compressibility at larger token budgets than prior work.

entry.title: SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation

author.name: Wen Wang, Jiahua Bao, Tu Yongsiqi, Yihao Liu, Haotian Zhou, Haoxuan Ma, Mengyu Zhou, Wenkui Fan, Junwei He, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: SMOPD tackles multi-reward RL where dense fine-grained rewards and sparse binary rewards have mismatched granularity, which existing decoupled-normalization methods still handle poorly. It trains specialists per reward and merges them through online policy distillation.

entry.title: Argus: A General-Purpose Agentic Runtime for Long-Horizon Reasoning

author.name: Boxiu Li, Zimo Wen, Yijia Fan, Junxiang Lei, Sufeng Guo, Jiaao Wu, Ruize Tang, Mukai Li, Yifei Shen, Xiaoyu Chen, Wanbo Zhang, Runjing Gu, Yifei Gao, Yuheng Wu, Xuyao Huang, Zelong Zhao, Jiachen Zhang, Shibo Hu, Hangxi Guo, Yilin Chen, Yuzhe Zhang, Fan Yang, Chuan Wen, Xian Zhang, Xuanhe Zhou, Zhijie Deng

entry.summary: Argus is a persistent agentic runtime in which manager, planner, engineer, and reviewer roles execute bounded missions over durable project state, separating stable user intent from operational objectives and verification criteria. Model weights stay fixed and self-improvement happens through curated runtime state, skills, verifiers, and routing policies admitted only after role-owned review.

entry.title: Behavioral Skill Reconstruction: Reconstructing Hidden Functionality from LLM Agent Skills

author.name: Peichun Hua, Haoxuan Xu, Mengyuan Li

entry.summary: Introduces behavioral skill reconstruction, an attack where a user clones the functionality of a hidden, proprietary LLM agent skill purely from ordinary task requests and observed outputs, without ever exfiltrating the underlying files. It shows that defenses aimed at preventing file disclosure do not protect the intellectual property those files encode.

entry.title: Provable Limits and Certified Deferral for Verbalized Uncertainty in Small Language Models

author.name: Jianru Shen

entry.summary: This work evaluates whether verbalized confidence from small open-weight models (0.5B to 14B, eleven models, over 25,000 predictions) can support risk-controlled deferral to humans. It proves that monotone calibration preserves the risk-coverage frontier and error-detection AUROC, that temperature scaling cannot fix models whose stated confidence exceeds accuracy, and uses Clopper-Pearson bounds to certify deferral thresholds.

entry.title: Optimizing What Policies Learn From: Recoverability-aware Rollout Intervention Learning

author.name: Zheyuan Zhang, Manqing Mao, Hong Wang, Zhuoer Wang, Samson Koelle, Jie Yuan, Yanjun Lin, James Feng, Nikki Lijing Kuang, Yanfang Ye, Wei Niu

entry.summary: Introduces a recoverability-aware intervention scheme for critic-free group RL post-training of LLMs, deciding not just how many rollouts to generate but where in a trajectory to intervene and how. It adapts as the policy changes rather than relying on static heuristics, aiming to spend rollout compute where the learning signal is highest.

entry.title: Multimodal Spatiotemporal Atmospheric Data Assimilation with Latent Flow-matching

author.name: Dibyajyoti Chakraborty, Romit Maulik

entry.summary: Reformulates atmospheric data assimilation as posterior sampling from a latent video flow-matching prior trained on ERA5 reanalysis over 69 variables and 8-day windows, then conditions on real radiosonde and surface observations. Because the prior produces continuous trajectories, one model handles filtering, smoothing, and reconstruction without a bespoke Bayesian update per task.

entry.title: Emulate or Estimate? The Divergent Strengths of Base and Post-Trained Language Models for Opinion Simulation

author.name: Seth Grief-Albert, Jessica Bo, Difan Jiao, Ashton Anderson

entry.summary: Distinguishes two tasks often conflated in LLM social simulation: emulating individual respondents whose answers aggregate into a distribution, versus directly estimating a population distribution. Using matched base and post-trained model pairs on Pew survey data, finds base models are the better emulators while post-training helps the estimation task.

entry.title: LoRetta: A Foundation Model and Extensive Dataset for Global-Scale Remote Sensing Dense Image Matching

author.name: Siwei Yu, Han Guo, Zhenwei Shi, Zhengxia Zou

entry.summary: LoRetta reformulates global-scale remote sensing dense image matching as localization followed by registration, first finding the matchable overlap and affine geometry then refining dense residuals in the aligned frame. It ships as a foundation model with a large accompanying dataset spanning seasonal, viewpoint, and resolution variation.

entry.title: SIGNPOST-Bench: Benchmarking Text-Vision Conflict Resolution in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Sirun Li, Minghao Liu, Ling Dai, Yong Li, Haoxin Lyu, Junting Zhou, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: SIGNPOST-Bench builds counterfactual quintuplets of each scene image (original, blank, similar, random, adversarial scene text) to measure how multimodal models arbitrate when embedded text conflicts with visual evidence for geolocation-style tasks. It contains over 5,000 controlled counterfactual items.

entry.title: ReGround: Restoring Visual Grounding in Multi-Step Reasoning through Self-Diagnosis and Visual Re-Examination

author.name: Lei Peng, Shuai Lv, Wei Hu

entry.summary: ReGround shows that vision-language models progressively lose visual grounding over long reasoning chains, with attention entropy over image tokens falling during initial reasoning and recovering after the image is re-injected. Crucially, re-injecting the image only helps when paired with targeted self-diagnosis; blind re-examination can hurt performance.

entry.title: CofactVLA: Deconfounding Vision-Language-Action Models via Counterfactual Intervention

author.name: Yan Zhang, Yinan Wu, Haoran Duan, Jungong Han

entry.summary: CofactVLA formalizes the vision-override failure in vision-language-action models, where dense visual streams cause policies to ignore sparse language instructions and latch onto spurious visual confounders. It applies a causal intervention framework with a dual-path deconfounding graph to restore language as the causal driver of actions.

entry.title: FocusMem: Factorizing Content, Readout, and Trust in Latent GUI Memory

author.name: Zhuoran Zhang, Bowen Li, Jingcheng Ju, Yang Shi, Qixun Wang, Haotian Wang, Wei Chen, Tengjiao Wang

entry.summary: FocusMem factorizes latent memory for GUI agents into separate content, readout, and trust components so that a single compressed trajectory block does not have to serve every decision stage and irrelevant retrieved trajectories can be discounted. It targets detail loss and misleading retrieval in compressed multimodal agent memory.

entry.title: Talk2Sensors: 3D Visual Grounding in Autonomous Driving via Sensor-Adaptive Physical Cue Matching

author.name: Runwei Guan, Di Tian, Ningwei Ouyang, Ruixiao Zhang, Shaofeng Liang, Haocheng Zhao, Lianqing Zheng, Xiaokai Bai, Guotao Wang, Daizong Liu, Henghui Ding, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: Talk2Sensors introduces the first multi-sensor 3D visual grounding dataset combining camera, LiDAR, and 4D radar, with 8,682 language instructions referring to 20,558 objects in outdoor driving scenes. It enables query-adaptive grounding that draws on texture, geometry, or kinematics depending on what the instruction requires.

entry.title: Out-Of-The-Loop Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Gustavo Sutter, Hao Wang, Luis Ricardez-Sandoval, Pascal Poupart, Agustinus Kristiadi

entry.summary: Addresses multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization in the realistic case where the true highest-fidelity function is too expensive to query inside the loop, but gold-standard observations from previous experiments exist. The method exploits that offline high-fidelity data to guide optimization over cheaper fidelities.

entry.title: Breadcrumbing Search Agents

author.name: Xuebin Li, Hanqing Zhao, Siyuan Liang, Kejiang Chen, Weiming Zhang, Dacheng Tao, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: Demonstrates that the search and page-retrieval channel itself is a fragile trust boundary for LLM search agents: a mediated search interface can repeatedly shape which evidence an agent gathers across follow-up queries, steering its final answer even when single-page prompt injection would be diluted or rejected. The attack is called breadcrumbing.

entry.title: OneDayAgent: Towards a Long-Horizon Harness for Autonomous Agents

author.name: Jingsheng Zheng, Xinyuan Fang, Jintian Zhang, Zhengke Gui, Huajun Chen, Ningyu Zhang

entry.summary: OneDayAgent is a harness for long-horizon, cross-environment agent tasks that decomposes open-ended requests into bounded subtasks, maintains execution memory under context pressure, and aims to jointly mitigate goal drift, state loss and context overflow across different model backends. It targets everyday multimodal requests spanning work, study and personal tasks.

entry.title: Capability-Gated Planning: Cost-to-Goal Discovery and the Limits of Myopic Experiment Selection

author.name: Ahmed Hassoon, Mark Dredze

entry.summary: This paper identifies a structural failure of automated-discovery systems that select experiments by myopic scores such as expected information gain per cost: constructive actions that build capabilities (instruments, assays, pipelines) pay off only through the future actions they unlock. It proposes capability-gated planning with cost-to-goal discovery so planners can commit to chains of constructive steps.

entry.title: MDLMPE: Distribution Aware Positional Encoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Tong Ling, Hang Lei, Feng Xiao, Changhui Sun, Jiahang Xie, Hao Liu, Lu Liu, Yanlong Du

entry.summary: Points out that standard rotary position encodings assume a contiguous prefix and are blind to the shifting pattern of revealed versus masked tokens during diffusion denoising. Proposes a positional encoding that makes representations explicitly aware of the evolving token-availability structure in masked diffusion language models.

entry.title: Single Canonical Prompts Underestimate LLM Safety's Surface-Form Sensitivity

author.name: Yongxi Zhou, Junwei Yao, Yuanzhe Liu, Zihan Dong, Wenbo Ye, Jiaxi Wen, Lai Yun Choi

entry.summary: Argues that benchmarks reading each item at one canonical surface form systematically misestimate behavior, and tests this in safety by pre-authoring meaning-preserving reformulations via back-translation and a code-switch generator so identical prompts reach every model. Separates genuine surface-form sensitivity from decoding and judge noise using a single human-anchored scorer.

entry.title: BrainBench: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Comprehensive EEG Understanding

author.name: Yangxuan Zhou, Sha Zhao, Yuning Chen, Chen Wu, Jiquan Wang, Shijian Li, Gang Pan

entry.summary: BrainBench measures whether LLMs can perform end-to-end EEG workflows that link natural-language instructions, signal processing, quantitative evidence, and clinical interpretation, spanning foundational analysis, sleep, neurocognitive assessment, and physiological integration across 17 datasets. It targets a capability the authors call comprehensive EEG understanding rather than isolated decoding accuracy.

entry.title: What Is a Skill Worth? Structure-Aware Shapley Valuation of Agent Skills

author.name: Tao Li, Junfeng Liu, Qinghua Zhao, Yifan Li, Lei Wang, Bo Shao, Xuejun Liu, Linjun Shou

entry.summary: SkillSV assigns Shapley-style credit to the internal units of an agent skill document, such as rules, examples, scripts, and heuristics, while respecting dependencies, document hierarchy, and prompt-context budgets so that only valid counterfactual skill variants are evaluated. This provides a principled way to prune and curate auto-optimized agent skill artifacts.

entry.title: Hierarchical Graph Memory for LLM Agents with Path-level Localization and Rewrite

author.name: Xiawei Yue, Boran Wang, Xiaoqing Zhang, Shuxin Zheng, Ziwei Zhang

entry.summary: HiGram organizes agent memory as an evolving hierarchical graph with path-level localization and rewriting, instead of a flat graph where accumulated history injects irrelevant context and raises retrieval cost. Related changes can be applied along a path rather than requiring repeated independent unit-wise rewrites.

entry.title: Wiring Beats Blending: What Transfers Between Transformer Sizes -- and What Doesn't

author.name: Ravi Satya Durga Prasad Yenugula

entry.summary: Studies whether a pretrained large model can be converted into a smaller sibling, using a 1.4B to 410M conversion in the Pythia family. Representations align strongly across sizes while parameters do not; dense weight projection is shown to be functionally destructive because basis mixing breaks rotary, per-head, activation, and normalization structure, so the only real value of conversion lies in initialization.

entry.title: Hallucinations on the Board: Tool-Augmented Evaluation of LLM Chess Commentary

author.name: S. Ashwin Hebbar, Peiyao Sheng, Sewoong Oh, Pramod Viswanath

entry.summary: ACT-Eval decomposes LLM-generated chess commentary into atomic claims and verifies each against a chess engine plus expert gold annotations, rather than relying on reference overlap or an LLM judge. It provides a way to detect factual hallucinations in a domain where ground truth is cheaply computable.

entry.title: Compass: Continuously Aligning Social Media Feeds via In-Situ Reflections

author.name: Aadit Barua, Leijie Wang, Amy X. Zhang

entry.summary: Compass is a system that continuously realigns a social media feed with a user's reflective preferences by prompting lightweight in-feed reflection rather than requiring users to visit configuration pages. It targets the gap between impulsive engagement signals and the preferences people would endorse on reflection.

entry.title: Mind the Cap: Output-Budget Regimes Change the Measured Multilingual Reasoning Gap

author.name: Ankit Goyal, Jaideep Ray

entry.summary: Demonstrates that the reported multilingual reasoning gap between native-language and translate-then-solve prompting on MGSM is largely an artifact of a fixed output-token cap, since languages need different token counts for the same content. The measured gap swings by as much as 57 points across budgets, and length normalization can even reverse which prompting strategy appears better.

entry.title: Eliciting Intrinsic Hallucinations in LLMs via Semantically Equivalent Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Atri Vivek Sharma, Brian Formento, Alessio Lomuscio

entry.summary: Builds an adversarial framework that searches for semantically equivalent rewordings of a user query which cause retrieval-augmented LLMs to produce content unsupported by the retrieved evidence. Enforcing strict semantic equivalence isolates intrinsic hallucination from prompt meaning changes.

entry.title: A Counterexample to Fourier Alignment in Single-Neuron Modular Addition

author.name: Gautam Neelakantan Memana

entry.summary: Provides a counterexample refuting the conjecture that single-neuron ReLU networks trained on modular addition must align with Fourier frequency components, constructing initial conditions of positive probability where a neuron dies and freezes with energy spread across all frequency classes. An appendix produced by GPT-5.6 Sol extends the counterexample to all Clarke trajectories, smooth ReLU approximations, and fixed-step full-batch gradient descent.

entry.title: Suppression Sticks, Locality Is Fragile: A Closed-Loop Target-and-Control Audit of Task-Vector Negation in VLA Policies

author.name: Shaoguang Wang, Weiyu Guo, Rushi Dai, Yiren Zhao, Yandong Guo, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: Audits per-skill task-vector subtraction in multitask vision-language-action policies with closed-loop robot rollouts, finding three regimes across ten LIBERO-Goal skills: clean target suppression, resistance, and global collapse. Even for successfully suppressed skills, retention on supposedly unrelated control skills averages only 52 percent, so the edits are not behaviorally local.

entry.title: OncoTriad-QA: A Patient-Level Radiology-Pathology-Genomics Benchmark for Pan-Cancer Reasoning

author.name: Ahnaf Munir, Dannong Wang, Michael W. McDonald, Mubarak Shah, Pegah Khosravi, Yu Tian

entry.summary: OncoTriad-QA is a patient-level pan-cancer benchmark of 86.1k questions over 9,281 TCGA cases that jointly aligns CT and MRI imaging, whole-slide pathology, mutations, copy-number alterations, methylation, RNA-seq, and clinical metadata. It moves medical model evaluation from isolated modality tasks to integrated multi-evidence oncology reasoning.

entry.title: Scalable Frequency- and Length-Aware Subdocument Deduplication for Large Language Model Pretraining

author.name: Hai Wang, Chenhao Wang, Qifeng Cai, Yixiu Liu, Miao Peng, Nuo Chen, Yuanlin Tu, Chengcheng Xu, Feng Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a corpus-scale subdocument deduplication framework that decouples duplicate detection from copy-retention policy, using natural-boundary segmentation and global hashing to catch cross-shard duplicates missed by per-shard suffix-array methods. Retention becomes frequency- and length-aware rather than a fixed rule.

entry.title: WorldCup Arena: Prospective, Leakage-Free Evaluation of Frontier LLMs on a Live Tournament

author.name: Zhenran Wang, Zhonghan Bian, Jinsong Li, Zhangyang Qi

entry.summary: Ran a prospective forecasting evaluation over the 2026 World Cup in which six frontier models with extended thinking and live web search filled seven-market prediction cards before each of 104 matches, producing 4,494 scored predictions where no answer existed at question time. The design makes leakage impossible by construction rather than by contamination filtering.

entry.title: LACE: Large Language Model Aided Multi-Agent Framework for Agile RISC-V Instruction Extension

author.name: Pingqing Zheng, Jiayin Qin, Fuqi Zhang, Zishen Wan, Shang Wu, Yu Cao, Caiwen Ding, Yang Katie Zhao

entry.summary: LACE is a multi-agent LLM workflow that converts natural-language descriptions of RISC-V instruction set extensions into localized RTL edits via a two-level intermediate representation, then verifies them with formal riscv-formal checks. It aims to remove the per-core manual adaptation that makes custom instruction development slow.

entry.title: GSTEP: Global Spatio-Temporal Density-Driven Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Video Large Language Models

author.name: Mengjie Zhang, Qihui Zhu, Tao Zhang, Shuangwu Chen, Huihuang Qin, Yu Guo, Shenghao Ye, Zijian Wen, Yunpeng Hou, Dong Jin, Xiaobin Tan, Huasen He, Jian Yang

entry.summary: GSTEP prunes visual tokens in video LLMs using a global spatio-temporal density criterion instead of the usual segment-local selection, so short but information-dense segments are not under-sampled and globally important tokens are not dropped. It is presented as a plug-and-play module for long-video inference.

entry.title: Evaluating LLMs in Database Scenarios: A Lifecycle Benchmark for Assessing Their Potential in Core Database Tasks

author.name: Shunfan Zheng, Dongsheng Shi, Yue Li, Xin Yi, Linlin Wang, Gerard de Melo

entry.summary: DBLifeBench evaluates LLMs across five database lifecycle phases (design, implementation, operation, debugging, maintenance) rather than the usual narrow focus on text-to-SQL. It aims to measure whether models can act as autonomous database administrators in realistic workflows.

entry.title: Teaching Foundation Models to Read mmWave: Pose-Guided Kinematic Representation for Human Behavior Understanding

author.name: Duo Zhang, Zhehui Yin, Zhiyun Yao, Haotong Qin, Xusheng Zhang, Hongliu Yang, Jianyu Sun, Junzhe Wang, Zizhou Fan, Michele Magno, Daqing Zhang

entry.summary: mmMind pretrains a spatio-temporal millimeter-wave radar encoder using synchronized 3D human pose as training-only supervision, then discards the pose head so inference needs radar alone, and aligns the representation with an LLM for behavior captioning. This gives privacy-friendly, camera-free human behavior understanding for embodied agents.

entry.title: muSync-GS: Physics-Synchronized Driving Video Synthesis for Weather and Geometric Road Hazards

author.name: Yang Chen, Yicheng Zhu, Tao Li, Zilin Bian

entry.summary: muSync-GS generates driving video for rare hazardous conditions by coupling Gaussian-splatting scene edits (adverse weather, uneven road geometry) with a vehicle dynamics model so that braking, wheel slip, load transfer, and camera motion change consistently with the edited road condition. Existing editing methods change appearance while leaving the original trajectory physically inconsistent.

entry.title: EgoAfford: Task-Oriented Affordance Grounding via Egocentric Referring Segmentation

author.name: Xinyuan Guan, Feifan Chen, Xinyu Zhan, Fu-Cheng Zhang, Cewu Lu, Lixin Yang

entry.summary: EgoAfford is a benchmark of about 15.5k human-verified egocentric images from 2,000 multi-step tabletop scenes where a model must produce the remaining plan and segment the functional regions of the direct object, instrument, and destination for the next action. It links task planning to part-level affordance grounding rather than treating them separately.

entry.title: EviGraph: Evidence-Guided Autonomous Research Agents

author.name: Zhenjiang Ren, Ruiji Li, Xujing Zhang, Ziliang Pang, Shuo Ren, Jiajun Zhang

entry.summary: EviGraph restructures autonomous research agents around a typed evidence graph with problem, gap, hypothesis, experiment, finding, and claim nodes that serves as the live operational state rather than a post-hoc log. The aim is to reduce unsupported claims and inconsistencies between questions, experiments, results, and conclusions.
