entry.summary: MemSIF organizes agent memory into topical segments plus a dual-track fact store to counter two misalignments: temporal proximity not matching topical relatedness, and write-time salience not predicting future query usefulness. Targets long-horizon interaction retrieval.

entry.title: CockpitHAT: Dependency-Graph-Driven Hierarchical Attribution for Embodied Multi-Agent Cockpits

author.name: Wei Wang, Shuanghe Liu, Zhu Zhuo, Jiaqi Zhong, Xiaozhao Zhao, Xiaojie Zuo, Jie Su

entry.summary: CockpitHAT attributes failures in embodied multi-agent automotive cockpit systems using dependency distances from interaction DAGs plus multi-channel evidence, weighting high-risk safety failures during consensus analysis. Targets correctness collapse where task-level accuracy hides dangerous process-level errors.

entry.title: Evolving in the Agent Jungle via History-Informed Opponent Awareness

author.name: Zhaofeng Zhang, Linhan Xia, Rui Liu, Yihao Wang, Binrui Shen, Shengxin Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces OASE, which decides whether an LLM agent skill revision is genuinely beneficial in multi-agent settings where opponents also change strategies, using paired comparisons against an opponent-aware reference rather than a stale static baseline. Addresses nonstationarity in skill-library self-improvement.

entry.title: MemArbiter: Decision-Time Memory Arbitration for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Jiajun Dong, Yutao Hu, Fengrui Fan, Shihan Dou, Yueming Wu, Deqing Zou

entry.summary: MemArbiter names the Memory-Action Gap, where retrievable memory still fails to influence the current decision, and addresses it by decomposing histories into atomic items sorted into five functional memory banks with demand-, relevance-, and time-gated presentation. Targets coherence in long-horizon agent tasks.

entry.title: ELECTRIC: Evidential Learning-Enhanced CT Reconstruction via Iterative Correction

author.name: Ge Wang

entry.summary: ELECTRIC is a physics-guided Bayesian CT reconstruction loop where an evidential network proposes an image plus an epistemic-uncertainty surrogate that becomes an adaptive precision field inside a Poisson-weighted MAP update. Treats prior confidence as a learned state variable, with two simulation studies on low-dose CT slices.

entry.title: Verifiable Checks for Business Rule Consistency

author.name: Joseph Tafese, Milad Hooshyar, Sam Bayless, Nick Feng, Arie Gurfinkel

entry.summary: SIRNA checks whether natural-language business-rule documentation matches evolving code implementations by having an LLM translate documentation into candidate SMT formulas, validating those translations, then verifying the implementation against them with an SMT solver. It is demonstrated on tax cost-calculation rules.

entry.title: Auditable Release Control for Pedagogical Leakage in LLM Tutors

author.name: Nizam Kadir

entry.summary: This paper formalizes pedagogical leakage, where an LLM tutor discloses an answer or decisive reasoning before disclosure is authorized, and imposes a complete-mediation release boundary with five disclosure contracts, trusted gates, inspectable checks, and replayable traces separating selection, generation, verification, and enforcement failures. Component attribution on 599 fixed Gemini 3.5 proposals exposes an explicit safety-utility frontier.

entry.title: Hierarchical Solomonoff Induction: An Unbounded Machine Learning Model

author.name: Nathan Young

entry.summary: Extends Solomonoff induction with a hyperprior over Solomonoff priors via de Finetti's exchangeability theorem, producing Hierarchical Solomonoff Induction, and proves it is equivalent to standard Solomonoff induction while bounding its excess error. The goal is a theoretical model of training-then-extrapolation as done by LLMs.

entry.title: VLAGuard: A Framework for Evaluating and Mitigating Physical Attention Hijacking in Vision-Language-Action Robots within Wireless Sensor Networks

author.name: Dongfu Yin, Jinquan Zhang

entry.summary: VLAGuard introduces a printable-patch attack that hijacks the action-conditioned cross-attention of vision-language-action robots, plus an attention-protective fine-tuning defense with no inference overhead. It evaluates both in simulated and physical settings framed as edge nodes in wireless sensor networks.

entry.title: What Could the Agent See at 19:05? Generating Temporal Enterprise Scenarios from Real Research and Replaying Them to Evaluate Agents

author.name: Tezan Sahu, Himani Arora

entry.summary: Proposes generating temporal enterprise scenarios and replaying them so agents can be graded against what data existed and who could see it at each moment, rather than a single end-of-episode snapshot. It addresses time-travel and permission leakage in offline enterprise agent evaluation.

entry.title: Auditing Semantic Gains in Sequential Recommendation: A Lightweight Recovery Test

author.name: Kong Wang, Zhongke He, Xiang Chen, Hongwei Zeng, Kai Deng, Long Wang, Kehua Yang

entry.summary: LIME-Rec is a lightweight audit that fuses a sequential recommender, an item co-occurrence expert and frozen text embeddings to test whether reported gains from semantic and generative-retrieval recommenders actually require language-model reasoning. It attributes improvements to specific components rather than end-to-end architectures.

entry.title: Coding Agents as Test-Suite Auditors: Finding What Official Suites Miss While Approaching What They Catch

author.name: Shuyang Xie, Shuxiao Xie, Feng Zhu, Yanli Ji, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: The paper uses an off-the-shelf coding agent as a test-suite auditor that generates adversarial tests to expose submissions wrongly accepted by online-judge suites, plus a certification chain using agreement among independent accepted solutions to confirm real bugs without trusting the judge. It offers a practical remedy to label noise in code benchmarks and training data.

entry.title: Self-Improving Large Language Models via Progressive Experience Evolution

author.name: Shijie Ren, Xiting Wang, Meng Li, Yujie Guo, Yunhang Yao, Ziheng Peng, Xunlong Wang, Yuetan Chen, Haoyang Zhou, Yunlong Liang, Fandong Meng

entry.summary: SPEE proposes experience distillation as the missing bridge between test-time methods that extract reusable experience without changing weights and training-time optimization that changes weights without accumulating explicit experience. It progressively converts interaction experience into persistent parameter-level capability for self-improving LLMs.

entry.title: Lossless Tensor Compression as Program Synthesis

author.name: Jieke Shi (James), Junda He (James), Wenjia Jiang (James), Weifeng Sun (James), Shidong Pan (James), Zhensu Sun (James), Chengran Yang (James), Peixin Zhang (James), Yifan Jia (James), Zhou Yang (James), Thong Hoang (James), Xiwei Xu (Sherry), Zhenchang Xing, David Lo

entry.summary: Brevis formulates lossless tensor compression as program synthesis, defining a typed domain-specific language of reversible operators that capture recurring tensor structure and synthesizing a bit-exact reconstruction program per tensor, guided by a learned checkpoint-specific prior. It targets the growing archival and transfer cost of model checkpoints.

entry.title: Benign interpolation and Occam's razor

author.name: Tom F. Sterkenburg, Daniel A. Herrmann, Jan-Willem Romeijn

entry.summary: A philosophy-of-science analysis arguing that recent explanations of benign interpolation, which appeal to a simplicity bias among interpolating models, leave an explanatory gap compared with classical learning theory. It clarifies for a philosophical audience what Occam-style arguments can and cannot justify methodologically.

entry.title: A Theory of Conditional Collapse under Low-Rank Weight-Space Ablations: I. The Single-Block Theory and Synthetic Validation

author.name: Abdallah Khemais

entry.summary: Provides exact theoretical conditions under which weight-space ablation and activation patching agree about a component being causally responsible for a behavior, using an idealized additive residual-stream model. Results characterize when deleting carriers collapses matched input pairs onto identical outputs and quantify the error when conditions hold only approximately.

entry.title: Omega-S: A Functional Resilience Index for LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Alberto Acedo

entry.summary: Omega-S is a regularization penalty computed only from the current weight matrix that reduces catastrophic forgetting during fine-tuning, requiring no old data, Fisher information, or stored reference weights. On Llama-3-8B with LoRA it retains substantially more coding ability after prose fine-tuning than no regularization, tuned weight decay, or tuned EWC across ten seeds.

entry.title: Assessment of Conditional Diffusion Model for Synthetic Histopathology Image Generation

author.name: Seyed Kahaki, Shijie Li, Weijie Chen, Nicholas Petrick

entry.summary: Argues that FID and Inception Score are poorly suited to evaluating synthetic histopathology images because they depend on ImageNet-pretrained features, and proposes domain-specific metrics plus downstream task validation instead. The work comes from FDA-affiliated researchers assessing conditional diffusion generation for pathology.

entry.title: MemArena: An Ego-Centric Benchmark for On-Device Agentic Personal Memory Assistants at Scale

author.name: Jiadong Zhang, Xiaosong Ma

entry.summary: MemArena is a benchmark for on-device personal memory assistants built from a simulated world of 50 agents over 15 days, producing dense ego-centric multi-session interaction histories with co-generated ground truth across recall, reasoning, and trustworthiness dimensions. It evaluates five open-weight readers against several memory backends including BM25 RAG and oracle retrieval.

entry.title: DenialRAG: Single-Document RAG Poisoning via Embedded Parametric Denial

author.name: Abay Zhurekbay, Tao Liu, Fan Li

entry.summary: DenialRAG poisons a retrieval corpus with a single document that explicitly names the correct answer, refutes it, and supplies an attacker-controlled justification for the wrong answer, in contrast to prior attacks that avoid mentioning the truth. Placing both answers in the same retrieved passage embeds the conflict directly in the context.

entry.title: TQLite: Multi-LLM Jury Guided Distillation for Real-time MQM Translation Quality Evaluation

author.name: Bhavin Jawade, Cameron R. Wolfe

entry.summary: Benchmarks small, large, and reasoning models on MQM-based translation quality evaluation, then introduces TQLite, a distillation framework using a multi-LLM jury to teach small models the required evaluation reasoning. The goal is real-time quality scoring at deployment scale without paying reasoning-model inference costs.

entry.title: Stochastic Saddle Avoidance Beyond Unit Excitation and Smoothness: A Pathwise Lyapunov-Perron Framework

author.name: Junwen Qiu, Bohao Ma, Andre Milzarek, Junyu Zhang

entry.summary: Proves almost-sure avoidance of strict saddle points for stochastic recursions without the unit excitation assumption that noise be uniformly informative in every direction. This matters for interpolation regimes where noise vanishes near stationarity and finite-sum problems where gradient noise lies in a low-dimensional subspace.

entry.title: ContinualSkillBench: Can LLM Agents Truly Evolve Their Capabilities?

author.name: Tianyi Guan, Yiding Wang, Haotong Yang, Siyuan Cao, Shirui Liu, Yi Hu, Jiaqi Li, Muhan Zhang

entry.summary: ContinualSkillBench evaluates whether LLM agents with external skill libraries genuinely accumulate and reuse capability, across five domains of 100 interconnected subtasks ordered by difficulty. Sequential execution helps unevenly across models and domains, and in-context learning performs comparably to explicit skill libraries. Questions the value proposition of current skill-library agent frameworks.

entry.title: OncoTriad-QA: A Patient-Level Radiology-Pathology-Genomics Benchmark for Pan-Cancer Reasoning

author.name: Ahnaf Munir, Dannong Wang, Michael W. McDonald, Mubarak Shah, Pegah Khosravi, Yu Tian

entry.summary: OncoTriad-QA is a patient-level pan-cancer benchmark with 86.1k questions over 9,281 TCGA cases, aligning CT/MRI imaging, whole-slide pathology, mutations, copy-number, methylation, RNA-seq, and clinical metadata. It tests whether medical LLMs and VLMs can integrate several evidence streams rather than answering isolated single-modality questions. Fills a real gap in clinically realistic multimodal evaluation.

entry.title: Emulate or Estimate? The Divergent Strengths of Base and Post-Trained Language Models for Opinion Simulation

author.name: Seth Grief-Albert, Jessica Bo, Difan Jiao, Ashton Anderson

entry.summary: Resolves conflicting findings on LLM opinion simulation by distinguishing emulation (generating individual responses that aggregate to a distribution) from estimation (directly predicting the population distribution), evaluating six matched base and post-trained models on the Pew American Trends Panel. Base models are stronger emulators while post-trained models are better estimators. Clarifies methodology for computational social science uses of LLMs.

entry.title: GUI-Lens: Coarse-to-Fine Cropping for GUI Grounding with General-Purpose VLMs

author.name: Zichuan Fu, Shirong Wang, Wenlin Zhang, Guojing Li, Yimin Deng, Jingtong Gao, Junjia Qi, Hanyu Yan, Yefeng Zheng, Xiaopeng Li, Wanyu Wang, Xian Wu, Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: GUI-Lens lets a general-purpose vision-language model ground GUI instructions through a coarse-to-fine cropping loop with OCR text and detected UI elements, instead of committing to a single direct click prediction. This prevents an inaccurate first estimate from propagating on dense high-resolution interfaces.

entry.title: StreamDAM: Presence-Aware Memory for Real-Time Streaming Video Object Segmentation

author.name: Xiang Chen

entry.summary: StreamDAM shows that accuracy-leading video object segmentation trackers collapse under an honest 30 frames per second streaming protocol where late frames are penalized, tracing the failure to slow memory pipelines and lack of object-presence awareness. It rebuilds the memory machinery to run at frame rate governed by a learned presence signal.

entry.title: When and Where to Look: Adaptive Visual Evidence Scheduling for Efficient Long Video Understanding

author.name: Ke Li, Jiayu Chen, Maoliang Li, Zihao Zheng, Hailong Zou, Hengyi Zhang, Xuanzhe Liu, Xiang Chen

entry.summary: EcoFrame is a training-free scheduler that decides how many video frames a vision-language model needs and where to look for more, using output entropy to stop early and feedback signals to expand the candidate pool. It aims for agent-like adaptivity without the cost of multi-round agentic search.

entry.title: CoT-Core: Accelerating LLM Evaluation via CoT-Aware Coreset Selection

author.name: Qihua Pan, Zhenheng Tang, Peijie Dong, Xiang Liu, Huacan Wang, Bo Li, Xiaowen Chu

entry.summary: CoT-Core is a training-free method for selecting a small representative subset of benchmark questions so LLM evaluation can be run cheaply during iterative development. Instead of lexical similarity, it clusters questions by embedding zero-shot chain-of-thought reasoning trajectories, capturing shared underlying logic and avoiding the cold-start problem of item-response-theory approaches. This targets the growing cost of continuous evaluation in model development pipelines.

entry.title: Request-Level Energy Attribution for Batched LLM Serving

author.name: Qi Luo, Kunlin Li, Ziwen Wang, Dongsheng Wang, Yun Chen

entry.summary: JouleShare tackles the problem that GPU power telemetry is aggregate while sustainability reporting and chargeback need per-request energy figures in batched serving. An offline replay harness under vLLM establishes measured ground truth for request-level energy, allowing the authors to quantify how far common accounting heuristics deviate from a Shapley-fair allocation. It provides the first measured baseline for evaluating attribution rules.

entry.title: Personalizing Large Language Model Agents with Small Policy Models

author.name: Dian Jin, Zhi Zhang, Huichao Li, Yihe Pan, Rundong Huang, Doudou Zhou

entry.summary: FABLE personalizes a frozen, possibly black-box LLM agent by learning a lightweight per-user execution policy from scalar bandit feedback, factorizing decisions about memory use, information acquisition, and response style. It avoids fine-tuning a proprietary backbone by placing a contextual bandit layer outside the host agent. This targets execution-level adaptation rather than merely surfacing user facts in the prompt.

entry.title: More Debate, Same Evidence: Structural Limits of Homogeneous Multi-Agent Groundedness

author.name: Yuelyu Ji

entry.summary: This study tests the common assumption that multi-agent judge panels improve groundedness verification, evaluating a homogeneous three-agent panel against a single-agent reference on six fact-verification and hallucination benchmarks. Accuracy differences range from plus 8.5 to minus 4.4 percentage points, with reliable gains on only two datasets, one reliable loss, and three inconclusive. The result argues that debate among similar models adds process without adding evidence.

entry.title: DGA$_2$D: Directed Graph-Guided Automated Algorithm Design with Large Language Models

author.name: Jiale Zhao, Zimu Chen, Sirui Mao, Wentao Yang, Yuxiang Bai, Liyuanjun Lai

entry.summary: DGA2D structures the open-ended program space for LLM-driven automated heuristic design as a directed graph where nodes are functional components, aiming to move beyond rigid solver templates toward system-level algorithm design for NP-hard problems. The graph structure is intended to address unreliable generated operators, huge search spaces, and poor credit assignment. It follows the FunSearch and evolutionary program-search lineage.

entry.title: Assuming You Knew: Fixing an Epistemic Semantics for Flow Policies Using Agentic AI

author.name: David A. Naumann

entry.summary: This paper corrects and machine-checks in the Rocq proof assistant an epistemic semantics for information flow policies with selective downgrading, repairing a formalization from a 2018 security conference paper that was acknowledged as flawed. Notably, the corrected proof development was produced with the aid of an agentic AI coding assistant. It doubles as a case study in AI-assisted formal verification of security semantics.

entry.title: Modeling Social Dynamics with an LLM-Enabled Agent Based Network-Dynamic (LAND) Model

author.name: Lynnette Hui Xian Ng, Kathleen M. Carley

entry.summary: The LAND model couples LLM-driven agents with network dynamics to simulate large-scale social behavior, instantiated in a scenario where 314,244 heterogeneous cyber-social and human agents exchange 529,327 messages over 30 days around a fictional contest. The authors analyze emergent dynamics across ego-network topology, semantic network evolution, coordination, and influence. It is a methodological demonstration of LLM-enabled social simulation at scale.

entry.title: Agentic Stage-One Stellarator Optimization: Autonomous Multi-Objective Search for Finite-Beta Equilibria

author.name: Tingjia Zhang, Hongke Lu, Zhuoran Meng, Runlai Xu

entry.summary: An agentic system autonomously orchestrates stage-one stellarator design, coordinating multi-objective optimization over 3D plasma boundaries and finite-beta MHD equilibria including resolution and objective-priority choices. Aims to raise design throughput beyond expert-driven iteration.

entry.title: Computing with Agentic Oracles

author.name: Jie Wang

entry.summary: Extends stochastic-oracle Turing machine theory to agentic oracles that pursue goals and touch environments, distinguishing orchestration token costs visible to the caller from hidden agentic token costs. Provides a complexity-style accounting framework for AI-augmented computation.

entry.title: Constructing Executable Analytical Knowledge Representations for Meta-Analysis Synthesis Using an Agentic Harness

author.name: Lingbo Li, Anuradha Mathrani, Teo Susnjak

entry.summary: Proposes an Executable Analytical Knowledge Representation that makes meta-analysis decisions such as effect-size formulation, outcome alignment, and admissibility explicit and independently verifiable rather than hidden in generated code or model outputs. Implemented via an agentic harness.

entry.title: HALT: Verification-Aware Stopping for Retrieval-Augmented Search Agents

author.name: Daeyoung Roh, Donghee Han

entry.summary: HALT is a lightweight stopping policy for retrieval-augmented search agents that halts when accumulated evidence covers the expected hop claims, instead of relying on generator confidence. Across three multi-hop QA benchmarks it cuts redundant retrieval while mostly preserving exact-match accuracy.

entry.title: Self-Certification of Representation Adequacy: Sequential Certification at Minimum Task Loss

author.name: Zijie Huang

entry.summary: Develops a four-layer theory of whether an agent can certify from its own transcript that its compressed state representation is adequate for optimal action, showing an irreducible per-round loss when the representation aliases histories requiring different actions. Prices external verification via a total-variation threshold and casts certification as optimal stopping in task-loss currency.

entry.title: AgentMemBench: A Systematic Benchmark for Evaluating Long-Term Memory Management Strategies in Conversational AI Agents

author.name: Ahmed Cherif

entry.summary: AgentMemBench compares five long-term memory strategies for conversational agents (context windowing, external key-value store, graph episodic memory, summarization, web-augmented memory) under identical conditions on LoCoMo, MultiDoc2Dial, and MSC. Reports retrieval, answer quality, faithfulness, footprint, and cost metrics together.

entry.title: SPARC-Rad: A Multimodal Benchmark Dataset and Evaluation Pipeline for Spatial and Anatomical Reasoning in Radiology Vision-Language Models

author.name: Satvik Tripathi, Mustafa Ege Seker, Kristian Quevada, Ebubechukwu D Enwerem, Pratham Khandelwal, Emine Meltem, Bera Koca, Shahriar Faghani, Jacinta Arnold, Dania Daye, Tessa S. Cook

entry.summary: SPARC-Rad is a manually curated benchmark of 300 radiologist-authored image-question pairs from healthy-control CT, MRI, and radiography studies, targeting spatial and anatomical reasoning rather than disease classification or report generation. It fills a gap in medical vision-language evaluation where existing benchmarks reward pattern recall over geometric and anatomical grounding.

entry.title: Counting the Cost of War Under Satellite Embargo: Zero-Shot Estimation of Impacted Infrastructure

author.name: Saleh Sakib Ahmed, M. Sohel Rahman

entry.summary: This work estimates conflict-damaged buildings without post-strike satellite imagery by having LLMs extract weapon payload data from incident reports, projecting blast radii via Hopkinson-Cranz scaling onto archival maps, then counting exposed structures with adaptive field-of-view segmentation and pseudo-height estimation. It offers a workaround when imagery blackouts block humanitarian damage assessment.

entry.title: ORCA: ORgan-Centroid Aggregation for Training-Free 3D CT Visual Token Compression

author.name: Renjie Liang, Zijian Xu, Jinqian Pan, Chengkun Sun, Zhengkang Fan, Shawn Li, You Qin, Mei Liu, Jie Xu

entry.summary: ORCA is a training-free visual token compressor for 3D CT input to vision-language models that merges adjacent tokens using organ segmentation guidance and adds sinusoidal encodings of each region's centroid to retain spatial layout. It replaces grid-average pooling, which can blend lesion, organ, and air into a single token.

entry.title: Tensor Probabilistic Model Checking of Finite-Horizon Markov Chains (Extended Version)

author.name: Jianlin Li, Nick Guo, Peter Ye, Yizhou Zhang

entry.summary: The paper recasts step-bounded reachability verification of Markov chains as dense tensor computation, proves the mapping sound, and implements it so off-the-shelf compiler toolchains can run the verification on GPUs and other accelerators. It targets the dense-transition regime where sparse symbolic and explicit representations scale poorly.

entry.title: Pretrain on Small Synthetic Data, Scale Large for Free: Symmetry-Aware Foundation Model for Logic Rule Induction

author.name: Yin Jun Phua

entry.summary: This work builds a symmetry-respecting foundation model for logical rule induction, adding a canonical export that decodes a discrete DNF rule from literal scores and is exactly equivariant to atom renaming, example order, polarity flips, and label swaps. Enforcing these symmetries lets a model pretrained on small synthetic schemas generalize to larger unseen schemas without retraining.

entry.title: CeQe: Grounding Lexical Retrieval in Semantic Evidence

author.name: Adam Kahirov, Umesh Deshpande, Swaminathan Sundararaman

entry.summary: CE-QE expands BM25 queries with terms that a cross-encoder, applied to top semantic search results, treats as decisive according to its per-token relevance attributions. Unlike classical pseudo-relevance feedback that recycles BM25's own possibly wrong top hits, expansion is seeded from semantic retrieval, letting lexical search cross the vocabulary gap.

entry.title: RadYOLO: Computationally Efficient 3D Object Detection and Segmentation in CT and MRI

author.name: Kai Geissler, Laurens M\"uller-Groh, Hans Meine

entry.summary: RadYOLO adapts YOLO11 to 3D medical volumes for joint detection and segmentation, and is compared against nnU-Net and nnDetection on five CT and MRI datasets. It beats nnDetection on four of five datasets and is stronger on lesion detection than nnU-Net while running fast on resource-constrained hardware.

entry.title: Coverage-Driven Adaptive Keyframe Selection for Video Understanding

author.name: Junyang Zhang, Puhan Luo, Chen Tang, Yuxi Shi, Xiang-Yang Li

entry.summary: CSES is a training-free keyframe selector for long-video understanding that adaptively decides how many frames to score and how many to keep, by estimating how peaked the frame-query relevance profile is rather than scoring hundreds or thousands of frames uniformly. It cuts vision-language model inference cost while preserving query-relevant coverage.

entry.title: Less Is More: Tuning Configurable Systems with Imperfect Fidelity

author.name: Yulong Ye, Miqing Li, Tao Chen

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates a less-can-be-more effect in configuration tuning: spending part of the budget measuring in a cheaper, imperfect-fidelity environment that merely resembles the target environment substantially improves final tuning quality per unit cost. The authors codify a conceptual fidelity framework for configurable systems to explain and exploit this.

entry.title: Who Belongs in the Eval Set? A Capability-Taxonomy-Driven Pipeline for Curating Regression Eval Sets in Agent-Extensibility Platforms

author.name: Tezan Sahu, Aritra Das, Pankaj Mittal, Sudipta Das

entry.summary: Describes an industrial pipeline for curating platform-side regression evaluation sets for agent extensibility surfaces in Microsoft 365 Copilot, projecting incoming customer eval queries into a capability taxonomy under a hard query-count budget. It formalizes a curation problem that existing customer-side eval frameworks ignore.

entry.title: KING: Embodiment-Aware Kinematic Graph Neural Network for Unified Motion Representation of Legged and Wheeled Robots

author.name: Taku Okawara, Aoki Takanose, Kenji Koide, Shuji Oishi, Masashi Yokozuka

entry.summary: KING is a graph neural network kinematic model that encodes robot embodiment structure (joints, wheels, feet) as a graph so a single learned motion model transfers across legged and wheeled platforms. It improves odometry in feature-poor environments where visual sensing and IMU integration fail.

entry.title: DynActiveGS: Active Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Hongbo Duan, Pengting Luo, Chengzhi Zhao, Yuanhao Chiang, Fangming Liu, Xueqian Wang

entry.summary: DynActiveGS performs active 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction in dynamic scenes by explicitly separating structural uncertainty from motion-induced uncertainty, then using those fields for viewpoint selection and path planning. It suppresses motion-corrupted observations during autonomous exploration.

entry.title: When Replanning Becomes the Bottleneck: Budgeted Replanning for Embodied Agents

author.name: Shuaijun Liu, Feiyang You, Xingwei Chen, Ningxin Su

entry.summary: BRACE treats LLM replanning in embodied agents as a budgeted control loop, deciding whether to replan, which mode to use, and how many tokens and how much latency to allocate against a service-level objective. It targets heavy-tailed replanning latency that average-latency and success metrics hide.

entry.title: DeepVoyager-VL: Incentivizing Vision-in-the-Loop Search for Long-Horizon Multimodal Agents

author.name: Huanyao Zhang, Jiepeng Zhou, Runhao Zhao, Yanzhe Shan, Jiaoyang Chen, Bowen Zhou, Bo Li, Fang Wang, Jialong Wu, Zhengwei Tao, Lang Mei, Xiaohan Yu, Liyan Liu, Chong Chen, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: DeepVoyager-VL trains multimodal agents for long-horizon deep search in which visual evidence drives intermediate reasoning steps and subsequent retrieval, not just the input or final answer. It targets knowledge-intensive open-world questions where static parametric knowledge fails.

entry.title: IACM-RL: Intent-Aware Context Management and Reinforcement Learning for Complex Tool Invocation under Dynamic Intent Fluctuations

author.name: Dingwei Zhu, Jiahan Li, Chengjun Pan, Yunxian Yang, Yunbin Zhao, Yunke Zhang, Zhonghang Lu, Zhuohui Sheng, Chenhao Huang, Jiahang Lin, Yajie Yang, Junlin Shang, Shichun Liu, Yuhui Wang, Honglin Guo, Junjie Ye, Xin Guo, Jiazheng Zhang, Ming Zhang, Shihan Dou, Zhiheng Xi, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xipeng Qiu, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: IACM-RL tackles long-horizon tool invocation when user intent fluctuates mid-task, synthesizing training trajectories across thirteen fluctuation scenarios and adding belief-state context management plus reinforcement learning to prevent obsolete constraints from causing intent drift and repeated API loops. It comes with a five-dimensional diagnostic metric suite.

entry.title: Population-Robust Feature Selection via Generalized Welfare Optimization

author.name: Ruiqi Lyu, Alistair Turcan, Bryan Wilder

entry.summary: PopFS learns a single shared, deployable feature set that works across multiple heterogeneous populations while allowing each population to fit its own model, using a tunable welfare objective to trade average benefit against protection of the worst-served group. Multitask sparse methods make the objective scalable.

entry.title: Scaling an Autoregressive Transformer for Single-Cell Generation

author.name: Aleksandr Sharipov, Yusif Mukhtarov, Igor Molybog

entry.summary: Trains a causal transformer with a learned quantized VAE tokenizer to generate single-cell gene expression vectors conditioned on cells of the same type, and characterizes both biological fidelity and pretraining-loss scaling behavior. Frames single-cell generation as a next-token prediction problem with measurable scaling laws.

entry.title: A Graph Signal Processing Perspective on Numerical Sequence Representations in LLM In-Context Learning

author.name: Jiajun Bao, Zihao Qi, Toni J. B. Liu, Gurbir Arora, Rapha\"el Sarfati, Nicolas Boull\'e, Christopher J. Earls

entry.summary: Applies a graph signal processing lens to how LLMs internally organize numerical sequences during in-context learning, treating attention as a token graph and hidden states as signals on its nodes. Spectral diagnostics and token-graph visualizations show representations become progressively differentiated in ways prior output-level error analyses could not reveal.

entry.title: On the Implicit Flatness Bias of Sharpness-Aware Minimization: A Linear Stability Analysis with Quantitative Hyperparameter Bounds

author.name: Jiaxin Deng, Junbiao Pang

entry.summary: Analyzes sharpness-aware minimization near an interpolating minimum via linear stability, proving that stable minima satisfy an explicit bound on the largest Hessian eigenvalue involving batch size, learning rate, and perturbation radius. This turns the perturbation radius from an isolated hyperparameter into part of a quantitative flatness relation.

entry.title: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Self-Distilled Reward Shaping

author.name: Ranxu Zhang, Guinan Chen, Chenshaodong, Jinghao Lin, Xiaozhou Xu, Sunzhe, Yanyong Zhang, Chao Wang

entry.summary: ADRS densifies sparse trajectory-level rewards in agentic reinforcement learning by having a frozen policy snapshot rescore fixed tokens from skill-free trajectories while conditioned on task-matched procedural skills, then calibrating those teacher scores across interaction steps and against realized returns. The calibrated signal is folded into native advantage construction for credit assignment.

entry.title: Tight Worst-Case Bounds for the Smallest Eigenvalue of ReLU NTK Gram Matrices

author.name: Zhao Song

entry.summary: Proves matching upper and lower bounds on the smallest eigenvalue of the ReLU neural tangent kernel Gram matrix in terms of a projective separation measure, showing the rate is tight up to constants. This eigenvalue controls convergence and generalization guarantees in overparameterized network analyses.

entry.title: Crayotter: Learning Long-Horizon Video Editing Agents via Group-Relative Preference Backpropagation

author.name: Lecheng Yan, Jianze Lin, Yichong Zhang, Ben Pan, Wenxi Li, Chenyang Lyu, Liting Zhou, Cathal Gurrin

entry.summary: Crayotter trains long-horizon video editing agents by converting same-task rankings into zero-sum advantages and redistributing them as bounded credit across semantic editing segments, since a global scalar quality score is ambiguous and temporally uninformative. A lagged allocator and guarded transmission stabilize the credit assignment.

entry.title: Explainable AI for the EU Right to Explanation: A Systematic Review of the Law-XAI Translation Gap

author.name: Benjamin Fresz, Elena Dubovitskaya, Marco F. Huber

entry.summary: Systematic review of over 2600 records on whether explainable AI methods can actually satisfy the EU Right to Explanation under GDPR Article 15 and AI Act Article 86, covering literature from 2024 onward. It documents a translation gap between legal requirements and what XAI techniques deliver.

entry.title: Particle-based Generalised Stochastic Optimisation

author.name: Jiechen Jackie Zhang, O. Deniz Akyildiz

entry.summary: Develops diffusion-based interacting particle methods for optimizing losses whose gradients are integrals over parameter-dependent distributions, covering generative model training, fine-tuning, and latent-variable learning. It proves exponential convergence of the mean-field dynamics and non-asymptotic error bounds for the particle approximation.

entry.title: LLM Serving in the Wild: An Empirical Study of Frameworks, Methods, and System Designs

author.name: Forough Majidi, Mohammad Mehdi Morovati, Foutse Khomh, Heng Li

entry.summary: Empirically studies how open-source projects actually adopt LLM serving frameworks including vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, LMDeploy, and FlashInfer, and which optimization techniques are used in combination. It documents the gap between what inference research proposes and what practitioners deploy.

entry.title: Beyond Initialization Loss: A Systematic Study of Token Embedding Initialization Strategies for LLM Vocabulary Extension

author.name: Raviraj Joshi, Utkarsh Vaidya, Sanjay Singh Chauhan, Niranjan Wartikar

entry.summary: Systematically compares more than twenty embedding-initialization strategies for extending an LLM vocabulary to Hindi, using Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B as the base. Subword composition methods beat vocabulary averaging and learned or external mappings such as FOCUS and top-k retrieval, and input-output asymmetry matters. Practical guidance for adapting existing models to new languages efficiently.

entry.title: Learning Clinical-Trial Strategy: Offline Policy Training for Decision Agents

author.name: William Bolton, Philip Torr

entry.summary: Frames oncology clinical development as an offline decision problem where an agent predicts a drug program's next six-month trial portfolio, backed by a new dataset of 31.7k heterogeneous public records forming 881 decision episodes across 45 programs. Compares behavioral cloning, reward-weighted cloning, and other offline objectives. A rare attempt to bring offline RL to strategic pharma decision-making.

entry.title: Aligned in Form, Not in Meaning: The Comprehension - Containment Decoupling of LLM Safety in Low-Resource Bangla Derogatory Speech

author.name: Shadab Bin Habib, A K M Ferdous Reza Habib, Subarno Neel, Adib Sakhawat

entry.summary: Audits five frontier LLMs on native Bangla derogatory speech across six protocols and finds a comprehension-containment decoupling: models comprehend low-resource slurs slightly worse yet leak harmful tokens at essentially identical high rates as in English, with severity judgments tracking surface anatomical cues instead of compositional harm. Argues safety alignment is bound to high-resource surface forms rather than harmful meaning. Important evidence on the multilingual limits of current alignment.

entry.title: Scalable Frequency- and Length-Aware Subdocument Deduplication for Large Language Model Pretraining

author.name: Hai Wang, Chenhao Wang, Qifeng Cai, Yixiu Liu, Miao Peng, Nuo Chen, Yuanlin Tu, Chengcheng Xu, Feng Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a scalable subdocument deduplication framework for pretraining corpora that decouples duplicate detection from retention policy, using natural-boundary segmentation and global hash-based counting to catch cross-shard duplicates missed by per-shard suffix arrays. Retention becomes frequency- and length-aware rather than a fixed copy policy. Data-pipeline work with direct effect on pretraining quality and compute efficiency.

entry.title: ICO: Enhancing Semantic-Shift Jailbreaks via Iterative Context Optimization

author.name: Hujian Zhu, Yihao Huang, Felix Juefei-Xu, Xinfeng Li, Peng Zeng, Simeng Qin, Qing Guo, Geguang Pu

entry.summary: Improves semantic-shift jailbreaks, which swap harmful terms for benign ones and rely on context to make the model reinterpret them, by showing that contexts differ greatly in their semantic-shift capability and optimizing context iteratively. Reports substantially higher attack effectiveness than prior semantic-shift methods. Contributes an attack-side insight relevant to defense design.

entry.title: TASQ: Temporal-Adaptive Bit Sparsification Quantization for Diffusion Models

author.name: Seokho Han, Dongwei Wang, Jinhee Kim, Yiran Chen, Kang Eun Jeon, Huanrui Yang, Jong Hwan Ko

entry.summary: TASQ decouples storage and compute cost in quantized diffusion models by keeping one maximum-precision weight buffer while learning a temporal-spatial mask that truncates least-significant bits per layer and denoising step. Memory stays at the worst case while bit operations drop at less sensitive timesteps.

entry.title: Bridging Online and Offline Handwriting via Differentiable Physical Rendering

author.name: Seonmi Park, Seunghyun Shin, Vihaan Misra, Dongmin Shin, Ukcheol Shin, Jean Oh, Hae-Gon Jeon

entry.summary: This work links online handwriting trajectories to offline handwriting images through a differentiable physical rendering model of the pen, allowing stroke kinematics and pixel appearance to be trained jointly without paired trajectory-image data. It unifies two previously separate paradigms of handwriting generation.

entry.title: Test-Time Scaling for Safe Text-Guided Image Generation via Intermediate Clean Estimates

author.name: Jinya Sakurai, Shueicheng Yan, Xun Xu

entry.summary: This safety method detects prohibited content during text-to-image generation by inspecting the intermediate clean image estimate with a sparse margin objective, then intervening at test time rather than unlearning concepts through training. It argues prompt-only defenses miss visual signals that only appear mid-generation.

entry.title: PolyLayout: Multi-room Manhattan Layout Estimation

author.name: Gustav Hanning, Shaohui Liu, R\'emi Pautrat, Marc Pollefeys, Kalle {\AA}str\"om, Viktor Larsson

entry.summary: PolyLayout estimates indoor room layouts as Manhattan 3D polygons and optimizes multiple rooms jointly, sharing building-level structure such as dominant directions, floor plane, and ceiling height. A network on top of pretrained visual features predicts the optimization objective and is trained end to end with layout-only supervision.

entry.title: MT-Web2Code: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Multi-Turn Regional Reconstruction and Localized Modification

author.name: Qiming Li, Shujie Hu, Haohan Liu, Xiaocheng Feng, Songxiang Liu, Guanglu Wan

entry.summary: MT-Web2Code benchmarks coding agents on multi-turn web development tasks that mirror real workflows: reconstructing missing page regions and making localized element edits inside existing code, across 102 tasks in 16 domains. Deterministic repair trajectories are generated by a scalable reverse-construction process instead of costly per-turn human annotation.

entry.title: IRIS: Visual-Semantic Binding for Forgery-Resistant Watermarking of Diffusion Images

author.name: Xiaoyan Feng, Zheng Gao, Tong Guan, Rui Bao, Bokang Zeng, Xiaoyu Li, Jiaojiao Jiang

entry.summary: IRIS is a training-free in-generation watermark for diffusion images that binds the mark to the semantics of the very image it marks, resolving the chicken-and-egg problem that the mark must enter sampling before the image exists. Binding is designed to break under semantic change while surviving benign processing, preventing transplantation of marks onto unmarked images.

entry.title: MuRA: Multi-Rank Adaptation for Efficient and Effective Test-Time Vision-Language Generalization

author.name: Gengyuan Liu, Nanzhou Wang, Chang Liu, Qinwen Wu, Zhenhao Wang, Jiacong Wang, Bokui Chen, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: MuRA argues that fixed-rank LoRA is a bottleneck for test-time adaptation of vision-language models because visual inputs vary in information density, causing underfitting on complex scenes and overfitting on simple ones. It dynamically selects and fuses adapter modules of different ranks based on token-level visual complexity.

entry.title: Pattern over Pixels: Measuring Pattern Completion Bias in Multimodal Code Generation

author.name: Khai-Nguyen Nguyen, Oscar Chaparro, Antonio Mastropaolo

entry.summary: This benchmark measures whether multimodal models translating webpage screenshots into front-end code default to repeated UI patterns instead of reading the actual pixels, by perturbing one element in a repeated pattern and asking the model to recover the masked value. It builds 1,440 test screenshots from curated Design2Code pages across structural and text-style patterns.

entry.title: NeuroMosaic: Anatomically Grounded Multimodal Large Language Modeling for Molecularly Aware Glioma Reasoning from 3D MRI and Clinical Narratives

author.name: Yantong Liu, Zheyu Zhang, Runpeng Liu, Mu Xitang, Seong-Yoon Shin, Hyun-Ae Lee

entry.summary: NeuroMosaic converts multi-sequence 3D brain MRI into anatomy-indexed regional tokens, aligns them with clinical narratives and molecular concepts, and produces glioma subtype predictions linked back to specific MRI regions with selective risk control. Reported internal and external macro-F1 scores are in the high seventies to low eighties across four cohorts.

entry.title: Staying on Spec: Real-Time Monitoring under Uncertainty with a Maritime Case Study

author.name: Elizabeth Dietrich, Hanna Krasowski, Emir Cem Gezer, Roger Skjetne, Asgeir Johan S{\o}rensen, Murat Arcak

entry.summary: A real-time framework monitors whether a robotic system is satisfying complex task and safety specifications under uncertainty, using data-driven reachable sets instead of requiring explicit uncertainty distributions or large datasets. It is instantiated for maritime navigation traffic rules and validated in simulation and on hardware.

entry.title: ValueFormer: A Causal Transformer Value Function with Stage-Aware Labels for Semi-Autonomous Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Inkyu Sa, Konstantin Stulov, Rajat Bhageria

entry.summary: ValueFormer trains a compact causal transformer over frozen visual features to predict dense per-frame progress values for vision-language-action policies, so that silently failing rollouts can be detected without reinforcement learning or expensive real-robot exploration. The paper argues the critical design choice is the label shape, requiring dense continuous stage-aware supervision rather than a terminal success bit.

entry.title: PFM-HR: Pose Flow Matching for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Yukang Gao, Yi Gu, Yangchen Zhou, Xingyu Chen, Zhaorui Wang, Fanghai Zhang, Hanyang Cao, Zhengyang Shen, Ji Ma, Runhan Zhang, Lei Han, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: PFM-HR trains a reusable flow-matching pose prior on large amounts of unordered humanoid pose data and introduces a pose geometry score that measures whether policy-induced joint changes align with the local geometry of pose variation captured by the prior. The score modulates tracking rewards so exploration favors structured pose transitions while the prior stays frozen.

entry.title: CrystalMem: Elastic Memory for Self-Evolving LLM Agents via Knowledge Crystallization

author.name: Beining Wu, Jun Huang

entry.summary: CrystalMem addresses memory hysteresis in self-evolving agents: after a cloud memory quota is squeezed and later restored, agent capability does not recover to its prior level because deletion and one-way compression destroy material needed for rebuilding. The authors prove a residual-deficit floor for any keep-or-drop policy and propose an elastic sidecar that demotes entries across four fidelity states using a crystallization-energy schedule ordered by advantage weighting. It makes agent memory reversibly compressible under fluctuating budgets.

entry.title: Evolutionary Curriculum Learning Improves Biological Sequence Modeling

author.name: Richard Zhu, Kento Nishi

entry.summary: Evolutionary Curriculum Learning trains variational autoencoders on multiple sequence alignments by progressively exposing the model to homologous sequences of increasing evolutionary distance from sampled anchors on a power-law schedule, rather than treating all sequences as exchangeable. It is applied to two architecturally distinct VAE models on two biological tasks. The idea exploits phylogenetic structure that standard training discards.

entry.title: PMMC: Prospective Multimodal Memory Compilation for Long-Term LVLM Agents

author.name: Jingyu Sun, Yan Lin, Yuyang Xue, Yifan Wang, Zhengtao Yao, Rui Qian, Zefeng Xu, Jiachen Li, Xianyang Liu, Jiancheng Pan, Jingyuan Sun, Syed Murtuza Baker, Hongpeng Zhou

entry.summary: PMMC shifts multimodal memory work from query time to consolidation time: a Questioner predicts likely future questions, a Planner compiles question-conditioned memory programs over accumulated interactions, and a Doubter verifies them. This avoids reducing visual experience to text summaries or relying on brittle retrieve-then-reason pipelines when questions need image-text binding, temporal updates, or fine visual detail. The target is long-horizon large vision-language model agents.

entry.title: Fighting Fire with Fire: On the Feasibility of Protecting Exercises Against AI Cheating

author.name: Tobias Braun, Jonas Grebe, Louis Rethfeld, Marcus Rohrbach

entry.summary: Tests whether adversarial perturbations on images in multimodal multiple-choice homework can steer AI solvers toward preset wrong answers, creating a statistical fingerprint of students who copy from a model. Frames adversarial ML as an education-integrity defense.

entry.title: A New Theory of Value for Post-AGI Economics

author.name: Keyun Ruan

entry.summary: Proposes Flourishing Value Theory as an economic value framework for a post-AGI world, defining value as counterfactual, distribution-sensitive contribution to durable human capabilities within social and planetary limits. Argues price, labour input, and output measures diverge from welfare once cognitive work is automated.

entry.title: GABench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Agents on Graph Analysis Tasks

author.name: Jiarui Tan, Zhongjian Zhang, YaBo Guo, Jiawei Liu, Yujie Xing, Muhan Zhang, Cheng Yang, Chuan Shi

entry.summary: GABench evaluates LLM agents on graph analysis by requiring them to operate in an actual graph environment with tools rather than answering text-embedded graph questions. Covers a wider range of graph tasks and graph types than prior benchmarks.

entry.title: RL-Lock: Reinforcement Learning for Generating Interlocking Assemblies

author.name: Xuyang Ma, Chaewoon Kim, Haonan Zhang, Rulin Chen, Ziqi Wang, Peng Song

entry.summary: RL-Lock casts generation of interlocking 3D assemblies as sequential voxel assignment learned by reinforcement learning, rather than one-shot shape decomposition. Produces parts held together purely by geometry without glue or fasteners.

entry.title: Trajectories That Segment Themselves: Agent-Declared Boundaries as a Training Unit

author.name: Jingxi Wei

entry.summary: Proposes collection-time semantic self-segmentation, where a coding agent declares its own falsifiable hypotheses and phase boundaries while generating a trajectory, producing variable-length semantic training units without gold patches, replay, or a retrospective segmenter. Named conjectures also give reviewers something to negate directly.

entry.title: Not All EEG Moments Are Equal: Position-Adaptive Time Scheduling for EEG Generation

author.name: Boheng Liu, Ziyu Li, Chenghua Duan, Qing Li, Xia Wu

entry.summary: Proposes conditional flow matching for EEG generation with position-adaptive time scheduling that modulates per-position flow progress using reconstruction error, plus factorized spatio-temporal attention. Motivated by the observation that channels and time segments within an EEG sample are not equally difficult and should not share one global time schedule.

entry.title: GRAIN: Molecules Are Not the Right Granularity -- Active-Ingredient Modeling for Safe Medication Recommendation

author.name: Juao Fan, Jinhan Li, Shengxin Zhu

entry.summary: GRAIN argues that the right granularity for safe medication recommendation is the active ingredient rather than the drug code or molecular substructure, and builds a recommender on a selective state-space backbone over longitudinal patient records. The goal is accurate polypharmacy recommendation with fewer adverse drug-drug interactions.

entry.title: Optimising for Flourishing: Flourishing Metrics and Return on Flourishing as Success Criteria for Artificial Intelligence and Post-AGI Economic Systems

author.name: Keyun Ruan, Jonathan D. Teubner, John M. Bremen

entry.summary: The authors argue human flourishing should be a primary success criterion for AI and for prospective post-AGI economies, proposing an extensible Flourishing Metrics framework across physical, emotional, financial, relational, and spiritual dimensions plus a Return on Flourishing measure to sit alongside capability and safety evaluations. It is a conceptual synthesis rather than an empirical study.

entry.title: Learning-Based Motion Planning for Dynamic Environments: From Foundational Algorithms to Emerging Paradigms

author.name: Zongyuan Shen, Shalabh Gupta, Shancheng Zhao, Dehua Zhou, Gao Wang, Rui Cheng, Yaming Ou, Zhongqiang Ren, Yikui Zhai, C. L. Philip Chen

entry.summary: This survey reviews motion planning in dynamic environments from roughly 2015 to 2025, revisiting classical planners as algorithmic foundations and then examining how learning-based methods extend, complement, or interact with them across autonomous driving, service robotics, crowd navigation, and multi-robot systems. It is positioned as a reference framework connecting the two literatures.

entry.title: Beyond Gene Reconstruction: Learning Cell Representations through Complementary Transcriptomic Views

author.name: Jiaqi Xiong, Yuntao hu, Yu Zheng, Yifei Shi, Xinyue Guo, Jiaxin Qi

entry.summary: Proposes contrastive pretraining for single-cell foundation models using complementary transcriptomic views built from co-expression-guided gene partitioning, expression-aware negative sets and competence-gated contrastive loss. It targets whole-cell representation quality rather than masked gene reconstruction.

entry.title: Caliber: Cross-Architecture Extraction-Cost Control for Score-Returning APIs

author.name: Chi Wang, Hanwen Wang, Yu Xia, Zihan Wang, Guangdong Bai

entry.summary: Caliber defends score-returning prediction APIs against model extraction by adding calibrated Gaussian noise to logits, with proofs that agreement degrades monotonically in noise scale and that attackers face a provable per-query cost to denoise. It frames the utility-versus-extraction tradeoff as a calibration problem.

entry.title: ACE-GraphRAG: Agentic Context Engineering for Hierarchical GraphRAG

author.name: Yongfeng Huang, Yuren Lai, Ruiying Chen, Haoyu Huang, Mingming Zhao, James Cheng

entry.summary: ACE-GraphRAG adds an inference-time context policy layer over hierarchical GraphRAG that adaptively supplements retrieved context via parallel depth-oriented and breadth-oriented retrieval branches and task-conditioned adaptation. It targets the mismatch between multi-resolution graph representations and query-specific context needs.

entry.title: Linear Multi-Timescale Retention as a Memory-Efficient Vision-Language Bridge

author.name: Ashfak Yeafi, Mehedi Hasan, Md Khairul Islam

entry.summary: LIA-MTR is a linear-complexity cross-modal bridge for vision-language models that uses ELU positive feature maps, adaptive write gating and log-linearly distributed recurrent decays to compress visual token sequences into bounded memory states. It seeks the O(N) scaling of MLP connectors without losing spatial routing and global scene understanding.

entry.title: Weights or Skills? A Survey of Robot-Learning Techniques: from Action-Predicting Weights to Robots that Write their Own Skills

author.name: Gaytri Jena, Kapil Wanaskar, Vinija Jain, Aman Chadha, Vasu Sharma, Amitava Das

entry.summary: This survey organizes robot learning along a weights-versus-skills axis, contrasting vision-language-action policies that bake competence into frozen parameters with agents that author and refine executable skill code. Its main analytic move is ranking code-as-policy systems by degree of self-improvement, up to loops combining execution feedback, skill memory, and evolutionary search.

entry.title: Energy-Efficient LLM Serving via Disaggregated Attention--FFN and Flexible Frequency Scaling

author.name: Cunchen Hu, Liangliang Xu, Tian Liu, Min Lyu, Yongkun Li, Sa Wang, Shuo Quan, Yanan Yang, Wenda Tang, Yiduo Wang, Fu Yu, Jie Wu

entry.summary: AFlex observes that attention and feed-forward operators have different energy-optimal GPU frequencies that shift with inference phase and workload, and exploits this with disaggregated attention-FFN execution plus flexible frequency scaling. It cuts LLM serving energy while respecting service-level objectives.

entry.title: Divisive Normalization Shapes Low-Rank Slow Manifolds for Continuous Working Memory

author.name: Zhaotian Gu, Jie Su, Weiwei Wang, Chang Liu, Tianyi Qian, Dahui Wang

entry.summary: The Recurrent Divisive Normalization Network adds a minimal dynamic division operation, inspired by a canonical cortical computation, to recurrent networks and shows via dynamical systems analysis that it yields low-rank slow manifolds supporting continuous working memory. This addresses both the fine-tuning fragility of classic continuous attractors and the tendency of GRUs and LSTMs to shatter continuous variables into discrete attractors.

entry.title: CompanionBench: A Theory-Anchored, Real-World-Grounded Benchmark for AI Emotional Companionship

author.name: Yao Liu, Guangjia Chai, Yuming Huang, Jihao Huang, Lei Wang, Junchen Wan

entry.summary: CompanionBench is an interactive bilingual benchmark for emotional companion agents that grounds both its scenarios and its trained user simulator in de-identified real conversation data, uses a hidden disclosure gate to branch trajectories on agent behavior, and evaluates ten theory-derived capabilities. It also explicitly measures judge pathologies such as same-family favoritism and scale drift.

entry.title: Who Should Be Generated? Justifying Demographic Targets in Open-Ended Generation

author.name: Zeshen Zheng, Yujia He, Qianmian Lin, Xiangyue Huang, Wenqing Chen

entry.summary: Formalizes the missing-target problem in generative fairness audits: when a prompt leaves demographics unspecified, what reference distribution should outputs be compared against? The paper decomposes target construction into explicit normative commitments (evaluative object, prior admissibility, allocation, and more) so audits can justify rather than assume their targets.

entry.title: Sphere Retraction Normalizations

author.name: Jie Zhang, Cheng-Fang Su, Yi-Jui Huang, Min-Te Sun

entry.summary: Generalizes geodesic normalization of residual connections by showing that on the hypersphere the whole family of Riemannian retraction maps reduces to one scalar design choice, namely how update magnitude converts to rotation angle. Provides a unified view of norm-preserving residual streams in deep networks.

entry.title: GoT-CD: Graph-of-Thoughts Causal Discovery and the Fragility of Post-hoc Path-Specific Fairness Audits

author.name: Nitish Nagesh, Elahe Khatibi, Thomas Dean Hughes, Mahdi Bagheri, Pratik Gajane, Amir M. Rahmani

entry.summary: Shows that path-specific counterfactual fairness audits inherit errors from the causal-discovery step, and that graph-of-thoughts style LLM discovery can produce graphs whose aggregate structural scores look acceptable while the specific pathway an audit depends on is missing. Argues audits should be evaluated on pathway survival rather than global edge metrics.

entry.title: Bayesian Data Reweighting Improves Multimodal Retrieval for Knowledge-Based Visual Question Answering

author.name: Jingchen Sun, Shaobo Han, Ruiyi Zhang, Naresh Kumar Devulapally, Ming Liu, Yitao Long, Vishnu Suresh Lokhande, Changyou Chen

entry.summary: Proposes Bayesian data reweighting for training multimodal retrievers, treating query-document importance as latent variables and inferring posterior weights that downweight likely false negatives rather than treating all unmatched pairs as equally negative. Reports consistent retrieval gains for knowledge-based visual question answering across several retrievers.

entry.title: Double Descent in Gradient Boosting Decision Trees via Split-Candidate Scaling

author.name: Ryuichi Kanoh

entry.summary: Proposes the number of split candidates as an operational capacity axis for gradient boosted trees, enabling study of double descent in a model class lacking an obvious width parameter. An empirical tree-kernel diagnostic links growth of kernel rank toward sample size to the interpolation-threshold regime.

entry.title: Noise-Aware Shrinkage for Differentially Private Zeroth-Order Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

author.name: Lele Zheng, Weifeng Kong, Xinyi Zhang, Ke Cheng, Tao Zhang, Yulong Shen

entry.summary: SAGE improves differentially private zeroth-order fine-tuning of LLMs by adaptively shrinking privatized update estimates according to estimated signal quality, subtracting the known Gaussian noise variance from the observed second moment and stabilizing the estimate over time. This prevents noise-dominated updates from receiving full weight when useful signal is weak.

entry.title: Quantization Effects on Biomedical LLM Reliability

author.name: Anton Rasmussen, Hong Qin

entry.summary: Controlled study of Mistral-7B variants on biomedical sentence classification across FP16, INT8, and INT4 shows that the probability extraction protocol, especially summed versus mean token log-likelihood, dominates apparent calibration more than quantization does. Switching scoring rules can reverse the calibration ranking between models.

entry.title: When Correct Solutions Repeat: Rarity-Aware Credit Redistribution for GRPO

author.name: Zhe Cao, Miaowen Wen, Fangjiong Chen

entry.summary: Identifies a structural bias in GRPO-style RL with verifiable rewards: frequently sampled correct solution forms accumulate disproportionate positive advantage mass while rare correct forms get little credit. Cue-GRPO clusters verified-correct rollouts using deterministic strategy cues and redistributes advantages by cluster rarity, without any auxiliary model. Aims to preserve solution diversity during RLVR training.

entry.title: Sensitivity, Causality, and Repair Dissociate: A Layer-Wise Analysis of Perturbation Robustness and Its Scaling

author.name: Nathan Labiosa, David Buff, Ena Nayak, Erica Donno

entry.summary: Shows that three natural notions of which layer is responsible for a model's failure on surface-perturbed text (representation divergence, causal activation restoration, and adapter repairability) yield dissociating layer maps, with sensitivity and causality anti-correlated on models passing an identity-patch gate. Identifies two propagation regimes across a five-model panel and studies within-family scaling on Qwen2.5. A cautionary result for single-metric localization claims in interpretability.

entry.title: RealWeather: Realistic and Scene-Faithful Weather Translation with Driving World Models

author.name: Yuwei Ning, Liangzhi Wang, Yi Xiao, Zhenhua Wu, Yun Pang, Mingkun Chan, Jichang Li, Guanbin Li

entry.summary: RealWeather is a driving world model that translates driving videos into different weather conditions while preserving scene geometry, learning weather dynamics from real footage instead of synthetic renderings. It uses iterative data refinement with a pseudo-clear generation pipeline to avoid needing paired same-scene videos.

entry.title: HyperbolicDiffusion: Sharp & Scalable Tiled Generation on the Hyperbolic Plane

author.name: Hugo Caselles-Dupr\'e

entry.summary: HyperbolicDiffusion generates coherent images on the hyperbolic plane, where no rectangular canvas exists and area grows exponentially with radius, using a training-free window placement dynamic program with theoretical guarantees and a shared latent surface. A second geometry-derived stage re-noises and repairs blur at multi-window junctions.

entry.title: MultiCompose: Multi-Concept Personalized Composition with Per-Subject Attribute Binding

author.name: Ruirui Zhang, Zhengkai Zhao, Pan Gao

entry.summary: MultiCompose tackles generating one image containing several personalized subjects, each correctly bound to user-specified attributes such as clothing or held objects, by decoupling per-concept personalization from multi-subject composition. It also introduces a benchmark that jointly measures identity degradation and attribute leakage.

entry.title: Low-Dimensional High-Leverage Subspace Optimization: Beyond Full-Parameter Coupled Training for Neural Network Quantization

author.name: Peng Xia, Junbiao Pang, Zheng Huang

entry.summary: This paper identifies normalization affine parameters as a low-dimensional but high-leverage subspace controlling quantization robustness and proposes preconditioning them separately rather than coupling all parameters during quantization-aware training. The target is severe accuracy loss when low-bit quantizing compact networks.

entry.title: Progressive Learning of a Diffusion-based Inpainting Model for Separating Overlapped Fingerprints

author.name: Noor Hussein, Anil K. Jain, Karthik Nandakumar

entry.summary: This work reformulates separation of overlapping fingerprints as an inpainting problem and progressively trains a diffusion model across stages, motivated by latent prints from crime scenes and residue on live-scan sensors. It contrasts with rule-based orientation field completion and monolithic end-to-end networks.

entry.title: POMDPs for Autonomous Science Exploration

author.name: Daniel Guirguis, Nathan Wallace, Hanna Kurniawati, Salah Sukkarieh

entry.summary: The Science Hypothesis Map POMDP makes science-driven belief-space planning tractable by branching on inferred physical properties rather than raw high-dimensional sensor observations, while retaining learned observation models. This lets an exploring robot reason jointly about navigation and scientific hypotheses with principled uncertainty.

entry.title: Learning Context-Aware Motion Priors for Humanoid Control

author.name: Yunyang Mo, Yi Gu, Yangchen Zhou, Hanyang Cao, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: Context-Aware Motion Priors adapt a general humanoid motion prior to the current task context using high-advantage policy rollouts, avoiding manual skill labels, dataset partitioning, or separate skill discovery. This prevents a uniform prior from supplying guidance drawn from irrelevant or conflicting reference motions.

entry.title: Stochastic Multiple Shooting Trajectory Optimization via Sequential Local Policy Evaluation

author.name: Ashwin Gupta, Joseph Moore

entry.summary: Extends sampling-based trajectory optimization such as MPPI from single shooting to a multiple-shooting formulation where short action segments are linked by local feedback policies. This improves sample efficiency and convergence to terminal constraint sets and enables synthesis of approximate stabilizing policies along the trajectory.

entry.title: RF-HOI: Recognize Human-Object Interaction with Radio Frequency Signals

author.name: Lihao Wang, Linlu Gao, Jiacan Yu, Yanyu Lin, Yifan Yin, Jianxin Wang, Tianmin Shu, Renjie Zhao

entry.summary: RF-HOI is presented as the first framework to recognize human-object interactions using only radio frequency sensing, fusing mmWave radar for action recognition with RFID for object identification to overcome the fact that neither modality alone suffices. It targets privacy-sensitive and low-light settings where cameras fail. The paper also addresses limited training data across diverse interaction types.

entry.title: WM-Cov: Test Adequacy for Interactive World-Model-Style Autonomous Driving Simulation

author.name: Jianxun Cui, Ping Wu, Stanisa Peric, Marko Milojkovic, Vladan Devedzic

entry.summary: WM-Cov defines test adequacy for autonomous driving simulation built on interactive world models, where a scenario is no longer a fixed replayed trajectory but a reactive family whose evolution depends on the planner under test. It proposes a provider-agnostic evaluation layer that converts raw generative simulator outputs into evidence sufficient to justify a stopping decision for a stated testing intent. The framing addresses when closed-loop generative testing is enough.

entry.title: TrAC: Trace-Conditioned Answer Consistency for Efficient Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs

author.name: Dahai Yu, Lin Jiang, Rongchao Xu, Guang Wang

entry.summary: TrAC estimates answer reliability by feeding a completed reasoning trace back to the model and re-eliciting an answer, then measuring whether the re-elicited answer is consistent with and supported by the original. This fills a gap between passive token-confidence methods, expensive multi-sample approaches, and prefix-probing techniques. It offers a cheaper signal for abstention, human review routing, and adaptive compute allocation.

entry.title: CADIR: A Cross-Backend Editable Intermediate Representation for Agentic CAD Generation

author.name: Yu Liu, Jingzhe Ni, Yiming Chen, Junqi Huang, Ruofeng Tong, Min Tang, Peng Du

entry.summary: CADIR is an executable intermediate representation for agentic CAD generation built on the OCCT kernel, providing explicit compositional modeling operations, stable topological references, preserved construction history, and fine-grained execution diagnostics that work across CAD backends. It addresses the brittleness of generating backend-specific scripts or static geometry from natural language or images. The diagnostics are designed to feed agent repair loops.

entry.title: TrajWiki: Source-Grounded Memory Trajectories for Long-Horizon Dialogue Agents

author.name: Jingyu Sun, Yuyang Xue, Mingyang Li, Zhengtao Yao, Jiachen Li, Yang Cui, Wenhao Cai, Haozhe Liu, Fangying Wang, Magdalene Katharina Montgomery, Syed Murtuza Baker, Hongpeng Zhou

entry.summary: TrajWiki represents each long-horizon dialogue memory as a source-grounded evolution trajectory built from immutable episodic snapshots and claim-level updates, rather than as isolated records or overwritable state. This preserves how information originated, changed, conflicted, or became obsolete, making memory traceable, updatable, and diagnosable. It targets robustness failures in long conversational agents.

entry.title: The Graph Language: How Knowledge Graphs Speak to Large Language Models

author.name: Giuseppe Pirr\`o

entry.summary: GRALAN trains a language mediator that converts knowledge-graph structure into relational tokens inside a frozen LLM's embedding space, reframing KG question answering as entity classification over question subgraphs. Reports gains on multi-hop reasoning.

entry.title: CRAFTS: Collaborative Role-Adaptive Fine-Tuning of LLM Agents for Chemical Process Simulation

author.name: Ziyun Zhang, Yuxin Lin, Eldin Wee Chuan Lim, Xinghao Ding

entry.summary: CRAFTS decomposes chemical process simulation building into seven role-specialized fine-tuned LLM agents with deterministic IDAES/Pyomo verification gates between stages. Converts natural-language requests plus flowsheet diagrams into executable process models.

entry.title: MEGRAG: Multi-Granular Evidence Graphs for Answer-Aware Multi-Hop RAG

author.name: Weidong Bao, Yingying Sun, Jun Yang, Yilin Wang, Zili Wei, Yubin Bao, Fangling Leng, Minghe Yu, Tiancheng Zhang, Ge Yu

entry.summary: MEGRAG builds multi-granular evidence graphs for iterative multi-hop RAG and makes each retrieval step answer-aware so intermediate errors and redundancy do not accumulate before final aggregation. Targets the density-versus-noise tradeoff of single-granularity evidence.

entry.title: KC-Agent: A Dual-Process Cognitive Architecture for Efficient ML Model Improvement

author.name: Gusseppe Bravo-Rocca, Jordi Guitart, Ajay Dholakia, David Ellison, Puneet Jain

entry.summary: KC-Agent is a dual-process agent for maintaining production ML models under data drift, pairing fast memory-based reuse of previously discovered fixes with slower deliberate incremental updates, plus atomic changes and rollback for safe deployment. Evaluated on five datasets including real-world drift cases.

entry.title: ParEvalLayer: When Partial LLM-Agent Evaluations Support a Decision

author.name: Wei-Jung Huang, Bonan Shen

entry.summary: ParEvalLayer is a decision layer that reads partial paired agent-benchmark outcomes against a pre-registered comparison policy and reports whether one system is better, is not better, needs more evidence, or should not be compared. Guards against misleading early stopping when cheap or easy tasks are run first.

entry.title: LLM-OSDA: An Optimal-Stopping Dynamic Auction for Native Advertising in Multi-Turn LLM Conversations

author.name: Yan Fang, Jialin Chen, Chun Gan, Hang Yu, Mingjun Nie, Yeyu Zhang, Fengxiang He, Ching Law

entry.summary: LLM-OSDA designs an auction for advertising inserted natively into multi-turn LLM conversations, where the seller must choose not only which advertiser wins but when in the dialogue to insert, coupling optimal stopping with allocation. It combines Bellman stopping, winner allocation, and envelope pricing while keeping a bid-independent LLM layer to estimate contextual click quality and preserve truthfulness.

entry.title: Sixteen models, fewer than two voices: measuring ensemble dispersion where no answer is uniquely correct

author.name: Mario Vega-Barbas, Lidia Mora-Valenciano, Iv\'an Pau, Fernando Seoane, Farhad Abtahi

entry.summary: Sixteen language models from ten families produced only about 1.69 effective distinct formulations of a psychotherapeutic case, barely above the 1.43 obtained from repeated runs of a single model, measured with the Vendi Score. The paper argues that ensemble dispersion metrics validated against correctness break down on tasks with no uniquely correct answer, and that aggregate diversity numbers hide where the diversity actually lies.

entry.title: GraRe: Grasp Candidate Re-Ranking for Frozen 6-DoF Grasp Detectors

author.name: Jibao Yuan, Yuhui Zhao, Yinzhen Lv, Chao Xu, Shun Li, Chenxi Deng, Shaofei Chen

entry.summary: Observes that 6-DoF grasp detector confidence scores correlate poorly with actual grasp success, and introduces a transformer re-ranker that scores frozen detectors' candidates using candidate attributes, stratified local geometry and object context. It improves execution ordering without retraining the detector.

entry.title: CallScreenBench: Benchmarking On-Device Models as Phone Secretaries

author.name: Simiao Ren

entry.summary: CallScreenBench evaluates small on-device language models acting as phone secretaries screening unknown, potentially adversarial inbound callers, scoring five quality dimensions with paired counter-metrics rather than task success. It formalizes an agent setting where the user is absent and the counterparty may be hostile.

entry.title: Policy Optimality Measurement for Multi-Vehicle Decision-Making: From Extrinsic Indicators to Intrinsic Quality

author.name: Ye Han, Lijun Zhang, Dejian Meng

entry.summary: Proposes an information-theoretic diagnostic for multi-agent RL driving policies that uses a converged Monte Carlo tree search as an oracle baseline and scores policies by forward KL divergence, decomposed into lateral and longitudinal components. It aims to expose policy degradation that reward curves and success rates hide.

entry.title: MNC: Scope-Bound Semantic Declassification for Private LLM-Agent Communication

author.name: Jinghan Xu, Longze Fan, Zeyuan Wang, Xinjin Li, Hankai Liu

entry.summary: Minimum-Necessary Communication is a typed declassification protocol for multi-agent LLM systems that picks a task-sufficient disclosure from application-defined candidates and binds it to explicit recipient, purpose, forwarding, lifetime, logging, and memory scopes, enforced by a reference monitor. It targets leakage through internal messages, tool arguments, logs, and persistent memory rather than only final outputs.

entry.title: AdaThinkV: Adaptive Thinking for Token-Efficient Video Reasoning

author.name: Jingqi Tian, Haoji Zhang, Lin Chen, Hongbo Jin, Haonan Xu, Tianrui Zhu, Xingming Shui, Shilin Ma, Wenjing Yang, Yansong Tang

entry.summary: AdaThinkV learns when a video multimodal model should reason explicitly versus answer directly, using reinforcement learning over matched rollouts in both modes and a ThinkGain signal that trades accuracy improvement against extra response length. It requires no difficulty labels, tuned thresholds, or external router.

entry.title: Geometry-Guided Layerwise FFN Width Allocation in Transformers

author.name: Timur Mudarisov, Mikhail Burtsev, Radu State

entry.summary: This paper allocates per-layer feed-forward width in transformers using forward-pass geometric measurements of how each layer transports token representations, quantified with correspondence-preserving shift, Gromov-Wasserstein distortion, and persistent homology. Across seven pretrained models it finds normalized geometric work is front-loaded, and derives an exact fixed-budget allocation from a layerwise surrogate.

entry.title: Can AI Agents Simulate A/B Test Outcomes? A Validation Framework for Agentic Experimentation

author.name: Stefan Hut, Lorenzo Masoero

entry.summary: This work formalizes using LLM agents conditioned on behavioral profiles to simulate randomized controlled trials before spending live traffic, and derives a two-layer error decomposition separating agent approximation error from subsampling error. The validation framework is agent-agnostic, so any behavioral model can be plugged in and audited.

entry.title: GROVE: Growing and Reasoning over Temporally Stratified Memory from Streaming Video Experience

author.name: Sitong Gong, Caixin Kang, Tianyu Yan, Guo Chen, Bo Zheng, Kaipeng Zhang, Yunzhi Zhuge, Xiang Ruan, Huchuan Lu, Yifei Huang

entry.summary: GROVE is a training-free memory system for wearable assistants that grows one hierarchy from a continuous video stream, consolidating fine-grained perceptual evidence into timestamped moments, episodes, and cross-day recurring patterns, each with a matched retrieval skill. It supports both answering questions about visual history and proactively recognizing when past experience is relevant now.

entry.title: Deep Divide-and-Reduce in Symbolic Regression

author.name: Yusong Deng, Yanjie Li, Weijun Li

entry.summary: Proposes a Deep Divide-and-Reduce method for symbolic regression that generalizes the mathematical simplification machinery of AI Feynman with proof-backed decomposition rules, reducing dependence on brute-force sub-expression search. Aims to recover complex governing equations more reliably.

entry.title: Multimodal Auto-regressive Transformer Surrogate for Modeling Variable Operations and Quantifying Uncertainty in Geological Carbon Storage

author.name: Yifu Han, Louis J. Durlofsky

entry.summary: Builds a multimodal autoregressive transformer surrogate that fuses 3D geomodels, scalar rock-physics parameters, and time-varying well controls to predict CO2 storage behavior under geological uncertainty, including staged perforation strategies. Enables fast uncertainty quantification and operational optimization for carbon sequestration.

entry.title: Verifier-Guided Model Discovery for Physical Dynamical Systems with Pretrained Symbolic Transformers

author.name: Farbod Faraji, Francesco Belardinelli

entry.summary: Wraps a pretrained symbolic transformer (ODEFormer) in a verifier-guided workflow that generates a pool of candidate equations from multiple trajectories and selects among them using dynamical and physical-admissibility checks. Improves transfer of symbolic model discovery to higher-dimensional real physical data.

entry.title: NANQ: Noise-Floor-Aware Mixed-Precision Non-Uniform Quantization for Analog Compute-in-Memory

author.name: Yizhe Chen, Wenshuai Yao, Saiya Wang, Yuannuo Feng, Wenbo Qi, Kechao Tang, Ngai Wong, Wenyong Zhou, Wang Kang

entry.summary: NANQ allocates quantization precision for analog compute-in-memory accelerators using measured, magnitude-dependent device noise profiles, giving finer resolution only where noise is low and assigning layer-wise bit-widths accordingly. Targets accuracy loss of low-bit models under real analog device variation.

entry.title: Contrast-invariant deep ptychography neural networks
