author.name: Albert Vong, Steven Henke, Oliver Hoidn, Hanna Ruth, Junjing Deng, Apurva Mehta, David Shapiro, Alexander Hexemer, Nicholas Schwarz

entry.summary: Improves generalization of deep ptychography reconstruction networks by factorizing learned object texture from measurement scaling and predicting real and imaginary components instead of amplitude and phase, plus a synthetic sampling strategy that matches phase distributions to experiments. Reports up to a fivefold reduction in Fourier-domain error under varying illumination.

entry.title: Joint Affine Spectral Shaping: Coupling Weight and Bias Updates Beyond Weight-Only Muon

author.name: Gongyue Zhang, Honghai Liu

entry.summary: Questions whether matrix spectral optimizers such as Muon should delegate bias vectors to a separate optimizer, instead forming a joint momentum matrix over weights and scaled biases and applying a capped regularized-inverse spectral map to both. A five-seed ablation on a small BERT trained on sentiment data reports modest accuracy and loss gains from joint affine shaping.

entry.title: SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation

author.name: Wen Wang, Jiahua Bao, Tu Yongsiqi, Yihao Liu, Haotian Zhou, Haoxuan Ma, Mengyu Zhou, Wenkui Fan, Junwei He, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: SMOPD tackles multi-reward reinforcement learning where rewards differ in granularity, such as a dense score combined with a binary signal, which per-dimension normalization alone fails to balance. It specializes separate policies per reward and merges them through online policy distillation.

entry.title: FinVerse: Financial Time-Series Benchmark

author.name: Jaehoon Lee, Jun Seo, Seunghan Lee, Tae Yoon Lim, Dongwan Kang, Hwanil Choi, Minjae Kim, Sungdong Yoo, Junhyeok Kang, Sangjun Han, Soonyoung Lee, Wonbin Ahn

entry.summary: FinVerse is a finance-domain time-series forecasting benchmark that evaluates models with decision-relevant criteria, such as directional accuracy tied to realized returns, rather than only uniform point-error metrics. It responds to the rise of time-series foundation models whose benchmark scores may not translate into useful decisions.

entry.title: ED-DiT: Physics-Guided Diffusion Pretraining for Transferable Molecular Representations from Electron Density

author.name: Liang Shuang, Haocheng Wang, Jiayi Song, Shuquan Ye, Ben Fei

entry.summary: ED-DiT pretrains a diffusion transformer on electron-density point clouds by reconstructing corrupted and partially masked log-density fields, producing transferable molecular representations grounded in electronic structure rather than graphs or SMILES. It tests whether density-field self-supervision transfers across electronic-structure-related downstream tasks.

entry.title: GENESIS: Towards Explainable Causal Discovery

author.name: Abhinav Thorat, Ravi Kumar Kolla, Vishak K Bhat, Harsh Vardhan Singh Chauhan, Niranjan Pedanekar

entry.summary: GENESIS makes LLM-assisted causal discovery auditable by producing a decision trace explaining why each edge was included or excluded from the learned DAG. This targets real deployments where no ground-truth graph exists and each structural claim must be defended independently.

entry.title: BBOWP-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Black-Box Optimization Word Problems

author.name: Yutaro Yamada, Kei Hiroshima, Nozomu Yoshinari, Kento Uchida, Shinichi Shirakawa

entry.summary: BBOWP-Bench evaluates whether LLMs can turn natural-language descriptions into well-posed black-box optimization problems, including designing the search space and choosing an algorithm, rather than writing explicit mathematical objectives. This covers practically common settings that existing formulation benchmarks omit.

entry.title: Field Aware Agent Skill Retrieval

author.name: Paimon Goulart, Liang Wu, Kelly Wan, Evangelos E. Papalexakis, Liangjie Hong

entry.summary: Argues that agent skill libraries should be retrieved as structured multi-field objects rather than flattened documents, computing sparse and dense similarities per field and combining them in a tensorized representation. As lifelong agents accumulate large skill banks, retrieval accuracy becomes the bottleneck.

entry.title: Quality Control Algorithms for Pattern Counting

author.name: Cassandra Marcussen, Ronitt Rubinfeld, Madhu Sudan

entry.summary: Extends the recently introduced quality-control problem framework, which asks algorithms to accept typical samples from a distribution while rejecting any input whose statistic deviates far from baseline, and develops sublinear algorithms for pattern-counting statistics. Exploits the asymmetry between worst-case soundness and average-case completeness. Theoretical work on testing randomness quality.

entry.title: Enhancing Tabular Learners with Context-Aware Semantic Embeddings

author.name: G\"unther Schindler, Maximilian Schambach, Johannes H\"ohne

entry.summary: CASE injects LLM-derived semantics into tabular learners by pre-filling the KV cache of a Gemma-3-based tabular language model with representative rows, so each row embedding is contextualized by dataset-level semantics rather than embedded in isolation. Targets the semantic blindness of gradient-boosting and neural tabular models to feature names and cell text. A neat use of KV-cache conditioning as a context anchor.

entry.title: Geo-Embed: Towards Unified Multimodal Embeddings for Urban Understanding

author.name: Jiapeng Li, Yong Li, Junjie Zhou, Fan Zhang, Yu Liu

entry.summary: Introduces GeoMEB, a benchmark standardizing 45 urban tasks over street-view imagery, remote sensing, text, region proposals, and temporal change, plus a unified multimodal embedding model for geospatial retrieval and reasoning. Tests whether a single embedding space can support spatial relations, fine-grained semantics, and temporal change beyond generic image-text matching. Relevant to geospatial foundation-model development.

entry.title: AgenticVAU: Multi-Agent Explore-Verify Reasoning for Video Anomaly Understanding

author.name: Yuxiang Duan, Huining Li, Ao Li, Shuai Feng, Lanju Kong, Ning Liu, Jian Zhang, Xingdong Sheng, Yuntao Du

entry.summary: AgenticVAU is a training-free multi-agent system for video anomaly understanding that separates exploration, verification, and decision roles so evidence for an anomaly is gathered and cross-checked rather than produced in a single reasoning pass. It aims to explain causes, not just flag abnormal frames.

entry.title: Calibrated Bayesian Inference for Stochastic Intervention Effects

author.name: Tyler M. Schmidt, Nathan B. Wikle

entry.summary: Develops a post-processing correction applied to posterior samples from nonparametric Bayesian models so that credible intervals for stochastic intervention effects become asymptotically efficient and frequentist-calibrated. The fix requires no change to the prior or fitting algorithm.

entry.title: DiffusionGemma Technical Report

author.name: DiffusionGemma Team, Adrien Ali Ta\"iga, James Assiene, Daniele Calandriello, Rahma Chaabouni, Jo\~ao Gante, Tamara von Glehn, Nate Keating, Chris Knutsen, Martin Kukla, Tianlin Liu, Ivan Lobov, Ofir Nabati, Jo\~ao Gabriel Oliveira, Nicolas Perez-Nieves, Nastasia Prutianova, Bobak Shahriari, Jean Tarbouriech, Pavel Tyletski, \c{C}a\u{g}lar \"Unl\"u, Cindy Wu, Glenn Cameron, Jerome Connor, Sertan Girgin, Maarten Grootendorst, Alon Levkovitch, Eliya Nachmani, Omar Sanseviero, Piotr Stanczyk, Quentin Berthet, Andrew Campbell, Cl\'ement Crepy, Valentin De Bortoli, Arnaud Doucet, Romuald Elie, Alexandre Galashov, Klaus Greff, Alexis Jacq, David Ruhe, Yu-Han Wu, Sebastian Flennerhag, Brendan O'Donoghue, George Scrivener, Shantanu Thakoor

entry.summary: Covered in yesterday's Research roundup, The DiffusionGemma technical report from Google DeepMind documents an open-weight discrete-diffusion language model obtained by fine-tuning the mixture-of-experts Gemma 4 backbone (3.8B active, 25.2B total) so it refines 256-token blocks in parallel rather than decoding autoregressively. The two-stage pipeline (bidirectional denoising SFT then a further stage) uses under 10 percent of the base model's training token budget, showing that strong diffusion LMs can be converted from existing AR checkpoints cheaply. Note DiffusionGemma was made generally available in June 2026, so this is the accompanying technical documentation rather than a launch.

entry.title: TRACE-TS: Attribution-Grounded and Traceable Sensor-Language Reasoning for Human Activity Understanding

author.name: Sparsh Rastogi, Tanmay Kumar, Baiyu Chen, Jatin Bedi, Zechen Li, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: TRACE-TS grounds natural-language explanations of wearable sensor time series in actual signal evidence by using attribution from an expert classifier to locate salient spatio-temporal regions, building directed-acyclic-graph reasoning traces with explicit provenance, and distilling a compact language model to reproduce them. It targets the problem that sensor-to-language systems produce fluent but unverifiable narratives. The result is traceable human activity understanding.

entry.title: Gene Ontology-Guided Hierarchical Spatial Gene Expression Prediction from Histopathology Images

author.name: Zhiwen Xu, Xiaoming Yan, Chengkun Wu, Juan Chen, Haoang Chi, Liyang Xu

entry.summary: MSGR predicts spatial gene expression from histopathology images while injecting the Gene Ontology functional hierarchy as an explicit structural prior, organizing target genes into a four-level tree and refining predictions progressively through a GO-guided decoder. This replaces the common practice of decoding genes as a flat unstructured vector that ignores pathway-level dependencies. The aim is cheaper large-scale transcriptomic profiling.

entry.title: SymboUQ: Symbolic Uncertainty Quantification for Spatial Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Dahai Yu, Lin Jiang, Rongchao Xu, Guang Wang

entry.summary: SymboUQ estimates the reliability of a model's final answer in spatial reasoning by analyzing its reasoning trace with a symbolic verifier, explicitly separating whether a claim can be expressed in the verifier's formal language from whether executing it yields a definite entailment or contradiction. This handles the common case where formal verification is only partially applicable. The result is a confidence signal grounded in semantics rather than token probability.

entry.title: Behavioral Grammar: Detecting Adaptive Malware via Tiny Language Model Priors and Second-Order Temporal Analysis

author.name: Zihan Luo

entry.summary: Behavioral Grammar treats host runtime behavior as a language, discretizing each system event into eight tokens covering event type, process, arguments, path category, parent process, user, destination, and timing, then learning normal behavior self-supervised with a 0.88M-parameter causal Transformer. Anomaly scores derive from the learned conditional distribution, aiming for auditability and scale where signatures are evaded and heavy deep models are impractical. It adds second-order temporal analysis for adaptive threats.

entry.title: SCHEDBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Constraint Faithfulness in Natural-Language Combinatorial Scheduling

author.name: Shrenil Shaun Sharma, Avi Sharma

entry.summary: SCHEDBench tests whether LLMs produce schedules with consistent constraint-feasible behavior when the same underlying problem is paraphrased into different natural-language surface forms, spanning 1,132 instances across job-shop scheduling, resource-constrained project scheduling, nurse rostering, and curriculum timetabling. Feasibility and optimality ground truth come from classical solvers. The focus is faithfulness to constraints rather than answer accuracy alone.

entry.title: PosterMELD: Multi-Agent Paper-to-Poster Generation for Controllable Design Diversity with Editable Print-Ready Outputs

author.name: Haojie Hu, Chenhao Dang, Yaojia Liu, Hengrui Kang, Conghui He, Weijia Li

entry.summary: PosterMELD is a template-conditioned multi-agent pipeline that turns papers into print-ready, element-editable posters, with capacity-aware slot planning, deterministic quality gates, and VLM review routing failures to bounded repair. Reports a print-ready rate metric across 621 papers and exports editable PPTX and PNG.

entry.title: Amplitude-Only FFN Intervention for Tool-Structured LLM Inference Method: Gated Evaluation Protocol, and Cross-Model Empirical Results

author.name: Sheng Xu, Junhua Wang, Boyuan Huang, Ke Jia, Jiadun Zhu, Zhen Chen

entry.summary: Explores inference-time FFN intervention to fix structured tool-call outputs without retraining, abandoning a direction-changing residual projection in favor of Amplitude Gating that preserves pretrained weight directions and only modulates activation magnitudes. Includes a gated evaluation protocol and cross-model results on SwiGLU intervention sites.

entry.title: Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yibo Wan, Jinyu Cai, Seekiong-Ng

entry.summary: ReCAP replaces the fixed text prompts or learned visual tokens used as normal and abnormal references in CLIP-based medical anomaly detection with input-conditioned visual prototypes re-centered per image through bounded gated modulation. The language-free design aims to transfer across unseen organs and imaging modalities.

entry.title: Radar Detection in the CBRS Band: Techniques, Challenges, and Future Directions

author.name: Madan Baduwal, Priyanka Paudel

entry.summary: This work observes that the disagreement between two independent feature forecasts in cached diffusion sampling is a free runtime reliability signal, and uses it to decide how much to trust each forecast instead of blindly reusing cached features. It closes the loop on training-free diffusion acceleration under aggressive step skipping.

entry.title: CausalOPD: First-Wrong-Step Supervision for Distilling Causal Chain Reasoning

author.name: Jian Zhang, Bingyi Wang, Yizhi Liu

entry.summary: CausalOPD distills causal-chain reasoning into small deployable models using on-policy process supervision that targets the first incorrect step in the student's own rollouts. A knowledge-augmented teacher seeds trajectories grounded in domain rules before the curriculum online phase begins.

entry.title: DiagLoop: A Counterfactual Data Flywheel with Stage-Localized Reinforcement for Diagnostic LLMs

author.name: Jian Zhang, Bingyi Wang, Yizhi Liu

entry.summary: DiagLoop generates counterfactual training worlds from codified physical or clinical mechanism rules, filters them with an independent validity checker, and applies stage-localized reinforcement across symptom abstraction, causal chain construction, and root-cause attribution. The aim is to overcome scarcity of documented reasoning paths for rare diagnostic cases.

entry.title: Stylometric Defenses Against Author Impersonation in Software Repositories

author.name: Leonid Ravich, Michael Fire

entry.summary: Fine-tunes a cross-modal transformer on more than 20 years of Linux kernel commits to embed code diffs and commit messages into a shared stylometric space, reaching 0.93 ROC AUC for open-world authorship verification at patch level. The embeddings feed a streaming anomaly detector validated retrospectively on supply-chain incidents.

entry.title: VIVID: A Culturally Grounded Benchmark Exposing the Figurative Language Gap in Vietnamese NLP

author.name: Tu Tran Do, Nhat Ngoc Nguyen, Khanh-Tung Tran, Hoang D. Nguyen, Tu Minh Phuong, Long Hoang Dang

entry.summary: VIVID benchmarks culturally grounded figurative language understanding in Vietnamese with 1636 idioms and proverbs annotated for five complexity traits and seven semantic themes, using both generative and discriminative tasks. Notably, Vietnamese-specialized models substantially underperform multilingual systems, and the LLM-as-judge protocol was validated against human agreement.

entry.title: M-GATE: Multilingual Grammar, Accuracy in Translation, and Efficiency Benchmark for Large Language Models

author.name: Tom\'a\v{s} Burkert, Angelika Peljak-{\L}api\'nska, David Zelen\'y

entry.summary: M-GATE benchmarks linguistic proficiency rather than task performance in 30 typologically diverse languages, using linguist-crafted adversarial grammatical error detection, round-trip translation judged by a validated multi-provider panel, and efficiency measures. Argues existing multilingual benchmarks conflate fluency with command of a language. Useful for exposing weaknesses in low-resource language handling.

entry.title: Information-Geometric Forward Policy Training in GFlowNets

author.name: Yordan Raykov, Rodrigo Veiga

entry.summary: Recasts forward-policy training in GFlowNets through information geometry, showing the intrinsic first-order geometry is the Fisher-Rao metric of the induced trajectory family and deriving an exact decomposition of the trajectory Fisher information for natural-gradient updates. Provides a principled canonical local update rule for amortized samplers. Theoretical foundation work for GFlowNet optimization.

entry.title: PAMT: Process-Aligned Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Domain Machine Translation

author.name: Yongshi Ye, Biao Fu, Chongxuan Huang, Yidong Chen, Xiaodong Shi

entry.summary: Analyzes explicit reasoning in multi-domain machine translation across 15 domains and four directions and finds it helps long-form and hard cases but drifts on terminology-intensive and stylistically constrained text. PAMT introduces process-aligned RL that assigns credit to individual intermediate translation steps instead of only final outputs or coarse trajectories. Addresses a credit-assignment bottleneck in reasoning-model post-training for translation.

entry.title: Double Down on Defense: Strengthening Deep Perceptual Hashes against Evasion Attacks without Retraining

author.name: Bangjie Sun, Nayoung Kim, Mun Choon Chan, Jun Han

entry.summary: DualShield hardens deployed deep perceptual hashes against adversarial evasion without retraining, combining randomized smoothing at match time with an imperceptible protective perturbation added when reference images are published. This targets content provenance, copyright, and abuse detection pipelines.

entry.title: Rectify Then Diffuse: Disentangling Concepts Before Denoising Trajectory Unfolds

author.name: Ning Zhu, An Chen, Mengfei Zhao, Juntao Xu, Jingze Liang, Boyuan Gu, Liang-Jian Deng

entry.summary: Rectify-then-Diffuse treats multi-concept text-to-image failures as an initialization problem: before denoising, prompt-conditioned attention often assigns different concepts to overlapping spatial regions, which keeps them entangled. The training-free method rectifies this initial allocation once with a soft-overlap disentanglement step instead of steering the whole trajectory.

entry.title: From Routes to Steps: Separating Semantic Progress from Local Execution in Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Xiangyun Huang, Xiangchen Wang, Runfeng Lin, Yihao Xu, Kangyu Huang, Jiang Hengchen, Xiwang Dong, Lin Jiarong

entry.summary: Route2Step separates tracking semantic progress along a route instruction from executing the current local step in vision-and-language navigation, arguing next-action supervision alone conflates the two error types. Explicit progress supervision prevents agents from continuing to act from an incorrect belief about where they are in the instruction.

entry.title: Surface Keypoint Representation for Multi-Object and Articulated Human-Object Interaction Generation

author.name: Xiaogang Peng, Zeyu Han, Zichong Meng, Yiming Xie, Jihua Zhu, Gang Hua, Huaizu Jiang

entry.summary: This paper represents object motion in human-object interaction generation as trajectories of a few non-collinear surface keypoints per rigid part, letting one formulation cover multiple objects and articulated assemblies with different joint mechanisms. It avoids explicit per-object kinematic modeling.

entry.title: iFAN: Inference-Aware Learning for Plain Mask Transformers

author.name: Fang Li, Yu He, Haoyang Tong, Lichen Ma, Jingling Fu, Wenxiao Fan, Tongxuan Liu, Luohang Liu, Ke Zhang, Junshi Huang

entry.summary: iFAN aligns training of query-based mask transformers with how they actually decode at inference, fixing two mismatches: the highest-scoring query is not always the best mask, and final-layer decoding discards better intermediate-layer predictions. It adds adjusted probability-mask ranking and cross-layer supervision.

entry.title: Can Text-to-Image Models Draw from the Right Frame of Reference?

author.name: Zheyuan Gu, Ruihang Li, Yong Huang, Yiqian Zhang, XIangzhao Hao, Jiaxin Niu, Jiahao Hu, Zhenyu Zhang

entry.summary: FoR-T2I is a benchmark of 1,200 prompt pairs testing whether text-to-image models honor a specified frame of reference, distinguishing viewer-centric from object-intrinsic interpretations of directions like left of. Existing spatial benchmarks conflate these cases.

entry.title: Earth Embeddings

author.name: Adam J. Stewart, Heng Fang, Isaac A. Corley, Xiao Xiang Zhu

entry.summary: This chapter surveys Earth observation embedding products, comparing implicit location encoders and explicit patch or pixel embeddings on coverage, resolution, dimensionality, storage, licensing, and reproducibility. It reviews downstream uses in land cover, crop mapping, ecology, and hazard modeling as the field shifts from self-hosted foundation models to distributed embedding datasets.

entry.title: Hi-Token: Hierarchical Coordinate Tokenization for Generative Visual Grounding

author.name: Xiuyuan Zhu, Ke Lu, Kun Dong, Siwen Jiao, Hao Wu, Zijin Du, Shun Mao, Dongming Zhang, Jian Xue

entry.summary: Hi-Token tokenizes bounding-box coordinates with axis-specific hundreds, tens, and ones digit tokens so generative vision-language models encode numeric order and axis semantics explicitly, improving token reuse. A companion geometry-based reward trains grounding with group relative policy optimization.

entry.title: From Multi-Resolution Cells to Gigapixel Whole Slide Images Foundation Model for Computational Pathology

author.name: Basit Alawode, Moshira Ali Abdalla, Dwarikanath Mahapatra, Muhammad Muzammal Naseer, Sajid Javed

entry.summary: MRPT is a computational pathology model that hierarchically aggregates features from cell-level to tissue-level to whole-slide scale with consecutive cross-resolution attention, rather than pretraining at a single magnification. The design mirrors how pathologists move between magnifications on gigapixel slides.

entry.title: Keep the Needle, Prune the Haystack: Defect-Preserving Token Pruning for Efficient Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yanning Hou, Jingyuan Zhang, Xiaoyun Wang, Qixiang Ma, Sihang Zhou, Ke Xu

entry.summary: This work identifies an asymmetric risk in token pruning for zero-shot anomaly detection: discarding normal tokens only wastes compute, while discarding anomalous tokens destroys the sole evidence of a defect. The proposed pruning strategy preserves candidate defect tokens especially in early layers where savings are largest.

entry.title: TDVR: Joint Text Disambiguation and Viewpoint Reasoning for Zero-Shot 3D Visual Grounding

author.name: Qingxi Du, Junbo Wang, Yuke Li, Yining Zhu

entry.summary: TDVR is a training-free pipeline for zero-shot 3D visual grounding that first builds a semantic scene graph from detected point-cloud instances, then uses an LLM to disambiguate the query and chain-of-thought reasoning to infer the correct observation viewpoint. It targets two known bottlenecks: vague language and view-dependent spatial relations.

entry.title: FlowForm: Synergizing Fluid Physics with Topological Consistency for Satellite Flood Synthesis

author.name: Zhang Weihui, Wang Ruizhi, Xu Hongye, Wang Huiqiong, Sun Li, Song Mingli

entry.summary: FlowForm synthesizes paired satellite flood imagery by regularizing a diffusion model with residuals of the steady-state shallow water equation in latent space and injecting terrain, depth, semantic, and edge conditioning. The aim is physically plausible flood layouts for training flood assessment models where real paired data is scarce.

entry.title: LiteMVS: Efficient Multi-View Stereo with Foundation Distillation and Expert Aggregation

author.name: Tianbao Zhang, Zeyu Liu, Shuyu Wu, Fanxing Li, Zhaoxin Fan, Wenjun Wu, Danping Zou

entry.summary: LiteMVS distills monocular depth foundation model priors into a lightweight multi-view stereo network and aggregates expert branches to remain robust in textureless or repetitive regions. It is positioned as a real-time geometry front end for robotics and later 4D spatiotemporal representations.

entry.title: A Hierarchical Approach to Imitation Learning for Manipulation Tasks Requiring Time Varying Forces

author.name: Rishabh Shukla, Adithya Santhosh, Shaili Gandhi, Samrudh Moode, Satyandra K. Gupta

entry.summary: This work addresses the latency trade-off that prevents diffusion policies from handling contact-rich disassembly tasks needing time-varying forces, where action chunking makes the system blind to rapid fracture transients. The proposed hierarchy augments a diffusion policy with a fast trajectory generator so high-frequency force responses remain closed-loop.

entry.title: DigitCode: Symbolic Tokenization of Hand Motion by Anatomical Units

author.name: Haoyu Gu, Haotian Lu, Jingrun Du, Xiao-Ping Zhang

entry.summary: DigitCode builds a discrete symbolic tokenization of hand motion by adapting Hand Labanotation and asking what anatomical unit a symbol should span: bone, finger, or whole hand. The motivation is that continuous joint-angle or MANO parameters cannot be indexed, edited, or validated as symbols.

entry.title: Shaping Wind-Tunnel Airflow for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles using Online Learning

author.name: Ghadeer Elmkaiel, Michael Muehlebach

entry.summary: An online learning controller shapes the airflow field of a multi-fan vertical wind tunnel, combining a simplified physical model with iterative measurement-based updates for sample-efficient convergence to target profiles. It produces uniform, Gaussian, and parabolic fields plus a profile tailored to enable passive soaring by a small aerial robot.

entry.title: Nova: An End-to-End MLIR Compiler for Deep Learning

author.name: Adwaid Suresh, Aparna A, Harshini V M, Jona Delcy C A, Killi Uma Maheswara Rao, Ram Charan Golla, Surendra Vendra

entry.summary: Nova is an end-to-end MLIR-based just-in-time compiler that captures eager tensor-framework execution and lowers it to hardware with whole-graph visibility, cross-boundary operator fusion, memory hierarchy optimization, and register-level tuning. It aims to close the gap between flexible eager frameworks and peak hardware utilization. The work sits in the ML compiler infrastructure space alongside XLA and TVM-style systems.

entry.title: SIRIN: A Unified Toolkit for Detecting Contextual Hallucinations in Retrieval-Augmented and Memory-Grounded LLM Systems

author.name: Julia Belikova, Rauf Parchiev, Mikhail Filimonov, Konstantin Polev, Andrey Savchenko, Maksim Makarenko

entry.summary: SIRIN is an open toolkit and web interface that unifies three families of contextual hallucination detectors (representation probing, uncertainty estimation, and LLM-judge verification) plus pre-generation query answerability under a single configuration and evaluation pipeline. It supports both response-level and span-level inspection in white-box and black-box settings for RAG, agentic, and memory-grounded systems. The value is standardization and comparability across detector paradigms.

entry.title: HetGPS: Scalable Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Physics-Anchored Adaptive Safety for EV Charging

author.name: Xiangwei Wang, Nanduni Nimalsiri, Yu Xia, Peng Wang, Saman Halgamuge

entry.summary: HetGPS combines a learned graph residual risk model that schedules how much authority a safety intervention has with a physics model that determines the correction direction, applied to electric vehicle charging with a parameter-shared heterogeneous graph soft actor-critic policy. Separating intervention magnitude from direction avoids unnecessarily overriding task-oriented decisions while protecting shared network constraints. Model size stays independent of fleet size across five nested distribution networks.

entry.title: Passing Coarse Marginal Checks Can Be Cheap: Persona Mixtures and Imprecise Treatment-Response Estimates in an LLM Persona Panel

author.name: Yohei Nakajima

entry.summary: This study examines a panel of sixteen persona-conditioned GPT-4.1 configurations used as synthetic research participants in repeated strategic games, showing they can pass coarse marginal validation checks in most preregistered cells while treatment-response estimates remain imprecise. Between-prompt variance shares range widely (roughly 47 to 96 percent) depending on uncertainty assumptions, meaning persona choice dominates results. The message is that matching human marginals is a cheap and insufficient validation standard.

entry.title: Perspectives on Tsallis Statistics for Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Kleyton da Costa, Bernardo Modenesi

entry.summary: A perspective paper mapping Tsallis generalized statistics onto modern AI components, including sparsemax and entmax sparse attention, maximum-entropy RL with tunable exploration, heavy-tailed probabilistic models, and generalized losses. Offers a unifying parameterization view.

entry.title: KoVRE: Training an Efficient Embedding Model for Korean Visual Document Retrieval

author.name: Yongbin Choi, Gyuho Shim, Youngjoon Jang

entry.summary: KoVRE is a single-vector Korean visual document retrieval embedding model trained on roughly 709k query-page pairs with positive-aware hard-negative mining, plus ablations on data mix and negative selection. Addresses English-centric, storage-heavy multi-vector VDR systems.

entry.title: A Contractualist Argumentation Framework for Moral Decision-Making

author.name: Luis Marcos-Vidal, Giulio Antonio Abbo, Tony Belpaeme

entry.summary: Builds a formal moral reasoning framework for autonomous agents based on Scanlon's contractualism, operationalized with the ASPIC+ structured argumentation formalism plus value-based filtering of which reasons count as morally relevant. Produces machine-checkable permissibility judgments for actions affecting multiple stakeholders.

entry.title: Evidence-Unit Fairness and the Limits of Query-Adaptive Sparse-Dense Fusion in Financial Document Retrieval

author.name: Chenyu Wu, You Lin

entry.summary: Studying hybrid sparse-dense retrieval over 10-K filings, the authors show a methodological confound: when the retrieval unit exceeds the dense encoder's context window, the dense model never sees much of the labeled evidence, invalidating comparisons with full-text BM25. After segmenting into encoder-sized windows, fusing BM25 with a compact dense encoder improves Hit@10 by roughly 28 percent over either component.

entry.title: Unleashing the Power of Text: Text-Guided Flow Matching for Image Fusion under Complex Degradations

author.name: Axi Niu (School of Computer Science, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Xi'an, China), Jieheng Li (School of Computer Science, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Xi'an, China), Kang Zhang (School of Electrical Engineering, KAIST, Daejeon, Republic of Korea), Qingsen Yan (School of Computer Science, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Xi'an, China), Jinqiu Sun (School of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Xi'an, China), Yanning Zhang (School of Computer Science, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Xi'an, China)

entry.summary: TGFusion is a text-guided latent flow-matching framework for infrared-visible image fusion under realistic degradations, replacing fixed global text injection with guidance that adapts to spatially varying corruption, local structure, and thermal saliency. It jointly handles restoration and fusion in one generative process.

entry.title: Me and My Bot: What Users Talk About in AI Companion Communities on Reddit

author.name: Richard A. Fabes

entry.summary: Multiple LLMs were used to code 5,504 Reddit posts from eight AI companion communities for relationship focus, topic, and emotional valence, finding that despite relationally weighted search terms only 45 percent of posts concerned the poster's own relationship with their bot. Posts about one's own companion differed sharply in topic and emotional tone from posts about companion bots in general.

entry.title: RefactorAssist: Agentic Refinement for Reliable Code Refactoring

author.name: Jonathan Cordeiro, Shayan Noei, Ying Zou

entry.summary: Analyzes why LLM-generated Java refactorings break functionality and builds RefactorAssist, an agent that iteratively repairs refactorings against native test suites across ten open-source projects. It targets the practical reliability gap that blocks adoption of LLM refactoring tools.

entry.title: AdaHAT: Adaptive Hard Attention to the Task in Task-Incremental Learning

author.name: Pengxiang Wang, Hongbo Bo, Jun Hong, Weiru Liu, Kedian Mu

entry.summary: AdaHAT extends hard-attention-to-the-task continual learning with an adaptive mechanism that allows controlled updates to parameters previously frozen for older tasks, mitigating the capacity exhaustion that occurs over long task sequences. It targets the tradeoff between forgetting and plasticity in architecture-based methods.

entry.title: Ranking Image Fusion the Way Humans Do: A Learned Pairwise Preference Metric for Infrared-Visible Fusion Assessment

author.name: Haoran Liu, Mingzhe Liu, Peng Li, Guibin Zan

entry.summary: LPIFM learns a source-conditioned pairwise preference model that predicts which of two infrared-visible fused images a human prefers, replacing quadratically expensive human A/B comparisons with a scalable surrogate metric. It targets the mismatch between scalar objective fusion metrics and human judgment.

entry.title: StreamTalk: Streaming Co-Speech Gesture Generation with Key-Pose Anchoring

author.name: Xiangyue Zhang, Jianfang Li, Jiaxu Zhang, Kaixing Yang, Steven Hoi

entry.summary: StreamTalk generates 3D co-speech gestures in a streaming fashion but adds a closed-loop generate-retrieve-refine cycle that anchors each clip to a plausible end key pose retrieved from a speaker-specific bank. This forward constraint is argued to be the main fix for cumulative drift in long real-time gesture sequences.

entry.title: Few-Shot Concept Prompt Learning for Segmentation Foundation Models via Visual Grounding

author.name: Rahul Venkataramani, Rachana Sathish

entry.summary: The authors argue that promptable segmentation foundation models underperform on medical images because natural language is a weak control signal where paired image-text data is scarce, not because of insufficient pretraining. They learn a small visually grounded prompt from a handful of target examples to recover performance without retraining the backbone.

entry.title: Investigating Social Bias in Narrative Image Generation

author.name: Junyeong Park, Sowon Min, Euna Jang, Soobin Kim, Jiho Jin, Hyunseung Lim, Gahyeon Bae, Hwajung Hong

entry.summary: This study extends a text-based bias evaluation framework to image generation and compares how social biases manifest in photo, storyboard, and comic outputs across six text-to-image models. It finds that bias expression differs by narrative format, which single-image benchmarks cannot reveal.

entry.title: Hear, Invoke, and Understand: A Skill-Calling Multimodal Agent for Large Audio Language Models

author.name: Yuwen Wang, Tian-Hao Zhang, Minghao Cai, Yilin Ren, Ziyang Jiang, Xin Wang, Zhichao Wang, Pan Zhou, Kun Zhan, Xinyuan Qian

entry.summary: SpeechAgent-R is an audio agent that combines a large audio-language model's intrinsic understanding with calls to external audio-processing skills and tools, trained via trajectory supervised fine-tuning then multi-turn reinforcement learning. It is supported by HIU-Corpus, roughly 65k trajectories and 500 hours of audio across two dozen tasks.

entry.title: Effective and Efficient Context Retrieval via Partial Dependency Graph for Repository-Level Code Generation

author.name: Zhongxin Liu, Zhonghao Jiang, Zhifan Ye, Haoye Wang, Jiakun Liu, Xiaoxue Ren

entry.summary: This work retrieves repository context for code generation by building partial dependency graphs on demand, mimicking how developers explore only the code they need, instead of relying on rule-based static global graphs. It targets both retrieval quality for dependency-heavy functions and the cost of graph construction and maintenance.

entry.title: SPARE: Structural Parameter-Free Affinity Regularization for Flow Matching

author.name: Zong-Wei Hong, Jinglun Li, Shen Zhang, Yuhan Liu, Linze Li, Yao Tang

entry.summary: SPARE accelerates diffusion transformer training with a parameter-free regularizer that preserves spatial affinity structure among internal representations, avoiding both an external teacher encoder and the structure-discarding repulsion of target-free methods. It builds on evidence that spatial structure rather than global semantics drives representation-alignment gains.

entry.title: Human-Centered Reflections on Care Robots: A Comparative Study of Caregiver Perspectives

author.name: Laura Londo\~no, Klaus Baumann, Abhinav Valada, Markus Langer

entry.summary: A mixed-methods study of 298 caregivers in the US, Mexico, and Chile assessing acceptance of four categories of care robots (supply delivery, patient transfer, vital-sign monitoring, mobility assistance) using established technology-acceptance and cognitive-affective-normative constructs. It surfaces cross-cultural and task-dependent differences relevant to ethical deployment of assistive robots.

entry.title: Learning Molecular Representations from Cellular Phenotypes with Structure Preservation

author.name: Xuan Lin, Jingyu Sheng, Tengfei Ma, Li Sun, Dapeng Xiong

entry.summary: PhenMol learns molecular representations aligned with cellular phenotype data while explicitly disentangling shared and private components and preserving chemical structure through a dedicated molecular branch. Aims to avoid the representation distortion caused by naive cross-modal alignment in phenotypic drug discovery.

entry.title: Designing a Good Virtual Node: Addressable and Cardinality-Preserving Global Memory for Message Passing Architectures

author.name: F\'elix Marcoccia

entry.summary: Analyzes what makes a good virtual node in message-passing networks, arguing that a single homogeneous broadcast state is a capacity bottleneck and proposing factorized, addressable cross-attention memory slots. It also shows addressability alone loses multiplicity because softmax attention is invariant to uniform replication, motivating per-slot key/value anchors.

entry.title: When Should Graph Attention Be Sparse? Learning a Per-Edge Tsallis Index

author.name: Kleyton da Costa, Bernardo Modenesi

entry.summary: LTGA replaces the fixed softmax in graph attention with a Tsallis entropic normalization whose index is learned jointly with the weights, interpolating between heavy-tailed, softmax, and compact-support attention at granularities down to individual edges. Evaluated across eight benchmarks with ten seeds and initialized to match the standard GAT baseline.

entry.title: Exploiting Separability in Multi-Scale Grey-Box Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Joshua E. Hammond, Tyler A. Soderstrom, Brian A. Korgel, Michael Baldea

entry.summary: Exploits separability in grey-box optimization by splitting variables into expensive black-box inputs and white-box variables governed by closed-form equations, then solving a bilevel problem with outer Bayesian optimization and inner global optimization. This enforces white-box constraints exactly instead of learning them with a surrogate.

entry.title: Convex-Hull-Neighborhood Smooth Dual Generalization: Controlling Local Correction Propagation in Offline RL

author.name: Yi Yang, Zhennan Chen, Mingfeng Lv, Hanlei Li, Zhengsen Ruan, Lvqing Yang

entry.summary: CSDG rewrites the offline RL Bellman backup as an in-sample value target plus an explicit local correction over a convex-hull neighborhood of dataset actions, so the influence of out-of-distribution generalization is separated from the in-sample reference path. Candidate corrections sampled at different perturbation radii are smoothed to control error amplification through bootstrapping.

entry.title: Can LLMs Test Terminal User Interfaces?

author.name: Chao Peng, Ruida Hu, Ajitha Rajan, Tegawend\'e F Bissyand\'e, Jacques Klein, Cuiyun Gao

entry.summary: Surveys 197 real-world terminal user interface applications, finding only 12 percent of test code exercises the interface and nearly half of those tests never send input, then builds a headless Docker-packaged benchmark across four TUI frameworks. Under equal wall-clock budgets four frontier LLMs fail to dominate random exploration. A sober reality check on LLM agents for interactive software testing.

entry.title: Computing Actual Causes for Neural Network Predictions under Structured Causal Inputs

author.name: Jannick Strobel, Muqsit Azeem, Stefan Leue

entry.summary: Formalizes neural-network explanations as Halpern-Pearl actual causes over Boolean structural causal models of the inputs, so that structured feature dependencies are respected rather than assumed away. Uses bound propagation and branch-and-bound to compute causes with completeness and minimality guarantees, outperforming brute-force and ILP baselines on scalability. Advances formally grounded explainability.

entry.title: SeqLLM: Augmenting LLMs with Behavioral-Sequence Modeling for High-Stakes Decisions at WeChat Pay

author.name: Guilin Li, Jiaxing Zhang, Matthias Hwai Yong Tan, Bo Wang, Weiran Huang

entry.summary: SeqLLM adds behavioral-sequence modeling to a pretrained LLM for merchant risk screening at WeChat Pay, using a compact discrete vocabulary of behavioral events as native tokens plus a lightweight two-stage-aligned projector so language ability is preserved. Targets hard cases requiring joint reasoning over textual merchant profiles and long event sequences at tens of millions of merchants daily. A concrete pattern for fusing tabular/sequential signals into LLMs without catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Adaptive Two-Stage Visual Token Pruning for Efficient Inference in Video-Language Models

author.name: Paribesh Regmi, Qingshuang Chen, Chi Zhang, Heba Aly, Yelin Kim, Hongda Mao

entry.summary: This work prunes visual tokens for video-language models in two adaptive stages, exploiting temporal and inter-frame redundancy and varying the pruning ratio per input rather than using a fixed uniform ratio. The target is lower latency for edge deployment and real-time video analysis.

entry.title: SlimVLM: Sensitivity-aware Dynamic Structured Pruning with Adaptive Visual Token Selection for Efficient Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yaozhi Wen, Jialong Guo, Zhenliang Ni, Han Shu, Xinghao Chen

entry.summary: SlimVLM structurally prunes vision-language models after first selecting visual tokens adaptively via average text-to-visual attention, since redundant visual tokens corrupt importance estimates when LLM pruning recipes are applied directly. The goal is deployable compressed VLMs with preserved task performance.

entry.title: Fast Object Removal Attacks on Safety-Critical Video-based Perception Systems

author.name: Mohammad Imtiaz Hasan, M Sabbir Salek, Nathan Jones, Mashrur Chowdhury, Rong Ge

entry.summary: This paper builds a near-real-time pipeline that removes target objects from video streams feeding safety-critical transportation perception systems, by localizing targets, retrieving coherent patches from earlier frames, and blending them with context-aware compositing. It demonstrates a practical attack path that could hide vulnerable road users from downstream modules.

entry.title: Bimanual Manipulation Within an 8 GB Budget: Zero-Copy Sensing and Quantized ACT on an Entry-Level Jetson

author.name: Ekansh Singh, Eva Samuel, Alessandra Reneau, Ryan Schmeelk, Yashvi Gandhi

entry.summary: An empirical deployment study running a bimanual imitation-learning policy entirely on an entry-level 8GB Jetson, with zero-copy camera capture and quantized ACT inference. A notable negative result is that the conventional capture path already fit in memory, so zero-copy mainly buys CPU headroom rather than memory savings.

entry.title: Tight Information Complexity of the Coin Problem in the Broadcast Model

author.name: Hadi Kazemi, Varun Jog

entry.summary: Characterizes, up to universal constants, the information complexity of distinguishing two Bernoulli distributions in the shared-blackboard distributed model, showing three regimes whose optimal protocols use clean samples, a binary symmetric channel, or an asymmetric Z-channel. The lower bounds introduce a mixed Hellinger and Jensen-Shannon inequality of independent interest.

entry.title: Google's AI & Economy ATLAS v1.0: Mapping Gemini Usage in the Economy

author.name: Zanna Iscenko, Scott Strand, Yiyuan Chen, Guillaume Aimard, Mihai Codreanu, Vivek Sampathkumar, Alex Imas, Julian Jacobs, Evalyne Muiruri, Juan Mateos-Garcia, Jia Jen Ng, Samirah Javed, Josh Martin, Omar Ajmeri, Denis Calin, Andrew Kim, Fabien Curto Millet, James Manyika

entry.summary: Covered in yesterday's Research roundup, Google's AI and Economy ATLAS v1.0 maps 15 million de-identified interactions across the Gemini app, AI Mode, and the Gemini API onto more than 800 occupations, 4,000 tasks, 300 household activities, 150 countries, and 140 languages using privacy-preserving classification. Reports that adoption spans occupations covering over 88 percent of US employment while task-level penetration remains uneven.

entry.title: Geometric Self-Supervised Pre-training for Neural Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: David Aguado, Daniel Fuertes, Carlos R. del-Blanco, Fernando Jaureguizar

entry.summary: The authors introduce a geometric self-supervised pre-training scheme for neural combinatorial optimization on routing problems such as the traveling salesman problem, where graphs offer little beyond 2D coordinates for constructing pretext tasks. Pre-training is intended to improve generalization of RL-trained solvers to larger instances. The work imports a pretraining paradigm from vision and language into routing.

entry.title: Diagnose Before You Compress: Prediction-Independent Bottleneck Witness Refinement for LLM Serving Traces

author.name: Liming Liu, Chao Hu, Mingfei Lu, Cong Tan, Yiwei Ge, Chijin Zhou, Yongjun Xie, Runzhe Wang, Xiaohai Shi, Heyuan Shi

entry.summary: This work proposes Bottleneck-Preserving Witnessing, a trace-reduction framework for LLM serving that keeps evidence for every bottleneck component rather than preserving overall workload distributions, on the argument that bottleneck-revealing requests are rare and non-representative. It also avoids the circular evaluation of using predicted bottlenecks as ground truth. The output is a compact but diagnostically reliable replay trace.

entry.title: DASH: Decoupled Adaptive Surrogate - Acquisition Harness for Automated Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Changquan Zhao, Yuxiang Sun, Ruihao Zhu, Cheng Hua, Yulian He

entry.summary: DASH is an LLM-enhanced automated Bayesian optimization system that decouples surrogate model selection from acquisition function adaptation, arguing that surrogates should be chosen by predictive reliability while acquisitions should respond to campaign context. Prior AutoBO methods either adapt one component or select pairs under a single shared criterion. The decoupling is intended to remove bottlenecks from mismatched components.

entry.title: AgentSLABench: Evaluating and Benchmarking Agentic Systems Under Resource Constraints

author.name: Meher Bhaskar Madiraju, Meher Sai Preetam Madiraju

entry.summary: AgentSLABench profiles autonomous agents on correctness alongside latency, cost, compute, memory, and network usage under declared resource budgets, analogous to systems profilers but with task success as a first-class dimension. It provides 16 task environments across six categories in isolated Docker containers with sealed test sets and explicit CPU, memory, time, and network limits. The goal is service-level-agreement style reporting for agent deployment decisions.

entry.title: Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals: Separating Matching and Content Retrieval Across Depth

author.name: Kehan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes decoupling depth-routing in residual Transformer variants so queries and keys read from one layer depth while values read from an independently learned depth, separating attention matching from content retrieval. A minimal architectural change to block attention residual designs.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Complex Eigenfrequency Identification and Mode Structure Reconstruction of the Ground-State ITG Branch

author.name: Dengdi Sun, Bingbing Zhang, Xiao Wang, Zikang Yan, Yuqiang Tao, Qingquan Yang, Guosheng Xu, Jin Tang

entry.summary: Applies physics-informed neural networks to jointly identify complex eigenfrequencies and reconstruct 2D complex-valued mode fields for ion-temperature-gradient drift waves in tokamak pedestals. Handles strong real-imaginary coupling and localized high-frequency oscillations.

entry.title: Multimodal Wearable-Based Olfactory-Induced Emotion Recognition in Arousal-Valence Dimensions

author.name: Chen-Yang Xu, Lan Zhang, Fei-Yi Fan, Bin Hu, Qing-Hao Meng

entry.summary: Constructs a large multimodal dataset of 111 subjects with synchronized central and peripheral physiological signals during odor stimulation, labeled in both arousal and valence dimensions, and builds recognition models for olfactory-induced emotion. Addresses the field's overemphasis on valence and lack of synchronized multimodal olfaction data.

entry.title: MetaRoute-Bench: Evaluating Meta-Decision Policies for Agentic Workflow Routing

author.name: Natan Vidra, Alina Kapanova, Arun Kanhai, Spurthi Setty

entry.summary: MetaRoute-Bench is an inspectable benchmark for the meta-decisions agentic systems make (answer directly, decompose, call a tool, delegate, verify, recover), comparing eight routing policies over 180 synthetic task profiles and 43,200 traces with cost and latency accounted for. It isolates orchestration policy quality from end-task accuracy.

entry.title: Boosting Generalizable Depth Estimation in Endoscopy by Mixture of Lightweight Experts and Intrinsic Image Alignment

author.name: Liangjing Shao, Beilei Cui, Yiming Huang, Changjing Liu, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: EndoMINI is a self-supervised depth and ego-motion estimation framework for endoscopy that uses a mixture of low-rank experts for parameter-efficient adaptation across diverse scenes and adds an intrinsic image decomposition alignment loss to suppress specular reflectance effects. It targets generalizable 3D perception in surgical video.

entry.title: Anticipatory Digital Twins for Online Head-and-Neck Adaptive Proton Therapy via Foundation-Model Registration

author.name: Yizhou Wu, Yuheng Li, Xiaofeng Yang, Chih-Wei Chang

entry.summary: Proposes a digital-twin pipeline that predicts a head-and-neck cancer patient's treatment-day anatomy before imaging, by transferring longitudinal deformation patterns from a population database using foundation-model image registration. The goal is to make online adaptive proton therapy feasible without repeated CT scans and week-long replanning delays.

entry.title: Riemannian Attention Mechanisms for Transformers: A Theoretical Framework and Architecture Design

author.name: Sen Song

entry.summary: Proposes replacing the Euclidean inner product in transformer attention with learned per-token Riemannian metrics, proving that the resulting scores are non-Gram and thus not factorizable as low-dimensional query-key products. It is offered as a theoretical route around known rank-collapse results for deep self-attention stacks.

entry.title: Improved Quantum Algorithms for Reinforcement Learning Under a Generative Model

author.name: Joao F. Doriguello

entry.summary: Proposes quantum algorithms for computing approximately optimal policies in finite-horizon and discounted infinite-horizon MDPs under a generative model, combining value iteration with quantum mean estimation and maximum finding. The results improve on prior sample and query complexities using techniques from sample-optimal classical RL.

entry.title: ScoreField: Neural Inverse Scattering with Score-Based Generative Priors

author.name: Wenhan Guo, Yuan Gao, Yu Sun

entry.summary: ScoreField solves electromagnetic inverse scattering by jointly optimizing two implicit neural representations for permittivity contrast and induced currents under the Lippmann-Schwinger equations, with a pretrained score-based generative prior supplying gradients on the contrast. This combines full-wave physics enforcement with a learned expressive prior.

entry.title: Activation-Guided Neuron Intervention to Induce Alzheimer's-Related Computational Language Phenotypes in a Large Language Model

author.name: Rui He, Ercong Nie, Hong Jiang, Iris E. Sommer, Philipp Homan, Wolfram Hinzen

entry.summary: Identifies feed-forward neurons in Qwen3-8B that activate more for Alzheimer's-patient transcripts than controls, then scales their down-projection weights to produce nine edited model variants, which are run through the same 12-turn neuropsychological battery. Goes beyond detection to test whether the identified representations functionally drive the clinical language phenotype. An interesting causal-intervention approach to computational psychiatry.

entry.title: Relational Priors as Convergence Pressure in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Ming Shen, Chao Shang, Sadat Shahriar, Devang Kulshreshtha, Yi Zhang, Sandesh Swamy, Yanjun Qi

entry.summary: Makes inter-agent relation semantics explicit in LLM multi-agent systems by injecting natural-language renderings of a minimal signed-network relational prior into system prompts while holding the task protocol fixed. Across a commons-governance simulation and multi-agent debate, greater relational positivity mainly acts as convergence pressure, helping when agreement is aligned with utility and hurting when independent challenge is needed. Practical guidance for MAS design and premature-consensus failure modes.

entry.title: EditFlow3D: Automated Local Editing of 3D Assets with Trajectory Preservation

author.name: Rui Nie, Chuang Wang, Haitao Zhou, Jiahe Song, Buyu Li, Sheng Wang, Qian Yu

entry.summary: EditFlow3D is a training-free pipeline for localized editing of 3D assets in which a vision-language model interprets the instruction, builds a visual guidance image, and derives a refined 3D mask, after which mask-guided differential flow confines the edit. It targets preserving untouched geometry and appearance.

entry.title: Efficient Video Dataset Distillation via Cluster-Guided Prototype Blending

author.name: Chongle Ren, Guang Li, Wenbo Huang, Naoki Saito, Takahiro Ogawa, Miki Haseyama

entry.summary: ProtoBlend constructs distilled video datasets without gradient-based optimization of the stored videos, instead clustering to pick informative temporal segments and blending prototypes to cover intra-class variation within a tight per-class budget. This avoids the heavy cost that the temporal dimension adds to iterative distillation.

entry.title: LocAnyMed: Vision-Language Grounding for Multimodal Medical Images

author.name: Zihan Wang, Tong Liu, Zhiwei Wang, Tao Huang, Wentao Jiang, Sihan Ma, Shanshan Ye, Xiaohui Yang, Jing Zhang

entry.summary: LocAnyMed introduces a roughly 200K-example multimodal medical visual grounding dataset spanning CT, optical imaging, ultrasound, and X-ray, harmonizing fragmented detection resources into a unified free-form instruction format. It supports single and multiple target localization from clinical queries.

entry.title: NCGR: Noise-Conditional Gated Rectification for Camera Extrinsic Perturbations in BEV 3D Object Detection

author.name: Wenbin Pan, Wanhao Liu, Liwei Luo, Panshuo Li, Yong Xu, Renquan Lu

entry.summary: NCGR improves camera-based bird's-eye-view 3D detection robustness when camera extrinsics drift, by predicting a small 2D rectification offset per query-camera pair gated by a learned camera-level signal instead of solving for full six-degree-of-freedom correction. Training uses perturbation-derived supervision.

entry.title: Perceptual Anchoring: Prototype-Guided Text Calibration for Training-free Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Wanli Ma, Jiangwen Lu, Qinmu Peng, Xinge You

entry.summary: This paper argues that training-free open-vocabulary segmentation is limited by treating generic text embeddings as fixed classifiers, and proposes calibrating text references using visual prototypes drawn from the image itself. The intent is to close the gap between generic category concepts and instance-specific appearance.

entry.title: Hear to See: Discerning Stateful Listening for Audio-Visual Instance Segmentation

author.name: Leiye Liu, Miao Zhang, Jiahong Jiang, Jingjing Li, Jialong Zhong, Kai Peng, Tingwei Liu, Wei Ji, Yongri Piao, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: Hear to See addresses audio-visual instance segmentation by disentangling mixed audio into semantic then spatial correspondences with visual instances, and adding stateful listening to handle temporal misalignment between sound and appearance. The targets are overlapping sound sources and asynchronous audio-visual dynamics.

entry.title: Pivot-Centric Trajectory Prediction: Bridging Long Horizons via Dynamical Guidance

author.name: Xiucong Zhao, Jindong Tian, Hao Miao

entry.summary: Pivot-Centric Trajectory Prediction decomposes long-horizon agent forecasting into predicting intermediate pivot points at multiple scales, then refining trajectories between them, rather than completing from a single endpoint or iteratively refining a whole path. The goal is to reduce weak guidance and compounding error as prediction horizons grow.

entry.title: AutoFOAM: The Self-Refining Autonomous OpenFOAM Agent

author.name: Arun Govind Neelan, A Seshaditya

entry.summary: AutoFOAM is a fine-tuned Qwen-coder 2.5-14B agent that writes, runs, evaluates, and iteratively evolves OpenFOAM computational fluid dynamics cases from natural-language prompts, using a seven-stage evolution loop with guards against model degeneration. It targets seven solvers and thirteen parametrized mesh templates with a y-plus aware numerical policy. The work shows domain-specialized self-improving agents can reduce expert setup burden in scientific simulation.

entry.title: Shared Organizational Memory for Enterprise Coding Agents: System Design and Deployment Snapshot

author.name: Harsh Rao Dhanyamraju, Leonidas Raghav

entry.summary: This deployment report describes a shared organizational memory layer for enterprise coding agents that captures task-adjacent experience with contributor consent, curates it into reusable question-answer memories, and gates retrieval, so internal DSLs, proprietary platforms, and tacit conventions are not repeatedly rediscovered. It emphasizes making capture a platform default rather than relying on agents to notice what is worth recording. The paper reports an ongoing production rollout snapshot.

entry.title: CraftAlign: Feature-Grounded Evaluation and Revision Guidance for AI Stories

author.name: Yang Yang, Boyun Xu, Shaofeng Liang, Yun Han, Zining Zhong, Songning Lai, Kaishen Yuan, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: CraftAlign scores AI-generated stories on interpretable craft features such as cliche use, over-explanation, and linear causality, then converts those diagnostics into story-wide revision guidance. Moves beyond binary AI-text detection and local edits.

entry.title: Leveraging AI for fine-grained food safety risk forecasting in sparse data conditions

author.name: Dongqi Wang, Weiwei Chen, Han Zhou, Weihua Zhou

entry.summary: Builds a Transformer forecaster of city-level food safety risk from over 11 million inspection records plus demographic and economic indicators, using Wilson-interval partial supervision and semi-supervised label refinement for sparse regions. Aims to target scarce inspection resources.

entry.title: Fast Generation of Representative Synthetic Dataset with Salsa to Train ATR Models with Electromagnetic Couplings Data-Augmentation

author.name: Benjamin Camus (DGA.MI), Julien Houssay (DGA.MI), Corentin Le Barbu (DGA.MI), Eric Monteux (DGA.MI), C\'edric Saleun (DGA.MI), Jean-Christophe Louvign\'e (DGA.MI)

entry.summary: Demonstrates that the Salsa SAR simulator can generate over 21,000 synthetic radar images in under ten minutes on a single consumer GPU, and uses electromagnetic-coupling data augmentation with a deep learning pipeline to train automatic target recognition models without real measurements. Reports on the speed-fidelity-resource tradeoff for representative synthetic datasets.

entry.title: EduPluginBench: Executable Assurance for AI-Generated Educational Plugins

author.name: Nizam Kadir

entry.summary: EduPluginBench is an executable benchmark and staged admission procedure testing whether AI-generated educational plugins satisfy least privilege, telemetry consent, provenance, privileged-write authority, lifecycle constraints, and bounded failure, beyond compiling and passing functional tests. Across 1,440 activation-checked mutants from 30 specifications, the fuller staged pipeline raised release-blocking-defect recall by about 75 percentage points with no false rejections among 120 clean references.

entry.title: SG-Layout: Structured Scene Graph-Guided Layout Generation with LLMs

author.name: Junsheng Wang, Chao Chen, Mengying Xie, Mingyan Li, Fuqiang Gu

entry.summary: SG-Layout injects scene-graph structure into an LLM through a relational graph encoder aligned to the language embedding space, followed by LoRA instruction tuning, to generate spatially coherent layouts from natural language. It targets LLMs' weakness at explicit geometric relations.

entry.title: Imprecise Belief Fusion Improves Multi-agent Social Learning

author.name: Zixuan Liu, Jonathan Lawry, Michael Crosscombe

entry.summary: Models social learning among agents whose beliefs are propositional formulas fused with operators parameterized by degree of imprecision, and shows via difference equations and agent-based simulation that more imprecise fusion can improve collective learning. It connects logical belief representation with distributed consensus dynamics.

entry.title: CRAFT: Compression via Recursive Adaptive Fusion of Video Tokens for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yu Chen, Xiaohong Li, Xiaole Wang, Jianjin Zhang, Jun Sun, Yafeng Deng

entry.summary: CRAFT compresses redundant video tokens for vision-language models by recursively merging them in an adaptive way, aiming to keep the prefill cost low without discarding fine detail. It targets the gap between training-free heuristic pruning and methods that need costly extra alignment training.

entry.title: SyncPlan: Long-Horizon LLM Coordination with Explicit Synchronization and Adaptive Correction

author.name: Shen You, Xiaoming Zhu, Weining Weng, Hefei Mei, Weixuan Wang, Zhongshen Li, Zeji LI, Ye-Wen Wang, Zijun Liao, Juchao Zhuo, Yang Wei, Fuhao Qiu, Siqin Li, Zhenjie Lian, Danei Gong, Junkai Ji, Xiangtao Li, Qiuzhen Lin, Liang Wang, Ka-Chun Wong

entry.summary: SyncPlan is a plan-execute-correct framework for LLM multi-agent coordination that inserts explicit synchronization points and localized corrections instead of either constant re-planning or one-shot open-loop plans. It aims to cut coordination latency while staying robust to asynchronous agent progress and environment change.

entry.title: TIDES: A Longitudinal Bilingual Dataset for Modeling Multi-Party Social Dynamics

author.name: Heechan Lee, Jeonggyu Kang, Junho Myung, Jaywoong Jeong, Juho Kim, Joseph Seering

entry.summary: TIDES is a longitudinal bilingual dataset of about 76k utterances from twelve university project teams recorded across a full semester of in-person meetings, with annotations for interaction types and emergent social roles. It aims to support modeling of long-term multi-party social dynamics that lab-style group conversation corpora miss.

entry.title: TextNCA: Neural Cellular Automata for Language Modeling via Hierarchical Local Attention

author.name: Avni Mittal, Avinash Anand, Ashutosh Kumar, Dikshant Kukreja, Kritarth Prasad, Sushane Dulloo, Erik Cambria, Timothy Liu, Zhengkui Wang, Rajiv Ratn Shah

entry.summary: TextNCA implements a neural cellular automaton primitive as causal windowed attention with shared weights and multiple iterations, and studies which of locality, iteration, or weight sharing drives behavior at roughly 30M parameters on WikiText-103. The authors report it does not match parameter-matched transformers and explicitly present it as an analytical probe rather than a proposed replacement.

entry.title: PhyCheck: Fine-Grained Evidence-Grounded Dataset for Physical Law Understanding in Video-LLMs

author.name: Zhongjie Ba, Shengwang Xu, Peng Cheng, Jinyang Zou, Ting Yu, Zhibo Wang, Zhan Qin

entry.summary: PhyCheck is a video question answering dataset for testing whether video language models can judge if observed events obey specific physical laws, organized at coarse and fine granularity with evidence grounding. It complements existing benchmarks that mainly rate the physical plausibility of generated video.

entry.title: Can Foundation Models Hear What Made That Sound? A Tiered Benchmark of Audio-Language Models and Traditional Classifiers for Closed-Set Sound Source Identification

author.name: Sajjad Abdoli, Ghassan Al-Sumaidaee, Ahmad ElShiekh, Ahmed Rashad

entry.summary: This benchmark compares eleven audio classification approaches on closed-set sound source identification over about 2,200 clips and 23 fine-grained classes, grouping them into four tiers because task specification and scoring differ fundamentally across method types. The strongest entry is a Gemini 3.1 Pro preview model, which reaches roughly 86 percent category-level F1 but much lower fine-grained accuracy, exposing a large granularity gap.

entry.title: CoWAM: Coordination Contracts for Selective Policy Intervention with WAMs

author.name: Shuaijun Liu, Qifu Wen, Shuyang Hao, Qi Luo, Chenglong Zhang, Feiyang You, Chengyu Wu, Ningxin Su

entry.summary: CoWAM adds a selective intervention layer over bimanual robot policies augmented with world action models, encoding synchronization, role compatibility, and collision constraints as verifiable coordination contracts with calibrated gates. The nominal policy action is kept unless an alternative provably satisfies all obligations, otherwise the system abstains.

entry.title: GLOBE: Trajectory-Aligned Gradient Matching with Structured SparseOptimization for Coreset Selection

author.name: Hetian Liu, Jin Cui, Mengcheng Shi, Yanbin Hu, Xinyue Long, Boran Zhao, Pengju Pen

entry.summary: GLOBE selects training coresets by representing each sample with a gradient trajectory across multiple checkpoints and solving a global sparse weighting problem, instead of greedy selection from a single snapshot. Targets on-device training where memory and compute prohibit full datasets.

entry.title: Can Training Logs Make Model Comparisons More Precise?

author.name: Wei-Jung Huang

entry.summary: Asks whether training-log statistics from the same runs can sharpen comparisons between stochastically trained models, using arm-specific covariate adjustment so the reported effect remains the raw mean difference. Across three architectures and three vision datasets, early-training log covariates often reduce uncertainty, with covariate selection identified as the main pitfall.

entry.title: Evaluation Blindness: How Silent Measurement Failures Corrupt AI Systems from Training to Deployment

author.name: Priyanka Bajaj (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: Introduces the notion of evaluation blindness, where a measurement function returns healthy-looking readings while the system is actually failing, and argues that training-time reward gaming, silent importance-sampling errors, and benchmark contamination are instances of the same phenomenon as production monitoring gaps. Frames these as a unified lifecycle measurement problem.

entry.title: NOMADD: Numerical Optimization of Models Adapting to Data Drift

author.name: Swapn Shah, Keith Burghardt

entry.summary: NOMADD is a post-hoc numerical adjustment method that mitigates concept drift for tabular models without retraining, applicable across trees, neural networks, and tabular foundation models. It targets deployment settings where labels are delayed and retraining is impractical.

entry.title: Paired Recipient-based Evaluation of Survival Prediction for Deceased Donor Kidney Transplants

author.name: Misaki Matsuura, Mohammadreza Nemati, Dulat Bekbolsynov, Stanislaw Stepkowski, Kevin S. Xu

entry.summary: Evaluates survival prediction models for deceased-donor kidney transplants using a novel paired-recipient framework that compares graft outcomes for two recipients receiving kidneys from the same donor, approximating counterfactual matching benefit. The design addresses whether predictions are actually useful for allocation decisions rather than just accurate on average.

entry.title: PLAN: Parallel Liquid-Inspired Approximation Network for Efficient Representation Learning in Flexible Job Shop Scheduling

author.name: Dhivya Dharshini Kannan, Wei Zhang, Jieyi Bi, Yingpeng Du, Tianjun Wei, Jie Zhang, Zuming Liu, Anupam Trivedi

entry.summary: PLAN reformulates continuous liquid neural network dynamics into a discretized, parallelizable form to give flexible job shop scheduling a lightweight alternative to heavy attention-based deep reinforcement learning policies. The goal is comparable scheduling quality with far fewer parameters and lower inference latency.

entry.title: SynEnergy: Anomaly Semantic-Guided Diffusion for Synthetic Energy Data Generation

author.name: Lin Jiang, Dahai Yu, Ravikumar Gelli, Guang Wang

entry.summary: SynEnergy generates synthetic fine-grained energy consumption data using an anomaly-semantics-guided diffusion model, explicitly preserving sparse anomalous events from extreme weather, outages, and behavior shifts that existing generators smooth away. It targets privacy-constrained sharing of data for forecasting, demand response, and grid reliability studies.

entry.title: Lightweight Chunk Selection for Mobile Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Sicong Chang, Yidan Shen, Wen Yu, Jiefu Chen, Xin Fu, Renjie Hu

entry.summary: Studies lightweight retrieval chunk selection for on-device RAG, framing selection as evidence alignment and combining three cheap complementary features rather than invoking an extra LLM or compressor. The motivation is that the top-ranked chunk by similarity is often not the most evidence-supporting one, while mobile budgets forbid heavy rerankers.

entry.title: AS-FedBridge: Pseudo-Spike Bridge Distillation for Heterogeneous ANN-SNN Federated Learning

author.name: Shengyang Li, Yiting Dong, Liuyang Song, Ximing Wang, Luyuan Xie, Cong Li, Qingni Shen, Zhaofei Yu

entry.summary: AS-FedBridge enables federated training that mixes conventional neural networks with spiking neural networks by bridging the semantic gap between continuous activations and discrete spikes using pseudo-spike distillation. It targets energy-constrained edge deployments where SNNs are attractive.

entry.title: ConformalShift: Targeted Event Reordering Against Adaptive ECG Monitoring

author.name: Arash Vashagh, Yasmin Vashagh

entry.summary: Shows that adaptive conformal prediction on streaming ECG events can be attacked purely by reordering authentic events, without touching waveforms, labels, or scores, suppressing detection of ventricular beats. Success rates far exceed random reordering on MIT-BIH records.

entry.title: Learning and Clustering on Temporal Graphs: Principles, Primitives, and Pooling

author.name: Nelson Aloysio Reis de Almeida Passos, Emanuele Carlini, Salvatore Trani

entry.summary: A survey-style synthesis of learning and clustering on temporal graphs, connecting graph neural pooling with classical community detection through shared spectral foundations. It questions whether GNN-based pooling actually beats established clustering algorithms once efficiency and recovery accuracy are considered.

entry.title: PRISM: Powerful Time Series to Image (TS2I) Representations for Multivariate Anomaly Detection

author.name: Mateusz Smendowski, Kamil Faber, Piotr Nawrocki, Nathalie Japkowicz, Roberto Corizzo

entry.summary: PRISM systematically studies how to convert multivariate time series into multi-channel images for anomaly detection and whether vision backbones can match time-domain baselines. Over 7000 experiments show well-designed image representations are competitive.

entry.title: Should the Boundary Term Be Learned in Reflected Diffusion? Conormal Trace and Reflection Masking

author.name: Ziyue Wang, Takafumi Kanamori

entry.summary: Analyzes score matching for reflected diffusion on bounded domains and shows the leftover boundary term reduces to a single scalar per boundary point, the diffusion-weighted normal component of the score. The paper proposes a parametrization that enforces the required boundary trace without extra trainable parameters or stochastic boundary losses. Improves the theoretical soundness of constrained-domain generative diffusion.

entry.title: FOUND-AF: Benchmarking ECG Foundation Models for Atrial Fibrillation Detection

author.name: Amirhossein Taleshinosrati, Yangyang Wang, Atitaya Phoemsuk, Vahid Abolghasemi, Naser Hossein Motlagh, Sadasivan Puthusserypady, Daniel Teichmann, Abdolrahman Peimankar

entry.summary: FOUND-AF benchmarks nine public ECG foundation models from five families for atrial fibrillation detection under a single leakage-controlled, deployment-oriented protocol with identical preprocessing and classifiers. Resolves the confound that prior comparisons used different datasets and validation setups. Provides a fair picture of which pretrained ECG representations actually transfer.

entry.title: Cross-Layer Interaction under Weight-Space Ablation: A Closed-Form Attention Jacobian Bound and a Test on a Real Pretrained Model

author.name: Abdallah Khemais

entry.summary: Extends a companion theoretical result on when activation patching and weight-space ablation agree, decomposing interaction effects from ablating carriers across multiple layers and testing the closed-form attention Jacobian bound on a real pretrained model rather than toy transformers. Aims to put interpretability ablation practice on firmer footing. Contributes to the reliability of causal interpretability tooling.

entry.title: FLARE: Few-shot Learning-based Adaptive Reflective Engine

author.name: Dhanasekar Sundararaman, Bharat Gandhi, Aashna Garg, Minjie Li

entry.summary: Challenges the claim that reflective instruction evolution such as GEPA supersedes few-shot optimization, introducing FLARE which pairs reflective mechanisms with a small set of few-shot reference examples. Evaluated on retrieval-augmented reasoning, tool calling, and multi-label emotion classification benchmarks. Contributes to the fast-moving prompt-optimizer literature.

entry.title: On the Non-Specificity of Statistical Measures Used in Script Decipherment

author.name: Nikhil Raghavendra

entry.summary: Tests the specificity premise behind statistical arguments that undeciphered sign systems encode language, by constructing SIGIL, a 3,000-text generative emblem corpus with compositional meaning but no phonological values. A pre-registered registry of 54 published methods shows SIGIL is classified the same as the Indus corpus on every reproducible criterion. A constructive negative result for computational decipherment claims.

entry.title: What Language Does and What the Evidence Supports: A Functional Role Taxonomy and Evidence Audit of Language Grounding in Embodied Agents

author.name: Yifan Guo, Chenghao Li, Zhu Wang, Wei Xu, Yu Li, Yulong Zhu, Zhuo Sun, Bin Guo, Zhiwen Yu

entry.summary: A survey that separates what language does inside embodied agents from what the evidence actually supports, defining five functional roles (specification, embodied representation, action orchestration, grounding regulation, execution coupling) and the observations or interventions needed to test each claim. Applying the framework reveals a recurring gap where interpretable linguistic intermediates may be wrong, unused, or causally inert. Useful epistemic hygiene for the language-conditioned robotics literature.

entry.title: Aligning Large Vision-Language Models at Test Time: A Trajectory-Guided Structured Sampling Approach

author.name: Tianbao Jiang, Weicong Ni, Gerard de Melo, Linlin Wang

entry.summary: Proposes test-time alignment for large vision-language models using trajectory-guided structured sampling, curating a reasoning memory bank that decomposes complex questions into ordered primitive steps and using it to refine inference dynamically. Motivated by the cost of post-training RL and the mismatch between training objectives and inference-time distributions. An inference-time alternative to RL alignment for visual reasoning.

entry.title: RIDGE: Re-Noising with Internal Dynamic Guidance for Image Editing

author.name: Ruiliang Gong, Zhen Wang, Yanghao Wang, Long Chen

entry.summary: RIDGE is a training-free, inversion-free image editing method that corrects the geometry of the target-side state used at each flow step, replacing the standard equal-displacement construction whose updates become too aggressive at high noise levels. It maintains the edited state as an evolving approximation of the unavailable clean target.

entry.title: Predictive Enhancement Calibration for Latent Breast MRI Virtual Contrast Enhancement

author.name: Qin Lei, Hao Wu

entry.summary: Predictive Enhancement Calibration addresses a mismatch between natural-image latent autoencoders and the non-canonical intensity scale of MRI when synthesizing contrast-enhanced breast MRI from pre-contrast scans. It uses a shared case-adaptive coordinate during training and predicts the missing upper intensity endpoint at inference, integrated with a pretrained latent flow transformer.

entry.title: A fully nonlinear structural vector autoregressive model identified via independent innovation analysis

author.name: Savi Virolainen

entry.summary: Introduces a structural VAR model in which the contemporaneous mapping from shocks to observables may be nonlinear and non-additive, identified by exploiting how an observed exogenous variable shifts the conditional distributions of independent shocks. A contrastive learning objective recovers the shocks, and added structure strengthens identification beyond the componentwise-transformation ambiguity of standard independent innovation analysis.

entry.title: Agentic Coding in the Wild: Characterizing GitHub Copilot Traces at Production Scale
