entry.summary: This paper combines MediaPipe keypoint extraction with a hybrid deep and bidirectional reservoir computing pipeline and ridge regression readout for isolated sign language recognition on low-cost edge hardware. The motivation is avoiding the compute cost of deep sequence models.

entry.title: Unsupervised Adversarial Domain Adaptation for Uterine layer Segmentation: From Labeled Cine to Unlabeled Dynamic EPI MRI

author.name: Smiti Tripathy, Milauni Desai, Jordina Aviles Verdera, Jana Hutter

entry.summary: This work introduces a dynamic multi-echo EPI MRI protocol to jointly characterize uterine peristalsis and tissue relaxation changes at low field, and uses unsupervised adversarial domain adaptation to transfer uterine layer segmentation from labeled cine MRI to unlabeled EPI data. The adaptation avoids the burden of manual annotation on the noisier modality.

entry.title: Flying over The Uncertain Nature (FORTUNE): Intelligent and Humanistic 3D Path Planning for Low-Altitude Collaboration

author.name: Minghui Liwang, Wenhan Jia, Xinlei Yi, Wenbo Zhu, Yuhan Su, Xianbin Wang

entry.summary: FORTUNE plans 3D paths and assigns tasks for multiple UAVs under uncertain ground point-of-interest demands, modeling persistent, predictable, and emergent demand types in one framework. It adds altitude-dependent societal costs such as noise exposure and public safety risk to balance sensing quality against community impact.

entry.title: Optimization and Constraint Modeling using LLMs with a Retrieval Augmented Generation Process

author.name: Prateek Roy, Akash Singirikonda

entry.summary: The authors build a synthetic corpus of 500 optimization problems derived from Text2Zinc seeds and persona-conditioned generation, then test whether retrieval augmentation over this corpus improves LLM-generated optimization and constraint models. The focus is on combinatorial formulations where models often produce structurally inconsistent output. It is an empirical study of RAG as a fix for formal modeling errors.

entry.title: Co-evolution of social reward and punishment under institutional interventions

author.name: Van An Nguyen, Vuong Khang Huynh, Hoai Thuong Nguyen, Duc Tin Duong, An Nguyen Gia, Tat Kien Nguyen, Huu Loi Bui, My Nguyen Tra, Ho Nam Duong, Ba Thanh Phan, Thanh Vo, Dinh Anh Trung Hoang, Adeela Bashir, Zhao Song, Manh Hong Duong, Le Hong Trang, The Anh Han

entry.summary: Studies replicator dynamics and lattice agent-based simulations where peer punishment and reward coexist with a central institution that can target any strategy subset. Evaluates which intervention mixes maximize cooperation and enforcement efficiency.

entry.title: Skillsets on the Chain: A Blockchain-based Zero-Trust Framework for Agentic AI Networking

author.name: Yayu Gao, Yong Xiao, Hao Hu, Xubo Li, Zhiwei Liu, Yingyu Li, Guangming Shi, Ping Zhang

entry.summary: TrustAgentNet proposes a two-tier blockchain design for agentic AI networks: a global chain governing skillset metadata lifecycle with off-chain auditing, plus transient task-specific chains for trustless multi-agent collaboration. It targets the mismatch between what third-party agent skills claim and what they actually do.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence and Modeling & Simulation: An Overview

author.name: Niclas Feldkamp, Philippe J. Giabbanelli, Istvan David

entry.summary: This overview maps the two-way relationship between AI and modeling and simulation: AI augmenting or replacing simulation components at each stage from specification through validation and output analysis, and simulation serving as data generator, training environment, and evaluation platform for AI. It is a structured community-oriented survey.

entry.title: Asking Questions the Right Way: A Multi-Agent Conversational System for Prompt Formulation in Complex Task Resolution

author.name: B. Sankar, Pawni Yadav, Srinidhi Ranjini Girish, Amogh A. S

entry.summary: PAWNI is an eight-agent conversational interface that turns unstructured user queries into structured prompts through guided question-and-answer dialogue backed by a self-evolving knowledge base, organized around 18 prompt elements in three tiers. It optimizes the question rather than the model response.

entry.title: Statistical Mechanics of Learning on Product Wasserstein Manifolds

author.name: Srinivasa Rao P Vangmayi P Reddy

entry.summary: Reframes weight-distribution constraints in learning theory as defining intrinsic geometry rather than reducing capacity, formulating deep networks and variational quantum circuits as gradient flows on products of classical and quantum Wasserstein manifolds. It applies statistical mechanics tools within this geometric setting.

entry.title: When Extreme Darkness Meets Motion Blur: MeanFlow for Unified RAW Restoration

author.name: Zepu Wang, Jingze Liang, Weijie Xiao, Kexin Chen

entry.summary: This work jointly handles extreme low-light RAW enhancement and motion blur, contributing the SIDED dataset with controlled motion degradation on real low-light RAW pairs plus a unified RAW tokenizer and a MeanFlow-based restoration model. It argues prior low-light methods ignore motion degradations that occur in practice.

entry.title: BRiG-AFA: Bellman Risk-to-Go Learning for Non-Myopic Active Feature Acquisition

author.name: Jiaorong Feng, Qian Li, Ying Li

entry.summary: BRiG-AFA learns a candidate-conditioned risk-to-go function separately for each remaining acquisition budget, fitted backward with Bellman targets from one-step terminal classification risk, to decide which feature to measure next. It offers a supervised, non-myopic alternative to greedy heuristics, deep reinforcement learning, and generative conditional density estimation.

entry.title: From fragmented data to actionable design: Physics-calibrated learning for plastic upcycling

author.name: Jingyang Bai, Zijia Wang, Xiangyi Long, Marcos Millan, Binjian Nie, Mingyue Ding

entry.summary: This work learns from heavily incomplete plastic-upcycling experiment literature by treating structured missingness as an informative signal, using a physics-calibrated, missingness-gated mixture-of-experts that avoids target imputation and reconstructs physically consistent product distributions. Complete-case learning would have discarded about 89 percent of the curated experiments.

entry.title: Schedule-Informed Temporal Fusion Forecasting of Hourly Airport Security-Checkpoint Throughput

author.name: Yinxiao Zhang, Sen Wang, Yi Gao

entry.summary: Builds an airport checkpoint throughput forecaster that converts flight schedules into passenger-arrival intensity signals using truncated Poisson kernels and feeds them to a temporal fusion transformer alongside historical throughput. Applied to two years of screening and schedule data for a major hub to support staffing decisions.

entry.title: A Hyperfinite Framework for Score-Based Generative Modeling

author.name: Sunder Ram Krishnan

entry.summary: Reformulates score-based diffusion using nonstandard analysis, starting from an internal diffusion on a hyperfinite grid and deriving the generator, the correspondence with Fokker-Planck, and a constructive reverse-time drift identity. It shows the internal score-matching objective recovers the score function.

entry.title: AI World Cup 2026: Benchmarking Large Language Models for End-to-End Football Tournament Prediction

author.name: Jonaid Shianifar, Iias Faiud

entry.summary: Reports a completed forecasting benchmark in which ten LLM assistants each produced a single pre-tournament prediction of the entire 2026 World Cup under identical snapshots, prompts, schemas, and scoring, then scored against all 104 actual matches. GPT-5.5 Thinking, an existing model, ranked first. The value lies in standardized, prospective, non-contaminated forecasting evaluation.

entry.title: Accelerating Dynamic Graph Clustering on GPU Architectures with cuGraph

author.name: Nelson Aloysio Reis de Almeida Passos, Emanuele Carlini, Salvatore Trani

entry.summary: Ports spectral clustering and modularity-based community detection to GPUs via the NVIDIA RAPIDS cuGraph ecosystem, extending them to snapshot-based dynamic graphs with multi-GPU Leiden optimization and a Bethe-Hessian eigendecomposition backend. Reports up to roughly three orders of magnitude speedup over CPU references under equal-work budgets. Infrastructure contribution for temporal graph analytics.

entry.title: Character Iconicity vs. Arbitrariness: An Arabic NLP Perspective

author.name: Dorieh Alomari, Irfan Ahmad, Maged S. Al-shaibani

entry.summary: Uses the historical fact that early undotted Arabic manuscripts remained readable to test whether dotless Arabic NLP performance depends on preserving original rasm groupings or merely on any consistent mapping to a reduced symbol set. Compares dotted, dotless, and arbitrary constrained remappings. A clean linguistic experiment on iconicity versus arbitrariness in orthographic representation.

entry.title: Localize, Don't Beautify: Client-Side Control of Image-Editing APIs for Cosmetic Surgery Previews

author.name: Sukhrobbek Ilyosbekov

entry.summary: A pilot benchmark tests how much a client can constrain commercial image-editing APIs to a requested facial region for cosmetic surgery previews, comparing prompt-only control, landmark-mask compositing, and inpainting. The finding is that closed editing APIs frequently alter unrequested attributes such as skin texture or lighting.

entry.title: Test Time Adaptation Methods for Point Cloud Registration in Laparoscopic Surgery

author.name: Nina Bodelot, Soufiane Belharbi, Eric Granger

entry.summary: The work adapts test-time adaptation techniques, originally built for classification, to 3D point cloud registration between intraoperative reconstructions and preoperative organ meshes in laparoscopy. It addresses the asymmetric synthetic-to-real domain shift where only the intraoperative cloud is noisy and occluded.

entry.title: LDU-Bench: Multimodal LLM Evaluation for Lithography Defect Understanding under Layout-Varying Circuit Backgrounds

author.name: Huanglong Ji, Botong Zhao, Shujing Lv, Yue Lv

entry.summary: LDU-Bench evaluates multimodal LLMs on lithography defect review across four tasks: triage, morphology recognition, coarse localization, and image-conditioned cause analysis, using real semiconductor review images. It tests whether models can reason about defect causes rather than only flag anomalies.

entry.title: SGFormer: Structure-Guided Transformer for Robust Local Feature Matching

author.name: Runyu Zhu

entry.summary: SGFormer identifies attention divergence in detector-free local feature matching, where unconstrained global attention places confident matches outside the true overlapping region under large viewpoint change. It adds structural guidance to focus attention on salient structures for photogrammetry and 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: Active Stiffness Control of a Supportive Continuum Robot

author.name: Rana Danesh, Farrokh Janabi-Sharifi, Farhad Aghili

entry.summary: Presents an active task-space stiffness control framework for tendon-driven supportive continuum robots, where a second arm mechanically couples to the primary arm to raise load capacity. The method projects closed-chain variable-strain dynamics onto constrained coordinates so stiffness can be regulated online for varying payloads.

entry.title: Trust and Its Betrayal under Three Representational Strategies

author.name: Mihnea C. Moldoveanu, Joel A. C. Baum

entry.summary: This theoretical paper models trust as a subjunctive epistemic state, formalizing competence as the belief that the trustee would know a truth and integrity as the belief that they would disclose it. Three representations are compared: lexicographic assumption, ordinal closeness in Lewis-Stalnaker spheres, and strong belief in conditional probability systems, with attention to whether betrayal is representable in each. The relevance to AI is indirect but bears on human trust in automated agents.

entry.title: An Information Theoretic Treatment of Yager's Probability Distribution Negation

author.name: Roberto Bruno, Ugo Vaccaro

entry.summary: The paper gives an information-theoretic and majorization-based analysis of Yager's negation of a probability distribution, unifying and strengthening previously scattered properties and its generalizations. The conclusion is that Yager's definition is the principled choice under a range of criteria.

entry.title: Neural network realization of binary refinement iterates via a two-chart atlas selector

author.name: Tsogtgerel Gantumur

entry.summary: Gives a new constructive proof that finite iterates of scalar binary refinement operators admit exact ReLU network realizations with fixed width and depth growing linearly in the number of refinement steps. The difficulty addressed is that refinement is driven by discontinuous binary digit choices while ReLU networks are continuous, handled via a two-chart atlas selector.

entry.title: Distilled Roads: Generalisable Road Network Extraction Across Sensors, Resolutions, and Region

author.name: Sanayya, Rakshith Sathish, Ashwathi Nambiar

entry.summary: Reframes global road-network extraction from satellite imagery as a continual adaptation problem rather than an architecture problem, combining distillation with adaptation to handle new sensors, resolutions, and regions without full retraining or catastrophic forgetting. Targets the poor generalization of models trained on narrow region-resolution combinations. Useful for large-scale remote sensing mapping.

entry.title: Learning a Vector-Symbolic Model for Socio-Cultural Tasks

author.name: Meera Ray, Swapnika Dulam, Christopher L. Dancy

entry.summary: Proposes a declarative memory system for the ACT-R cognitive architecture using vector-symbolic representations, so that sociocultural associations and self-representations can be modeled at multiple levels of semantic abstraction. Argues co-occurrence-based LLM or corpus embeddings alone miss the role of self-representation in culturally shaped decision making. Contributes to cognitive architecture and computational social modeling.

entry.title: AIDE: Automated Instruction via Distilled Expertise for Reference-Free Motor Skill Coaching

author.name: Yoshiki Ito

entry.summary: AIDE distills a teacher that sees paired learner and expert poses into a student that generates natural-language coaching feedback from the learner's pose sequence alone at inference. This removes the need for expert reference demonstrations at deployment time.

entry.title: SeCo-SBIR: Semantically Consistent Prompt Learning for Zero-Shot Sketch-Based Image Retrieval

author.name: Long Hoang Dang, Tuan Nguyen Huu, Nguyen Minh Hieu, Tu Minh Phuong

entry.summary: SeCo-SBIR adapts CLIP for zero-shot sketch-based image retrieval by routing learnable prompts through the text encoder and injecting the resulting representations into every visual layer, aiming to bridge the sketch-photo gap without overfitting to seen categories. It explicitly balances task adaptation against retained zero-shot generalization.

entry.title: Frequency-Decorrelated Temporal Ensembles for EEG--fNIRS Imagined-Handwriting Decoding

author.name: Xiao Fan, Hongbin Guo, Yubo Han, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: FRED decodes imagined handwriting from synchronized EEG and fNIRS by training compact multi-scale temporal networks on three complementary EEG frequency views and ensembling across bands. Cross-band ensemble members make less correlated errors than same-band replicas, improving subject-independent four-class accuracy.

entry.title: Recurrent Contrastive Learning for Imbalanced Medical Image Classification

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhu, Xinling Meng, Junxuan Yu, Jiongquan Chen, Qiongying Ni, Tuhang Shao, Yuhao Huang, Luping Zhou, Ruiyang Huang, Yuxue Wang, Rongliang Zhang, Xue Wang, Tianhong Tang, Likun Wang, Junbo Chen, Yong Jiang, Yongping Lu, Xin Yang

entry.summary: Recurrent Contrastive Learning tackles class imbalance in medical image classification by reusing historical feature states across training phases to enlarge the latent support region of rare classes, rather than only resampling or reweighting losses. It builds on a strong self-supervised vision backbone with lightweight adaptation.

entry.title: Detecting Pose Estimation Failures via Keypoint Self-Consistency

author.name: Robin Chan

entry.summary: This paper proposes hand-crafted geometric features capturing self-consistency among predicted 2D keypoints to flag likely failures of keypoint-based 6D pose estimation, since rigid rotations should preserve object shape. Detecting unreliable pose estimates matters for downstream robotic use.

entry.title: Compass: Degradation-Simulated Reciprocal Learning with Lightweight Needle RWKV for Multimodal Crack Segmentation under Missing Modalities

author.name: Hui Liu, Chen Jia, Fan Shi, Xu Cheng, Mianzhao Wang, Shengyong Chen

entry.summary: Compass segments cracks in industrial multimodal imagery robustly when modalities are missing, using a degradation-simulation stream that mimics worse conditions and distills reciprocally with the full-modality stream, plus a lightweight recurrent block and evidential topology-preserving fusion. The emphasis is on low compute for deployment.

entry.title: Impacts of Single-objective Landscapes on Multi-objective Optimization

author.name: Shoichiro Tanaka, Keiki Takadama, Hiroyuki Sato

entry.summary: This study examines how the local optima networks of the constituent single-objective problems relate to the Pareto optima network of the combined multi-objective combinatorial problem, decomposing the joint network into components characterized by overlap relations. Results indicate most Pareto optimal solutions are reachable from single-objective optima.

author.name: Xidong Yang, Xingyi Zhang, Wenhao Li, Wenyan Liu, Junjie Sheng, Yun Hua, Wei Yin, Tao Fang, Chuyun Shen, Xiangfeng Wang

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.01149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lifelong LLM agents increasingly adapt through external learning states that store past interactions as retrievable memories or reusable skills, yet ex...

entry.title: Emergence Invariance: From Symbolized Thought to Interface Refinement

author.name: Yi Liu

entry.summary: A philosophical formalization arguing language is a consequence-governed symbolic projection of broader cognition, so language-first LLMs inherit structural incompletenesses that emergent capabilities cannot fully compensate. Introduces symbolization premises and asks whether emergence closes every missing distinction.

entry.title: SymNet: A Multi-Task Network for Joint Radio Map Reconstruction and Transmitter Localization

author.name: Lyuzhou Ye, Thanh Dat Le, Yan Huang

entry.summary: SymNet is a multi-task neural network that jointly reconstructs directional radio coverage maps and localizes the transmitter from sparse measurements, arguing that in directional propagation the strongest-signal point no longer coincides with the transmitter. The work matters for wireless network planning and spectrum management where angular effects, reflections, and building occlusion break omnidirectional assumptions.

entry.title: Hybrid Attention Estimation Pipeline for Adaptive HRI Using an Expressive Robotic Head

author.name: Pablo Moraes, Monica Rodriguez, Christopher Peters, Hiago Sodre, Tobias Doernbach, Bruna Guterres, Ricardo Grando

entry.summary: This applied case study estimates human attention for an expressive robotic head by combining a fast geometric face and head-pose layer with a slower vision-language semantic layer that labels whether a person attends to the robot, uses a phone, or looks elsewhere, fused by a finite state machine controlling interaction behavior. It is a systems integration report for adaptive human-robot interaction.

entry.title: Rethinking and formalising the state across languages: a unified computational learning theory account

author.name: Mohamed El Idrissi

entry.summary: The paper argues that the linguistic notion of state, traditionally treated as an Afroasiatic construct-state peculiarity, is a general context-dependent morphosyntactic mechanism selecting grammatical templates, and formalizes it as a set-valued function over templates within a template-based modular cognitive framework with an accompanying learning algorithm. Riffian serves as the primary empirical basis.

entry.title: Rethinking Generative AI Literacy: An Integrative, Developmental, and Dialectical Framework for K-12 Teacher Education

author.name: Shahin Hossain, Sima Ahmadi, Leqi Li, Idowu David Awoyemi, Wei Huang, Chenxi Zhou, Jujia Li, Samaa Haniya, Shapla Khanam, Tasbirun Mashreka Subaha

entry.summary: This position and review paper proposes RAIL-Ed, a framework for generative AI literacy in K-12 teacher education, developed from a systematic review of dozens of prior frameworks and studies. It treats ethics, equity, and agency as constitutive rather than add-on competencies.

entry.title: Disagree to Accelerate: Closing the Loop on Diffusion Feature Forecasts

author.name: Yanchao Li, Jiaqing Xie, Ben Gao, Wanhao Liu, Yanbo Wang, T. Y. Tsui, Jinfei Liu, Yuqiang Li, Tianfan Fu

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.01740v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Training-free feature forecasting accelerates diffusion sampling by predicting features at skipped denoising steps. Recent work has mainly focused on...

entry.title: Can Urban Blight Be Accessed with Vision-language Models: A Case Study in Detroit

author.name: Xiaohao Yang, Aohua Tian, Derek Van Berkel, Xu Qiang, Mark Lindquist

entry.summary: This case study uses open-weight vision-language models with structured prompts over multiple street-level views to estimate residential blight in Detroit, scoring roof, wall, and opening conditions and comparing against survey-based references. It explores whether VLMs can replace labor-intensive periodic blight surveys.

entry.title: Multi-Source Dynamic Graph Learning for Compound-Flood Forecasting in Managed Coastal Systems

author.name: Liangjun You, Min Wu, Orlando Woods, Dongsheng Luo

entry.summary: An anchored multi-source dynamic graph learning framework forecasts compound coastal flooding by fusing signals from many monitoring stations while preventing cross-site fusion from destabilizing local temporal predictions. It emphasizes reproducing prolonged high-water plateaus that average error metrics hide.

entry.title: TALSC: Timeliness-Aware Large-Small VLM Collaboration for Infrastructure-Assisted Autonomous Driving

author.name: Mengmeng Zhu, Yuxuan Sun, Wei Chen, Bo Ai

entry.summary: TALSC decides when an autonomous vehicle should offload perception to a large vision-language model at an edge server versus rely on its small on-board model, modeling age-of-information decay so that stale but accurate remote answers are not overvalued. It formalizes the accuracy-versus-timeliness trade-off in infrastructure-assisted driving.

entry.title: TBSG-Net: Temporal Bipartite Scene Graph Network for Fine-Grained Video Moment Retrieval

author.name: Ji Huang, Yongsheng Dai, Tianyu Ren, Barry Devereux, Hui Wang

entry.summary: TBSG-Net replaces static frame-level scene graphs in video moment retrieval with a temporal bipartite scene graph that models how object relations evolve and explicitly encodes relation durations. This targets the loss of temporal dependencies and imprecise localization in scene-graph-based retrieval.

entry.title: GLAIM: Learning Global and Local Adaptive Inter-Variable Dependency for Multivariate Time Series Imputation

author.name: Mingyang Wang, Rongwen Li, Xiao Wang, Changjian Chen

entry.summary: GLAIM imputes missing values in multivariate time series by combining a stable global inter-variable dependency structure with adaptive per-sample local dependencies, so that local adaptivity does not propagate errors when observations are sparse. It explicitly trades off the failure modes of purely global and purely local dependency modeling.

entry.title: Bridging Artificial Intelligence and Power Systems Education Using a Hands-On Executable Framework

author.name: Junjie Yin (Fran), Buxin She (Fran), Xinyu Feng (Fran), Fangxing (Fran), Li

entry.summary: Proposes an executable, hands-on curriculum framework for teaching AI in power and energy systems, motivated by a survey where the large majority of practitioners report setup barriers and want domain-specific courses. Advocates engineering-grounded AI workflows that respect power-system rules rather than treating models as generic black boxes.

author.name: Shahrukh Mohiuddin, Chalamalasetti Kranti, Sherzod Hakimov, David Schlangen

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.03388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Abductive reasoning requires forming hypotheses that explain observed evidence and revising them as new evidence becomes available. While large languag...

author.name: Akhilesh Kakolu Ramarao, Kevin Tang, Wiebke Petersen, Dinah Baer-Henney

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.03452v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a transformer learns an irregular morphological pattern, what has it learned? Our test case is the Spanish \emph{L-shaped morphome}, a complex irr...

author.name: Ahmed Amine Aliane, Nasredine Semmar, Hassina Aliane

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.03480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The adoption of large pre-trained multilingual models for neural machine translation (MNMT) faces a major challenge: excessive memory and computational...

author.name: Jinhong Jeong, Seungyeop Yi, Sangah Lee, Youngjae Yu

entry.title: The Bayesian Reflex: A Predictive Coding Engine for Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Sourabh Bhattacharya

entry.summary: This paper proposes the Bayesian Reflex, a framework instantiating predictive coding through hierarchical generative belief maintenance, sequential Bayesian updating by prediction-error minimization, and uncertainty-driven action via active inference. It argues that recent advances in ellipsoidal decomposition sampling, recursive Gaussian processes, and derivative-aware Bayesian optimization supply the previously missing scalable ingredients. It is a synthesis and architectural proposal rather than an empirical result.

entry.title: Supporting Cybersecurity Risk Management for Medical Devices via the SECUMAN Ontology and Shapes

author.name: Martin Diller, Anne Esslinger, Piotr Gorczyca, Evi Hartig, Lia Kacholdt, Hannes Strass

entry.summary: SECUMAN is an OWL ontology plus SHACL shapes for representing cybersecurity risk-management documentation for connected medical devices, covering risk context, assessment, control measures, and residual-risk evaluation, aligned with VDE Spec 90025. It makes consistency checking, certification review, and reuse tractable where documentation is currently semi-structured prose.

entry.title: A Unified Resolution-Conditioned Framework for Orthogonal Line-Scanning Image Fusion

author.name: Yiming Gong, Kai Wang

entry.summary: A single resolution-conditioned network fuses orthogonal line-scan microscopy images to recover near-isotropic resolution, using feature-wise linear modulation on the resolving-power ratio so one model spans many optical configurations. An adaptive linear-attention variant replaces fixed-kernel rank enhancement.

entry.title: CRIL-U-Net: Compact Ratio-Interaction Learning for Focal Cortical Dysplasia Segmentation from T1w and FLAIR MRI

author.name: Soumen Ghosh, Amit Soni Arya, Tilottama Goswami, Subhojit Mandal, John Phamnguyen, Rajat Vashistha

entry.summary: CRIL-U-Net is a 3D U-Net with a module that mixes T1-weighted and FLAIR MRI voxel-wise and through bidirectional ratio interactions rather than simple channel concatenation, targeting small and subtle focal cortical dysplasia lesions. It is compared to standard and self-attention 3D U-Nets with cross-validation.

entry.title: BayesSeg: A Bayesian Optimization Framework for State Segmentation of Electricity Consumption Time Series

author.name: Zhenya Zhang, Wendi Zhu, Ping Wang, Hongmei Cheng, Shuguang Zhang

entry.summary: BayesSeg unifies time-series segmentation, multidimensional evaluation, and automatic hyperparameter optimization for non-intrusive load monitoring, using a dual steady-state criterion based on tail values and means of preceding subsequences plus complement-set parsing to separate steady and transition segments. Bayesian optimization replaces heuristic parameter tuning. The target application is appliance recognition from household electricity data.

entry.title: Multi-Dimensional Assessment for AI Cognition (MAAC): A Theoretical Framework for Process-Oriented Cognitive Evaluation of Text-Based AI Systems

author.name: Abdalla Doleh, Ratna Babu Chinnam

entry.summary: MAAC proposes shifting AI evaluation from outcome benchmarks to process-oriented cognitive assessment, defining nine dimensions including cognitive load, tool execution, memory integration, and content quality for text-based systems. The stated goal is diagnostic insight into how systems reason rather than only what they output. The paper is a theoretical framework without reported empirical validation.

entry.title: DeBERTa-Sentinel: Toward Transparent and Trustworthy Detection of AI-Generated Text

author.name: Muhammad Yousaf Rehman, Muhammad Islam

entry.summary: DeBERTa-Sentinel detects AI-generated text using DeBERTa-v3 disentangled attention and exposes token-level explanations for transparency, targeting generalization to unseen generators and paraphrase attacks. It positions interpretability as a requirement for trustworthy detection.

entry.title: Retrieval Augmented Biomedical Question Answering with Weak Question Recovery and Neural Reranking for BioASQ Task 14b

author.name: Xueying Zhao, Lee Mai, Balaji Anandganesh

entry.summary: Describes a BioASQ Task 14b biomedical QA pipeline combining PubMed retrieval, fine-tuned MiniLM reranking, reciprocal rank fusion, a conditional recovery strategy for weak queries, and OpenBioLLM answer generation. It reports improved document ranking and evidence coverage.

entry.title: Entity-Aware Sequence Transduction for Player-Centric Ball Action Spotting

author.name: Ruifeng Wang, Di Yang, Jiangtao Wang

entry.summary: ME-DST keeps an explicit player role-slot dimension throughout the encoder and factorizes attention into temporal per-slot and spatial cross-slot components for spotting ball actions with actor attribution in sports video. The design gives the model a stronger inductive bias for per-player temporal evolution than flattened frame-level baselines.

entry.title: TransNRank: Towards Accurate Neoantigen Ranking with Transformer

author.name: Zhiyin An, Yuenan Hou, Shumeng Duan, Yiming Zhou, Yuanting Zheng, Leming Shi

entry.summary: TransNRank applies a transformer with self-attention and a positive-aware objective to rank candidate neoantigens, addressing extreme class imbalance and noisy immunogenicity labels that limit linear and gradient-boosting baselines. The goal is higher recall of truly immunogenic peptides for personalized cancer vaccines.

entry.title: Agentic Self-Healing for Data and AI Pipelines: An Affordable Vendor-Agnostic Architecture using Open-Source Software

author.name: Solomon Eshun, Dennis Murage, Sharleen Muoki, Chih-Chun Chen, Stephen Adjignon, Matteo Staar, Oliver Ang\'elil

entry.summary: This paper compares commercial data and machine-learning operations platforms and proposes an affordable vendor-agnostic architecture built from open-source components for agentic self-healing of failing data and model pipelines. It targets smaller teams for whom existing observability and AIOps tooling is too expensive or too locked in.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Crossmodal Fusion for Classification of Animal Behavior

author.name: Ehsan Yaghoubi, Florian Haselbeck

entry.summary: This work fuses raw waveform and spectrogram representations for animal vocalization classification with uncertainty awareness, since the two representations degrade differently under clipping, reverberation, and noise in uncontrolled field recordings. The goal is robust acoustic monitoring for livestock welfare and wildlife conservation.

entry.title: Assessing the Impacts of Imperfect Datasets on Client Selections in Federated Learning

author.name: Yuan-Heng Tsai, Li-Hsing Yen, Yan-Wei Chen

entry.summary: This study experimentally measures how non-IID data, label and quantity skew, noisy labels, and fairness constraints in client selection affect federated learning accuracy and convergence speed. It then uses those measurements to inform selection strategies that avoid the pitfalls of both indiscriminate inclusion and heavily biased exclusion.

entry.title: Context-Aware Mixture of Domain Experts for Bodily Expression of Emotion in the Wild

author.name: Mohammad Mahdi Dehshibi, David Masip

entry.summary: CA-MoDE treats scene and object cues as structured priors over emotion categories rather than auxiliary features, with dedicated domain experts producing soft distributions that modulate a body-posture expert at the distribution level. It targets in-the-wild bodily emotion recognition where identical postures mean different things in different contexts.

entry.title: On the Performance of Malware Detection Classifiers Using Hardware Performance Counters

author.name: Alireza Abolhasani Zeraatkar, Parnian Shabani Kamran, Inderpreet Kaur, Nagabindu Ramu, Tyler Sheaves, Hussain Al-Asaad

entry.summary: Evaluates ensemble machine learning classifiers over hardware performance counter traces for run-time malware detection, positioning hardware-based detectors as a complement to antivirus software. It reports improvements from ensembling over single classifiers.

entry.title: Task-Oriented Candidate-Latent Feedback for Coarse-to-Fine Sensing in Distributed OFDM-ISAC Networks

author.name: Shiv Shankar, Radha Krishna Ganti, J Klutto Milleth

entry.summary: Proposes a learned coarse-to-fine feedback scheme for distributed integrated sensing and communication networks, where a lightweight scorer proposes candidate delay-Doppler cells and a learned encoder sends compact latents instead of raw channel tensors. Targets bandwidth-constrained interfaces between sensing hardware and inference functions. Mainly a wireless-systems contribution using learned compression.

entry.title: Hybrid LLM-Augmented Reinforcement Learning Agents for Complex Sequential Decision Tasks

author.name: Christophe D. Hounwanou, John Emeka Eze, Ya\'e Ulrich Gaba

entry.summary: Combines an LLM planner that emits subgoals and structured plans with an RL agent that optimizes low-level actions, aiming to fix both the poor action precision of LLM agents and the weak abstraction of pure RL. Reports gains on long-horizon sequential decision tasks. A familiar hierarchical hybrid architecture.

entry.title: Channel-wise Dynamic Knowledge Distillation via Adaptive Sample Generation for Action Recognition

author.name: Ping Li, Chenhao Ping, Jie Song, Mingli Song

entry.summary: This paper distills large action recognition models using adaptively generated training samples and channel-wise dynamic distillation strengths that change over training epochs. The motivation is that fixed inputs and uniform per-channel weighting misalign teacher and student features.

entry.title: Multimodal Plant Root Phenotyping with Integration of 3D Skeleton Extraction and Language Analysis

author.name: Jiakai Lin, Zijun Li, Guoyu Lu

entry.summary: This framework extracts 3D root skeletons from robotic point cloud scans via unsupervised weighted Laplacian contraction, computes morphological descriptors, and uses language-guided reasoning to interpret them. The goal is interpretable and data-efficient plant root phenotyping.

entry.title: DRPFNet: Dual-domain Residual Progressive Fusion Network for RGB-Thermal Object Detection

author.name: Zian Wang, Changchun Li

entry.summary: DRPFNet fuses visible and thermal features for object detection using progressive residual fusion across scales plus joint frequency and spatial processing, instead of independent per-scale spatial fusion. The aim is robust detection under poor illumination and adverse weather.

entry.title: OliveGemma: A 3 Billion Visual Language Model for Recognising the Mediterranean & European Diet

author.name: Dimitrios I. Zaridis, Traianos Tsiokris, Vasileios C. Pezoulas, Daphni Plati, Eugenia Mylona, Eleni Georga, Nikos Tsiknakis, Antonis Sakellarios, Dimitrios I. Fotiadis

entry.summary: OliveGemma fine-tunes a 3B open-weight vision-language model with low-rank adaptation on about 17K images and 100K instruction-style question-answer pairs to recognize and reason about Mediterranean and European dishes. It targets image-based dietary assessment as an alternative to self-reported food diaries.

entry.title: Solving the solvent problem

author.name: Steve Nadis | Department of Nuclear Science and Engineering

entry.summary: MIT researchers led by Ju Li report progress on sodium-metal batteries, focusing on the solvent chemistry problem created by sodium metal's extreme reactivity. The motivation is reducing dependence on lithium, cobalt, nickel and graphite supply chains for grid and vehicle storage.

entry.title: Enhancing LLMs with Context-Specific Knowledge for Mitigating Misinformation in SMEs: A RAG-based Modeling and Analysis

author.name: Md. Samiul Islam, Iqbal H. Sarker, Chadni Islam, Ahmad Mohsin, Ahmed Ibrahim, Helge Janicke

entry.summary: This paper compares vector-based and graph-based retrieval augmentation for reducing hallucination and misinformation in question answering deployed at small and medium enterprises. It evaluates both pipelines on business-context knowledge and reports effectiveness for grounding LLM answers. The contribution is mainly an applied deployment study rather than a new method.

entry.title: AI-Based Thesis Assessment: An Empirical Study of Human Evaluation Priorities and Their Impact on Automated Assessment

author.name: Garv Vikram Gursahaney, Baskhad Idrisov, Thorsten Fr\"ohlich, Tim Schlippe

entry.summary: This empirical study surveys 84 thesis supervisors across four disciplines to elicit weights for 35 assessment criteria, then compares these against the default weights of an existing rubric-based AI grading system and measures the downstream effect on automated scores. Substantial divergence is found between supervisor-derived and default weights. It highlights that rubric weighting choices materially shape AI assessment outcomes.

entry.title: Beyond the Gegenbauer Paradigm: q-Orthogonal Kernels for Machine Learning

author.name: \'Alvaro S\'anchez-Paniagua R\'ios, Juan P. Llerena, Alberto Lastra, Nuria Torrado, Edmundo J. Huertas

entry.summary: Introduces a support vector machine kernel built from discrete q-Hermite I polynomials, proving Mercer validity and analyzing boundedness properties. The deformation parameter offers an extra tuning knob relative to classical orthogonal polynomial kernels.

entry.title: Test-Time Augmentation for Tabular-to-Image Classifiers under Distribution Shifts

author.name: Malena Loza, Felipe Grijalva, Eva Milara, Luis Bote-Curiel, Francisco J. Lara-Abelenda, David Chushig-Muzo

entry.summary: Evaluates whether test-time augmentation improves robustness of tabular-to-image classifiers under distribution shift, across six encoding methods including TINTO, IGTD, and DeepInsight. Finds that image-style augmentation aggregation interacts with the artificial spatial structure these encodings create. An empirical robustness study of a niche modeling paradigm.

entry.title: Material-Segmented Per-Pixel Emissivity Correction for Thermographic Anomaly Detection in Cultural Heritage Digital Twins

author.name: Jonathan Klingspon, Scott McAvoy, Maurizio Seracini, Falko Kuester

entry.summary: A training-free thermography pipeline estimates per-pixel emissivity by segmenting a co-registered RGB image with an open-vocabulary segmenter and mapping materials to literature emissivity values, then solving inverse-Planck per pixel. This reduces false thermal anomalies caused by assuming one global emissivity on heterogeneous heritage surfaces.

entry.title: Clarity Contrast and Similarity Selection for Multi-Focus Image Fusion

author.name: Yicheng Zhang, Haoyou Deng, Zhiqiang Li, Wenti Yin, Nong Sang, Changxin Gao

entry.summary: CSNet fuses multi-focus images by explicitly contrasting clarity between the source images to mutually amplify sharp features and suppress blurred ones, then selecting by similarity to locate focus boundaries. The claim is better interpretability from direct cross-source interaction.

entry.title: The Transformer Revolution, Part 1: Dynamic Processing through Output- Weight Interconnections

author.name: Marco Giunti, Fabrizia Giulia Garavaglia

entry.summary: This conceptual paper argues against the stochastic parrot view by interpreting Transformer inference as constructing prompt-dependent transformations whose parameters are generated at inference time, terming this sequence-level interactive dynamic parallel processing. Token vectors are cast as concepts and attention-derived operators as transforming concepts.

entry.title: Multi-tenant Kubernetes Use Cases for AI, Secure Computing and Data Services, and More

author.name: Jake Watson, Sadaf R Alam, Christopher Woods, Abdelwahab Kawafi, Thomas Green, Ian Johnson, Ellis Pires, Jessica R. Jones, Utz-Uwe Haus

entry.summary: This report describes multi-tenant Kubernetes use cases in supercomputing environments, covering AI workloads, confidential computing for sensitive data, data services, and mixed workload orchestration, positioning Kubernetes as a complement to rather than a replacement for batch schedulers. It argues that traditional single-tenant batch systems lack the flexibility and reproducibility cloud users expect.

entry.title: X-KGRank: A Knowledge Graph RAG Framework for Explainable Recommendations via Pattern Mining and LLM Re-Ranking

author.name: Meenakshi Rajpurohit, Jainish Patel

entry.summary: X-KGRank builds a heterogeneous knowledge graph from MovieLens interactions, mines structural patterns for candidate generation, and uses an LLM to re-rank and explain recommendations. The goal is explanations grounded in a user's actual interaction graph rather than free-form LLM narration.

entry.title: Automatic Annotation of Ancient Greek Vowel Length

author.name: Albin Th\"orn Cleland, Eric Cullhed

entry.summary: The paper builds the first general-purpose system for marking phonemic vowel length in Ancient Greek, a context-dependent long-tail annotation task no public corpus covers at scale. It moves beyond static corpus-specific lookup dictionaries toward a standalone macronizer.

entry.title: Detecting high-frequency brain disorder signals using dynamic mode decomposition from EEG

author.name: Jacob Kang, Jong-Hyeon Seo

entry.summary: Uses dynamic mode decomposition to extract high-frequency dynamical modes from EEG channels as classification features for brain disorder detection. About 70 percent of samples showed consistent high-frequency dynamics in a specific channel under a random distribution test.

entry.title: From SQL Errors to Concept Gaps: An AI-Powered Knowledge Graph Analytics Platform for Personalized Feedback

author.name: Abdulrahman AlRabah, Weijian Zhou, Xing Gao, Abdussalam Alawini

entry.summary: Describes an educational platform that maps student SQL errors onto a knowledge graph of course concepts so feedback points to conceptual gaps rather than surface correctness, for example linking a NATURAL JOIN misuse to intertwined JOIN, GROUP BY, and HAVING misunderstandings. Aimed at database systems courses where autograders detect wrongness without explaining it. An applied AI-for-education contribution.

entry.title: Frozen High-Resolution Inference for Cross-City Object Detection: An AI City Challenge 2026 Study

author.name: Jaeuk Kim

entry.summary: A challenge report finds that running a detector trained at 704 pixel resolution at 1120 pixels without any parameter update gave the best aggregate cross-city detection accuracy among the archived configurations, beating a warm-start fine-tune at the higher resolution. Gains were largest for small and medium objects.

entry.title: Deep Learning CNN and Recurrence Analysis for Alpha Gamma EEG Biomarkers in Fragile X Syndrome

author.name: Zag ElSayed, Payton Siekierski, Jack Yanchen Liu, Ernest Pedapati

entry.summary: Combines CNNs, LSTMs and recurrence-plot representations to classify EEG signatures of Fragile X Syndrome from alpha and gamma band activity. It aims to automate biomarker characterization for a neurodevelopmental disorder with known cortical hyperexcitability.

entry.title: To Describe or Construct Statistical Learning Models Using the Category-theoretical Language

author.name: Congwei Song

entry.summary: A tutorial-style report that recasts classical statistical learning models and algorithms in category-theoretic language, aimed at newcomers and mathematicians from adjacent fields. Its stated goal is to attract more pure-mathematics researchers into learning theory.

entry.title: Micro-Segmentation Anomaly Detection in Zero-Trust Software-Defined Network Fabrics

author.name: Ashly Joseph

entry.summary: Compares a Vision Transformer and a 1D CNN for anomaly detection on simulated zero-trust software-defined network flows, finding that micro-segmented input improves accuracy and F1 over coarse-grained monitoring. The evaluation uses a synthetic zero-trust dataset.

entry.title: A Human-in-the-Loop Deep Learning Framework for Color Reconstruction of Lenticular Films

author.name: Saptarshi Neil Sinha, Tiago Kleist, Giorgio Trumpy

entry.summary: A human-in-the-loop deep learning system reconstructs color from historical lenticular film by letting experts edit a vector representation of lenticule boundaries before automated color extraction. It targets cases where fully automated methods fail, such as curved or low-contrast lenticules.

entry.title: Revisiting Classic Thought Experiments to Measure Consciousness for Artificial Intelligence Safety

author.name: Peter David Fagan

entry.summary: A research note reinterprets Leibniz's mill, the Turing test, and the Chinese Room using a proposed Conservation-Congruent Encoding framework, defining an efficiency-style metric called operational consciousness that separates task success from how compactly internal structure is reused. It argues a lookup table and a compact generative model can match behaviorally while differing sharply on this metric. Relevance to AI safety is asserted rather than empirically demonstrated.

entry.title: Fast Discovery of Inclusion Dependencies with Desbordante

author.name: Alexander Smirnov, Anton Chizhov, Ilya Shchuckin, Nikita Bobrov, George Chernishev

entry.summary: This paper details implementation-level engineering for two inclusion dependency discovery algorithms inside an open-source data profiling tool, arguing that engineering choices matter as much as algorithmic design for this computationally expensive task. It contributes efficient implementations rather than new algorithms.

entry.title: ShielDroid: A Hybrid Approach Integrating Machine and Deep Learning for Android Malware Detection

author.name: Md Faisal Ahmed, Zarin Tasnim Biash, Abu Raihan Shakil, Ahmed Ann Noor Ryen, Arman Hossain, Faisal Bin Ashraf, Muhammad Iqbal Hossain

entry.summary: Presents a hybrid classical-machine-learning and deep-learning pipeline for real-time Android malware detection that aims to catch behaviors activated only at runtime. Positioned against static-analysis screening that malicious apps routinely evade. Practical security engineering rather than fundamental research.

entry.title: Design and Evaluation of an AI-Enabled Cloud-Edge Architecture for Connected Precision Agriculture Farms

author.name: Deckshitha Angadi, Koteshwar Goud Surga, Nagaraju Lakkaraju, Naveena Budda, Vikas Agarwal, Giridhara Venkata Ram Raj Mulasa, Ravi Killamsetty, Chandrasekhara Sarma Mallubhotla, Narsimlu Kemsaram

entry.summary: Describes an IoT plus UAV plus cloud-edge system architecture using Azure services and deep learning to detect tomato leaf diseases in real time, with mobile, web and embedded interfaces. Training and validation rely on public plant-disease image datasets.

entry.title: HomoEnsNER: Does Language Alignment Outperform Architectural Complexity in Gujarati Named Entity Recognition?

author.name: Chandrakant K. Bhogayata

entry.summary: Asks whether, for morphologically rich low-resource Gujarati NER, a homogeneous ensemble of five independently fine-tuned monolingual GujaratiBERT models beats architecturally diverse ensembles and multilingual encoders. Combines the members by majority voting against single-model baselines. A focused low-resource NLP result.

entry.title: An AI-Based Decision-Support Pipeline for Day-Ahead Photovoltaic Forecasting

author.name: Fariba Dehghan, Sebastian Stein, Vahid Yazdanpanah, Stephanie Gauthier, Masood Nazari

entry.summary: This applied study builds a day-ahead hourly photovoltaic forecasting pipeline for a UK charging station with short and imperfect operational records, combining measured inverter output with public meteorological inputs. It emphasizes deployment concerns such as timestamp alignment, baseline calibration, and avoiding overstated skill from non-temporal validation.

entry.title: TS-MAMP: A Remanufactured Agricultural Robot Powered by Second-Life EV Components and NMS-Free On-Device Weed Detection

author.name: Weijie Shi, Zicheng Xu, Zhenbang Cheng, Haoran Xuan, Mingbo Duan, Gan Ge

entry.summary: TS-MAMP is a low-cost agricultural robot assembled from retired electric-vehicle hub motors and screened second-life battery modules, running an anchor-free, non-maximum-suppression-free weed detector on device. It targets smallholder farms priced out of standard Agriculture 4.0 platforms while advancing circular-economy reuse.

entry.title: FastGFDs: Efficient Validation of Graph Functional Dependencies with Desbordante

author.name: Anton Chernikov, Yurii Litvinov, Kirill Smirnov, George Chernishev

entry.summary: FastGFDs makes validation of graph functional dependencies feasible on consumer hardware by optimizing the dominant subgraph-matching stage that consumes nearly all runtime in the original cluster-oriented algorithm. It is delivered inside an open-source data profiling platform.

entry.title: CPrefix: A Combinatorial Tensor Framework for Structured Discrete Color Mappings

author.name: Yvan Richard

entry.summary: CPrefix proposes a combinatorial tensor representation for discrete multi-channel color mappings based on multinomial counting observables arranged on a Pascal simplex, separating combinatorial structure from measured values. It is offered as an analysis and reconstruction framework rather than a learning method.

entry.title: Predictive Maintenance: Deep Learning-Based Remaining Useful Life Prediction for Combat Aircraft Engines

author.name: Fatih \"Urgen, Do\u{g}ay Alt{\i}nel

entry.summary: A deep sequence model predicts remaining useful life of combat aircraft engines from multivariate sensor windows on the standard NASA C-MAPSS subsets, reporting improvements over random forest, CNN-LSTM, and BiLSTM baselines. The framing is predictive maintenance for operational readiness.

entry.title: Semantic Networks as Clues: A Theoretical Foundation and Process Optimization for Semantic Network Construction

author.name: JinWoo Ha, Dongsoo Kim

entry.summary: This theoretical paper argues that a class of semantic networks representing non-propositional textual knowledge should be treated as clues to reality rather than surrogates, which makes gold-standard evaluation impossible, and grounds their legitimacy in abductive reasoning. It then proposes ClueNetwork for ranking candidate networks produced by different keyphrase extraction, edge weighting, and community detection pipelines.

entry.title: Non-Destructive Quantification of Urea Adulteration in Bovine Milk Using Transmittance Multispectral Imaging

author.name: Sharukshan Niranjan, Iresha Ranaweera, Tharindu Chandrarathne, Kalana Dissanayaka, Roshan Godaliyadda, Vijitha Herath, Parakrama Ekanayake, Janak Vidanarachchi

entry.summary: The study builds a low-cost transmittance multispectral imaging rig and regression pipeline to quantify urea adulteration in milk without reagents or lab preparation. It is validated against laboratory measurements under controlled density conditions.

entry.title: A Context-Aware Cultural Heritage Guide Powered by LLMs

author.name: Liliana Ardissono, Fabio Ferrero, Angelo Geninatti Cossatin, Claudio Mattutino, Noemi Mauro

entry.summary: This short paper describes extending a cultural heritage web application with LLM-provided contextual information in a loosely coupled, model-agnostic architecture. It is a system description of context-dependent content enrichment and presentation.
